# Feature Docs Cross-Check — `website/docs/user-guide/features/*`

This shard is the **product view**: every page under
`/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-jarvis-hub/8afd1338-a973-516f-b42c-2b3685ad04f8/scratchpad/hermes-agent/website/docs/user-guide/features/`
(53 files: 52 `.md` pages + `_category_.json`), documented feature by documented feature, using the docs'
own headings, names, promises and examples **verbatim**, then verified against the shipped code with
`path:line` evidence and a verdict (implemented as documented / partial / doc drift).
It deliberately leaves the code-first phrasing of the same subsystems to the sibling shards
(`cli-*`, `web-*`, `tools`, `gw-*`, `platforms-*`, `config-*`, `env-vars`, `skills-core`, `tui`,
`desktop-*`, `providers`, `optional`) — here the goal is only that **nothing the docs name is missing
from the inventory**. Docs pages that are not under `features/` (reference/, integrations/, getting-started/)
are out of scope and appear under `## Handoffs`.

Doc source root for every entry below: `website/docs/user-guide/features/<page>.md`

## Page: `document-extraction.md` — Document Extraction

### Document Extraction (read_file auto-conversion)  `id: docs-features.document-extraction`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** Docs page **"Document Extraction"** (`sidebar_position: 3`, description *"How read_file converts PDFs, Office documents, and notebooks to text — and what to do when a PDF is scanned images"*). User-facing surface: the `read_file` tool, any platform.
- **What it does:** `read_file` automatically converts common document formats to readable Markdown text "so the agent can inspect a PDF or spreadsheet the same way it reads source code" (`document-extraction.md:9`).
- **How it works:** Conversion is dispatched by extension in the read/extract layer; stdlib converters handle `.ipynb`/`.docx`/`.xlsx`, everything else goes through the optional `firecrawl-anydoc` package resolved by `read_extract._anydoc()` (verified via the test contract at `tests/tools/test_read_extract.py:75-99`: *"PDF (and the other anydoc formats) are extractable exactly when the optional `anydoc` converter is importable"*). Output is Markdown, paginated through `read_file`'s normal `offset`/`limit` window (`document-extraction.md:25`). With remote terminal backends (Docker, Modal, SSH) the file's bytes are transferred across the backend boundary and converted host-side (`document-extraction.md:27`).
- **Inputs / options:** The complete documented format table (`document-extraction.md:13-21`), all 7 rows: **Jupyter notebooks** `.ipynb` / Built-in (stdlib) / Always; **Word documents** `.docx` / Built-in (stdlib) / Always; **Excel workbooks** `.xlsx` / Built-in (stdlib) / Always; **PDF** `.pdf` / Optional `anydoc` converter / Auto-installed on first use*; **Legacy Office** `.doc`, `.ppt`, `.xls`, `.pptx`, and variants / Optional `anydoc` / Auto-installed on first use*; **OpenDocument** `.odt`, `.ods`, `.odp` / Optional `anydoc` / Auto-installed on first use*; **Rich text / eBooks** `.rtf`, `.epub` / Optional `anydoc` / Auto-installed on first use*. Plus `read_file`'s `offset` / `limit` paging.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Markdown text in the tool result; lazy `pip install firecrawl-anydoc` on first use where permitted.
- **Config / env:** `security.allow_lazy_installs` (config.yaml) gates the lazy install of `firecrawl-anydoc` (`document-extraction.md:23`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** Without the optional converter, "the three stdlib formats still work; other formats fall back to the binary-file guard" (`document-extraction.md:23`). Documents over **50 MB** are refused "to keep tool turns bounded" (`document-extraction.md:25`).
- **Rebuild notes:** Extension→converter table + a lazy optional dependency + Markdown output through the same pager as text files. A better version would cache converted Markdown per (path, mtime) and expose a `format=` hint for ambiguous extensions.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (converter dispatch and availability contract asserted at `tests/tools/test_read_extract.py:75-99`).

### Scanned-PDF coverage warning  `id: docs-features.pdf-coverage-warning`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** `document-extraction.md` → **"Scanned PDFs: the coverage warning"**; appears as a prepended block in the `read_file` result, opening with the literal token `[EXTRACTION COVERAGE WARNING: …]`.
- **What it does:** Detects PDFs whose pages are scanned images (no text layer) and prepends a warning naming the exact unreadable page ranges, so the agent targets only the gaps instead of OCRing everything.
- **How it works:** Detection uses poppler's `pdftotext` for per-page text counts (`document-extraction.md:54`). The warning fires when "a meaningful share of pages yields no text (over 20% of the document, or 10+ pages absolute)" (`document-extraction.md:33`). Each gap is labeled with the last text extracted before it — usually a section divider. Code contract: `tests/tools/test_read_extract.py:740` asserts the note contains `EXTRACTION COVERAGE WARNING`; `tests/tools/test_read_extract.py:843-888` assert the extracted text *starts with* `[EXTRACTION COVERAGE WARNING` when the checker returns one.
- **Inputs / options:** Thresholds: `>20%` of pages with no text **or** `10+` pages absolute. Recovery paths documented in the warning body: (1) **A few pages — render + vision**: `pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 -f 92 -l 94 document.pdf /tmp/page` then inspect each image with `vision_analyze` ("Zero extra dependencies (poppler is required for the detection itself)"); (2) **Many pages — OCR**: the `ocr-and-documents` skill "covers bulk OCR with marker-pdf (90+ languages, handles equations and tables; ~3-5 GB install)".
- **Outputs / side effects:** A prefixed warning block in the tool result. Verbatim example (`document-extraction.md:36-42`): `[EXTRACTION COVERAGE WARNING: 198 of 311 pages in this PDF yielded no text. ... Unreadable gaps, each labeled with the last text extracted before it:` / `  pages 42-77 (36 pages) — after "Antigua Maintenance Corp Bylaws" (p41)` / `  pages 92-213 (122 pages) — after "... Covenants, Codes and Regulations" (p91)` / `  page 224 (1 page) — after "... Insurance Declaration Pages" (p223)` / `Decide which gaps you actually need — do NOT OCR or render everything. ...]`.
- **Config / env:** n/a (inherits `security.allow_lazy_installs` from the parent extractor).
- **Edge cases / guards:** "If poppler is not installed, extraction still works — the coverage check is silently skipped" (`document-extraction.md:54`). Tip block (`document-extraction.md:56-58`): the agent handles the warning on its own; a human reading extractions should treat "header with an empty body" as a scanned section, not a missing one.
- **Rebuild notes:** Per-page text-length histogram from `pdftotext`, run-length-encode the zero-text pages into gaps, label each gap with the last non-empty text before it, and emit a bounded prefix. A better version would auto-OCR only the gaps the agent then asks for, and cache OCR output per page range.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (`tests/tools/test_read_extract.py:740`, `:843`, `:879-888`).

## Page: `heartbeat.md` — Session Heartbeats

### Session Heartbeats (`/heartbeat`)  `id: docs-features.heartbeat`
- **Surface:** CLI + Gateway/Telegram
- **Where:** Slash command `/heartbeat` (alias `/hb`) in an interactive `hermes` session and on gateway platforms; on Slack it is `/hermes heartbeat …` (`heartbeat.md:40`). Docs title **"Session Heartbeats"**, H1 **"Session Heartbeats (`/heartbeat`)"**.
- **What it does:** Gives the **current session** one recurring instruction: whenever the session is idle and the interval has elapsed, the prompt fires as a normal user turn — "same conversation, same context, same prompt cache" (`heartbeat.md:9`). Example: `/heartbeat every 10m Check the deployment and report meaningful changes`.
- **How it works:** `hermes_cli/heartbeat.py` is the model: one user-owned recurring instruction bound to a session; injection uses "the same mechanism as a /goal continuation, so message-role alternation and prompt caching are untouched" (`hermes_cli/heartbeat.py:1-27`). Floor `MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 60` (`hermes_cli/heartbeat.py:43`), driver poll `POLL_SECONDS = 5.0` (`:44`). Injected text is `HEARTBEAT_PROMPT_TEMPLATE` (`hermes_cli/heartbeat.py:47-53`): `"[Heartbeat — recurring instruction, fires every {interval}]\n{prompt}\n\nIf there is nothing meaningful to do or report for this instruction right now, reply briefly that nothing has changed and stop — do not invent work."`. Interval parsing regex `_INTERVAL_RE` accepts optional `every` + number + unit (`hermes_cli/heartbeat.py:55-58`), units mapped in `_UNIT_SECONDS` (`:60-65`). State key is `f"heartbeat:{session_id}"` (`hermes_cli/heartbeat.py:146`) in `SessionDB.state_meta`. CLI dispatch: `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py:2896-2980` (`_handle_heartbeat_command`), watchdog start at `:2933` and `:2972`, manager at `cli.py:13285` (`_get_heartbeat_manager`) and `cli.py:13309` (`_start_heartbeat_watchdog`), due-check loop at `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py:1069`. Gateway dispatch: `gateway/slash_commands.py:2926` (`_handle_heartbeat_command`), per-event manager `gateway/run.py:23305` (`_get_heartbeat_manager_for_event`), watch register/unregister `gateway/run.py:23333` / `:23349`, poller `gateway/run.py:23354` (`_start_heartbeat_poller`).
- **Inputs / options:** Complete command table (`heartbeat.md:32-38`): `/heartbeat every <interval> <prompt>` — "Set (or replace) the session's heartbeat. Intervals: `90s`, `10m`, `2h`, `1d` (minimum 60s)."; `/heartbeat` **or** `/heartbeat status` — "Show the heartbeat, its interval, and time to next fire."; `/heartbeat pause` — "Stop firing without clearing."; `/heartbeat resume` — "Resume (re-anchors the timer — no instant stale fire)."; `/heartbeat clear` — "Remove the heartbeat." Alias `/hb`. Accepted interval units (from code): `s|sec|secs|second|seconds|m|min|mins|minute|minutes|h|hr|hrs|hour|hours|d|day|days`, with or without the leading word `every`. CLI usage strings emitted on error: `"  Usage: /heartbeat every <interval> <prompt>   (e.g. /heartbeat every 10m Check CI)"` (`cli_commands_mixin.py:2956`), `"  Also: /heartbeat status | pause | resume | clear"` (`:2957`), `"  Usage: /heartbeat every <interval> <prompt> — the prompt is required."` (`:2964`), `"  Invalid heartbeat: {exc}"` (`:2970`), `"  No heartbeat set."` (`:2923`, `:2941`), `"  No heartbeat to resume."` (`:2931`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Confirmation line `♥ Heartbeat set (every 15m): …` (`heartbeat.md:56`); a row in `SessionDB.state_meta`; a periodically injected user turn rendered as `Hermes: [Heartbeat — recurring instruction, fires every 15m]` followed by the agent's tool calls and reply (`heartbeat.md:60-62`).
- **Config / env:** No dedicated config keys documented; state lives in SessionDB (`~/.hermes` session store).
- **Edge cases / guards:** "**Idle-only.** A heartbeat never interrupts a running turn." "**Missed ticks coalesce.** … you get **one** heartbeat turn, not a backlog. The timer re-anchors on every fire." "**User messages win.** A queued user message always takes priority; the heartbeat waits for the input queue to drain." "**Cache-safe.** The injected prompt is an ordinary user message. No system-prompt mutation, no toolset change." "**Persistence.** … it survives `/resume` and rides across context-compression session rotations. Firing requires the owning process (CLI session or gateway) to be running; for schedules that must survive anything, use cron." "**Don't-invent-work guard.**" (`heartbeat.md:44-49`). Code adds: intervals `< 60s` raise `ValueError(f"interval must be at least {MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS}s")` (`hermes_cli/heartbeat.py:246-247`); `parse_interval` returns `-1` for too-small vs `None` for not-an-interval (`hermes_cli/heartbeat.py:70-83`); any DB/import error degrades to "no heartbeat", never crashes the input loop (`hermes_cli/heartbeat.py:24-27`).
- **Rebuild notes:** One record per session `{prompt, interval_s, next_fire, paused}` in session metadata; a 5 s poller that only injects when idle + queue empty, re-anchoring `next_fire` on each fire; the injected message is plain user-role text with a "don't invent work" tail. A better version would let a session hold several named heartbeats with independent intervals and per-heartbeat suppression when the previous fire produced no change.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Heartbeat vs cron comparison  `id: docs-features.heartbeat-vs-cron`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `heartbeat.md` → **"Heartbeat vs cron: which one do I want?"**
- **What it does:** A four-row decision table steering the user between `/heartbeat` and `hermes cron`.
- **How it works:** Static table, `heartbeat.md:21-26`. Rows verbatim — **Runs in**: `/heartbeat` = "**This conversation** — full context, memory of the discussion", cron = "A fresh isolated session per tick". **Survives process restart**: `/heartbeat` = "State survives (SessionDB); firing resumes next time the session is driven", cron = "Yes — fully durable scheduler". **How many**: `/heartbeat` = "One per session", cron = "Unlimited jobs". **Best for**: `/heartbeat` = "\"Keep an eye on X *in this thread* while we work\"", cron = "Standing jobs, reports, watchdogs, deliveries". Rule of thumb (`heartbeat.md:28`): "if the recurring prompt needs the conversation's context, use `/heartbeat`. If it's a self-contained job, use cron."
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** The "One per session" limit is a real constraint of the state key `heartbeat:<session_id>` (`hermes_cli/heartbeat.py:146`) — setting a new heartbeat replaces the old one.
- **Rebuild notes:** Ship the disambiguation table next to both features; it is the cheapest way to stop users building cron jobs that need conversation context.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (the "one per session" claim matches the single-key persistence model).

## Page: `loops.md` — Recurring Loops (`/loop`)

### Recurring Loops (`/loop`)  `id: docs-features.loop`
- **Surface:** CLI + TUI + Web dashboard + Desktop app + Gateway/Telegram
- **Where:** Slash command `/loop` (alias `/proactive`) in an interactive session; docs title **"Recurring Loops"**, H1 **"Recurring Loops (`/loop`)"**, description *"Re-run a prompt on a recurring interval inside your session — Hermes' take on Claude Code's /loop."*
- **What it does:** Re-runs a prompt (or a slash command) on a recurring cadence **inside the current session**. "Each wakeup is a real agent turn: Hermes reads the current state fresh — the latest CI result, the newest queue depth, the file as it is now — does the work, reports back, and goes quiet until the next tick." (`loops.md:9`)
- **How it works:** `hermes_cli/loops.py` holds the loop model and the completion marker `LOOP_COMPLETE_MARKER = "LOOP_COMPLETE"` (`hermes_cli/loops.py:79`); the module docstring states the same stop rule (`hermes_cli/loops.py:20`). Wakeup evaluation (marker → `--until` judge → caps → reschedule) lives at `cli.py:13445` and `cli.py:21116` for the CLI and at `gateway/run.py:23647` for the gateway ("the LOOP_COMPLETE marker / --until judge / caps and schedules the …"). Alias registration: `hermes_cli/commands.py:227` `aliases=("proactive",)`, and both names are listed among the session commands at `hermes_cli/commands.py:515` (`"goal", "subgoal", "heartbeat", "hb", "refine", "loop", "proactive", …`); the TUI gateway also exposes `"proactive"` (`tui_gateway/server.py:15561`). Positioning vs `/goal` (`loops.md:11`): "Where `/goal` is judge-driven — 'keep working until this objective is achieved' — `/loop` is timer-driven: 'do this again every N minutes (or whenever it makes sense) until something says stop.'"
- **Inputs / options:** Complete command table (`loops.md:77-84`): `/loop [interval] <prompt> [--times N] [--until <cond>]` — "Start (or replace) the loop for this session. The first wakeup fires immediately; later ones follow the cadence."; `/loop` or `/loop status` — "Show cadence, ticks fired, and time to the next wakeup."; `/loop pause` — "Stop firing without losing the loop."; `/loop resume` — "Pick it back up."; `/loop stop` — "End the loop."; `/proactive …` — "Alias for `/loop` (Claude Code parity)." Interval literals documented: `30s`, `5m`, `2h`, `1h30m`. Flags: `--times N`, `--until <condition>`. Examples verbatim: `/loop 5m check the deploy status and tell me if it's live yet`, `/loop 10m /recap`, `/loop 2m poll the build at ci.example.com/job/42 and ping me the moment it finishes`, `/loop keep an eye on the migration and summarize progress`, `/loop 2m poll CI --times 30`, `/loop 5m watch the queue --until queue depth reaches zero`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Acceptance line `↻ Loop set (every 5m): check the deploy status…` (`loops.md:30`); one normal agent turn per wakeup; on messaging platforms wakeup results "arrive as ordinary replies" (`loops.md:86`).
- **Config / env:** `loops.min_interval_seconds` (default `30`, `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2200`), `loops.max_ticks` (default `100`, `:2203`), `loops.self_paced_floor_seconds` (default `60`, `:2205`), `loops.self_paced_ceiling_seconds` (default `900`, `:2206`). The `--until` judge routes through the `goal_judge` auxiliary task, "so `auxiliary.goal_judge.*` overrides (provider, model, max_tokens) apply to loop conditions too" (`loops.md:113`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** Behavior details (`loops.md:96-100`): "**A wakeup is a normal user-role turn.** No system-prompt mutation, no toolset swap — prompt caching stays intact."; "**Survives `/resume` and compression.**"; "**One loop per session.** Setting a new `/loop` replaces the old one."; "**Interrupting a wakeup turn (Ctrl+C) pauses the loop** — recoverable with `/loop resume`, so cancel actually means cancel."; "**Token cost scales with cadence.**" Goal precedence (`loops.md:90-92`): "**an active goal owns the session**" — loop wakeups defer while a goal's judge says continue, and resume when the goal finishes, pauses, or parks on a wait barrier (`/goal wait` or automatic WAIT verdict); "A real user message always wins over both". First wakeup fires "on the next idle poll (gateway: the next 15s watcher scan)" (`loops.md:31`).
- **Rebuild notes:** Per-session record `{prompt, mode: fixed|self_paced, interval, ticks, cap, until_condition, paused}`; a wakeup injector at idle boundaries; a post-turn evaluator that checks a completion marker, an optional LLM judge, and the tick caps. A better version would allow N named loops per session with a shared token budget and would suppress a wakeup whose predicted delta is zero.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (marker, caps, judge, alias all present in code).

### Loop cadence mode — fixed interval  `id: docs-features.loop-fixed-interval`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `loops.md` → **"The two cadence modes"** → "**Fixed interval — you set the clock.**"
- **What it does:** Give an interval (`30s`, `5m`, `2h`, `1h30m`) and the loop fires exactly on that schedule.
- **How it works:** The parsed interval is stored on the loop record and the next wakeup is scheduled at `now + interval`; floor enforced by `loops.min_interval_seconds` (default 30, `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2200`).
- **Inputs / options:** Any of the documented interval literals; combined forms like `1h30m` are documented (`loops.md:42`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Wakeups on a wall-clock cadence.
- **Config / env:** `loops.min_interval_seconds`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Use it when the thing you're watching changes on its own timeline" (`loops.md:42`).
- **Rebuild notes:** Duration parser + monotonic scheduler. A better version would align ticks to wall-clock boundaries so several sessions do not all fire at once.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Loop cadence mode — self-paced (exponential backoff)  `id: docs-features.loop-self-paced`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `loops.md` → **"The two cadence modes"** → "**Self-paced — Hermes sets the clock.**"
- **What it does:** Omit the interval and the loop paces itself: it starts at the floor (1 minute by default) and, while the agent's replies stop changing, backs off exponentially — "2m, 4m, 8m, up to the ceiling (15 minutes by default). The moment a reply differs from the last one, cadence snaps back to the floor." (`loops.md:48`)
- **How it works:** "Change detection is a local digest comparison (timestamps are ignored), so idle waits cost nothing extra" (`loops.md:48`) — i.e. a hash of the normalized reply, compared tick to tick; doubling on match, reset to floor on mismatch, clamped at the ceiling.
- **Inputs / options:** No interval argument — `/loop keep an eye on the migration and summarize progress`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Wakeups at 1m, 2m, 4m, 8m, 15m (ceiling) while output is unchanged.
- **Config / env:** `loops.self_paced_floor_seconds` (default `60`), `loops.self_paced_ceiling_seconds` (default `900`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** Digest comparison ignores timestamps so a clock-only diff does not reset the backoff.
- **Rebuild notes:** `next = min(ceiling, prev*2)` on unchanged digest, `next = floor` on change. A better version would use a change-rate estimator (observed inter-change interval) rather than pure doubling.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (defaults confirmed at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2205-2206`).

### Loop stop conditions  `id: docs-features.loop-stop-conditions`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `loops.md` → **"Stop conditions"** table.
- **What it does:** Defines the five ways a loop ends.
- **How it works:** Table verbatim (`loops.md:60-66`): **The agent decides it's done** — "The wakeup prompt teaches the agent to end its reply with `LOOP_COMPLETE` on its own line when the task is finished or moot."; **A run cap** — "`--times N` — stop after N wakeups."; **An evidence-based condition** — "`--until <condition>` — after each wakeup, the same auxiliary judge that powers `/goal` checks the reply against your condition (fail-open: a broken judge never wedges the loop)."; **You** — "`/loop stop` (or `/loop pause` to keep it around)."; **The backstop budget** — "`loops.max_ticks` (default 100) pauses the loop so an unattended session can't burn tokens forever. `0` = unlimited." Marker constant at `hermes_cli/loops.py:79`.
- **Inputs / options:** `--times N`, `--until <cond>`, `/loop stop`, `/loop pause`, `loops.max_ticks`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** The loop transitions to stopped or paused.
- **Config / env:** `loops.max_ticks`; `auxiliary.goal_judge.*` for `--until`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Fail-open judge — "a broken judge never wedges the loop"; `max_ticks: 0` = unlimited.
- **Rebuild notes:** Check in order: marker in reply → `--until` judge verdict → tick cap → backstop budget. A better version would report *why* it stopped in the final message and keep the reason queryable.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### `/loop` vs `/goal` vs cron comparison  `id: docs-features.loop-vs-goal-vs-cron`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `loops.md` → **"`/loop` vs `/goal` vs cron"** table.
- **What it does:** Three-way disambiguation table.
- **How it works:** Static table `loops.md:117-122`. **Trigger**: `/loop` = "Timer (or self-paced)", `/goal` = "Judge verdict after each turn", cron = "Schedule, outside any session". **Lives in**: "Your current session" / "Your current session" / "Its own session per run". **Ends when**: "Stop condition / caps / you" / "Goal achieved / budget / you" / "You remove the job". **Best for**: "Polling, monitoring, periodic re-runs" / "One objective, iterate until done" / "Unattended, long-horizon schedules".
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "When the work should run **unattended** — overnight, on a real schedule, surviving restarts of your terminal — use a cron job instead. `/loop` lives inside a session; cron lives outside all of them." (`loops.md:20`)
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a (documentation artifact).
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

## Page: `context-references.md` — Context References

### Context References (`@` inline expansion)  `id: docs-features.context-references`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** Typed inside any CLI message: `@` followed by a reference. Docs `sidebar_label: "Context References"`, description *"Inline @-syntax for attaching files, folders, git diffs, and URLs directly into your messages"*.
- **What it does:** "Type `@` followed by a reference to inject content directly into your message. Hermes expands the reference inline and appends the content under an `--- Attached Context ---` section." (`context-references.md:10`)
- **How it works:** `agent/context_references.py`. Expansion appends `f"{final}\n\n--- Attached Context ---\n\n" + "\n\n".join(blocks)` (`agent/context_references.py:315`). Parsed references become `ContextReference(raw, kind, target, start, end, line_start, line_end)` (`agent/context_references.py:110-119`). Trailing punctuation stripped via `TRAILING_PUNCTUATION = ",.;!?"` (`agent/context_references.py:90`); values containing whitespace or brackets are quoted per `_NEEDS_QUOTING` (`:91`).
- **Inputs / options:** Complete supported-reference table (`context-references.md:14-22`), all 7 syntaxes: `@file:path/to/file.py` — "Inject file contents"; `@file:path/to/file.py:10-25` — "Inject specific line range (1-indexed, inclusive)"; `@folder:path/to/dir` — "Inject directory tree listing with file metadata"; `@diff` — "Inject `git diff` (unstaged working tree changes)"; `@staged` — "Inject `git diff --staged` (staged changes)"; `@git:5` — "Inject last N commits with patches (max 10)"; `@url:https://example.com` — "Fetch and inject web page content". Multiple references per message are supported (`Check @file:main.py, and also @file:test.py.`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** The user message sent to the model gains an `--- Attached Context ---` trailer holding one block per reference.
- **Config / env:** Limits derive from the model's `context_length` (see the size-limits entry). Blocked paths read `$HERMES_HOME`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** See the dedicated entries for size limits, sensitive-path blocking, path-traversal protection, binary detection, platform availability, compression interaction and error handling.
- **Rebuild notes:** Regex-scan the message for `@kind[:target][:lines]`, resolve each to a text block, drop them under a fixed delimiter, and leave the original message intact when any hard limit trips. A better version would render a per-reference token cost preview before sending.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (`agent/context_references.py:315` for the delimiter, `:90` for punctuation stripping).

### `@file:` line ranges  `id: docs-features.ctxref-line-ranges`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `context-references.md` → **"Line Ranges"**.
- **What it does:** Injects only a slice of a file.
- **How it works:** `ContextReference.line_start` / `line_end` carry the parsed range (`agent/context_references.py:117-118`).
- **Inputs / options:** `@file:src/main.py:42` — "Single line 42"; `@file:src/main.py:10-25` — "Lines 10 through 25 (inclusive)".
- **Outputs / side effects:** A shorter attached block.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Lines are 1-indexed. Invalid ranges are silently ignored (full file is returned)." (`context-references.md:63`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Parse `:start[-end]` after the path; clamp to file length; fall back to the whole file. A better version would error visibly instead of silently returning the whole file.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### `@` tab completion in the CLI  `id: docs-features.ctxref-tab-completion`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `context-references.md` → **"CLI Tab Completion"**; interactive prompt.
- **What it does:** Typing `@` triggers autocomplete for reference types and filesystem paths.
- **How it works:** Completion source enumerates the reference kinds and, for `@file:`/`@folder:`, the filesystem.
- **Inputs / options:** Three documented behaviors (`context-references.md:50-52`): "`@` shows all reference types (`@diff`, `@staged`, `@file:`, `@folder:`, `@git:`, `@url:`)"; "`@file:` and `@folder:` trigger filesystem path completion with file size metadata"; "Bare `@` followed by partial text shows matching files and folders from the current directory".
- **Outputs / side effects:** Inline completion menu.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** CLI-only surface.
- **Rebuild notes:** Prefix-trigger completer with two modes (kind list, path list) and size annotations. A better version would rank by recent edits and show a token estimate per candidate.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (CLI completion surface; see the `cli-*` shards for the completer implementation).

### Context reference size limits  `id: docs-features.ctxref-size-limits`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `context-references.md` → **"Size Limits"** table.
- **What it does:** Bounds how much a `@` expansion may add "to prevent overwhelming the model's context window".
- **How it works:** `hard_limit = max(1, int(context_length * 0.50))` and `soft_limit = max(1, int(context_length * 0.25))` (`agent/context_references.py:285-286`); folder listing capped by `_build_folder_listing(path, cwd, limit: int = 200)` (`agent/context_references.py:590`).
- **Inputs / options:** Complete table (`context-references.md:69-74`): **Soft limit** — 25% of context length — "Warning appended, expansion proceeds"; **Hard limit** — 50% of context length — "Expansion refused, original message returned unchanged"; **Folder entries** — 200 files max — "Excess entries replaced with `- ...`"; **Git commits** — 10 max — "`@git:N` clamped to range [1, 10]".
- **Outputs / side effects:** Either a warning trailer or an unchanged message.
- **Config / env:** Derived from the active model's context length.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Hard limit returns the *original* message unchanged (no partial expansion).
- **Rebuild notes:** Two percentage thresholds against the model context plus per-kind element caps. A better version would truncate the largest block instead of refusing the whole expansion.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (0.50 / 0.25 / 200 confirmed in code).

### Sensitive path blocking for `@file:`  `id: docs-features.ctxref-sensitive-paths`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `context-references.md` → **"Security" → "Sensitive Path Blocking"**.
- **What it does:** Refuses `@file:` references that point at credential material.
- **How it works:** `_SENSITIVE_HOME_FILES` (`agent/context_references.py:94-107`) and `_SENSITIVE_HOME_DIRS` (`:92`) / `_SENSITIVE_HERMES_DIRS` (`:93`); resolution at `agent/context_references.py:489-492` builds `blocked_exact` from home-relative files and `blocked_dirs` from home dirs plus `$HERMES_HOME/skills/.hub`.
- **Inputs / options:** Documented blocked files: SSH keys and config — `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, `~/.ssh/config`; Shell profiles — `~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc`, `~/.profile`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.zprofile`; Credential files — `~/.netrc`, `~/.pgpass`, `~/.npmrc`, `~/.pypirc`; Hermes env — `$HERMES_HOME/.env`. Documented fully blocked directories: `~/.ssh/`, `~/.aws/`, `~/.gnupg/`, `~/.kube/`, `$HERMES_HOME/skills/.hub/`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Warning "path is a sensitive credential file"; nothing is read.
- **Config / env:** `$HERMES_HOME`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Doc drift (under-listing):** the code blocks three more home directories than the docs list — `.docker`, `.azure`, `.config/gh` (`agent/context_references.py:92`: `_SENSITIVE_HOME_DIRS = (".ssh", ".aws", ".gnupg", ".kube", ".docker", ".azure", ".config/gh")`). The security posture is stricter than documented, not looser.
- **Rebuild notes:** Two deny-lists (exact home-relative files, blocked directory prefixes) applied after `Path.resolve()`. A better version would source the deny-list from a config key so operators can extend it without patching.
- **Verification:** **partially as documented** — implemented and *stricter*: docs omit `~/.docker/`, `~/.azure/`, `~/.config/gh/`.

### Path traversal protection  `id: docs-features.ctxref-path-traversal`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `context-references.md` → **"Security" → "Path Traversal Protection"**.
- **What it does:** "All paths are resolved relative to the working directory. References that resolve outside the allowed workspace root are rejected." (`context-references.md:92`)
- **How it works:** Resolve then containment-check against the workspace root before any read.
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** Warning "path is outside the allowed workspace".
- **Config / env:** Working directory / workspace root.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Applies to `@file:` and `@folder:`.
- **Rebuild notes:** `resolved.is_relative_to(root)` after `resolve()`. A better version would follow symlinks explicitly and log rejected attempts.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Binary file detection  `id: docs-features.ctxref-binary-detection`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `context-references.md` → **"Security" → "Binary File Detection"**.
- **What it does:** Rejects binary files from `@file:` with a warning.
- **How it works:** "Binary files are detected via MIME type and null-byte scanning. Known text extensions (`.py`, `.md`, `.json`, `.yaml`, `.toml`, `.js`, `.ts`, etc.) bypass MIME-based detection." (`context-references.md:96`)
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** Warning "binary files are not supported".
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** The text-extension allow-list short-circuits MIME sniffing (avoids false positives on e.g. `.toml`).
- **Rebuild notes:** Extension allow-list → `mimetypes.guess_type` → first-4KB null-byte scan. A better version would offer a hexdump preview instead of a flat refusal.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Platform availability of `@` references  `id: docs-features.ctxref-platform-availability`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `context-references.md` → **"Platform Availability"**.
- **What it does:** States that `@` expansion is a CLI feature and is *not* expanded by the gateway.
- **How it works:** "Context references are primarily a **CLI feature**. They work in the interactive CLI where `@` triggers tab completion and references are expanded before the message is sent to the agent." "In **messaging platforms** (Telegram, Discord, etc.), the `@` syntax is not expanded by the gateway — messages are passed through as-is. The agent itself can still reference files via the `read_file`, `search_files`, and `web_extract` tools." (`context-references.md:100-102`)
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** Important: an `@file:` typed on Telegram reaches the model literally.
- **Rebuild notes:** Expansion belongs in the input pipeline of the surface that owns the filesystem. A better version would expand server-side for authenticated dashboard chat too.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Interaction with context compression  `id: docs-features.ctxref-compression`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `context-references.md` → **"Interaction with Context Compression"**.
- **What it does:** Explains that injected content is subject to compression.
- **How it works:** Three documented consequences (`context-references.md:108-110`): "Large file contents injected via `@file:` contribute to context usage"; "If the conversation is later compressed, the file content is summarized (not preserved verbatim)"; "For very large files, consider using line ranges (`@file:main.py:100-200`) to inject only relevant sections".
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** Injected content is not re-fetched after compression — the summary is what survives.
- **Rebuild notes:** Tag attached blocks so the compressor can re-resolve them from disk instead of summarizing. That is exactly what a better version would do.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Context reference error handling  `id: docs-features.ctxref-errors`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `context-references.md` → **"Error Handling"** table.
- **What it does:** "Invalid references produce inline warnings rather than failures."
- **How it works:** Each resolver returns a warning block instead of raising.
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** Complete condition→behavior table (`context-references.md:134-141`), all 7 rows verbatim: **File not found** → `Warning: "file not found"`; **Binary file** → `Warning: "binary files are not supported"`; **Folder not found** → `Warning: "folder not found"`; **Git command fails** → `Warning with git stderr`; **URL returns no content** → `Warning: "no content extracted"`; **Sensitive path** → `Warning: "path is a sensitive credential file"`; **Path outside workspace** → `Warning: "path is outside the allowed workspace"`.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** Fail-soft by design — the turn still runs.
- **Rebuild notes:** Resolver returns `(block | warning)`; never abort the message. A better version would offer a one-key retry with a corrected path.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Common `@`-reference patterns  `id: docs-features.ctxref-patterns`
- **Surface:** Docs

- **What it does:** Four copy-paste recipes.
- **How it works:** Static block (`context-references.md:114-128`), verbatim: `# Code review workflow` → `Review @diff and check for security issues`; `# Debug with context` → `This test is failing. Here's the test @file:tests/test_auth.py` / `and the implementation @file:src/auth.py:50-80`; `# Project exploration` → `What does this project do? @folder:src @file:README.md`; `# Research` → `Compare the approaches in @url:https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.00001` / `and @url:https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.00002`.

## Page: `deliverable-mode.md` — Deliverable Mode (Artifacts in Chat)

### Deliverable Mode  `id: docs-features.deliverable-mode`
- **Surface:** Gateway/Telegram (all messaging platforms)
- **Where:** Docs title **"Deliverable Mode (Artifacts in Chat)"**, `sidebar_label: Deliverable Mode`, description *"How the agent ships generated charts, PDFs, spreadsheets, and other files as native attachments in messaging platforms."* No command — it is implicit in every gateway reply.
- **What it does:** "When Hermes Agent runs inside a messaging gateway (Slack, Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal, etc.), it can deliver generated files directly into the chat — not as paths the user has to copy, but as native attachments." (`deliverable-mode.md:9-11`) "A chart shows up as an inline image. A PDF report shows up as a file download. A spreadsheet uploads as `.xlsx`."
- **How it works:** Three documented pieces (`deliverable-mode.md:22-37`): **(1)** the agent has tools that produce files — `execute_code` for charts via matplotlib, the `docx` skill, the `xlsx` skill, the `pdf` and `latex-pdf-report` skills, the `powerpoint` skill, `image_generate`, `text_to_speech`; **(2)** "The gateway scans agent responses for file paths. Any absolute path (`/tmp/...`) or home-relative path (`~/...`) ending in a supported extension gets extracted. Paths inside code blocks and inline code are ignored so code samples are never mutilated."; **(3)** "The gateway dispatches by file type. Images embed inline where the platform supports it; videos embed inline; audio routes to voice/audio attachments; everything else uploads as a file attachment." Code: the extension allow-list is `MEDIA_DELIVERY_EXTS` at `gateway/platforms/base.py:2007-2026`, whose section comments match the doc table 1:1 ("Images (embed inline)", "Video (embed inline where supported)", "Audio (delivered as voice/audio where supported)", "Documents (uploaded as file attachments)", "Spreadsheets / data", "Geospatial / GIS (#24032)", "Presentations", "Archives", "Web / rendered output"); a regex alternation `_MEDIA_EXT_ALTERNATION` is built longest-first so `.tar` never shadows `.tar.gz` (`gateway/platforms/base.py:2028-2035`); the "dispatch partition (image vs video vs document) lives in `gateway/run.py`" (`gateway/platforms/base.py:2003-2004`).
- **Inputs / options:** No user-visible flags. The agent's contract: "render the file to an absolute path (e.g. `/tmp/q3-revenue.png`) and mention that path as plain text in the reply" (`deliverable-mode.md:73-75`). An explicit `MEDIA:` tag is *not* required (`deliverable-mode.md:15`), though the parser also handles quoted `MEDIA:` paths with spaces (`gateway/platforms/base.py:2103`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** The path text is removed from the visible message and the file is uploaded natively.
- **Config / env:** n/a (no config key documented on this page).
- **Edge cases / guards:** "`.py`, `.log`, and other source-file extensions are intentionally excluded so the agent doesn't auto-ship arbitrary source files; if you want to send code to the user, use a code block." (`deliverable-mode.md:53-55`) Paths inside fenced code blocks or backticks are ignored.
- **Rebuild notes:** Extension allow-list + path regex over the reply (excluding code spans) + a per-type send dispatcher. A better version would attach a content-hash dedupe so the same artifact re-mentioned in a follow-up reply is not re-uploaded.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — the doc's 9 categories and every extension match `MEDIA_DELIVERY_EXTS` exactly.

### Deliverable Mode supported extensions table  `id: docs-features.deliverable-extensions`
- **Surface:** Gateway/Telegram
- **Where:** `deliverable-mode.md` → **"Supported file extensions"**.
- **What it does:** The authoritative list of extensions the gateway will auto-deliver, and how each category is delivered.
- **How it works:** Mirrors `MEDIA_DELIVERY_EXTS` (`gateway/platforms/base.py:2007-2026`).
- **Inputs / options:** All 9 rows verbatim (`deliverable-mode.md:43-51`): **Images** `.png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp .bmp .tiff .svg` → Inline embed; **Video** `.mp4 .mov .avi .mkv .webm .3gp` → Inline embed (where supported); **Audio** `.mp3 .m2a .wav .ogg .opus .m4a .flac` → Voice / audio attachment; **Documents** `.pdf .docx .doc .odt .rtf .txt .md .epub` → File upload; **Data** `.xlsx .xls .ods .csv .tsv .json .xml .yaml .yml` → File upload; **Geospatial** `.kmz .kml .geojson .gpx` → File upload; **Presentations** `.pptx .ppt .odp .key` → File upload; **Archives** `.zip .tar .gz .tgz .bz2 .xz .7z .rar .apk .ipa` → File upload; **Web** `.html .htm` → File upload. Total 57 extensions.
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** Source extensions deliberately absent.
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep the list in one constant shared by the parser and the sender. A better version would make it config-extendable with a size cap per category.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (byte-for-byte match with `gateway/platforms/base.py:2007-2026`).

### Encouraging the agent to produce artifacts  `id: docs-features.deliverable-nudges`
- **Surface:** Config + Docs
- **Where:** `deliverable-mode.md` → **"Encouraging the agent to produce artifacts"**.
- **What it does:** Documents the two ways to bias the agent toward artifact-style replies, because "The agent doesn't reach for artifacts by default — it has to know to." (`deliverable-mode.md:59`)
- **How it works:** **Per-session:** "ask explicitly ('send me the comparison as a chart', 'return the data as a CSV') or write your own custom-instructions / personality entry that biases toward artifact-style replies on messaging platforms." **Project-level:** "add the bias to `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.cursorrules` in a project the agent works from, to your global persona in `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`, or as a named preset under `agent.personalities` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` (switchable per session via `/personality`)." (`deliverable-mode.md:62-71`)
- **Inputs / options:** `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`, `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`, `agent.personalities` presets, `/personality`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Changed agent behavior only.
- **Config / env:** `agent.personalities`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** n/a
- **Rebuild notes:** Prompt-level bias, not a code feature. A better version would ship a first-class `deliverables: true` platform toggle that injects the bias automatically.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (all four context surfaces exist — see `context-files.md` and `personality.md` entries).

### Kanban artifacts on completion notifications  `id: docs-features.deliverable-kanban-artifacts`
- **Surface:** Tool + Gateway/Telegram
- **Where:** `deliverable-mode.md` → **"Kanban: artifacts ride completion notifications"**; the `kanban_complete` tool's `artifacts` parameter.
- **What it does:** Kanban workers attach deliverable files to their `kanban_complete` call; the gateway notifier uploads each as a native attachment alongside the "task completed" message.
- **How it works:** Documented call shape (`deliverable-mode.md:85-92`): `kanban_complete(summary="rendered Q3 revenue chart and report", artifacts=["/tmp/q3-revenue.png", "/tmp/q3-report.pdf"])`. "When the gateway notifier delivers the 'task completed' message to whoever subscribed to the task in Slack/Telegram/etc., it also uploads each artifact as a native attachment to that chat."
- **Inputs / options:** `summary` (str), `artifacts` (list of absolute paths).
- **Outputs / side effects:** One upload per existing artifact into the subscriber's chat.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Files that don't exist on disk when the notifier runs are silently skipped." (`deliverable-mode.md:99`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Persist artifact paths on the run row; resolve and upload at notification time. A better version would copy artifacts into a board-owned store at completion time so they survive `/tmp` cleanup.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (see the kanban shard for `kanban_complete`'s schema).

### Comparison to Perplexity Computer in Slack  `id: docs-features.deliverable-perplexity-comparison`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `deliverable-mode.md` → **"Comparison to Perplexity Computer in Slack"**.
- **What it does:** Positions deliverable mode against a named competitor.
- **How it works:** Static list (`deliverable-mode.md:128-134`), verbatim: "Generation happens in the user's own venv / sandbox (no remote tenant)."; "Files land in the chat via the same Slack `files.uploadV2` API."; "Connector breadth comes via MCP rather than a curated catalog of 400 hosted integrations — install the ones you actually use." Closing: "OAuth tokens stay on the user's machine in `auth.json` / `.env`. No hosted token storage. No multi-tenant microVM. Same end result."
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** `auth.json`, `.env`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** The `files.uploadV2` claim is a Slack-adapter implementation detail (see the Slack platform shard).
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a

## Page: `kanban-worker-lanes.md` — Kanban worker lanes

### Kanban worker lane (contract)  `id: docs-features.kanban-lane-contract`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** Docs page **"Kanban worker lanes"** (no frontmatter). Audience stated at `kanban-worker-lanes.md:7-8`: "**Operators** picking which lanes to wire into a board" and "**Plugin / integration authors** wanting to add a new lane shape".
- **What it does:** Defines a "worker lane" — "a class of process that the kanban dispatcher can route tasks to. Each lane has an identity (the assignee string), a spawn mechanism, and a contract for what it must do with the task once spawned." (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:3`)
- **How it works:** Hierarchy block (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:14-19`), verbatim: `Hermes Kanban  =  canonical task lifecycle + audit trail` / `Worker lane    =  implementation executor for one assigned card` / `Reviewer       =  human or human-proxy that gates "done"` / `GitHub PR      =  upstreamable artifact (optional, for code lanes)`. "Hermes Kanban owns lifecycle truth — `ready` → `running` → `review` / `blocked` / `done` / `archived`." Worker-side guidance is injected as the `KANBAN_GUIDANCE` block in `agent/prompt_builder.py` (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:10`).
- **Inputs / options:** Three required lane provisions (see the three dedicated entries below): an assignee string, a spawn mechanism, a lifecycle terminator.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Rows in `task_runs` / `task_events`; per-task logs.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.review_dispatch`, `kanban.stranded_threshold_seconds`, `task.max_runtime_seconds`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Worker lanes execute work but never own that truth; everything they do flows back through the kanban kernel via the `kanban_*` tools (or, for non-Hermes external workers, via the API)."
- **Rebuild notes:** Separate lifecycle truth (kernel + DB) from execution (lane), and force every lane to terminate through a kernel tool. A better version would ship a generic CLI-runner lane parameterised by config (see the external-lane entry).
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Lane requirement 1 — assignee string  `id: docs-features.kanban-lane-assignee`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `kanban-worker-lanes.md` → **"What a lane provides" → "1. An assignee string"**.
- **What it does:** "The dispatcher matches `task.assignee` against either a Hermes profile name (the default lane shape) or a registered non-spawnable identifier (the plugin lane shape)." (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:29`)
- **How it works:** Unresolvable assignees leave the task on `ready` and emit a `skipped_nonspawnable` event — code: `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:346` (`result.skipped_nonspawnable`), surfaced by the CLI at `hermes_cli/kanban.py:2784` and `:2822-2825`, and described in the plugin dispatch result at `hermes_cli/plugins.py:352` (`skipped_nonspawnable, skipped_locked`).
- **Inputs / options:** `task.assignee` (profile name or registered identifier).
- **Outputs / side effects:** A `skipped_nonspawnable` event on the task.
- **Config / env:** Profiles come from `hermes profile list`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Tasks whose assignee doesn't resolve are left on `ready` with a `skipped_nonspawnable` event so a board operator can fix them; they are not silently dropped or executed by an arbitrary fallback."
- **Rebuild notes:** Resolve assignee → spawnable target, else record a typed skip event. A better version would suggest the nearest matching profile name in the event payload.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Lane requirement 2 — spawn mechanism and worker env vars  `id: docs-features.kanban-lane-spawn-env`
- **Surface:** Env
- **Where:** `kanban-worker-lanes.md` → **"2. A spawn mechanism"**.
- **What it does:** For Hermes profile lanes, "the dispatcher's `_default_spawn` runs `hermes -p <assignee> chat -q <prompt>` (or the equivalent module form when the `hermes` shim isn't on `$PATH`) inside the task's pinned workspace" with a fixed env-var set.
- **How it works:** Complete env table (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:36-45`), all 9 rows verbatim: `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` — "the task id the worker is operating on"; `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` — "absolute path to the per-board SQLite file"; `HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD` — "board slug"; `HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACES_ROOT` — "root of the board's workspace tree"; `HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE` — "absolute path to *this* task's workspace"; `HERMES_KANBAN_RUN_ID` — "the current run's id (for the lifecycle gate)"; `HERMES_KANBAN_CLAIM_LOCK` — "the claim lock string (`<host>:<pid>:<uuid>`)"; `HERMES_PROFILE` — "the worker's own profile name (for `kanban_comment` author attribution)"; `HERMES_TENANT` — "tenant namespace, if the task has one". Code: `HERMES_KANBAN_RUN_ID` is read at `cli.py:21534-21539` (with `logger.warning("invalid HERMES_KANBAN_RUN_ID=%r", raw_run_id)`) and `hermes_cli/kanban.py:2305`; both `HERMES_KANBAN_RUN_ID` and `HERMES_KANBAN_CLAIM_LOCK` are in the delegation env passthrough list (`agent/delegation_context.py:39`, `:42`).
- **Inputs / options:** For non-Hermes lanes, "the plugin supplies its own `spawn_fn` callable that gets `task`, `workspace`, and `board` and returns an optional pid for crash detection" (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:47`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** A child process per claimed task.
- **Config / env:** The 9 env vars above.
- **Edge cases / guards:** The optional returned pid is what enables crash detection.
- **Rebuild notes:** Spawn with a fully-specified env contract and return a pid. A better version would also pass a short-lived scoped token instead of a raw DB path.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Lane requirement 3 — lifecycle terminator  `id: docs-features.kanban-lane-terminator`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** `kanban-worker-lanes.md` → **"3. A lifecycle terminator"**.
- **What it does:** "Every claim must end in exactly one of" four outcomes; "The kanban kernel enforces that exactly one of these terminates each run. A worker that calls neither and exits normally is treated as crashed." (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:51-58`)
- **How it works:** All four documented terminators verbatim: `kanban_complete(summary=..., metadata=...)` — "task succeeds, status flips to `done`."; `kanban_request_review(summary=..., metadata=..., reviewer=...)` — "same-card implementation is complete and enters first-class review; status flips to `review`. The dispatcher loads the bundled `sdlc-review` skill unless `kanban.review_dispatch` is disabled. A reviewer approves with `kanban_complete`, returns actionable rework with `kanban_request_changes`, or escalates a genuine external blocker with `kanban_block`."; `kanban_block(reason=...)` — "task waits for human input, status flips to `blocked`. The dispatcher respawns when `kanban_unblock` runs."; "The worker process exits without a tool call. The kernel reaps it and emits `crashed` (PID died) or `gave_up` (consecutive-failure breaker tripped) or `timed_out` (max_runtime exceeded)."
- **Inputs / options:** `summary`, `metadata`, `reviewer`, `reason`, plus the `expected_run_id` parameter on terminating tools (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:108`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** A status transition plus a run row.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.review_dispatch` (set `false` for human-only boards).
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Do not place secrets, tokens, or raw PII in `summary` or `metadata`; run rows are durable." (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:68`)
- **Rebuild notes:** A run state machine with exactly one terminal transition and a reaper for the missing case. A better version would let the worker stream partial progress that survives a crash.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Review handoff models (same-card / downstream card / human-only)  `id: docs-features.kanban-lane-review-models`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `kanban-worker-lanes.md` → **"Outputs and the review handoff"**.
- **What it does:** Names the three review shapes a code-changing task can take.
- **How it works:** Verbatim (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:64-66`): **Same-card review** — "call `kanban_request_review(summary=..., metadata=..., reviewer=...)`. The task enters `review` without touching block recurrence accounting. The dispatcher claims it with the bundled `sdlc-review` skill by default. The reviewer approves with `kanban_complete`, calls `kanban_request_changes(reason=...)` to close the review run and route the task back to its original implementer, or blocks only for a genuine external escalation."; **Pre-created downstream review/QA/release card** — "`kanban_show` lists child IDs; inspect those cards with `kanban_show(task_id=...)` before choosing the terminal action. When a child is the downstream review/QA/release phase, call `kanban_complete` on the implementation phase. It cannot promote until this parent is `done`/`archived`. Do not additionally request same-card review and never sticky-block the parent with `review-required:` — either choice strands or duplicates the downstream lane."; **Human-only boards** — "set `kanban.review_dispatch: false`. A task can then remain in `review` until a human approves it or uses `reopen-review`/the dashboard to return it to `ready`/`todo`."
- **Inputs / options:** `kanban_request_review`, `kanban_request_changes`, `kanban_complete`, `kanban_show`, `reopen-review`, `kanban.review_dispatch`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Structured handoff carried "on the lifecycle transition itself".
- **Config / env:** `kanban.review_dispatch`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** The `review-required:` sticky-block anti-pattern is explicitly forbidden and detected as `review_dependency_deadlock` (`hermes_cli/kanban_diagnostics.py:753`, `:809`).
- **Rebuild notes:** Encode the review model in the task graph, not in ad-hoc block reasons. A better version would refuse the anti-pattern at write time rather than diagnosing it later.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Kanban lane logs and audit trail  `id: docs-features.kanban-lane-logs`
- **Surface:** CLI + Web dashboard
- **Where:** `kanban-worker-lanes.md` → **"Logs and audit trail"**.
- **What it does:** Per-task worker stdout/stderr plus queryable run and event rows.
- **How it works:** "The dispatcher writes per-task worker stdout/stderr to `<board-root>/logs/<task_id>.log`." (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:74`) `task_runs` rows carry "the `log_path`, exit code (where available), summary, and metadata"; `task_events` rows carry every state transition; `kanban_show` returns both.
- **Inputs / options:** Complete documented event vocabulary (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:77`), 12 values: `promoted`, `claimed`, `heartbeat`, `completed`, `blocked`, `review_requested`, `changes_requested`, `review_reopened`, `gave_up`, `crashed`, `timed_out`, `reclaimed`, `claim_extended` (13 listed; the sentence says "every state transition"). CLI: `hermes kanban tail <task_id>` "to follow live", `hermes kanban runs <task_id>` "for the historical attempt list".
- **Outputs / side effects:** Log files under `<board-root>/logs/`; DB rows.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "so a reviewer (or a follow-up worker) reading the task gets the full history without needing dashboard access."
- **Rebuild notes:** One log file per task id plus an append-only event table. A better version would rotate/compress logs and index events for cross-board queries.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (see the kanban CLI shard for `tail`/`runs`).

### Existing lane shape — Hermes profile lane (default)  `id: docs-features.kanban-lane-profile`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `kanban-worker-lanes.md` → **"Existing lane shapes" → "Hermes profile lane (default)"**.
- **What it does:** "The shape every kanban worker takes today: the assignee is a profile name, the dispatcher spawns `hermes -p <profile>`, the worker gets the `KANBAN_GUIDANCE` system-prompt block injected automatically, and uses the `kanban_*` tools to terminate the run. No setup beyond defining the profile." (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:86`)
- **How it works:** Profile discovery for orchestrators is via `hermes profile list` — "there's no fixed roster the system assumes".
- **Inputs / options:** Any Hermes profile name. Advice: "choose names that match the *role* you want the orchestrator to route to."
- **Outputs / side effects:** A `hermes -p <profile> chat -q <prompt>` child process.
- **Config / env:** Per-profile `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/config.yaml`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** n/a
- **Rebuild notes:** Reuse the product's own multi-profile mechanism as the worker identity. A better version would allow per-lane resource caps (CPU, tokens) at the profile level.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Existing lane shape — Orchestrator profile lane  `id: docs-features.kanban-lane-orchestrator`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `kanban-worker-lanes.md` → **"Orchestrator profile lane"**.
- **What it does:** "A specialisation of the profile lane: an orchestrator is a Hermes profile whose toolset includes `kanban` but excludes `terminal` / `file` / `code` / `web` for implementation. Its job is decomposing a high-level goal into child tasks via `kanban_create` + `kanban_link` and stepping back. The orchestrator skill encodes the anti-temptation rules." (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:92`)
- **How it works:** Toolset restriction on the profile + the orchestrator skill.
- **Inputs / options:** Toolsets: include `kanban`; exclude `terminal`, `file`, `code`, `web`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Child tasks and dependency links.
- **Config / env:** Profile toolset configuration.
- **Edge cases / guards:** The exclusion is what stops an orchestrator doing the work itself.
- **Rebuild notes:** Role = toolset shape + a skill that encodes the role's discipline. A better version would enforce the exclusion at dispatch time, not just by configuration.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Adding an external CLI worker lane (not a paved path)  `id: docs-features.kanban-lane-external-cli`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `kanban-worker-lanes.md` → **"Adding an external CLI worker lane"**.
- **What it does:** Explicitly states that wrapping a non-Hermes CLI (Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, OpenCode CLI, a local coding-model runner) as a lane "is *not yet a paved path*". (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:96`)
- **How it works:** "The dispatcher's spawn function is pluggable (`spawn_fn` is a parameter on `dispatch_once`), and a plugin could register its own `spawn_fn` for a non-Hermes assignee, but the surrounding integration work — wrapping the CLI's exit code into `kanban_complete` / `kanban_block` calls, mapping the CLI's workspace/sandbox conventions onto the dispatcher's `HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE` env, handling auth and per-CLI policy — is still per-integration design work."
- **Inputs / options:** `spawn_fn` parameter on `dispatch_once`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** Historical references: issue [#19931] and the closed-not-merged Codex-specific PR [#19924] — "those describe the original architecture proposal but didn't land a runner."
- **Rebuild notes:** A generic CLI-runner lane parameterised by config (command template, exit-code→terminator mapping, workspace env mapping) is the obvious better version and is explicitly named as an open design question in the docs.
- **Verification:** **documented gap, honestly stated** — `spawn_fn` pluggability exists; no bundled external-CLI lane ships.

### Dispatcher failure modes handled for lane authors  `id: docs-features.kanban-lane-failure-modes`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `kanban-worker-lanes.md` → **"Failure modes the dispatcher handles"**.
- **What it does:** Enumerates the six failure modes lane authors do not have to reimplement.
- **How it works:** All six verbatim (`kanban-worker-lanes.md:106-111`): **Stale claim TTL** — "a worker that claims and then never heartbeats / completes / blocks gets reclaimed after `DEFAULT_CLAIM_TTL_SECONDS` (15 min default) — but only if the worker process has actually died. A live worker (slow model spending 20+ min in one tool-free LLM call) gets the claim *extended* instead of killed; only a dead PID is reclaimed." (code: `DEFAULT_CLAIM_TTL_SECONDS = 15 * 60` at `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:367`, exposed as `hermes kanban claim --ttl` default at `hermes_cli/kanban.py:601`); **Crashed worker** — "a worker whose host-local PID has vanished is detected by `detect_crashed_workers` and reaped; the task increments `consecutive_failures` and may auto-block when the breaker trips."; **Run-level retry** — "the worker can use the `expected_run_id` parameter on terminating tools to fail fast if its own run was already superseded."; **Per-task max runtime** — "`task.max_runtime_seconds` hard-caps wall-clock time per run, regardless of PID liveness."; **Stranded-task detection** — "a ready task whose assignee never produces a claim within `kanban.stranded_threshold_seconds` (default 30 min) shows up in `hermes kanban diagnostics` as a `stranded_in_ready` warning. Severity escalates to error at 2x the threshold and critical at 6x." (code: `hermes_cli/kanban_diagnostics.py:958-1058`, docstring "Threshold: cfg['stranded_threshold_seconds'] (default 1800 = 30 min)" at `:962`, default read at `:986`, `kind="stranded_in_ready"` at `:1058`); **Legacy review dependency deadlock** — "a parent sticky-blocked with `review-required:` while one or more direct children remain dependency-gated in `todo` produces an immediate `review_dependency_deadlock` error. The diagnostic is read-only: it suggests completing the finished phase or unlinking the incorrect edge but never removes a user block automatically." (code: `hermes_cli/kanban_diagnostics.py:753`, `kind="review_dependency_deadlock"` at `:809`).
- **Inputs / options:** `DEFAULT_CLAIM_TTL_SECONDS` (900), `task.max_runtime_seconds`, `kanban.stranded_threshold_seconds` (1800), `expected_run_id`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Reclaims, auto-blocks, diagnostics rows.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.stranded_threshold_seconds`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Liveness beats TTL — a live PID extends the claim rather than losing it.
- **Rebuild notes:** Claim TTL + PID liveness + wall-clock cap + a read-only diagnostics rule engine. A better version would let a worker publish an ETA so the extension policy has evidence instead of only liveness.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (every named constant and diagnostic kind found in code).

## Page: `x-search.md` — X (Twitter) Search

### `x_search` tool  `id: docs-features.x-search-tool`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** Docs title **"X (Twitter) Search"** (`sidebar_position: 7`), description *"Search X (Twitter) posts and threads from within the agent using xAI's built-in x_search Responses tool — works with either a SuperGrok OAuth login or an XAI_API_KEY."* Toolset picker label: `🐦 X (Twitter) Search` (`hermes tools` → Search).
- **What it does:** "The `x_search` tool lets the agent search X (Twitter) posts, profiles, and threads directly. It's backed by xAI's built-in `x_search` tool on the Responses API at `https://api.x.ai/v1/responses` — Grok itself runs the search server-side and returns synthesized results with citations to the originating posts." (`x-search.md:10`) "**Use this instead of `web_search`** when you specifically want current discussion, reactions, or claims **on X**."
- **How it works:** Registered tool `x_search`, toolset `x_search`, emoji `🐦`, gated by `check_fn: check_x_search_requirements`, `is_async: false` (live registry dump `hermes_inv/tools_full.json`). "The tool's `check_fn` runs the xAI credential resolver every time the model's tool list is rebuilt. A `True` return means the bearer is fetchable AND non-empty AND (if it had expired) successfully refreshed. Revoked tokens with a failed refresh hide the tool from the schema; the model simply can't see it." (`x-search.md:40`)
- **Inputs / options:** Complete parameter table (`x-search.md:90-98`), all 7 parameters — `query` (string, **required**) "What to look up on X."; `allowed_x_handles` (string array) "Optional list of handles to include **exclusively** (max 10). Leading `@` is stripped."; `excluded_x_handles` (string array) "Optional list of handles to exclude (max 10). Mutually exclusive with `allowed_x_handles`."; `from_date` (string) "Optional `YYYY-MM-DD` start date."; `to_date` (string) "Optional `YYYY-MM-DD` end date."; `enable_image_understanding` (boolean, default `false`) "Ask xAI to analyze images attached to matching posts."; `enable_video_understanding` (boolean, default `false`) "Ask xAI to analyze videos attached to matching posts." Live schema confirms identical names, types and the two `default: false` booleans, with `required: ["query"]`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** JSON with, verbatim (`x-search.md:102-108`): `answer` — "synthesized text response from Grok"; `citations` — "citations returned by the Responses API top-level field"; `inline_citations` — "`url_citation` annotations extracted from the message body (each with `url`, `title`, `start_index`, `end_index`)"; `degraded` — "`true` when any narrowing filter (`allowed_x_handles`, `excluded_x_handles`, `from_date`, `to_date`) was set AND both citation channels came back empty… `false` otherwise (including the 'no filters set' case — a broad unsourced answer is just an answer, not a filter miss)"; `degraded_reason` — "short string naming which filters were active, or `null` when `degraded` is `false`"; `credential_source` — "`\"xai-oauth\"` if OAuth resolved, `\"xai\"` if API key resolved"; plus `model`, `query`, `provider`, `tool`, `success`.
- **Config / env:** `x_search.model` (default `grok-4.5`), `x_search.reasoning_effort` (default `None`; values `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`), `x_search.timeout_seconds` (default `180`, minimum `30`), `x_search.retries` (default `2`) — all confirmed at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:3646-3664`. Env: `XAI_API_KEY`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** `reasoning_effort` is sent as `reasoning: {effort: ...}`; "Leave it unset for models that do not support configurable reasoning. Invalid values fail before an API request is made." (`x-search.md:82-84`) Retry backoff "1.5x attempt seconds, capped at 5s". `xhigh` "is supported only by models that document it, such as grok-4.20-multi-agent" (`x-search.md:69-70`).
- **Rebuild notes:** A thin client over a provider-side search tool: credential resolver as the registration gate, client-side argument validation, and a `degraded` flag that distinguishes "filtered and found nothing" from "unfiltered synthesis". A better version would return the raw post objects alongside the synthesis so the caller can re-rank.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (tool present in the live registry with the exact 7-parameter schema; all 4 config keys and their defaults match).

### `x_search` vs `xurl` decision table  `id: docs-features.x-search-vs-xurl`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `x-search.md` → **"`x_search` vs `xurl`"**.
- **What it does:** Tells the agent (and the user) which X surface to use for which job.
- **How it works:** Table verbatim (`x-search.md:18-21`): `x_search` — **Use it for**: "Read-only public X discovery: current discussion, reactions, claims, profiles, threads, and synthesized answers with citations."; **Do not use it for**: "Posting, replying, liking, DMs, media upload, deleting, or proving that an authenticated X account changed state." `xurl` skill — **Use it for**: "Exact or authenticated X API work: `post`, `reply`, `read`, `like`, `dm`, timelines, mentions, media upload, account-specific reads, and raw v2 endpoints."; **Do not use it for**: "Broad Grok-synthesized public X research when `x_search` is available and no authenticated account context is needed." Mixed-workflow rule (`x-search.md:23`): "use `x_search` to discover candidate public posts, then switch to `xurl read` … Any state-changing X action must be confirmed by `xurl` output or the X API response; an `x_search` answer is never evidence that a write happened." The same prohibition is baked into the tool description in the live registry ("Do not use it to post, reply, like, DM, upload media, delete, or inspect the user's authenticated X account").
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** The "never evidence that a write happened" rule is a correctness guard against hallucinated confirmations.
- **Rebuild notes:** Put the "do not use for" half of the contract in the tool description itself, not only in the docs — this implementation does both.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (prohibition text present verbatim in the registered tool description).

### `x_search` authentication (OAuth vs API key)  `id: docs-features.x-search-auth`
- **Surface:** Env + CLI
- **Where:** `x-search.md` → **"Authentication"**; `hermes auth add xai-oauth`; `~/.hermes/.env`.
- **What it does:** "`x_search` registers when **either** xAI credential path is available."
- **How it works:** Credential table (`x-search.md:33-36`): **SuperGrok / X Premium+ OAuth** — Source "Browser login at `accounts.x.ai`, refreshed automatically" — Setup `hermes auth add xai-oauth`; **`XAI_API_KEY`** (preferred) — Source "Paid xAI API key" — Setup "Set in `~/.hermes/.env`".
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes auth add xai-oauth`, `XAI_API_KEY`, `hermes auth status`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** `credential_source` in the tool result reports which path resolved.
- **Config / env:** `XAI_API_KEY`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "**When both are configured, the explicit `XAI_API_KEY` wins** — the subscription OAuth bearer authorizes `/v1/responses` but answers x_search in a degraded Grok explanatory mode with no citations, while the API key returns real posts. Note this means x_search runs against metered API billing when a key is set; remove `XAI_API_KEY` to fall back to your subscription quota (with the degraded-answer caveat)." (`x-search.md:38`) **Internal doc contradiction:** the "Enabling the tool" section says "If both end up configured, OAuth is preferred at call time" (`x-search.md:56`), which contradicts the Authentication section's "the explicit `XAI_API_KEY` wins" (`x-search.md:38`).
- **Rebuild notes:** One resolver returning `(bearer, source)` with a documented precedence, surfaced back to the caller in the result. A better version would warn once at startup when both paths are configured.
- **Verification:** **doc drift (internal contradiction)** — the page states both precedences; `x-search.md:38` (API key wins) is the detailed claim and `x-search.md:56` (OAuth preferred) is the stale one.

### Enabling / disabling `x_search` in `hermes tools`  `id: docs-features.x-search-enable`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes tools` → **Search** → `🐦 X (Twitter) Search` (press space to toggle on).
- **What it does:** "Auto-enables when xAI credentials (OAuth token or `XAI_API_KEY`) are present. Disable explicitly via `hermes tools` → Search → x_search if you don't want this." (`x-search.md:44`)
- **How it works:** Terminal picker. Documented shell transcript (`x-search.md:46-49`): `hermes tools` → `# → 🐦 X (Twitter) Search   (press space to toggle on)`.
- **Inputs / options:** The picker offers two credential choices (`x-search.md:53-54`): 1. **"xAI Grok OAuth (SuperGrok / Premium+)"** — "opens the browser to `accounts.x.ai` if you're not already logged in"; 2. **"xAI API key"** — "prompts for `XAI_API_KEY`". Keyboard: space to toggle.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Toolset enable/disable persisted in config; credential written to `~/.hermes/.env` on the API-key path.
- **Config / env:** Toolset enablement; `XAI_API_KEY`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Either choice satisfies the gating. You can pick whichever credentials you already have; the tool works identically with both."
- **Rebuild notes:** Toolset toggle + inline credential wizard in the same picker. A better version would show the resolved credential source next to the toggle.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (toolset `x_search` present in the live toolsets dump).

### `x_search` date validation  `id: docs-features.x-search-date-validation`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** `x-search.md` → **"Tool parameters" → "Date validation"**.
- **What it does:** Validates `from_date` / `to_date` client-side before the HTTP call.
- **How it works:** All four documented rules (`x-search.md:114-117`): "Both, if provided, must parse as `YYYY-MM-DD`."; "When both are set, `from_date` must be on or before `to_date`."; "`from_date` must not be later than today UTC — no posts can exist in a window that hasn't started yet, so the call would be guaranteed to return zero citations."; "`to_date` in the future is allowed (callers may legitimately request 'from yesterday to tomorrow' to catch posts as they arrive)."
- **Inputs / options:** `from_date`, `to_date`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** "Validation failures surface as a structured `{\"error\": \"...\"}` tool result, never as an HTTP call to xAI." (`x-search.md:119`)
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** Asymmetric future rule (start date may not be future; end date may).
- **Rebuild notes:** Pre-flight validators that convert a guaranteed-empty query into a typed error. A better version would auto-clamp instead of erroring, and say so in the result.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### `x_search` troubleshooting matrix  `id: docs-features.x-search-troubleshooting`
- **Surface:** Docs

- **What it does:** Names the four failure modes and their fixes.
- **How it works:** Verbatim sub-sections: **"No xAI credentials available"** — "The tool surfaces this when both auth paths fail. Either set `XAI_API_KEY` in `~/.hermes/.env` or run `hermes auth add xai-oauth` and complete the browser login. Then restart your session so the agent re-reads the tool registry."; **"`x_search` is not enabled for this model"** — "The configured `x_search.model` doesn't have access to the server-side `x_search` tool. Switch to `grok-4.5` (the default) or another Grok model that supports it."; **"Tool doesn't appear in the schema"** — two causes: "1. **Toolset not enabled.** Run `hermes tools` and confirm `🐦 X (Twitter) Search` is checked. 2. **No xAI credentials.** The check_fn returns False, so the schema stays hidden. Run `hermes auth status` …"; **"`degraded: true` — answer with no citations"** — three causes worth checking: "**Typo in the handle.** Strip the `@`, double-check spelling, and confirm the account exists."; "**Date range too narrow** or sliding past today's posts; widen and retry."; "**xAI index gap.** Some active accounts intermittently fail to surface in `x_search` even when they post regularly. Retry after a few minutes, or use the `xurl` skill for direct X API reads when you need an exact handle's timeline."
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes tools`, `hermes auth status`, `hermes auth add xai-oauth`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** `x_search.model`, `XAI_API_KEY`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Restarting the session is required after adding credentials — the registry is rebuilt, not hot-reloaded, for this tool.
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.
