### xAI (Grok) web-search backend  `id: docs-features.web-xai`
- **Surface:** Config + Env
- **Where:** `web-search.md` → **"xAI (Grok)"** (`#xai-grok`).
- **What it does:** "Routes `web_search` through Grok's server-side web_search tool on the Responses API. Grok runs the actual searching and returns the top results as structured JSON." (`web-search.md:304`)
- **How it works:** "Works with either credential path — no new env vars, no new setup wizard": `XAI_API_KEY=sk-xai-your-key-here` or `hermes auth add xai-oauth`; then `web: {backend: "xai"}`. Optional knobs verbatim (`web-search.md:322-330`): `xai.model: grok-build-0.1` ("reasoning model required by web_search (default)"); `xai.allowed_domains` ("optional, max 5 — mutex with excluded_domains", example `arxiv.org`); `xai.excluded_domains` ("optional, max 5", example `example-spam.com`); `xai.timeout: 90` ("seconds (default)").
- **Inputs / options:** As above.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Structured JSON results.
- **Config / env:** `web.backend: "xai"`, `web.xai.*`, `XAI_API_KEY`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "**Search-only** — pair with Firecrawl / Keenable / Exa / Parallel if you also need `web_extract`. On 401 the provider performs a single forced OAuth-token refresh and retries (covers mid-window revocation and opaque tokens the proactive expiry check can't decode); env-var credentials skip the retry." (`web-search.md:334`) ":::caution Trust model Unlike index-backed providers (Brave, Keenable, Exa) which return verbatim search-engine results, xAI is an LLM choosing which URLs to surface and writing the titles and descriptions itself. The *content* of the query influences the output, so a maliciously crafted query (e.g. injected via untrusted upstream input the agent picked up) can in principle steer Grok into emitting attacker-chosen URLs. Treat returned URLs the same way you'd treat any model-generated link — validate before fetching, especially if the query came from untrusted input." (`web-search.md:336-338`) Also: "xAI Web Search is **not** in the auto-detection chain — having `XAI_API_KEY` set (or being signed in via xAI Grok OAuth) does not automatically route web traffic through xAI… Opt in explicitly with `web.backend: \"xai\"`." (`web-search.md:446`)
- **Rebuild notes:** State the trust model plainly when a "search" provider is actually a model. That caution is the most important paragraph on the page.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

## Page: `delegation.md` — Subagent Delegation

### `delegate_task` (subagent delegation)  `id: docs-features.delegate-task`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** The `delegate_task` tool. Docs title **"Subagent Delegation"** (`sidebar_position: 7`), description *"Spawn isolated child agents for parallel workstreams with delegate_task"*.
- **What it does:** "The `delegate_task` tool spawns child AIAgent instances with isolated context, inherited tool access, and their own terminal sessions. Each child gets a fresh conversation and works independently — only its final summary enters the parent's context." (`delegation.md:9`)
- **How it works:** "Top-level model calls run in the background automatically. Hermes returns a handle immediately so the conversation can continue, then posts the result back as a new message. An orchestrator subagent waits for its own workers so it can synthesize their results before returning." (`delegation.md:11`)
- **Inputs / options:** Single task (`delegation.md:16-19`): `delegate_task(goal="Debug why tests fail", context="Error: assertion in test_foo.py line 42")`. Batch (`delegation.md:27-31`): `delegate_task(tasks=[{"goal": ..., "context": ...}, …])`. Other documented parameters: `max_iterations`, `role` (`leaf` | `orchestrator`), `background`, and the control actions `list` / `steer` / `stop`. **Not** accepted: a model-facing `toolsets` parameter, or a per-task model.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A consolidated result entry per task; live transcripts; optional worktrees.
- **Config / env:** `delegation.*` (see the configuration entry).
- **Edge cases / guards:** See the context, blocking, timeout, stall and durability entries.
- **Rebuild notes:** Fresh child conversations with inherited (never widened) toolsets, background handles, and summary-only return. A better version would let the parent stream a child's partial output on demand instead of only via the transcript file.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (see the `tools` shard for `delegate_task`'s schema).

### Subagent context isolation  `id: docs-features.delegate-context`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"How Subagent Context Works"**.
- **What it does:** ":::warning Critical: Subagents Know Nothing Subagents start with a **completely fresh conversation**. They have zero knowledge of the parent's conversation history, prior tool calls, or anything discussed before delegation. The subagent's only context comes from the `goal` and `context` fields the parent agent populates when it calls `delegate_task`." (`delegation.md:36-38`)
- **How it works:** "One exception: when the parent has a resolved workspace directory, every subagent's system prompt embeds that workspace's **project context files** (`.hermes.md` > AGENTS.md chain > CLAUDE.md > `.cursorrules` — the same discovery, priority, and size caps as the main agent's system prompt; SOUL.md is excluded). Subagents working in a repo operate under the repo's own conventions without having to rediscover them." (`delegation.md:40`) "The subagent receives a focused system prompt built from your goal and context, instructing it to complete the task and provide a structured summary of what it did, what it found, any files modified, and any issues encountered." (`delegation.md:60`)
- **Inputs / options:** `goal`, `context`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** Bad/good example pair verbatim (`delegation.md:45-58`): BAD — `delegate_task(goal="Fix the error")` ("subagent has no idea what \"the error\" is"); GOOD — a `goal` naming the exact file and error plus a `context` spelling out the traceback, the call chain, the project path and the Python version.
- **Rebuild notes:** Inherit only the workspace conventions, never the parent transcript — and say so loudly in the docs.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Delegation practical examples (3)  `id: docs-features.delegate-examples`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Practical Examples"**.
- **What it does:** Three full-fidelity call examples.
- **How it works:** **"Parallel Research"** (`delegation.md:68-84`) — three tasks: "Research the current state of WebAssembly in 2025" ("Focus on: browser support, non-browser runtimes, language support"); "Research the current state of RISC-V adoption in 2025" ("Focus on: server chips, embedded systems, software ecosystem"); "Research quantum computing progress in 2025" ("Focus on: error correction breakthroughs, practical applications, key players"). **"Code Review + Fix"** (`delegation.md:90-98`) — goal "Review the authentication module for security issues and fix any found" with a context naming the project path, the three auth files, the stack (Flask, PyJWT, bcrypt), the focus areas, and the test command. **"Multi-File Refactoring"** (`delegation.md:104-118`) — goal "Refactor all Python files in src/ to replace print() with proper logging" with an explicit mapping table (`print(f"Error: ...")` → `logger.error(...)`, Warning → `logger.warning`, Debug → `logger.debug`, other → `logger.info`), exclusions ("Don't change print() in test files or CLI output"), and a verification step.
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** n/a
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Batch mode details  `id: docs-features.delegate-batch`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Batch Mode Details"**.
- **What it does:** Runs several subagents in parallel with one consolidated result.
- **How it works:** "When a top-level agent provides a `tasks` array, Hermes returns one background handle, runs the subagents in parallel, and posts one consolidated result after every child finishes. An orchestrator subagent waits for its batch in the current turn." (`delegation.md:122`) All five documented properties (`delegation.md:124-128`): "**Maximum concurrency:** 3 tasks by default (configurable via `delegation.max_concurrent_children` or the `DELEGATION_MAX_CONCURRENT_CHILDREN` env var; floor of 1, no hard ceiling). Batches larger than the limit return a tool error rather than being silently truncated."; "**Thread pool:** Uses `ThreadPoolExecutor` with the configured concurrency limit as max workers"; "**Progress display:** In CLI mode, a tree-view shows tool calls from each subagent in real-time with per-task completion lines. In gateway mode, progress is batched and relayed to the parent's progress callback"; "**Result ordering:** Results are sorted by task index to match input order regardless of completion order"; "**Cancellation:** Follow-up messages do not cancel a top-level background batch. `/stop` or closing/resetting the owning session cancels its active children. Synchronous orchestrator children still follow their parent's interrupt state".
- **Inputs / options:** `tasks` array; `delegation.max_concurrent_children`; `DELEGATION_MAX_CONCURRENT_CHILDREN`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** One consolidated result.
- **Config / env:** As above.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Synchronous single-task delegation from an orchestrator runs directly without thread pool overhead." (`delegation.md:130`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Error on over-cap batches rather than truncating — silent truncation is the worse failure.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Durable background completions  `id: docs-features.delegate-durable-completions`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Durable background completions"**.
- **What it does:** Persists completion events so a restart cannot lose a finished child's result.
- **How it works:** "When a background delegation finishes, Hermes stores its completion event in the active profile's `state.db` before publishing it to the normal fresh-turn queue. If Hermes restarts after completion but before delivery, the pending event is restored and routed through the same ownership checks. Competing consumers use a durable claim, so only the consumer that successfully accepts the synthetic turn acknowledges delivery; failed attempts release the claim for retry." (`delegation.md:132-139`)
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** Rows in `state.db`.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "This does not resume child execution after a crash. A delegation whose owner process disappears while it is still running is recorded as `unknown`, because Hermes cannot prove whether its external side effects happened. Pending and delivered records are bounded and profile-local." (`delegation.md:141-143`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Persist-then-publish with a claim per consumer. `unknown` (rather than failed/succeeded) is the honest state for an interrupted side-effecting run.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Child background-process notifications  `id: docs-features.delegate-child-notifications`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Child background-process notifications"**.
- **What it does:** Suppresses a child's own background-process notifications in the parent chat by default.
- **How it works:** "Background processes a subagent starts (e.g. `npm ci` with `notify_on_complete`) technically route their completion and watch-pattern notifications to the **parent** conversation, because anything that outlives the child needs a durable consumer. By default those notifications are **suppressed** in the parent chat — the child's consolidated delegation result is the deliverable… Suppressed events are logged at debug level with the process session ID and subagent task ID, so they remain diagnosable." (`delegation.md:145-153`)
- **Inputs / options:** `delegation: {surface_child_process_notifications: true}` — "default: false".
- **Outputs / side effects:** Restored notifications each carrying a "Started by subagent …" attribution line.
- **Config / env:** `delegation.surface_child_process_notifications`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The delegation result itself is never suppressed." (`delegation.md:155`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Suppress-but-log is the right default for noisy internal events.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Delegation model / provider override  `id: docs-features.delegate-model-override`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Model Override"**, **"Cost strategy: frontier planner, inexpensive workers"**.
- **What it does:** Routes all subagents to a different model/provider/endpoint.
- **How it works:** Basic form (`delegation.md:170-173`): `delegation: {model: "google/gemini-flash-2.0", provider: "openrouter"}` — "If omitted, subagents use the same model as the parent." Cost strategy (`delegation.md:183-190`): `model: {default: "your-frontier-model"}` + `delegation: {model: "your-inexpensive-model", provider: "openrouter"}`. Resolution order verbatim (`delegation.md:192`): "`delegation.base_url` (direct endpoint) takes precedence, then `delegation.provider` (full credential bundle resolved via the runtime provider system), and when neither is set children inherit the parent's provider and credentials; `delegation.model` applies in all cases, and when it is empty children inherit the parent's model. Setting `delegation.provider` alongside `delegation.base_url` keeps the explicit endpoint but carries that provider's request overrides and max output tokens into the child."
- **Inputs / options:** `delegation.model`, `delegation.provider`, `delegation.base_url`, `delegation.api_key`, `delegation.api_mode`, `delegation.request_overrides`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Child routing.
- **Config / env:** As above.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Note that the pin is global: `delegate_task` has no per-task model parameter, so every child in a batch runs on the configured delegation model. For quality-sensitive subtasks that need a stronger model, either leave `delegation.model` unset for that session or hand the task to the kanban board, which does support a per-task model override." (`delegation.md:194`) Rationale (`delegation.md:181`): "a parallel batch of subagents typically burns the large majority of a run's total tokens, so the worker model is where the cost actually lives."
- **Rebuild notes:** Frontier planner + cheap workers is the highest-leverage cost knob in the product; document the missing per-task override honestly, as this page does.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### `/review` command  `id: docs-features.review-command`
- **Surface:** CLI + TUI + Desktop app + Gateway/Telegram
- **Where:** `/review`; `delegation.md` → **"The `/review` Command"**.
- **What it does:** "`/review` spawns an independent, full-privilege background subagent whose only job is to review the work your conversation just produced — a PR, a diff, code, documentation, a design. It works on every surface: CLI, TUI, the Desktop app, and every gateway messaging platform." (`delegation.md:198`)
- **How it works:** All four documented steps (`delegation.md:207-210`): "1. The last 10 user/assistant messages are snapshotted as the reviewer's starting evidence (tool output and system messages are excluded)."; "2. A reviewer subagent is dispatched on the same background delegation rail as `delegate_task` — it gets the full normal subagent toolset (terminal, web, files, browser...), so it actually opens the PR, reads the diff, and runs code rather than judging from the excerpt."; "3. The reviewer inherits the primary agent's working context: any skills the primary agent had loaded (launch-preloaded or via `skill_view` during the session) are named in its briefing with an instruction to load them and judge the work against their conventions. Like every subagent, its system prompt also embeds the workspace's project context files (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / .cursorrules) as binding conventions."; "4. When it finishes, its full review re-enters the same session as a normal background-subagent completion — your primary agent sees it and can act on it."
- **Inputs / options:** `/review` — "review whatever the last 10 messages presented"; `/review focus on security` — "add extra instructions for the reviewer".
- **Outputs / side effects:** A review message re-entering the session.
- **Config / env:** `auxiliary.review.provider|model`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "By default the reviewer runs on your main model… `provider: auto` with an empty `model` means \"inherit the main agent's model\" — the default." (`delegation.md:215-226`) with the example `auxiliary: {review: {provider: openrouter, model: anthropic/claude-opus-4.6}}`. "`/review` is deliberately separate from `/refine`: `/refine` reviews the conversation to update memory and skills, `/review` reviews the *work product* the conversation created." (`delegation.md:226`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Give the reviewer real tools and the same conventions, not just the transcript excerpt. That is the difference between a review and a vibe check.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Inherited tool access and subagent tool blocks  `id: docs-features.delegate-tool-access`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Inherited Tool Access"**.
- **What it does:** "`delegate_task` does not accept a model-facing `toolsets` parameter. Each subagent inherits the parent's enabled toolsets so the model cannot grant a child capabilities that the parent does not have." (`delegation.md:230`)
- **How it works:** Blocked tools, all five verbatim (`delegation.md:233-237`): "`delegate_task` — blocked for leaf subagents (the default). Retained for `role=\"orchestrator\"` children, bounded by `max_spawn_depth`"; "`clarify` — subagents cannot interact with the user"; "`memory` — no writes to shared persistent memory"; "`send_message` — no cross-platform side effects"; "`cronjob` — no scheduling more work in the parent's name". "Both roles retain `execute_code` (programmatic tool calling) so children can batch mechanical work." (`delegation.md:239`)
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** Parent toolset configuration.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Configure the parent's tools before starting the conversation if delegated work needs additional capabilities."
- **Rebuild notes:** A child may never exceed its parent's capability set — the single most important delegation security rule.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Subagent max iterations  `id: docs-features.delegate-max-iterations`
- **Surface:** Tool + Config
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Max Iterations"**.
- **What it does:** "Each subagent has an iteration limit (default: 50) that controls how many tool-calling turns it can take."
- **How it works:** Per-call override (`delegation.md:245-249`): `delegate_task(goal="Quick file check", context="Check if /etc/nginx/nginx.conf exists and print its first 10 lines", max_iterations=10)` — "Simple task, don't need many turns".
- **Inputs / options:** `max_iterations` (per call); `delegation.max_iterations` (config default 50).
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** `delegation.max_iterations`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Hitting the budget is one of the documented legitimate failure causes.
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Subagent child timeout (opt-in)  `id: docs-features.delegate-child-timeout`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Child Timeout"**.
- **What it does:** "By default there is **no wall-clock timeout** on subagents. Children fail only from what they're actually doing — API errors, tool errors, or hitting their iteration budget — never from a delegation-level stopwatch." (`delegation.md:253`)
- **How it works:** History verbatim: "Earlier releases shipped a hard cap (300s, later 600s), which kept killing legitimately busy children mid-task: deep code reviews, large research fan-outs, and slow reasoning models routinely need more than 10 minutes while making steady progress the whole time." "Genuinely stuck children are still detected: the heartbeat staleness monitor stops refreshing the parent's activity when a child makes no progress (no API calls, no tool starts, and no activity-timestamp ticks), letting the gateway inactivity timeout fire on a truly wedged worker. An in-flight model wait still counts as progress." (`delegation.md:255`)
- **Inputs / options:** `delegation: {child_timeout_seconds: 0}` — "default: 0 = no timeout"; commented example `child_timeout_seconds: 1800` — "opt-in hard cap (floor 30s)". "A positive value enforces a hard wall-clock limit on each child; `0` or a negative value disables it." (`delegation.md:265`)
- **Outputs / side effects:** On a cap firing, structured metadata verbatim (`delegation.md:267-275`): `timeout_seconds` ("the configured cap"), `timed_out_after_seconds` ("actual wall clock"), and `timeout_phase` (`before_first_llm_call` "when the child never reached its first request", `after_llm_calls` otherwise). "All three are `null` on non-timeout errors."
- **Config / env:** `delegation.child_timeout_seconds`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Floor of 30 s on any positive value.
- **Rebuild notes:** Replace a stopwatch with a progress monitor, and when a stopwatch is opted into, emit structured metadata so callers never parse error text.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Subagent failure visibility  `id: docs-features.delegate-failure-visibility`
- **Surface:** CLI + Gateway/Telegram
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Failure Visibility"**.
- **What it does:** "A subagent that fails — non-retryable provider error (404/400), timeout, crash, or no usable output — is never silent."
- **How it works:** Three surfaces verbatim (`delegation.md:279-281`): "**CLI**: the delegation tree prints a one-line reason: `⚠️ Subagent failed — \"your goal\": HTTP 404: model not found (after 12s)`. Batch runs append the reason to the per-task `✗` completion line."; "**Gateway platforms** (Telegram, Discord, Slack, ...): the same clean line is delivered as a standalone chat notice, **even when `tool_progress` is off** for that platform."; "**Parent agent**: the tool result entry carries `status: \"failed\"` plus the full `error` text, so the model can react (retry, re-route, report)." "Error text is reduced to the single most informative line (the exception message, not a traceback wall) and capped in length." (`delegation.md:283`)
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** As above.
- **Config / env:** `tool_progress` (overridden for failures).
- **Edge cases / guards:** ":::tip Diagnostic dump on zero-call timeout With a hard cap configured, if a subagent times out having made **zero** API calls (usually: provider unreachable, auth failure, or tool-schema rejection), `delegate_task` writes a structured diagnostic to `~/.hermes/logs/subagent-timeout-<session>-<timestamp>.log` containing the subagent's config snapshot, credential-resolution trace, any early error messages, and stack traces for **all** live threads (not just the child's own) — a child parked waiting on a nested helper thread is indistinguishable from a slow provider without the full picture." (`delegation.md:285-287`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Dump all live thread stacks, not just the child's — the reasoning given here is exactly right.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Background subagent stall detection  `id: docs-features.delegate-stall-monitor`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Stall Detection for Background Subagents"**.
- **What it does:** "Background delegations (`delegate_task(background=true)`) are watched by a **progress-based stall monitor** — on by default, zero config. Unlike a wall-clock timeout, it never touches a child that is making progress, no matter how long it runs." (`delegation.md:291-294`)
- **How it works:** Sampled signals: "API-call count, current tool, and last-activity timestamp (which ticks on **every streamed token**, tool transition, and API-call boundary…)". Three documented rules (`delegation.md:301-310`): "1. **Progressing children are never touched.** Any advancing signal resets the clock."; "2. A child whose progress is completely frozen past the stale threshold (450s idle, 1200s while inside a tool — legitimately slow terminal commands and web fetches get the higher ceiling) is **interrupted** and given a 120s grace window. A child that unwinds in time delivers its partial results through the normal completion path."; "3. A child that never returns is force-finalized with a terminal `stalled` completion event, so the owning session hears an outcome instead of going silent, and the async slot frees for new work."
- **Inputs / options:** n/a (no config).
- **Outputs / side effects:** "The `stalled` event carries structured metadata mirroring the sync-path timeout fields: `stalled_after_quiet_seconds`, `stall_threshold_seconds`, `stall_phase` (`idle` / `in_tool`), and `stall_grace_seconds`." (`delegation.md:312-315`)
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** Root-cause note (`delegation.md:317-323`): "This closed a long-standing failure mode where a wedged background child left its session looking dead until a process restart. The underlying wedge (children hanging at their first API call after multi-day gateway uptime) was also fixed at the root: delegated children now run their OpenAI-wire API requests inline on their own conversation thread instead of a nested worker thread — the layer where the wedge lived. The stall monitor remains as the safety net for anything else."
- **Rebuild notes:** Two thresholds (idle vs in-tool), a grace window, then a terminal event — never leave a session silently waiting.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### `/agents` subagent monitor  `id: docs-features.agents-command`
- **Surface:** TUI + CLI + Gateway/Telegram
- **Where:** `/agents` (alias `/tasks`); `delegation.md` → **"Monitoring Running Subagents (`/agents`)"**.
- **What it does:** "turns recursive `delegate_task` fan-out into a first-class audit surface".
- **How it works:** TUI overlay features, all four verbatim (`delegation.md:329-332`): "Live tree view of running and recently-finished subagents, grouped by parent"; "Per-branch cost, token, and file-touched rollups"; "Kill and pause controls — cancel a specific subagent mid-flight without interrupting its siblings"; "Post-hoc review: step through each subagent's turn-by-turn history even after they've returned to the parent". "The classic CLI just prints `/agents` as a text summary; the TUI is where the overlay shines." (`delegation.md:334`) CLI/gateway output shape verbatim (`delegation.md:339-345`): `Background delegations: 1 running` / `- deleg_ab12cd34 · running · research the delegation stall monitor` / `  - child 1: 4 api calls · in web_search · active 12s ago` / `  - child 2: 7 api calls · between turns · active 3s ago`.
- **Inputs / options:** `/agents`, `/tasks`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Read-only view; kill/pause controls in the TUI.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "A delegation the stall monitor has flagged shows as `stalling · no progress 450s — interrupting`, and long-quiet-but-healthy children show their quiet time so you can tell \"slow\" from \"stuck\" at a glance." (`delegation.md:347-350`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Show quiet time, not just status — that is what distinguishes slow from stuck.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (see the `tui` shard for the overlay).

### Steering a running subagent  `id: docs-features.delegate-steering`
- **Surface:** Tool + API
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Steering a Running Subagent"**.
- **What it does:** "Interrupting a child throws away its in-flight work; often you just want to redirect it." (`delegation.md:354`)
- **How it works:** **Model-facing** control actions verbatim (`delegation.md:360-362`): `{"action": "list"}`; `{"action": "steer", "subagent_id": "sa-0-1a2b3c4d", "message": "focus on pricing instead"}`; `{"action": "stop", "subagent_id": "sa-0-1a2b3c4d"}`. Semantics (`delegation.md:364-366`): "**`list`** returns the conversation's live children: `subagent_id`, goal, status, `running_seconds`, `accepting_steer`, and the live transcript path. Ids also come back in the spawn dispatch response as `subagent_ids`."; "**`steer`** queues a course correction into a running child without stopping it"; "**`stop`** ends a child early at its next iteration boundary; the partial result still re-enters the conversation as a normal completion message." "Control actions run synchronously in-turn (never backgrounded), are scoped to the caller's own spawn tree — a conversation can never see or control another session's children — and never consume the per-turn subagent spawn cap, so `stop` keeps working even after the cap is hit." (`delegation.md:368`) **Session-facing** (`delegation.md:372-380`): "`steer_subagent(subagent_id, text)` in `tools/delegate_tool.py` is the redirection-side mirror of `interrupt_subagent()`: it queues text into a live child through the same mechanism as `/steer` — the text is appended to the child's last tool result at its next iteration boundary, the in-flight tool call is never cut, and the child sees it as an out-of-band user message." Gateway RPC verbatim: `{"method": "subagent.steer", "params": {"session_id": "owning-ui-session", "subagent_id": "sa-0-1a2b3c4d", "text": "focus on pricing instead"}}`, sitting "beside `subagent.interrupt`".
- **Inputs / options:** `list` / `steer` / `stop`; `subagent.steer` and `subagent.interrupt` RPCs; `delegation.status` / `list_active_subagents()` for ids.
- **Outputs / side effects:** `"queued"` or `"rejected"`; `pending_steer` / `missed_steer` on the completion entry.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The gateway accepts steering only from the exact live UI/gateway session that spawned the child. A missing, foreign, ambiguous, or stale/recycled session identity is rejected; knowing a global subagent id is not authority." (`delegation.md:382`) "**Queued is not delivered, but it is never synthetic success.** A `\"queued\"` response means the text was accepted before the child's completion boundary, not necessarily that the child has seen it. Acceptance and completion are synchronized: either the child can still consume the text, or its exact text is drained into the result as `pending_steer`. Calls after closure return `\"rejected\"`. If a child accepted the steer but had already produced its final answer, the completion entry the parent receives retains it as `missed_steer`, with a note appended to the summary: `[steer did not land — the subagent finished before it could be delivered: focus on pricing instead]`" (`delegation.md:384-390`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Never report a delivery you cannot prove; surface `missed_steer` explicitly. This is the model answer to "queued vs delivered".
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Live subagent transcripts  `id: docs-features.delegate-live-transcripts`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Live Transcripts"**.
- **What it does:** "Every `delegate_task` dispatch also creates one **append-only, human-readable log per task** so you (or the parent agent) can watch a subagent work in real time." (`delegation.md:394`)
- **How it works:** Path verbatim (`delegation.md:397`): `<hermes_home>/cache/delegation/live/<delegation_id>/task-<n>.log`. "The dispatch response includes the paths as `live_transcripts`, and the files are pre-created at dispatch time, so this works immediately": `tail -f ~/.hermes/cache/delegation/live/deleg_ab12cd34/task-0.log`. "Each line is timestamped and shows the child's assistant text, thinking snippets, tool calls (`-> tool_name({args})`), tool results, and a final status marker. A `manifest.json` in the same directory describes the batch (goals, task count, per-task status)." (`delegation.md:406`)
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** Log files + `manifest.json`.
- **Config / env:** `<hermes_home>/cache/delegation/`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The logs persist after completion — they double as the full-fidelity operational record alongside the summary — and directories older than 7 days are pruned automatically on new dispatches. Because they live under `cache/delegation`, they are also readable from remote terminal backends (Docker/Modal/SSH)."
- **Rebuild notes:** Pre-create the files at dispatch so `tail -f` works before the child produces output.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Depth limit and nested orchestration  `id: docs-features.delegate-depth`
- **Surface:** Tool + Config
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Depth Limit and Nested Orchestration"**.
- **What it does:** "By default, delegation is **flat**: a parent (depth 0) spawns children (depth 1), and those children cannot delegate further. This prevents runaway recursive delegation." (`delegation.md:410`)
- **How it works:** Orchestrator spawn (`delegation.md:414-418`): `delegate_task(goal="Survey three code review approaches and recommend one", role="orchestrator", context="...")`. All three documented rules (`delegation.md:421-423`): "`role=\"leaf\"` (default): child cannot delegate further — identical to the flat-delegation behavior."; "`role=\"orchestrator\"`: child retains the `delegation` toolset. Gated by `delegation.max_spawn_depth` (default **1** = flat, so `role=\"orchestrator\"` is a no-op at defaults). Raise `max_spawn_depth` to 2 to allow orchestrator children to spawn leaf grandchildren; 3+ for deeper trees. There is no upper ceiling — cost is the practical limit."; "`delegation.orchestrator_enabled: false`: global kill switch that forces every child to `leaf` regardless of the `role` parameter."
- **Inputs / options:** `role` (`leaf` | `orchestrator`); `delegation.max_spawn_depth`; `delegation.orchestrator_enabled`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Deeper trees.
- **Config / env:** As above.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "**Cost warning:** With `max_spawn_depth: 3` and `max_concurrent_children: 3`, the tree can reach 3×3×3 = 27 concurrent leaf agents. Each extra level multiplies spend — raise `max_spawn_depth` intentionally." (`delegation.md:425`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Default flat, opt-in depth, plus a global kill switch that overrides the model's own `role` request.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Delegation lifetime and durability  `id: docs-features.delegate-durability`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Lifetime and Durability"**.
- **What it does:** States exactly what survives what.
- **How it works:** All five documented facts (`delegation.md:432-437`): "Normal follow-up messages do not cancel background children. `/stop` cancels running background delegations, and closing or resetting the owning session discards its active children."; "Explicit session close/reset interrupts that session's background children. Closing a TUI viewer of a gateway-owned session does not kill the gateway's work."; "A Hermes process restart does **not** resume a running child. Its attempt becomes `unknown` because Hermes cannot prove which side effects happened."; "A child that completed before restart but whose result was not delivered is restored and routed back through the owning session's normal checks."; "Cancelled children return a structured result (`status=\"interrupted\"`, `exit_reason=\"interrupted\"`), but because the parent was interrupted too, that result often never makes it into a user-visible reply."
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** `status="interrupted"`, `exit_reason="interrupted"`.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** ":::warning Background completion durability is not durable execution" (`delegation.md:430`) — for durable execution use (`delegation.md:439-440`): "`cronjob` (action=`create`) — schedules a separate agent run; immune to parent-turn interrupts."; "`terminal(background=True, notify_on_complete=True)` — long-running shell commands that keep running while the agent does other things." "Stateless request/response endpoints fall back to synchronous execution when they cannot deliver a detached result later."
- **Rebuild notes:** Name the difference between durable *delivery* and durable *execution* — most systems blur it.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Delegation key properties  `id: docs-features.delegate-key-properties`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Key Properties"**.
- **What it does:** Seven summary invariants.
- **How it works:** All seven verbatim (`delegation.md:445-452`): "Each subagent gets its **own terminal session** (separate from the parent)"; "Subagents inherit the parent's enabled toolsets; the model cannot select or widen them per call"; "**Nested delegation is opt-in** — only `role=\"orchestrator\"` children can delegate further, and only when `max_spawn_depth` is raised from its default of 1 (flat). Disable globally with `orchestrator_enabled: false`."; "Leaf subagents **cannot** call: `delegate_task`, `clarify`, `memory`, `send_message`, `cronjob`. Orchestrator subagents retain `delegate_task` but keep the other blocks. Both roles retain `execute_code`…"; "**Cancellation follows ownership** — `/stop` or closing/resetting the owning session cancels its background children; synchronous descendants under orchestrators follow their parent's interrupt state"; "Only the final summary enters the parent's context, keeping token usage efficient"; "Subagents inherit the parent's **API key, provider configuration, and credential pool** (enabling key rotation on rate limits)".
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** n/a
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Worktree isolation for subagents  `id: docs-features.delegate-worktree-isolation`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Worktree Isolation"**.
- **What it does:** "By default, subagents share the parent's working directory — fine for research and read-heavy work, but parallel children editing the same repo can collide. Set `delegation.worktree_isolation: true` to give each child its own git worktree, branched from the repo's current `HEAD` (inspired by Muse Code's `--subagent-worktree-isolation`)." (`delegation.md:456-461`)
- **How it works:** All five documented behaviors (`delegation.md:468-484`): "Each child starts its terminal in `<repo>/.worktrees/subagent-<id>` on its own branch `hermes-subagent/subagent-<id>`, and its goal message tells it to work and commit there."; "The parent's checkout stays untouched; children can't clobber each other's edits."; "When a child finishes, its result entry gains a `worktree` field reporting `path`, `branch`, `commits` (ahead of the base), and `dirty`. The parent reviews or merges each branch (`git log <branch>`, `git merge <branch>`)."; "A worktree left with **no commits and a clean tree is pruned automatically** (`pruned: true`); anything holding work is kept."; "Pruning requires proof. If a git inspection probe fails — or finalization itself errors — the worktree and branch are kept and the entry carries `inspection_failed: true` plus a `note` — `commits`/`dirty` are then defaults, not measurements, so inspect the worktree rather than assuming the child produced nothing."
- **Inputs / options:** `delegation: {worktree_isolation: true}` — "default: false".
- **Outputs / side effects:** Worktrees under `<repo>/.worktrees/`; branches `hermes-subagent/<id>`; a `worktree` field on each result.
- **Config / env:** `delegation.worktree_isolation`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Scope: opt-in, git-only, and local-terminal-backend-only. In a non-git directory, on docker/ssh/modal backends, or if worktree creation fails, the setting degrades silently to today's shared-workspace behavior — never an error." (`delegation.md:486-490`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Never prune on a failed measurement — `inspection_failed: true` instead of assuming empty. That single rule prevents silent work loss.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### `delegate_task` vs `execute_code`  `id: docs-features.delegate-vs-execute-code`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `delegation.md` → **"Delegation vs execute_code"**.
- **What it does:** Seven-row comparison.
- **How it works:** Complete table (`delegation.md:493-501`), all 7 rows verbatim: **Reasoning** — "Full LLM reasoning loop" vs "Just Python code execution"; **Context** — "Fresh isolated conversation" vs "No conversation, just script"; **Tool access** — "All non-blocked tools with reasoning" vs "7 tools via RPC, no reasoning"; **Parallelism** — "3 concurrent subagents by default (configurable)" vs "Single script"; **Best for** — "Complex tasks needing judgment" vs "Mechanical multi-step pipelines"; **Token cost** — "Higher (full LLM loop)" vs "Lower (only stdout returned)"; **User interaction** — "None (subagents can't clarify)" vs "None". "**Rule of thumb:** Use `delegate_task` when the subtask requires reasoning, judgment, or multi-step problem solving. Use `execute_code` when you need mechanical data processing or scripted workflows." (`delegation.md:503`)
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** n/a
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Delegation configuration keys  `id: docs-features.delegate-config`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `config.yaml` → `delegation:`.
- **What it does:** Every documented delegation key.
- **How it works:** Documented block with comments verbatim (`delegation.md:508-517`): `max_iterations: 50` ("Max turns per child (default: 50)"); `max_concurrent_children: 3` ("Parallel children per batch (default: 3)"); `worktree_isolation: false` ("Give each child its own git worktree"); `max_spawn_depth: 1` ("Tree depth (floor 1, no ceiling, default 1 = flat). Raise to 2 to allow orchestrator children to spawn leaves; 3+ for deeper trees."); `orchestrator_enabled: true` ("Disable to force all children to leaf role."); `model: "google/gemini-3-flash-preview"` ("Optional provider/model override"); `provider: "openrouter"` ("Optional built-in provider"); `api_mode: anthropic_messages` ("optional; auto-detected from base_url for anthropic_messages endpoints"). Direct-endpoint form (`delegation.md:519-523`): `model: "qwen2.5-coder"`, `base_url: "http://localhost:1234/v1"`, `api_key: "local-key"`, with the `api_mode` comment naming the three wire protocols "chat_completions", "codex_responses", "anthropic_messages" and the endpoints the heuristic can't classify ("Azure AI Foundry, MiniMax, Zhipu GLM, LiteLLM proxies, …"). `request_overrides` example (`delegation.md:526-534`): `delegation: {model: "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731", base_url: "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1", api_key: "sk-or-...", request_overrides: {extra_body: {provider: {sort: throughput}}}}` — "children route to the fastest OpenRouter provider". Also documented on this page: `delegation.child_timeout_seconds`, `delegation.surface_child_process_notifications`.
- **Inputs / options:** As above; env `DELEGATION_MAX_CONCURRENT_CHILDREN`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Child spawn behavior.
- **Config / env:** `delegation.*`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "When `base_url` points at an Anthropic-compatible endpoint — for example a path ending in `/anthropic`, an Azure Foundry Claude route, or a MiniMax `/anthropic` proxy — `api_mode` is auto-detected as `anthropic_messages`… Set `api_mode` explicitly when the auto-detection guess is wrong (rare)." (`delegation.md:536`) "`delegation.request_overrides` works on **all three** resolution branches — direct `base_url`, named `provider`, and pure inherit — so it always takes effect. Top-level keys are API kwargs (e.g. `service_tier`); an `extra_body` sub-dict is merged into the request's `extra_body`. Explicit values merge **over** runtime- or parent-derived overrides: explicit top-level keys win, and `extra_body` is deep-merged one level, so a provider's own request personality (e.g. `thinking: {type: disabled}`) survives unless your key redefines it." (`delegation.md:538`) ":::tip The agent handles delegation automatically based on the task complexity. You don't need to explicitly ask it to delegate." (`delegation.md:540-542`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Specify merge semantics precisely (one-level deep merge, explicit wins) — vague override semantics are a permanent source of bugs.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

## Page: `codex-app-server-runtime.md` — Codex App-Server Runtime (optional)

### Codex app-server runtime  `id: docs-features.codex-runtime`
- **Surface:** Config + CLI
- **Where:** `/codex-runtime codex_app_server`; `model.openai_runtime`. Docs title **"Codex App-Server Runtime (optional)"**, `sidebar_label: Codex App-Server Runtime`.
- **What it does:** "Hermes can optionally hand `openai/*` and `openai-codex/*` turns to the Codex CLI app-server instead of running its own tool loop. When enabled, terminal commands, file edits, sandboxing, and MCP tool calls all execute inside Codex's runtime — Hermes becomes the shell around it (sessions DB, slash commands, gateway, memory and skill review)." (`codex-app-server-runtime.md:8`)
- **How it works:** JSON-RPC over stdio to a `codex app-server` subprocess; `AIAgent.run_conversation()` branches to `CodexAppServerSession` when `api_mode == codex_app_server` (architecture diagram, `codex-app-server-runtime.md:417-450`). Five documented motivations (`:18-22`): "Run OpenAI agent turns against your **ChatGPT subscription** (no API key required) using the same auth flow Codex CLI uses."; "Use **Codex's own toolset and sandbox** — `shell` for terminal/read/write/search, `apply_patch` for structured edits, `update_plan` for planning, all running inside seatbelt/landlock sandboxing."; "**Native Codex plugins** — Linear, GitHub, Gmail, Calendar, Canva, etc. — installed via `codex plugin` are auto-migrated and active in your Hermes session."; "**Hermes' richer tools come along** — web_search, web_extract, browser automation, vision, image generation, skills, and TTS work via an MCP callback."; "**Memory and skill nudges keep working** — Codex's events are projected into Hermes' message shape so the self-improvement loop sees a normal-looking transcript."
- **Inputs / options:** See the enabling entry.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Managed block in `~/.codex/config.toml`; `model.openai_runtime` in `config.yaml`.
- **Config / env:** `model.openai_runtime`, `CODEX_HOME`, `RUST_LOG`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "This is **opt-in only**. Default Hermes behavior is unchanged unless you flip the flag. Hermes never auto-routes you onto this runtime." (`:10`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Delegate the whole agent loop to another runtime while keeping the shell (sessions, slash commands, review) and bridging tools back through MCP. A better version would let both loops coexist per-turn.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (`agent/codex_runtime.py`, `agent/transports/hermes_tools_mcp_server.py` present in the tree).

### Codex built-in toolset (5 tools)  `id: docs-features.codex-builtin-tools`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** `codex-app-server-runtime.md` → **"1. Codex's built-in toolset (always on)"**.
- **What it does:** The five tools that ship with `codex app-server` itself.
- **How it works:** All five verbatim (`:32-36`): "**`shell`** — runs arbitrary shell commands inside the sandbox. This is how the model reads files (`cat`, `head`, `tail`), writes them (`echo > foo`, heredocs), searches them (`find`, `rg`, `grep`), navigates directories (`ls`, `cd`), runs builds, manages processes, and anything else you'd do in bash."; "**`apply_patch`** — applies a structured multi-file diff in Codex's patch format."; "**`update_plan`** — codex's internal todo / plan tracker. Equivalent of Hermes' `todo` tool, but managed entirely inside codex's runtime."; "**`view_image`** — load a local image file into the conversation so the model can see it."; "**`web_search`** — codex has its own built-in web search when configured. Hermes also exposes `web_search` (Firecrawl-backed) via the callback below; the model picks whichever it prefers."
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** Sandbox profile (`:workspace` by default).
- **Edge cases / guards:** "So **anything you'd do via terminal — read/write/search/find/run — codex does natively**. The sandbox profile (`:workspace` by default when you enable the runtime) controls what's writable." (`:38`)
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Native Codex plugin migration  `id: docs-features.codex-plugin-migration`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `codex-app-server-runtime.md` → **"2. Native Codex plugins"** and **"Native Codex plugin migration"**.
- **What it does:** "When you enable the runtime, Hermes queries codex's `plugin/list` RPC and writes a `[plugins.\"<name>@openai-curated\"]` entry for every plugin you have installed." (`:42`)
- **How it works:** "For each plugin where `installed: true`, Hermes writes a `[plugins.\"<name>@openai-curated\"]` block enabling it in your Hermes session." (`:354`) Documented examples (`:46-52`): **Linear** ("find/update issues"); **GitHub** ("search code, view PRs, comment"); **Gmail** ("read/send mail"); **Google Calendar** ("create/find events"); **Outlook calendar/email** ("same shape via the Microsoft connector"); **Canva** ("design generation"); "...whatever else you've installed via `codex plugin marketplace add openai-curated` + `codex plugin install ...`".
- **Inputs / options:** n/a (automatic on enable).
- **Outputs / side effects:** TOML plugin blocks in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
- **Config / env:** `~/.codex/config.toml`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Not migrated, all four verbatim (`:358-361`): "Plugins you haven't installed yet — install them in Codex first."; "Plugins where codex reports `availability != AVAILABLE` (broken install, expired OAuth, removed from marketplace, etc.). These are skipped to avoid writing config that would fail at activation time."; "ChatGPT app marketplace entries (the per-account `app/list` results — these are already enabled inside codex by virtue of your account auth)."; "Plugin OAuth — you authorize each plugin once in Codex itself; Hermes doesn't touch credentials."
- **Rebuild notes:** Skip unavailable plugins rather than writing config that fails at activation.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Hermes tool callback MCP server  `id: docs-features.codex-tool-callback`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** `codex-app-server-runtime.md` → **"3. Hermes tool callback"** and **"Hermes tool callback (the new MCP server)"**.
- **What it does:** "Hermes registers itself as an MCP server so codex can call back for tools codex doesn't ship with." (`:60`)
- **How it works:** Registered TOML block verbatim (`:369-375`): `[mcp_servers.hermes-tools]` with `command = "/path/to/python"`, `args = ["-m", "agent.transports.hermes_tools_mcp_server"]`, `env = { HERMES_HOME = "/your/.hermes", PYTHONPATH = "...", HERMES_QUIET = "1" }`, `startup_timeout_sec = 30.0`, `tool_timeout_sec = 600.0`. "When the model calls `web_search` (or another exposed Hermes tool), codex spawns the `hermes_tools_mcp_server` subprocess via stdio, the request is dispatched through `model_tools.handle_function_call()`, and the result is projected back to codex like any other MCP response." (`:377`)
- **Inputs / options:** Complete exposed-tool list (`:379`), all 17: `web_search`, `web_extract`, `browser_navigate`, `browser_click`, `browser_type`, `browser_press`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_back`, `browser_get_images`, `browser_console`, `browser_vision`, `vision_analyze`, `image_generate`, `skill_view`, `skills_list`, `text_to_speech`. Kanban tools are additionally exposed (see the kanban entry).
- **Outputs / side effects:** A subprocess per call.
- **Config / env:** `HERMES_HOME`, `PYTHONPATH`, `HERMES_QUIET`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "**Tools NOT available:** `delegate_task`, `memory`, `session_search`, `todo`. These need the running AIAgent context to dispatch (mid-loop state) and a stateless MCP callback can't drive them. Use the default Hermes runtime (`/codex-runtime auto`) when you need these." (`:381`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Expose only tools that are genuinely stateless over the callback; name the four that are not.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (`agent/transports/hermes_tools_mcp_server.py` exists).

### `/goal`, kanban and cron on the codex runtime  `id: docs-features.codex-workflow-features`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `codex-app-server-runtime.md` → **"Workflow features (`/goal`, kanban, cron)"**.
- **What it does:** States which workflow features survive the runtime switch.
- **How it works:** **`/goal`** — "**Works on this runtime.** Goals persist in `state_meta` keyed by session id, the continuation prompt feeds back as a normal user message through `run_conversation()`, and codex executes the next turn natively. The goal judge runs via the auxiliary client… independent of which runtime is active." (`:84`) **Kanban** — "**Works on this runtime, with one subtle dependency.** The kanban dispatcher spawns each worker as a separate `hermes chat -q` subprocess that reads the user's config — which means if `model.openai_runtime: codex_app_server` is set globally, workers also come up on the codex runtime." (`:90`) Callback-exposed kanban tools verbatim (`:98-100`): "**`kanban_complete` / `kanban_block` / `kanban_comment` / `kanban_heartbeat`** — the worker handoff tools. These read `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` from env (set by the dispatcher), gate access correctly, and write to the per-board SQLite DB pinned by `HERMES_KANBAN_DB`. Without these in the callback, a worker on this runtime could do its task but couldn't report back, hanging until the dispatcher's timeout."; "**`kanban_show` / `kanban_list`** — read-only board queries"; "**`kanban_create` / `kanban_unblock` / `kanban_link`** — orchestrator-only operations." **Cron** — "**Not specifically tested.** Cron jobs run via `cronjob` → `AIAgent.run_conversation`, the same code path as the CLI… If your cron job relies on those, scope the cron to a profile that uses the default runtime." (`:106`)
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`, `HERMES_KANBAN_DB`, `HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACES_ROOT`, `HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE`, legacy `HERMES_KANBAN_ROOT`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Goal caveat (`:86`): "each continuation prompt is a fresh codex turn, which means codex re-evaluates command approval policy from scratch. If you're doing a long-running goal with lots of writes, expect more approval prompts than you'd see on a single in-session task." Kanban sandbox overrides (`:102`): "keep `workspace-write` sandboxing, add the **board DB directory plus every Kanban path the dispatcher pinned** as extra writable roots (`HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACES_ROOT`, `HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE`, legacy `HERMES_KANBAN_ROOT` — deduplicated, DB-dir first), and keep network disabled by default. This avoids the brittle `:danger-no-sandbox` workaround" (issue #27941).
- **Rebuild notes:** Grant the narrowest extra writable roots rather than disabling the sandbox.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented; cron path explicitly labelled untested.

### Self-improvement loop on the codex runtime  `id: docs-features.codex-self-improvement`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `codex-app-server-runtime.md` → **"Self-improvement loop (memory + skill nudges)"**.
- **What it does:** Keeps the memory/skill nudges working when Codex owns the loop.
- **How it works:** Thresholds verbatim (`:202-203`): "Every 10 user prompts → a forked review agent looks at the conversation and decides whether anything should be saved to memory."; "Every 10 tool iterations within a single turn → same idea but for skills (`skill_manage` writes)." "**Both keep working on the codex runtime.** The codex path projects each completed `commandExecution` / `fileChange` / `mcpToolCall` / `dynamicToolCall` item into a synthetic `assistant tool_call` + `tool` result message, so by the time the review runs it sees the same shape it sees on the default Hermes runtime." (`:205`) Equivalence table (`:209-214`), all 5 rows: `_turns_since_memory` increments — "per user prompt, in run_conversation pre-loop" / "same code path, before the early-return"; `_iters_since_skill` increments — "per tool iteration in the chat-completions loop" / "by `turn.tool_iterations` after the codex turn returns"; Memory trigger (`_turns_since_memory >= _memory_nudge_interval`) — "computed in pre-loop, fires after response" / "computed in pre-loop, passed through to codex helper"; Skill trigger (`_iters_since_skill >= _skill_nudge_interval`) — "computed after the loop" / "computed after the codex turn"; `_spawn_background_review(...)` — "called when either trigger fires" / "called identically when either trigger fires".
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** Background review forks.
- **Config / env:** `auxiliary.background_review.*`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "One detail: the review fork itself needs to call Hermes' agent-loop tools (`memory`, `skill_manage`), which require Hermes' own dispatch. So when the parent agent is on `codex_app_server`, the review fork is **downgraded to `codex_responses`** — same OAuth credentials, same `openai-codex` provider, but talks to OpenAI's Responses API directly so Hermes owns the loop and the agent-loop tools work. This is invisible to the user." (`:216`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Project foreign runtime events into your own message shape so downstream consumers need no special cases.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Codex approvals in Hermes UI  `id: docs-features.codex-approvals`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `codex-app-server-runtime.md` → **"How approvals work"**.

- **How it works:** Rendered prompt verbatim (`:225-238`): `╭───…╮` / `│ Dangerous Command                     │` / `│ /bin/bash -lc 'echo hello > foo.txt'  │` / `│ ❯ 1. Allow once                       │` / `│   2. Allow for this session           │` / `│   3. Deny                             │` / `│ Codex requests exec in /your/cwd      │`.
- **Inputs / options:** All three options verbatim (`:240-242`): "**Allow once** → approve this single command."; "**Allow for this session** → Codex won't re-prompt for similar commands."; "**Deny** → command is rejected; Codex continues in read-only mode."
- **Outputs / side effects:** Approval decision sent back to Codex.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "For `apply_patch` (file edit) approvals, Hermes shows a summary of what changed (`1 add, 1 update: /tmp/new.py, /tmp/old.py`) when codex provides the data via the corresponding `fileChange` item." (`:244`)
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### ChatGPT-subscription aux-task cost warning  `id: docs-features.codex-aux-cost`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `codex-app-server-runtime.md` → **"Auxiliary tasks and ChatGPT subscription token cost"**.
- **What it does:** Warns that aux tasks bill against the ChatGPT subscription by default on this runtime.
- **How it works:** "When this runtime is on with the `openai-codex` provider, **auxiliary tasks (title generation, context compression, vision auto-detect, the background self-improvement review fork) also flow through your ChatGPT subscription by default**, because Hermes' auxiliary client uses the main provider/model when no per-task override is set." (`:264`) "This isn't specific to `codex_app_server` — it's true for the existing `codex_responses` path too — but it's more visible here because you're explicitly opting in for the subscription billing." (`:266`)

- **Rebuild notes:** Name the billing surface explicitly when a runtime switch changes who pays.

### Editing `~/.codex/config.toml` safely (managed block)  `id: docs-features.codex-config-markers`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `codex-app-server-runtime.md` → **"Editing `~/.codex/config.toml` safely"**.
- **What it does:** "Hermes wraps everything it manages between two marker comments."
- **How it works:** Markers verbatim (`:291-300`): `# managed by hermes-agent — \`hermes codex-runtime migrate\` regenerates this section` … `# end hermes-agent managed section`, with `default_permissions = ":workspace"`, `[mcp_servers.filesystem]`, `[plugins."github@openai-curated"]` inside. "Anything **outside** that block is yours. Re-running migration … replaces the managed block in place but preserves user content above and below it verbatim." (`:302`)
- **Inputs / options:** Four documented user-owned uses (`:304-307`): "Add your own MCP servers Hermes doesn't know about"; "Override `default_permissions` to `:read-only` if you prefer to be prompted"; "Configure codex-only options (model, providers, otel, etc.)"; "Add user-defined permission profiles in `[permissions.<name>]` tables".
- **Outputs / side effects:** TOML rewrites of the managed region only.
- **Config / env:** `~/.codex/config.toml`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Anything you add **inside** the managed block will get clobbered on the next migration. If you need a tweak that requires editing the managed block, file an issue and we'll add the knob." (`:309`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Marker-delimited managed regions are the right way to co-own a third-party config file.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Multi-profile Codex isolation (`CODEX_HOME`)  `id: docs-features.codex-multi-profile`
- **Surface:** Env
- **Where:** `codex-app-server-runtime.md` → **"Multi-profile / multi-tenant setups"**.
- **What it does:** "By default, Hermes points the codex subprocess at `~/.codex/` regardless of which Hermes profile is active. This means `hermes -p work` and `hermes -p personal` share the same Codex auth, plugins, and config." (`:313`)
- **How it works:** Opt-in isolation (`:318`): `CODEX_HOME=~/.hermes/profiles/work/codex hermes chat`. "You'll need to re-run `codex login` once with that `CODEX_HOME` set so the OAuth tokens land in the profile-scoped location." (`:320`)
- **Inputs / options:** `CODEX_HOME`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Isolated Codex state per profile.
- **Config / env:** `CODEX_HOME`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "We don't auto-scope this because moving an existing user's `~/.codex/` would silently invalidate their Codex CLI auth — anyone who already ran `codex login` would have to re-authenticate. Opt-in feels safer than surprising users." (`:322`)
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### MCP server migration to Codex TOML  `id: docs-features.codex-mcp-migration`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `codex-app-server-runtime.md` → **"MCP server migration"**.
- **What it does:** "Hermes' `mcp_servers` config is auto-translated to the TOML format Codex expects. The migration runs every time you enable the runtime and is idempotent." (`:335`)
- **How it works:** Complete translation table (`:339-345`), all 5 rows verbatim: "`command` + `args` + `env`" → "stdio transport"; "`url` + `headers`" → "streamable_http transport"; `timeout` → `tool_timeout_sec`; `connect_timeout` → `startup_timeout_sec`; "`enabled: false`" → "`enabled = false`".
- **Inputs / options:** n/a

### Codex runtime limitations (beta)  `id: docs-features.codex-limitations`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `codex-app-server-runtime.md` → **"Limitations"**.
- **What it does:** States what is verified working and what is known broken.
- **How it works:** Verified as of "Hermes Agent 2026.5 + Codex CLI 0.130.0", all 8 verbatim (`:397-404`): "Multi-turn conversations"; "`commandExecution` and `fileChange` (apply_patch) approvals via Hermes UI"; "MCP tool calls (verified against `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` and the new `hermes-tools` callback)"; "Native Codex plugin migration (verified against Linear / GitHub / Calendar inventory)"; "Deny/cancel paths"; "Toggle on/off cycle"; "Memory and skill nudge counters (verified live via integration tests)"; "Hermes web_search through codex (verified live…)". Known limitations, all 4 verbatim (`:408-411`): "**Hermes auth and codex auth are separate sessions.** You need both `codex login` AND `hermes auth add openai-codex` for the cleanest UX… Hermes won't share OAuth state with codex CLI to avoid clobbering each other on token refresh."; "**`delegate_task`, `memory`, `session_search`, `todo` are unavailable on this runtime.**"; "**No inline patch preview in approval prompts when codex doesn't track the changeset.** Codex's `fileChange` approval params don't always carry the changeset. Hermes caches the data from the corresponding `item/started` notification when possible, but if approval arrives before the item has streamed, the prompt falls back to whatever `reason` codex provides."; "**Sub-second cancellation isn't guaranteed.** Mid-stream interrupts (Ctrl+C while codex is responding) are sent via `turn/interrupt`, but if codex has already flushed the final message, you get the response anyway."
- **Inputs / options:** Bug reports: "open an issue with the output of `hermes logs --since 5m`. Mention `codex-runtime` in the title so it's easy to triage." (`:413`)
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** Labelled "**opt-in beta**".
- **Rebuild notes:** Publishing the verified list next to the known-broken list is the honest way to ship a beta runtime.
- **Verification:** **documented beta with named gaps** — accurate as written.

## Page: `built-in-plugins.md` — Built-in Plugins

### Bundled plugin discovery  `id: docs-features.builtin-plugins-discovery`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `<repo>/plugins/<name>/`; `built-in-plugins.md` → **"How discovery works"** (`sidebar_position: 12`, description *"Plugins shipped with Hermes Agent that run automatically via lifecycle hooks — disk-cleanup and friends"*).
- **What it does:** "Hermes ships a small set of plugins bundled with the repository… They use the same plugin surface as third-party plugins — hooks, tools, slash commands — just maintained in-tree." (`built-in-plugins.md:10`)
- **How it works:** "The `PluginManager` scans four sources, in order" (`:19-22`), all four verbatim: "1. **Bundled** — `<repo>/plugins/<name>/`"; "2. **User** — `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/`"; "3. **Project** — `./.hermes/plugins/<name>/` (requires `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=1`)"; "4. **Pip entry points** — `hermes_agent.plugins`". "On name collision, later sources win — a user plugin named `disk-cleanup` would replace the bundled one." (`:24`)
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "`plugins/memory/` and `plugins/context_engine/` are deliberately excluded from bundled scanning. Those directories use their own discovery paths because memory providers and context engines are single-select providers configured through `hermes memory setup` / `context.engine` in config." (`:26`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Ordered source list with later-wins override. A better version would warn on shadowing.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Bundled plugins are opt-in  `id: docs-features.builtin-plugins-optin`
- **Surface:** CLI + Config
- **Where:** `built-in-plugins.md` → **"Bundled plugins are opt-in"**.
- **What it does:** "Bundled plugins ship disabled. Discovery finds them (they appear in `hermes plugins list` and the interactive `hermes plugins` UI), but none load until you explicitly enable them." (`:30`)
- **How it works:** `hermes plugins enable disk-cleanup`, or `plugins: {enabled: [disk-cleanup]}` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`. Disable: `hermes plugins disable disk-cleanup` "or: remove it from plugins.enabled in config.yaml".
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes plugins enable|disable <name>`; `plugins.enabled`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Config writes.
- **Config / env:** `plugins.enabled`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Bundled plugins are never auto-enabled — not on fresh install, not for existing users upgrading to a newer Hermes. You always opt in explicitly." (`:44`)
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Shipped bundled plugins (11)  `id: docs-features.builtin-plugins-list`

- **Inputs / options:** n/a
