### `disk-cleanup` bundled plugin  `id: docs-features.plugin-disk-cleanup`
- **Surface:** Plugin (hooks + slash command)
- **Where:** `/disk-cleanup` in CLI and gateway sessions.
- **What it does:** "Auto-tracks and removes ephemeral files created during sessions — test scripts, temp outputs, cron logs, stale chrome profiles — without requiring the agent to remember to call a tool." (`:75`)
- **How it works:** Hook table (`:79-82`), both rows verbatim: `post_tool_call` — "When `write_file` / `terminal` / `patch` creates a file matching `test_*`, `tmp_*`, or `*.test.*` inside `HERMES_HOME` or `/tmp/hermes-*`, track it silently as `test` / `temp` / `cron-output`."; `on_session_end` — "If any test files were auto-tracked during the turn, run the safe `quick` cleanup and log a one-line summary. Stays silent otherwise." Deletion rules table (`:86-94`), all 7 rows verbatim (category / threshold / confirmation): `test` — "every session end" — Never; `temp` — ">7 days since tracked" — Never; `cron-output` — ">14 days since tracked" — Never; "empty dirs under HERMES_HOME" — always — Never; `research` — ">30 days, beyond 10 newest" — "Always (deep only)"; `chrome-profile` — ">14 days since tracked" — "Always (deep only)"; "files >500 MB" — "never auto" — "Always (deep only)".
- **Inputs / options:** All six slash forms verbatim (`:99-104`): `/disk-cleanup status` — "breakdown + top-10 largest"; `/disk-cleanup dry-run` — "preview without deleting"; `/disk-cleanup quick` — "run safe cleanup now"; `/disk-cleanup deep` — "quick + list items needing confirmation"; `/disk-cleanup track <path> <category>` — "manual tracking"; `/disk-cleanup forget <path>` — "stop tracking (does not delete)".
- **Outputs / side effects:** State files at `$HERMES_HOME/disk-cleanup/` (`:108-111`), all three verbatim: `tracked.json` — "Tracked paths with category, size, and timestamp"; `tracked.json.bak` — "Atomic-write backup of the above"; `cleanup.log` — "Append-only audit trail of every track / skip / reject / delete".
- **Config / env:** `HERMES_HOME`; `plugins.enabled`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "**Safety** — cleanup only ever touches paths under `HERMES_HOME` or `/tmp/hermes-*`. Windows mounts (`/mnt/c/...`) are rejected. Well-known top-level state dirs (`logs/`, `memories/`, `sessions/`, `cron/`, `cache/`, `skills/`, `plugins/`, `disk-cleanup/` itself) are never removed even when empty — a fresh install does not get gutted on first session end." (`:113`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Track-at-write + clean-at-session-end with a hard path allowlist and an append-only audit log. The protected-dirs list is what makes automatic deletion safe.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### `security-guidance` bundled plugin  `id: docs-features.plugin-security-guidance`
- **Surface:** Plugin (hooks)
- **Where:** Automatic on `write_file` / `patch` / `skill_manage`.
- **What it does:** "Fast pattern-matched security warnings on file writes… the plugin appends a `⚠️ Security guidance` block to the tool's result." (`:122`)
- **How it works:** Complete documented pattern list (`:122`), verbatim: `pickle.load`, `yaml.load` without `SafeLoader`, `eval(`, `os.system`, `subprocess(..., shell=True)`, JS `child_process.exec`, React `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, raw `.innerHTML =` / `.outerHTML =` / `document.write`, Node `crypto.createCipher`, AES ECB mode, TLS verification disabled, XXE-prone `xml.etree` / `minidom` parsers, `<script src="//..." >` without SRI, `torch.load` without `weights_only=True`, GitHub Actions `${{ github.event.* }}` injection. "**Coverage:** 25 rules total, covering unsafe deserialization, command injection, XSS sinks, crypto footguns, XXE, supply-chain (SRI), and CI/CD workflow injection. The pattern data is a verbatim Apache-2.0 fork of Anthropic's `claude-plugins-official`." (`:126`)
- **Inputs / options:** Mode table (`:130-134`), all 3 rows verbatim: (unset) — "**warn mode** (default) — file is written, warning appended to result"; `SECURITY_GUIDANCE_BLOCK=1` — "**block mode** — write refused, warning returned as the block reason"; `SECURITY_GUIDANCE_DISABLE=1` — "kill switch — plugin loads but does nothing".
- **Outputs / side effects:** A `⚠️ Security guidance` block appended to the tool result (warn) or a refusal (block).
- **Config / env:** `SECURITY_GUIDANCE_BLOCK`, `SECURITY_GUIDANCE_DISABLE`; `plugins.enabled`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The file is still written. The model reads the warning in the next turn's tool message and can either fix the code or document why the construct is safe in this context. Pattern matching has a non-trivial false-positive rate, which is why warn (not block) is the default." (`:124`) "**What it does not do (yet):** the upstream Anthropic plugin has two more layers — an LLM diff review on each agent turn that touched files, and an agentic commit-time review that traces data flow across files. Neither is ported. The agent can already run those reviews on demand via `delegate_task`." (`:140`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Warn-not-block by default when the detector has false positives, and say why.
- **Verification:** **partial (documented gap)** — 25 pattern rules ported; the two upstream LLM-review layers are explicitly not ported.

### `observability/langfuse` bundled plugin  `id: docs-features.plugin-langfuse`
- **Surface:** Plugin (hooks)
- **Where:** `hermes tools` → **Langfuse Observability** → **Cloud or Self-Hosted**; `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`.
- **What it does:** "Traces Hermes turns, LLM calls, and tool invocations to Langfuse… One span per turn, one generation per API call, one tool observation per tool call." (`:144`)
- **How it works:** Hook table (`:172-177`), all 4 rows verbatim: "`pre_api_request` / `pre_llm_call`" — "Open (or reuse) a per-turn root span \"Hermes turn\". Start a `generation` child observation for this API call with serialized recent messages as input."; "`post_api_request` / `post_llm_call`" — "Close the generation, attach `usage_details`, `cost_details`, `finish_reason`, assistant output + tool calls. If no tool calls and non-empty content, close the turn."; `pre_tool_call` — "Start a `tool` child observation with sanitized `args`."; `post_tool_call` — "Close the tool observation with sanitized `result`. `read_file` payloads get summarized (head + tail + omitted-line count) so a huge file read stays under `HERMES_LANGFUSE_MAX_CHARS`." "Usage totals, per-type token counts, and cost estimates come out of Hermes' canonical `agent.usage_pricing` numbers, so the Langfuse dashboard sees the same breakdown (input / output / `cache_read_input_tokens` / `cache_creation_input_tokens` / `reasoning_tokens`)." (`:144`) "Session grouping keys off the Hermes session ID (or task ID for sub-agents) via `langfuse.propagate_attributes`." (`:179`)
- **Inputs / options:** Manual setup (`:166-170`): `pip install langfuse`, `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`, then `.env`: `HERMES_LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-...`, `HERMES_LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-...`, `HERMES_LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com`. Verify (`:183-186`): `hermes plugins list` ("observability/langfuse should show \"enabled\""), `hermes chat -q "hello"`. Optional tuning table (`:190-196`), all 5 rows verbatim: `HERMES_LANGFUSE_ENV` (—) "Environment tag on traces (`production`, `staging`, …)"; `HERMES_LANGFUSE_RELEASE` (—) "Release/version tag"; `HERMES_LANGFUSE_SAMPLE_RATE` (`1.0`) "Sampling rate passed to the SDK (0.0–1.0)"; `HERMES_LANGFUSE_MAX_CHARS` (`12000`) "Per-field truncation for message content / tool args / tool results"; `HERMES_LANGFUSE_DEBUG` (`false`) "Verbose plugin logging to `agent.log`".
- **Outputs / side effects:** Traces in Langfuse.
- **Config / env:** The five vars above plus the three credentials; standard SDK vars `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_BASE_URL` also accepted — "Hermes-prefixed wins when both are set." (`:198`)
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The plugin is fail-open: no SDK installed, no credentials, or a transient Langfuse error — all turn into a silent no-op in the hook. The agent loop is never impacted." (`:146`) "**Performance:** the Langfuse client is cached after the first hook call. If credentials or SDK are missing, that decision is also cached — subsequent hooks fast-return without re-checking env vars or reloading config." (`:200`) "**Disabling:** `hermes plugins disable observability/langfuse`. The plugin module is still discovered, but no module code runs until you re-enable." (`:202`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Fail-open observability with a cached negative decision — telemetry must never cost the agent loop.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### NeMo Relay native integration (migration note)  `id: docs-features.plugin-nemo-relay`
- **Surface:** Env + Config
- **Where:** `built-in-plugins.md` → **"NeMo Relay native integration (migration note)"**.
- **What it does:** "NeMo Relay is no longer a bundled Hermes plugin. Do not run `hermes plugins enable observability/nemo_relay`; Hermes core now owns the Relay session, turn, LLM, and tool lifecycles." (`:206`)
- **How it works:** "To opt into Relay middleware or exporters, create a standard Relay `plugins.toml`, then set `HERMES_NEMO_RELAY_PLUGINS_TOML` to that file before starting Hermes. The policy is process-wide for every profile hosted by that Hermes process." (`:208`)
- **Inputs / options:** `HERMES_NEMO_RELAY_PLUGINS_TOML`. Session-span segmentation config (`:216-220`): `gateway: {telemetry: {session_segments: {on_compaction: false, max_turns: 0}}}` with the table (`:222-225`): `on_compaction` (default `false`) — "Rotate after compaction completes, at the next turn boundary."; `max_turns` (default `0`) — "Rotate after every N completed turns; `0` disables the cap."
- **Outputs / side effects:** "Rotated spans retain the same `session_id` and add `hermes.session.segment` plus `hermes.session.segment_reason` (`compaction` or `max_turns`)." (`:227`)
- **Config / env:** `HERMES_NEMO_RELAY_PLUGINS_TOML`; `gateway.telemetry.session_segments.*`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The old `HERMES_NEMO_RELAY_ATOF_*` and `HERMES_NEMO_RELAY_ATIF_*` settings no longer activate exporters. `hermes doctor` reports these stale settings when no replacement `plugins.toml` is selected." (`:210`) Rationale for segmentation (`:214`): "Relay exports a span when its scope closes. A continuous gateway session can keep its session span open for days even though each turn span exports normally."
- **Rebuild notes:** When a plugin graduates into core, have `doctor` detect and report the now-inert settings.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (a migration note, not a plugin).

### `google_meet` bundled plugin  `id: docs-features.plugin-google-meet`
- **Surface:** Plugin (standalone) + Toolset
- **Where:** `hermes plugins enable google_meet`; `hermes meet setup` / `hermes meet auth`.
- **What it does:** "Lets the agent **join, transcribe, and participate in Google Meet calls** — take notes on a meeting, summarize the back-and-forth after, follow up on specific points, and (optionally) speak replies back into the call via TTS." (`:231`)
- **How it works:** Four documented additions (`:235-238`): "A headless virtual participant that joins a Meet URL using browser automation"; "Live transcription of the meeting audio via the configured STT provider"; "A `meet_join` / `meet_status` / `meet_transcript` / `meet_leave` / `meet_say` toolset the agent invokes to join calls, poll the live transcript, and act on what it heard"; "Post-meeting artifacts (transcript, status) saved under `~/.hermes/workspace/meetings/<meeting_id>/`".
- **Inputs / options:** Setup commands verbatim (`:243-248`): `hermes plugins enable google_meet`; `hermes meet setup` ("preflight: playwright, chromium, auth file"); `hermes meet auth` ("opens a browser to sign into Google and saves session state — needs a Google account with Meet access. Host approval may be required if the meeting enforces \"only invited participants can join\"."). Usage example (`:252`): "Join meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij and take notes. After the call, send me a summary with action items."
- **Outputs / side effects:** Transcripts under `~/.hermes/workspace/meetings/`.
- **Config / env:** STT provider config; `plugins.enabled`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "**When to use it:** recurring standups where you want a bot to transcribe + summarize for async attendees; deposition-style interviews where you want structured notes; any case where you'd otherwise need Fireflies / Otter / Grain. When you'd rather not have an AI listening in — don't enable it." (`:256`) "**Disabling:** `hermes plugins disable google_meet`. Any saved transcripts stay in `~/.hermes/workspace/meetings/` until you remove them." (`:258`)
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (see the `optional` shard for the plugin's tools).

### `hermes-achievements` dashboard plugin  `id: docs-features.plugin-achievements`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** Dashboard **Achievements** tab; routes under `/api/plugins/hermes-achievements/`.
- **What it does:** "Adds a **Steam-style achievements tab to the dashboard** — 60+ collectible, tiered badges generated from your real Hermes session history. Tool-chain feats, debugging patterns, vibe-coding streaks, skill/memory usage, model/provider variety, lifestyle quirks (weekend and night sessions)." (`:262`)
- **How it works:** Four documented mechanics (`:266-269`): "Scans your entire `~/.hermes/state.db` session history on the dashboard backend"; "Per-session stats are cached by `(started_at, last_active)` fingerprint, so only new or changed sessions re-analyze on subsequent scans"; "First-ever scan runs in a background thread — the dashboard never blocks waiting for it, even on databases with thousands of sessions"; "Unlock state is persisted to `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/hermes-achievements/state.json`". "**Tier progression:** Copper → Silver → Gold → Diamond → Olympian. Each card exposes a \"What counts\" section listing the exact metric being tracked." (`:271`) Achievement states table (`:275-278`), all 3 rows verbatim: Unlocked — "At least one tier achieved"; Discovered — "Known achievement, progress visible, not yet earned"; Secret — "Hidden until Hermes detects the first related signal in your history".
- **Inputs / options:** Complete API table (`:282-289`), all 6 endpoints verbatim: `GET /achievements` — "Full catalog with per-badge unlock state (returns a pending placeholder while the first cold scan is running)"; `GET /scan-status` — "State of the background scanner: `idle` / `running` / `failed`, last duration, run count"; `GET /recent-unlocks` — "Twenty most recently unlocked badges, newest first"; `GET /sessions/{id}/badges` — "Badges earned primarily in one specific session"; `POST /rescan` — "Manual synchronous rescan (blocks; use when the user clicks the rescan button)"; `POST /reset-state` — "Clear unlock history and cached snapshot".
- **Outputs / side effects:** State files under `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/hermes-achievements/` (`:293-296`), all three verbatim: `state.json` — "Unlock history: which badges you've earned and when. Stable across Hermes updates."; `scan_snapshot.json` — "Last completed scan payload (served immediately on dashboard load)"; `scan_checkpoint.json` — "Per-session stats cache keyed by fingerprint (makes warm rescans fast)".
- **Config / env:** None — "`hermes-achievements` is a dashboard-only plugin (no lifecycle hooks, no model-visible tools). It auto-registers as a tab in `hermes dashboard` on first launch. The `plugins.enabled` config only gates lifecycle/tool plugins; dashboard plugins are discovered purely via their `dashboard/manifest.json`." (`:307`)
- **Edge cases / guards:** Performance notes, all four verbatim (`:300-303`): "Cold scan on ~8,000 sessions takes a few minutes. It runs in a background thread on first dashboard request; the UI sees a pending placeholder and polls `/scan-status`."; "**Incremental results during a cold scan** — the scanner publishes a partial snapshot every ~250 sessions so each dashboard refresh shows more badges unlocked as the scan progresses. No minute-long stare at zeros."; "Warm rescan reuses per-session stats for every session whose `started_at` + `last_active` fingerprint matches the checkpoint — completes in seconds even on large histories."; "The in-memory snapshot TTL is 120s; stale requests serve the old snapshot immediately and kick a background refresh." Opt-out (`:309`): "Delete or rename `plugins/hermes-achievements/dashboard/manifest.json`, or override it with a user plugin of the same name… The plugin's state files under `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/hermes-achievements/` survive — reinstalling preserves your unlock history."
- **Rebuild notes:** Fingerprint-keyed incremental scanning with partial snapshots — the "no minute-long stare at zeros" detail is the difference between usable and not.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (see the `web-*` shards for the dashboard tab).

### Adding a bundled plugin (criteria)  `id: docs-features.builtin-plugins-adding`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `built-in-plugins.md` → **"Adding a bundled plugin"**.
- **What it does:** States how bundled plugins differ and when bundling is appropriate.
- **How it works:** Three differences verbatim (`:317-319`): "Directory lives at `<repo>/plugins/<name>/` instead of `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/`"; "Manifest source is reported as `bundled` in `hermes plugins list`"; "User plugins with the same name override the bundled version". Four bundling criteria (`:323-326`): "It has no optional dependencies (or they're already `pip install .[all]` deps)"; "The behaviour benefits most users and is opt-out rather than opt-in"; "The logic ties into lifecycle hooks that the agent would otherwise have to remember to invoke"; "It complements a core capability without expanding the model-visible tool surface".
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Counter-examples — things that should stay as user-installable plugins, not bundled: third-party integrations with API keys, niche workflows, large dependency trees, anything that would meaningfully change agent behaviour by default." (`:328`) **Note the tension:** criterion 2 says bundled behavior should be "opt-out rather than opt-in", while the page's own "Bundled plugins are opt-in" section states the opposite policy for shipping.
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** **partial (internal inconsistency)** — the bundling criterion ("opt-out rather than opt-in", `:324`) contradicts the shipped policy ("Bundled plugins ship disabled", `:30`).

## Page: `kanban-tutorial.md` — Kanban tutorial

### Kanban tutorial setup  `id: docs-features.kanban-tutorial-setup`
- **Surface:** Docs + CLI

"Agent workers the dispatcher spawns never see the dashboard or the CLI — they drive the board through a dedicated `kanban_*` toolset (`kanban_show`, `kanban_list`, `kanban_complete`, `kanban_block`, `kanban_heartbeat`, `kanban_comment`, `kanban_attach`, `kanban_attach_url`, `kanban_attachments`, `kanban_create`, `kanban_link`, `kanban_unblock`). All three surfaces — dashboard, CLI, worker tools — route through the same per-board SQLite DB (`~/.hermes/kanban.db` for the default board, `~/.hermes/kanban/boards/<slug>/kanban.db` for any board you create later)." (`:13`)
- **Inputs / options:** The 12 worker tools named above.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A board DB.
- **Config / env:** `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Throughout the tutorial, **code blocks labelled `bash` are commands *you* run.** Code blocks labelled `# worker tool calls` are what the spawned worker's model emits as tool calls." (`:17`)

### Kanban board columns (6) and top bar  `id: docs-features.kanban-tutorial-board`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** Dashboard → **Kanban** page.
- **What it does:** Describes the board UI.
- **How it works:** All six columns verbatim (`:23-28`): "**Triage** — raw ideas. By default the dispatcher auto-runs the **decomposer** on tasks here: the built-in decomposer uses `auxiliary.kanban_decomposer`, reads your profile roster + descriptions, and produces a graph of child tasks routed to the best-fit specialists. The original task is held alive as the parent so its assignee (`kanban.orchestrator_profile`, or the active default profile when unset) wakes back up to judge completion when everything finishes. Flip the **Orchestration: Auto/Manual** pill at the top of the kanban page to switch modes. In Manual mode click **⚗ Decompose** on a card, or run `hermes kanban decompose <id>` / `/kanban decompose <id>`. For single tasks that don't need fan-out, **✨ Specify** does a one-shot spec rewrite (goal, approach, acceptance criteria) and promotes to `todo`."; "**Todo** — created but waiting on dependencies, or not yet assigned."; "**Ready** — assigned and waiting for the dispatcher to claim."; "**In progress** — a worker is actively running the task. With \"Lanes by profile\" on (the default), this column sub-groups by assignee."; "**Blocked** — a worker asked for human input, or the circuit breaker tripped."; "**Done** — completed." Top bar (`:30`): "filters for search, tenant, and assignee, plus a `Lanes by profile` toggle and a `Nudge dispatcher` button that runs one dispatch tick right now instead of waiting for the daemon's next interval. Clicking any card opens its drawer on the right." Flat view (`:34-38`): "toggle \"Lanes by profile\" off and the In Progress column collapses to a single flat list ordered by claim time".
- **Inputs / options:** UI labels quoted verbatim: **"Orchestration: Auto/Manual"** pill, **"⚗ Decompose"**, **"✨ Specify"**, **"Lanes by profile"**, **"Nudge dispatcher"**.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Board state changes.
- **Config / env:** `auxiliary.kanban_decomposer`, `auxiliary.triage_specifier`, `kanban.orchestrator_profile`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** n/a
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (see the `web-*` shards for the Kanban page).

### Tutorial Story 1 — solo dev with parent→child dependencies  `id: docs-features.kanban-tutorial-story1`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `kanban-tutorial.md` → **"Story 1 — Solo dev shipping a feature"**.
- **What it does:** Shows dependency promotion and the worker tool loop.
- **How it works:** Creation commands verbatim (`:44-59`) using `hermes kanban create "Design auth schema" --assignee backend-dev --tenant auth-project --priority 2 --body "…" --json | jq -r .id`, then two more with `--parent $SCHEMA` / `--parent $API`. "Because `API` has `SCHEMA` as its parent, and `tests` has `API` as its parent, only `SCHEMA` starts in `ready`." (`:62`) Worker loop verbatim (`:66-85`): `kanban_show()` → `kanban_heartbeat(note="schema drafted, writing migrations now")` → `kanban_complete(summary=…, metadata={"changed_files": [...], "decisions": [...]})`. "`kanban_show` defaults `task_id` to `$HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`, so the worker doesn't need to know its own id. `kanban_complete` writes the summary + metadata onto the current `task_runs` row, closes that run, and transitions the task to `done` — all in one atomic hop through `kanban_db`." (`:87`)
- **Inputs / options:** `--assignee`, `--tenant`, `--priority`, `--body`, `--parent`, `--json`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** `hermes kanban runs $SCHEMA` output verbatim (`:102-105`): `#  OUTCOME       PROFILE       ELAPSED  STARTED` / `1  completed     backend-dev        0s  2026-04-27 19:34` / `    → users(id, email, pw_hash), sessions(id, user_id, jti, expires_at); refresh tokens ...`.
- **Config / env:** Dispatcher tick "60s by default".
- **Edge cases / guards:** "When `SCHEMA` hits `done`, the dependency engine promotes `API` to `ready` automatically. The API worker, when it picks up, will call `kanban_show()` and see `SCHEMA`'s summary and metadata attached to the parent handoff." (`:89`)
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

Then `hermes gateway start` — "it hosts the embedded dispatcher that picks up all three specialist profiles' tasks on the same kanban.db". (`:128-134`)

### Tutorial Story 3 — role pipeline with retry  `id: docs-features.kanban-tutorial-story3`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `kanban-tutorial.md` → **"Story 3 — Role pipeline with retry"**.
- **What it does:** Shows both review models end to end.
- **How it works:** Downstream-card model (`:152`): "the implementation card has a dedicated reviewer child. In that model the engineer must call `kanban_complete` when implementation is ready so the reviewer child can leave `todo`. Never block the implementation parent merely to ask for review." Same-card lifecycle, full choreography verbatim (`:156-197`): `kanban_show()` → `kanban_request_review(summary="implemented reset flow; candidate is ready for review", metadata={"changed_files": ["auth/reset.py"], "tests_run": 8}, reviewer="reviewer")` → `kanban_show()` → `kanban_request_changes(reason="Add password-strength validation and make reset tokens single-use.")` → `kanban_show()` ("prior review evidence is in worker_context") → `kanban_request_review(summary="added zxcvbn validation and single-use reset tokens", metadata={"changed_files": [...3 files...], "tests_run": 11, "review_iteration": 2}, reviewer="reviewer")` → `kanban_complete(summary="review passed; acceptance criteria verified")`.
- **Inputs / options:** `kanban_request_review(summary, metadata, reviewer)`, `kanban_request_changes(reason)`, `kanban_complete(summary)`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** "The task's run history now records `review_requested → changes_requested → review_requested → completed`. Each attempt has its own actor, summary, metadata, and outcome." (`:199`)
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "`kanban_block` is reserved for a real external escalation (missing access, a product decision, unavailable infrastructure), not normal review feedback." (`:199`) "That is a separate card workflow; do not combine it with same-card `kanban_request_review` or you will duplicate the review lane." (`:205`)
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Tutorial Story 4 — circuit breaker and crash recovery  `id: docs-features.kanban-tutorial-story4`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `kanban-tutorial.md` → **"Story 4 — Circuit breaker and crash recovery"**.
- **What it does:** Shows the two dispatcher defenses.
- **How it works:** "The dispatcher has two lines of defense: a **circuit breaker** that auto-blocks after N consecutive failures so the board doesn't thrash forever, and **crash detection** that reclaims a task whose worker PID went away before its TTL expired." (`:209`) Circuit-breaker example verbatim (`:215-219`): `hermes kanban create "Deploy to staging (missing creds)" --assignee deploy-bot --tenant ops --max-retries 3`. "The dispatcher tries to spawn the worker. Spawn fails (`RuntimeError: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID not set`). The dispatcher releases the claim, increments a failure counter, and tries again next tick. Because this example sets `--max-retries 3`, the circuit trips after three consecutive failures: the task goes to `blocked` with outcome `gave_up`. If you omit the flag, Hermes uses `kanban.failure_limit` (default: 2)." (`:221`) Run history verbatim (`:233-239`): three rows — two `spawn_failed` with `! AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID not set in deploy-bot env`, then `gave_up`. Crash recovery (`:250-253`): "Worker claims, starts scanning 2.4M rows, OOM kills it at ~2.3M" / "Dispatcher detects dead pid, releases claim, increments attempt counter" / "Retry with a chunked strategy succeeds"; drawer shows "Run 1 — `crashed`, with the error `OOM kill at row 2.3M (process 99999 gone)`. Run 2 — `completed`, with `\"strategy\": \"chunked with LIMIT + WHERE id > last_id\"` in its metadata." (`:259`)
- **Inputs / options:** `--max-retries N`; `kanban.failure_limit` (default 2).
- **Outputs / side effects:** `blocked` + `gave_up`, or a reclaimed retry.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.failure_limit`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "No more retries until a human unblocks it."
- **Rebuild notes:** Record the failure reason on every attempt row so the retrying worker can pick a different strategy — exactly what happens in the OOM example.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Structured handoff (`summary` + `metadata`)  `id: docs-features.kanban-tutorial-handoff`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `kanban-tutorial.md` → **"Structured handoff — why `summary` and `metadata` matter"**.
- **What it does:** "That's not decoration — it's the primary handoff channel between stages of a workflow." (`:263`)
- **How it works:** `worker_context` returned by `kanban_show()` includes, both verbatim (`:267-268`): "B's **prior attempts** (previous runs: outcome, summary, error, metadata) so a retrying worker doesn't repeat a failed path."; "**Parent task results** — for each parent, the most-recent completed run's summary and metadata — so downstream workers see why and how the upstream work was done." "This replaces the \"dig through comments and the work output\" dance that plagues flat kanban systems." (`:270`)
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The bulk-close guard exists because this data is per-run. `hermes kanban complete a b c --summary X` (you, from the CLI) is refused — copy-pasting the same summary to three tasks is almost always wrong. Bulk close without the handoff flags still works for the common \"I finished a pile of admin tasks\" case. The tool surface doesn't expose a bulk variant at all; `kanban_complete` is always single-task-at-a-time for the same reason." (`:272`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Refuse bulk operations that would fabricate per-item evidence.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Follow-up on a done card (parent link)  `id: docs-features.kanban-tutorial-followup`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `kanban-tutorial.md` → **"Follow-up on a done card — CI remediation via the parent link"**.
- **What it does:** "Don't reopen the done card — completed cards are history, and their handoff flows forward. Create a remediation card with the done card as its **parent**." (`:276`)
- **How it works:** Command verbatim (`:279-286`): `hermes kanban create "Fix CI: test_backoff_jitter flakes on 3.11" --assignee backend-dev --parent t_impl --workspace worktree --branch wt/ci-fix-backoff --body "CI run #4812 failed after t_impl completed. FAILED tests/test_retry.py::test_backoff_jitter - TimeoutError Acceptance: tests/test_retry.py green on 3.11 and 3.12."` Three reasons it works (`:290-292`): "**Immediate dispatch.** Because the parent is already `done`, the child is created straight into `ready`… (A child of a still-open parent would wait in `todo`.)"; "**Inherited context.** The remediation worker's context includes a *Parent task results* section carrying `t_impl`'s completion summary and metadata"; "**Fresh evidence in the body.** The CI log didn't exist when `t_impl` completed, so it can't be in the parent's handoff — it goes in the new card's body, alongside explicit acceptance criteria."
- **Inputs / options:** `--parent`, `--workspace worktree`, `--branch`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A new `ready` card.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Prefer a fresh worktree/branch for the remediation card. Checking out the original branch gives the worker repo *state* but none of the *rationale* — the parent handoff carries that. Same assignee profile is usually right: the profile that wrote the code has the skills to fix it." (`:294`)
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

System deps table (`:82-86`), all 4 rows: **PortAudio** — "Microphone input and audio playback" — "CLI voice mode"; **ffmpeg** — "Audio format conversion (MP3 → Opus, PCM → WAV)" — "All platforms"; **Opus** — "Discord voice codec" — "Discord voice channels"; **espeak-ng** — "Phonemizer backend" — "Local NeuTTS provider". - **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### CLI voice mode (`/voice`)  `id: docs-features.voice-cli`
- **Surface:** CLI + TUI
- **Where:** `/voice` inside `hermes chat` or `hermes --tui`.
- **What it does:** Push-to-talk voice loop with auto-restart.
- **How it works:** Eight documented steps (`:129-136`): "1. Start the CLI with `hermes` and enable voice mode with `/voice on`"; "2. **Press Ctrl+B** — a beep plays (880Hz), recording starts"; "3. **Speak** — a live audio level bar shows your input: `● [▁▂▃▅▇▇▅▂] ❯`"; "4. **Stop speaking** — after 3 seconds of silence, recording auto-stops"; "5. **Two beeps** play (660Hz) confirming the recording ended"; "6. Audio is transcribed via Whisper and sent to the agent"; "7. If TTS is enabled, the agent's reply is spoken aloud"; "8. Recording **automatically restarts** — speak again without pressing any key". "This loop continues until you press **Ctrl+B** during recording (exits continuous mode) or 3 consecutive recordings detect no speech." (`:138`)
- **Inputs / options:** All five commands verbatim (`:121-125`): `/voice` ("Toggle voice mode on/off"); `/voice on` ("Enable voice mode"); `/voice off` ("Disable voice mode"); `/voice tts` ("Toggle TTS output"); `/voice status` ("Show current state"). Record key configurable via `voice.record_key` (default `ctrl+b`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Beeps; transcription; spoken reply.
- **Config / env:** `voice.record_key`, `voice.beep_enabled`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Voice mode is available in both the **classic CLI** (`hermes chat`) and the **TUI** (`hermes --tui`). Behavior is identical across both… The TUI additionally forwards crash-forensic logs to `~/.hermes/logs/` so push-to-talk failures on exotic audio backends can be reported with a full stack trace rather than disappearing silently." (`:113`)
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Voice silence detection (VAD)  `id: docs-features.voice-silence-detection`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `voice-mode.md` → **"Silence Detection"**.
- **What it does:** "Two-stage algorithm detects when you've finished speaking."
- **How it works:** Both stages verbatim (`:153-154`): "1. **Speech confirmation** — waits for audio above the RMS threshold (200) for at least 0.3s, tolerating brief dips between syllables"; "2. **End detection** — once speech is confirmed, triggers after 3.0 seconds of continuous silence". "If no speech is detected at all for 15 seconds, recording stops automatically." (`:156`)
- **Inputs / options:** `voice.silence_threshold` (RMS, default 200), `voice.silence_duration` (default 3.0), `voice.beep_enabled`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Auto-stop.
- **Config / env:** As above.
- **Edge cases / guards:** 15-second no-speech timeout.
- **Rebuild notes:** Two-stage VAD (confirm speech, then detect end) tolerates inter-syllable dips — a single-threshold VAD cuts people off.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Ending a voice chat by voice (`voice.stop_phrases`)  `id: docs-features.voice-stop-phrases`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `voice-mode.md` → **"Ending a voice chat by voice"**.
- **What it does:** "Say **\"stop\"** — and nothing else — to end the voice conversation hands-free." (`:162`)
- **How it works:** "The match is deliberately strict: the whole utterance (case-insensitive, surrounding punctuation ignored) must equal a configured phrase, so \"stop doing that and try X instead\" still reaches the agent normally. Customize the phrase list with `voice.stop_phrases` in `config.yaml` (e.g. `[\"stop\", \"goodbye hermes\"]`), or set it to `[]` to disable. A voice chat also ends on its own after three consecutive silent cycles."
- **Inputs / options:** `voice.stop_phrases` (default `["stop"]`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Voice chat ends.
- **Config / env:** `voice.stop_phrases`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "**Typing** a bare stop phrase while a voice chat is active works the same way on every surface (CLI, TUI, desktop): the message ends the voice chat instead of being sent to the agent. Outside a voice chat, typed \"stop\" is an ordinary message." (`:166`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Whole-utterance equality, never substring — the difference between a usable and an infuriating stop word.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Streaming TTS  `id: docs-features.voice-streaming-tts`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `voice-mode.md` → **"Streaming TTS"**.
- **What it does:** "the agent speaks its reply **sentence-by-sentence** as it generates text — you don't wait for the full response. This works with **every TTS provider**." (`:170`)
- **How it works:** Three documented steps (`:172-174`): "1. Buffers text deltas into complete sentences (min 20 chars)"; "2. Strips markdown formatting, emoji, and `<think>` blocks"; "3. Plays audio per sentence in real-time — providers with a chunked PCM API (ElevenLabs, OpenAI) stream raw audio for the lowest time-to-first-word; every other provider (including the default Edge) synthesizes and plays each sentence as it completes". "In a desktop voice conversation the reply text is fed **live** into a per-reply speech WebSocket as the model generates it, so speech overlaps generation — one socket and one audio clock per reply, no per-sentence connection gaps." (`:176`)
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** Audio playback.
- **Config / env:** `tts.provider`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** n/a
- **Rebuild notes:** One socket + one audio clock per reply avoids the audible gaps a per-sentence connection produces.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Desktop remote client-direct voice  `id: docs-features.voice-client-direct`
- **Surface:** Desktop app + API
- **Where:** `voice-mode.md` → **"Desktop remote: client-direct voice (lowest-hop path)"**.
- **What it does:** "When Hermes Desktop is connected to a **remote gateway**, audio does not need to be relayed through the gateway at all." (`:180`)
- **How it works:** "At voice-session start the desktop fetches the active profile's resolved STT/TTS settings (provider, model, language/voice, and credential) from the gateway over the authenticated REST channel (`GET /api/audio/voice-config`) and then calls the providers **directly**" — both paths verbatim (`:182-183`): "**Dictation / voice input:** the mic recording goes straight from your desktop to the profile's STT provider; only the resulting *text* is sent to the gateway as the prompt."; "**Spoken replies:** the reply text is already streaming to the desktop over the chat socket, so the desktop synthesizes it locally with the profile's TTS provider and plays it — the gateway link never carries audio."
- **Inputs / options:** `voice: {client_direct: false}` — "To force the relay for every provider".
- **Outputs / side effects:** Direct provider calls from the client.
- **Config / env:** `voice.client_direct`; endpoints `GET /api/audio/voice-config`, `/api/audio/transcribe`, the speech WebSocket.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "There is nothing to configure on the client: the profile you're talking to is the single source of truth for providers and keys… Keys are held in the desktop's memory for the session only — never written to disk on the client." (`:185`) "Providers that can only run on the gateway host (local whisper, `edge` TTS, command providers, plugins) automatically fall back to the relay path… as does any older backend without the endpoint." (`:187`) "Client-direct wire support: OpenAI (incl. Nous-managed audio), Groq, Mistral, and DeepInfra via the OpenAI-compatible shapes, xAI Grok STT, and ElevenLabs STT + TTS. xAI configured through OAuth stays on the relay (the OAuth bearer refreshes server-side)." (`:194`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Ship the *resolved* provider config to the client rather than making the client configure anything, and keep the credential in memory only.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Voice barge-in  `id: docs-features.voice-barge-in`
- **Surface:** CLI + Desktop app
- **Where:** `voice-mode.md` → **"Barge-in"**.
- **What it does:** "You can interrupt the agent at ANY point in its turn — the microphone stays live from the moment you finish speaking until the reply has fully played (full duplex)." (`:196`)
- **How it works:** Four documented interrupt paths (`:198-201`): "**Interject while it's thinking** — in continuous voice mode, speaking during LLM generation (before any audio plays) interrupts the in-flight turn and your interjection becomes the next message"; "**Talk over it** — speaking while the agent's reply plays cuts playback the moment you start talking and submits what you said. The detector calibrates its noise floor against the *quiet room* at turn start (never against the playback itself), so speaker bleed can't deafen it"; "**Type or press the record key** — sending a new message or hitting the push-to-talk key stops playback instantly on every surface."; "**Say \"stop\"** — the stop phrase works in both phases: mid-generation it interrupts the turn AND ends the voice chat; mid-playback it cuts the speech and ends the chat."
- **Inputs / options:** Tuning verbatim (`:203`): `voice.barge_in: false` ("disables it"); `voice.barge_in_threshold_multiplier` (default `3.0`, "scales the speech trigger over the quiet-room floor"); `voice.barge_in_grace_seconds` (default `0.5`, "suppresses trips right after playback starts"). "Set `HERMES_VOICE_DEBUG=1` to stream per-block VAD diagnostics (calibrated floor, RMS, trip decisions) to stderr for live tuning."
- **Outputs / side effects:** Playback cut; interjection submitted.
- **Config / env:** `voice.barge_in*`; `HERMES_VOICE_DEBUG`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The agent **knows** it was interrupted: the next message carries a short note telling the model its spoken reply was cut off, so it can react naturally (\"rude!\") or pick up where it left off instead of being oblivious." (`:205`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Calibrate the noise floor against the quiet room, not the playback; and tell the model it was cut off.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Whisper hallucination filter  `id: docs-features.voice-hallucination-filter`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `voice-mode.md` → **"Hallucination Filter"**.
- **What it does:** "Whisper sometimes generates phantom text from silence or background noise (\"Thank you for watching\", \"Subscribe\", etc.). The agent filters these out using a set of 26 known hallucination phrases across multiple languages, plus a regex pattern that catches repetitive variations." (`:209`)
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** Dropped transcripts.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** Troubleshooting (`:577-580`): "The hallucination filter catches most cases automatically. If you're still getting phantom transcripts: Use a quieter environment; Adjust `silence_threshold` in config (higher = less sensitive); Try a different STT model".
- **Rebuild notes:** A phrase list plus a repetition regex — cheap and effective against a well-known model failure.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Gateway voice reply (Telegram & Discord)  `id: docs-features.voice-gateway-reply`

Commands (`:254-260`), all 5 verbatim: `/voice` ("Toggle voice mode on/off"); `/voice on` ("Voice replies only when you send a voice message"); `/voice tts` ("Voice replies for ALL messages"); `/voice off` ("Disable voice replies"); `/voice status` ("Show current setting"). Modes table (`:266-269`), all 3 rows: `off` — `/voice off` — "Text only (default)"; `voice_only` — `/voice on` — "Speaks reply only when you send a voice message"; `all` — `/voice tts` — "Speaks reply to every message". "Voice mode setting is persisted across gateway restarts." (`:271`)
- **Inputs / options:** As above.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Platform delivery table (`:276-278`): **Telegram** — "Voice bubble (Opus/OGG)" — "Plays inline in chat. ffmpeg converts MP3 → Opus if needed"; **Discord** — "Native voice bubble (Opus/OGG)" — "Plays inline like a user voice message. Falls back to file attachment if voice bubble API fails".
- **Config / env:** `DISCORD_REQUIRE_MENTION`, `DISCORD_FREE_RESPONSE_CHANNELS`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Discord DM vs channel table (`:232-235`): **Direct Message (DM)** — "Open the bot's profile → \"Message\"" — mention required "No" — "Works immediately"; **Server Channel** — "Type in a text channel where the bot is present" — "Yes (`@botname`)" — "Bot must be invited to the server". "**Server channels:** The bot only responds when you @mention it (e.g. `@hermesbyt4 hello`). Make sure you select the **bot user** from the mention popup, not the role with the same name." (`:239`) ":::tip To disable the mention requirement in server channels, add to `~/.hermes/.env`: `DISCORD_REQUIRE_MENTION=false`. Or set specific channels as free-response (no mention needed): `DISCORD_FREE_RESPONSE_CHANNELS=123456789,987654321`" (`:241-249`)
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (see the `platform-telegram` / `platforms-*` shards).

### Discord voice channels  `id: docs-features.voice-discord-vc`
- **Surface:** Platform:Discord
- **Where:** `voice-mode.md` → **"Discord Voice Channels"**.
- **What it does:** "the bot joins a Discord voice channel, listens to users speaking, transcribes their speech, processes through the agent, and speaks the reply back in the voice channel." (`:285`)
- **How it works:** Five documented steps (`:392-396`): "1. **Listens** to each user's audio stream independently"; "2. **Detects silence** — 1.5s of silence after at least 0.5s of speech triggers processing"; "3. **Transcribes** the audio via Whisper STT (local, Groq, or OpenAI)"; "4. **Processes** through the full agent pipeline (session, tools, memory)"; "5. **Speaks** the reply back in the voice channel via TTS".
- **Inputs / options:** Commands (`:377-382`), all 4 verbatim: `/voice join` ("Bot joins your current voice channel"); `/voice channel` ("Alias for /voice join"); `/voice leave` ("Bot disconnects from voice channel"); `/voice status` ("Show voice mode and connected channel"). Setup: permissions table (`:297-301`) — **Connect** ("Join voice channels", Yes), **Speak** ("Play TTS audio in voice channels", Yes), **Use Voice Activity** ("Detect when users are speaking", Recommended); permission integers (`:305-308`) — "Text only" `309237763136` ("View Channels, Send Messages, Read History, Embeds, Attachments, Threads, Reactions, Create Public Threads"), "Text + Voice" `309240908864` ("All above + Connect, Speak"); invite URL `https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=YOUR_APP_ID&scope=bot+applications.commands&permissions=309240908864`. Privileged intents table (`:322-326`): **Presence Intent** ("Detect user online/offline status"), **Server Members Intent** ("Resolve usernames in `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS` to numeric IDs (conditional)"), **Message Content Intent** ("Read text message content in channels"). Opus install: `brew install opus` (macOS) / `sudo apt install libopus0` (Ubuntu/Debian); auto-load paths — "**macOS:** `/opt/homebrew/lib/libopus.dylib`", "**Linux:** `libopus.so.0`".
- **Outputs / side effects:** "Transcripts appear in the text channel: `[Voice] @user: what you said`"; "Agent responses are sent as text in the channel AND spoken in the VC"; "The text channel is the one where `/voice join` was issued" (`:402-404`).
- **Config / env:** `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`, `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS`, `GROQ_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `VOICE_TOOLS_OPENAI_KEY`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** ":::info You must be in a voice channel before running `/voice join`. The bot joins the same VC you're in." (`:384-386`) "**Echo Prevention** — The bot automatically pauses its audio listener while playing TTS replies, preventing it from hearing and re-processing its own output." (`:408-410`) "**Access Control** — Only users listed in `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS` can interact via voice. Other users' audio is silently ignored." (`:412-414`) "**Message Content Intent** is required. **Server Members Intent** is only needed if your `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS` list uses usernames… Voice-channel SSRC → user_id mapping comes from Discord's SPEAKING opcode on the voice websocket and does **not** require the Server Members Intent." (`:328`) ":::warning Re-inviting the bot to a server it's already in will update its permissions without removing it." (`:314-316`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Per-speaker streams with independent VAD + a listener pause during playback. The SSRC→user mapping note saves an unnecessary privileged intent.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

- **Surface:** Config

- **How it works:** Complete block with comments verbatim (`:428-476`): **voice** — `record_key: "ctrl+b"` ("Key to start/stop recording"); `max_recording_seconds: 120` ("Maximum recording length"); `auto_tts: false` ("Auto-enable TTS when voice mode starts"); `beep_enabled: true` ("Play record start/stop beeps"); `silence_threshold: 200` ("RMS level (0-32767) below which counts as silence"); `silence_duration: 3.0` ("Seconds of silence before auto-stop"); `stop_phrases: ["stop"]` ("Saying exactly one of these ends the voice chat; [] disables"). **stt** — `enabled: true` ("set to false to skip auto-transcription — the gateway still caches the audio file and passes its path to the agent as part of the inbound message, useful for custom pipelines (diarization, alignment, archival, etc.)"); `provider: "local"` ("\"local\" (free) | \"groq\" | \"openai\" | \"mistral\" | \"xai\""); `local.model: "base"` ("tiny, base, small, medium, large-v3"); `local.language: ""` ("optional ISO-639-1 hint; blank = use HERMES_LOCAL_STT_LANGUAGE if set, else auto-detect"); `groq.language: ""` (same); legacy `model: "whisper-1"` ("used when provider is not set"). **tts** — `provider: "edge"` ("\"edge\" (free) | \"elevenlabs\" | \"openai\" | \"neutts\" | \"minimax\" | \"mistral\" | \"gemini\" | \"xai\" | \"kittentts\" | \"piper\""); `edge.voice: "en-US-AriaNeural"` ("322 voices, 74 languages"); `elevenlabs.voice_id: "pNInz6obpgDQGcFmaJgB"` ("Adam"), `elevenlabs.model_id: "eleven_multilingual_v2"`; `openai.model: "gpt-4o-mini-tts"`, `openai.voice: "alloy"` ("alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, shimmer"), `openai.base_url: "https://api.openai.com/v1"` ("optional: override for self-hosted or OpenAI-compatible endpoints"); `neutts.ref_audio: ''`, `neutts.ref_text: ''`, `neutts.model: neuphonic/neutts-air-q4-gguf`, `neutts.device: cpu`.

## Page: `computer-use.md` — Computer Use

### Computer Use (`computer_use` toolset)  `id: docs-features.computer-use`
- **Surface:** Toolset
- **Where:** `hermes tools` → `🖱️  Computer Use`; `hermes -t computer_use chat`. Docs title **"Computer Use"** (`sidebar_position: 16`).
- **What it does:** "Hermes Agent can drive your desktop — clicking, typing, scrolling, dragging — in the **background** on **macOS, Windows, and Linux**. Your cursor doesn't move, keyboard focus doesn't change, and your virtual desktops / Spaces don't switch on you. You and the agent co-work on the same machine." (`computer-use.md:8-11`) "Unlike most computer-use integrations, this works with **any tool-capable model** — Claude, GPT, Gemini, or an open model on a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint. There's no Anthropic-native schema to worry about." (`:13`)
- **How it works:** "The built-in `computer_use` toolset… speaks MCP over stdio to `cua-driver`, an open-source background computer-use driver." (`:20`) Platform stack table (`:26-30`), all 3 rows verbatim: macOS — "AX (private SkyLight SPIs)" — "`SLPSPostEventRecordTo` — pid-scoped, no cursor warp"; Windows — "UIAutomation" — "`SendInput` + `PostMessage` — no focus steal"; Linux — "AT-SPI (X11 + Wayland)" — "XTest (X11) / virtual-keyboard (Wayland)". "the agent can read the accessibility tree of any visible window AND post synthesized events without bringing it to front, switching virtual desktops, or moving the real OS cursor." (`:32`)
- **Inputs / options:** Documented actions: `capture` (with `mode="som"` / `mode="ax"`, `app=`, `capture_after=`), `click` (`element=`), `type` (`text=`), `key` (`keys=`), `drag`, `scroll`, `focus_app`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Screenshots (saved to the image cache), synthesized input events.
- **Config / env:** `computer_use.permission_mode`, `computer_use.capability_manifest`, `computer_use.no_overlay`, `computer_use.allow_unsigned_driver`, `computer_use.cua_telemetry`; env `HERMES_CUA_DRIVER_CMD`, `HERMES_COMPUTER_USE_BACKEND`, `HERMES_CUA_DRIVER_VERSION`, `CUA_DRIVER_RS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** See the safety, limitations and troubleshooting entries.
- **Rebuild notes:** Background input via accessibility APIs + a stdio MCP driver, with a generic action vocabulary rather than a provider-specific schema. A better version would cache the AX tree between captures and diff it.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (toolset `computer_use` in the live toolsets dump).

### Enabling Computer Use / installing cua-driver  `id: docs-features.computer-use-install`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `computer-use.md` → **"Enabling"**.
- **What it does:** Installs and enables the driver.
- **How it works:** "**Fresh installs already have the driver.** The Hermes installer (`install.sh` / `install.ps1`) pre-installs `cua-driver` (best-effort; pass `--skip-computer-use` / `-SkipComputerUse` to opt out), so enabling Computer Use is just a config flip." (`:43`) Two enable paths (`:47-51`): "**`hermes tools`** → pick `🖱️  Computer Use` — installs the driver automatically if it's still missing."; "**Dashboard / desktop app** → toggle the Computer Use toolset — if the driver is missing, the toggle kicks off the install in the background automatically (watch progress in the toolset panel)." Manual fallback: `hermes computer-use install` — "fetches and runs the upstream cua-driver installer — `install.sh` on macOS/Linux, `install.ps1` on Windows. Use `hermes computer-use status` to verify the install." Prereqs table (`:83-87`), all 3 rows verbatim: **macOS** — "System Settings → Privacy & Security → **Accessibility** + **Screen Recording**. Grant the identity named by `hermes computer-use doctor`. Standard mode uses CuaDriver.app; bounded and unrestricted modes use the Hermes host identity."; **Windows** — "None at install time. If you're driving over SSH (not RDP / console), you need the autostart pattern"; **Linux** — "A reachable display server: `DISPLAY` set for X11, or `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`. Wayland sessions need an XWayland bridge for capture. AT-SPI must be on (default on GNOME/KDE/Xfce)."
- **Inputs / options:** `--skip-computer-use` / `-SkipComputerUse`; `hermes computer-use install|status|doctor`; `hermes -t computer_use chat`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** An installed `cua-driver` binary.
- **Config / env:** `DISPLAY`, `XDG_SESSION_TYPE`, `HERMES_CUA_DRIVER_CMD`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Already have cua-driver? Hermes reuses it when it supports the 0.20 runtime contract. During setup, toolset enablement, `hermes update`, and the first `computer_use` call of a session, Hermes checks the local version and manifest. It repairs an old or incomplete standard installation through the upstream installer (at most once per session at runtime). A binary selected with `HERMES_CUA_DRIVER_CMD` stays under your control, so Hermes reports the incompatibility and leaves it unchanged." (`:63`) "If you install Cua Driver first, `cua-driver skills install` installs Cua's skill pack under `~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver`. Hermes autodetection is a planned cua-driver follow-up." (`:73`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Never silently modify a user-pinned binary — report and stop.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Computer-use permission modes  `id: docs-features.computer-use-permissions`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `computer-use.md` → **"Permission modes and logged-in browser profiles"**.
- **What it does:** "Hermes maps its existing approval UX onto cua-driver's immutable runtime modes. Permission mode and capability manifest approval are launch settings. They cannot change after the runtime starts." (`:101`)
- **How it works:** Complete table (`:105-109`), all 3 rows verbatim (Hermes session / cua-driver mode / human intervention): "Manual or smart approvals (default)" — `standard` — "Normal Hermes approvals; Cua stops at its protected boundary"; "`computer_use.permission_mode: bounded` + reviewed manifest" — "private `bounded` daemon" — "You review and approve the capability manifest once, at launch"; "`--yolo`, `/yolo`, or `approvals.mode: off`" — "private `unrestricted` daemon" — "One explicit Hermes risk acceptance; no runtime Cua prompts".
- **Inputs / options:** `computer_use.permission_mode: standard | bounded`; `computer_use.capability_manifest`; `--yolo` / `/yolo` / `approvals.mode: off`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A private daemon for bounded/unrestricted.
- **Config / env:** As above; `computer_use.allow_unsigned_driver`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Browser work — including pages in a signed-in profile — goes through the `browser` toolset (`browser_exec`), not `computer_use`. The former `computer_use.grant_existing_profile` opt-in was removed along with the typed browser route; a leftover key in config.yaml is ignored." (`:111`) "`smart` approval remains `standard`: an LLM classification cannot stand in for a reviewed manifest." (`:166`) YOLO warning (`:168-173`): "YOLO/unrestricted mode does not protect against prompt injection or unintended input. Use it only in a disposable VM or with accounts and data whose full compromise you accept." Session scoping (`:157-164`): "Each MCP transport owns a private lifecycle session inside its runtime. A public session name is only a label for cursor identity and session-scoped state… One Hermes conversation cannot change another runtime's mode or grants."
- **Rebuild notes:** Immutable launch-time modes; an LLM classifier may never substitute for a human-reviewed manifest.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Bounded mode and capability manifest  `id: docs-features.computer-use-bounded`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `computer-use.md` → **"Bounded mode for repeatable automation"**.
- **What it does:** "For recurring browser automation (cron jobs, scheduled research against an authenticated app), `bounded` mode uses a capability manifest you review once." (`:118`)
- **How it works:** Config (`:122-125`): `computer_use: {permission_mode: bounded, capability_manifest: ~/.hermes/cua-manifest.yaml}`. "The manifest names the apps, browser profile kinds, allowed origins, and typed tools the session may use… Hermes launches a private runtime with `--capability-manifest ... --approve-capability-manifest`; anything outside the manifest fails closed inside cua-driver. A missing or unreadable manifest fails loudly at session start rather than silently downgrading. Session YOLO still overrides bounded for that one session." (`:127-135`)
- **Inputs / options:** `computer_use.permission_mode`, `computer_use.capability_manifest`, `computer_use.allow_unsigned_driver`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A private bounded daemon.
- **Config / env:** As above.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "On macOS, private-session daemons launch through the installed `CuaDriver.app` bundle (so permission grants attribute to the driver's own identity instead of resetting with every Hermes build), and Hermes verifies the bundle's code signature — exact `com.trycua.driver` identifier and the official signing team — before launching it. If you build cua-driver from source (unsigned), opt in explicitly: `computer_use: {allow_unsigned_driver: true}` (local driver development only)." (`:137-155`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Fail loudly on a missing manifest rather than downgrading; verify the code signature before launching a privileged helper.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### `hermes computer-use doctor`  `id: docs-features.computer-use-doctor`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes computer-use doctor`.
- **What it does:** "runs cua-driver's structured `health_report` MCP tool and prints a per-check matrix. It's the single fastest way to find out *why* an action isn't working." (`:177`)
- **How it works:** Sample output verbatim (`:182-191`): `⚠️  cua-driver VERSION on darwin: degraded` with checks `binary_version`, `platform_supported`, `session_active`, `bundle_identity` (❌ "Process has no CFBundleIdentifier." → "Run the binary inside CuaDriver.app so TCC grants attribute correctly."), `tcc_accessibility`, `tcc_screen_recording`, `ax_capability`, `screen_capture_capability`.
- **Inputs / options:** Three flags verbatim (`:197-201`): `--include CHECK` ("run only the listed checks (repeat for multiple)"); `--skip CHECK` ("skip a check (wins over `--include`)"); `--json` ("emit the raw structured payload, same shape as the `tools/call health_report` MCP response").
- **Outputs / side effects:** Exit codes verbatim (`:193-195`): "**Exit code 0** when overall is `ok`"; "**Exit code 1** when `degraded` or `failed`"; "**Exit code 2** when the cua-driver binary itself isn't reachable."
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The check matrix is platform-aware: `bundle_identity` / `tcc_*` are `skip` on Windows + Linux because those concepts don't apply. `ax_capability` checks AX on macOS, UIA on Windows, AT-SPI on Linux — each with the right diagnostic hint when it can't reach." (`:203`)
- **Rebuild notes:** A per-check matrix with per-failure hints and meaningful exit codes — the model diagnostic surface.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Agent cursor overlay and sessions  `id: docs-features.computer-use-cursor`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `computer-use.md` → **"The agent cursor and sessions"**.
- **What it does:** "When the agent acts, you'll see a **tinted overlay cursor** glide across the screen to where each click / type / scroll lands. The real OS cursor never moves." (`:209`)
- **How it works:** "Each Hermes run declares a public cua-driver **session name** (something like `hermes-3a7b9c14d2e8`). The name labels cursor identity and related state, so concurrent runs and subagents get distinct cursors. The MCP transport owns the private lifecycle session inside the runtime; the public name does not." (`:213`)
- **Inputs / options:** `computer_use.no_overlay: false` ("to force the cursor on… (or `true` to force it off) on any platform"); cua-driver CLI flags and the `set_agent_cursor_style` MCP tool ("built-in `arrow` vs `teardrop` silhouette, custom SVG / PNG / ICO via `--cursor-icon`, runtime gradient colors, bloom halo").
- **Outputs / side effects:** A visible overlay.
- **Config / env:** `computer_use.no_overlay`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The overlay cursor is cosmetic — captures, clicks, and typing all work without it. Hermes disables it automatically where it is a known failure mode: macOS (idle CPU burn), headless Linux / WSL2 / containers, and **Linux X11 desktops** (the overlay is a fullscreen always-on-top window that can get stuck over every workspace after an unclean session end, wedging desktop input). Linux Wayland and Windows keep the overlay." (`:219`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Disable cosmetic overlays automatically on platforms where they can wedge the desktop.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### cua-driver skill pack  `id: docs-features.computer-use-skill-pack`
- **Surface:** Skill
- **Where:** `cua-driver skills install`; `computer-use.md` → **"Going deeper — the cua-driver skill pack"**.

- **How it works:** Complete file table (`:249-257`), all 7 rows verbatim: `SKILL.md` — "The cross-platform core (snapshot invariant, no-foreground contract, click dispatch, AX-tree mechanics)"; `MACOS.md` — "macOS specifics: no-foreground contract, AXMenuBar navigation, SkyLight click dispatch, Apple Events JS bridge"; `WINDOWS.md` — "Windows specifics: UIA tree, UWP / `ApplicationFrameHost` hosting, Session 0 isolation, autostart pattern"; `LINUX.md` — "Linux specifics: AT-SPI tree, X11 / Wayland, terminal-emulator detection"; `RECORDING.md` — "Trajectory + video recording semantics"; `WEB_APPS.md` — "Browser-page interaction tips"; `TESTS.md` — "Replay-by-trajectory workflow".
- **Inputs / options:** `cua-driver skills install`; `cua-driver skills status` ("shows what's installed and which agent harnesses it's linked into").
- **Outputs / side effects:** Files under `~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver`.
- **Config / env:** n/a

(`:259`) "Today the autodetect list covers Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, and Antigravity; **Hermes autodetection is planned as a follow-up in `trycua/cua`** — until then, run `cua-driver skills install` once and point your harness at the resulting `~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver` directory (or symlink it into your usual skill space)." (`:264`)
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** **documented gap** — Hermes autodetection of the pack is explicitly not implemented.

### Computer-use worked example  `id: docs-features.computer-use-example`

Click the top result, read the body, summarise." "During all of this, your cursor stays wherever you left it and the email app never comes to front." (`:287`)

### Receiving the actual screenshot  `id: docs-features.computer-use-screenshots`
- **Surface:** Gateway/Telegram + Desktop app
- **Where:** `computer-use.md` → **"Receiving the actual screenshot"**.
- **What it does:** "every image capture also saves a bounded, shareable copy under Hermes' image cache and reports its path, so on attachment-capable surfaces (Telegram, Discord, Desktop, and other gateway platforms) you can simply ask: *\"Send me a screenshot of my screen.\"* and the agent delivers the real image as a native attachment." (`:291-301`)
- **How it works:** "On the CLI there is no attachment channel, so the agent gives you the saved file's path instead."
- **Inputs / options:** Natural language.
- **Outputs / side effects:** An image attachment or a path.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Only the 20 most recent capture files are kept, and screenshots are never sent automatically — only when you ask for one." (`:305`) Whole screen vs desktop surface (`:309-317`): "\"Screenshot my screen\" captures **everything currently displayed** — a composited grab of all visible windows, like pressing PrtScn. This image has no clickable elements, so to *act* on something in it the agent re-captures the specific app."; "Asking for the **desktop** instead targets the OS shell surface itself — wallpaper, desktop icons, taskbar — with its clickable elements, so requests like \"open the Recycle Bin on my desktop\" still work."
- **Rebuild notes:** Bound the shareable copy count and require an explicit request — screenshots are the most privacy-sensitive artifact the agent makes.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Computer-use provider compatibility  `id: docs-features.computer-use-providers`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `computer-use.md` → **"Provider compatibility"**.
- **What it does:** Six-row model/provider support matrix.
- **How it works:** Complete table (`:323-330`), all 6 rows verbatim: "Anthropic (Claude Sonnet/Opus 3+)" — vision ✅ — works ✅ — "Best overall; SOM + raw coordinates."; "OpenRouter (any vision model)" — ✅ ✅ — "Multi-part tool messages supported."; "OpenAI (GPT-4+, GPT-5)" — ✅ ✅ — "Same as above."; "Google (Gemini 2+)" — ✅ ✅ — "Tool-calling + vision both supported."; "Local vLLM / LM Studio / Ollama (vision model)" — ✅ ✅ — "If the model supports multi-part tool content."; "Text-only models" — ❌ — "✅ (degraded)" — "Use `mode=\"ax\"` for accessibility-tree-only operation."
- **Inputs / options:** `mode="ax"` for text-only models.
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Screenshots are sent inline with tool results as OpenAI-style `image_url` parts. For Anthropic, the adapter converts them into native `tool_result` image blocks. The image MIME type comes from cua-driver's explicit `mimeType` field (`image/png` or `image/jpeg`) — no client-side magic-byte sniffing." (`:332`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Offer an accessibility-tree-only mode so text-only models degrade instead of failing.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Computer-use safety guardrails  `id: docs-features.computer-use-safety`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `computer-use.md` → **"Safety"**.
- **What it does:** "Hermes applies multi-layer guardrails."
- **How it works:** All four layers verbatim (`:340-347`): "Destructive actions (click, type, drag, scroll, key, focus_app) require approval — either interactively via the CLI dialog or via the messaging-platform approval buttons."; "Hard-blocked key combos at the tool level: empty trash, force delete, lock screen, log out, force log out."; "Hard-blocked type patterns: `curl | bash`, `sudo rm -rf /`, fork bombs, etc."; "The agent's system prompt tells it explicitly: no clicking permission dialogs, no typing passwords, no following instructions embedded in screenshots."
- **Inputs / options:** `approvals.mode: manual`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Refusals and approval prompts.
- **Config / env:** `approvals.mode`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Pair with `approvals.mode: manual` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` if you want every action confirmed." (`:349`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Hard blocks at the tool level, not just prompt instructions — the prompt is the weakest of the four layers.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Computer-use token efficiency  `id: docs-features.computer-use-tokens`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `computer-use.md` → **"Token efficiency"**.
- **What it does:** "Screenshots are expensive. Hermes applies four layers of optimisation."
- **How it works:** All four verbatim (`:358-368`): "**Screenshot eviction** — the Anthropic adapter keeps only the 3 most recent screenshots in context; older ones become `[screenshot removed to save context]` placeholders."; "**Client-side compression pruning** — the context compressor detects multimodal tool results and strips image parts from old ones."; "**Image-aware token estimation** — each image is counted as ~1500 tokens (Anthropic's flat rate) instead of its base64 char length."; "**Server-side context editing (Anthropic only)** — when active, the adapter enables `clear_tool_uses_20250919` via `context_management` so Anthropic's API clears old tool results server-side."
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** "A 20-action session on a 1568×900 display typically costs ~30K tokens of screenshot context, not ~600K." (`:370`)
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** n/a
- **Rebuild notes:** Four independent eviction layers; the published before/after number (600K → 30K) is the right way to justify them.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Computer-use limitations  `id: docs-features.computer-use-limitations`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `computer-use.md` → **"Limitations"**.
- **What it does:** Five documented limitation groups.
- **How it works:** All verbatim (`:376-419`): "**Performance.** Background mode is slower than foreground — accessibility-routed events take ~5–20 ms on macOS, ~3–10 ms on Windows UIA, ~5–15 ms on Linux AT-SPI vs direct HID posting."; "**No keyboard password entry.** `type` has hard-block patterns on command-shell payloads; for passwords, use the system's autofill (macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager / GNOME Keyring / KWallet)."; "**Some apps don't expose an accessibility tree.** Modern UWP apps on Windows, Electron < 28 on Linux, and a few macOS apps with custom drawing (Logic, Final Cut, some games) have sparse or empty AX trees. Fall back to pixel coordinates if the tree is empty — or skip the task entirely."; "**Windows: elevated (admin) windows can't be driven from a normal agent.** Windows UIPI (User Interface Privilege Isolation) enforces integrity-level boundaries… Symptom: `capture(mode='som')` returns 0 elements and `click(...)` reports success while doing nothing, even though the screenshot renders fine (GDI capture sits below the integrity check). Keyboard events partially bypass UIPI, so Tab / Enter can still navigate an elevated dialog. This is an OS constraint, not a cua-driver bug… To drive elevated windows, run the Hermes agent itself at High integrity (launch from an elevated terminal)."; "**Platform-specific deployment gotchas:** **macOS** uses private SkyLight SPIs. Apple can change them in any OS update. Hermes warns when the installed cua-driver is older than the version it was tested against."; "**Windows** SSH sessions run in **Session 0**, which has no interactive desktop. Drive Hermes from inside the RDP / console session, or set up cua-driver's autostart Scheduled Task"; "**Linux** requires a reachable display server. Headless servers need Xvfb (`Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1920x1080x24`) before `computer_use` can capture or inject events. Pure Wayland sessions need an XWayland bridge for screen capture."
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** `DISPLAY`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "For cross-platform GUI automation without the desktop overhead (and without TCC / Session 0 / X11 setup), the `browser` toolset uses a real headless Chromium and is the right answer for web-only tasks." (`:421`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Document the exact symptom of each OS-level limitation (e.g. "click reports success while doing nothing") — that is what makes it diagnosable.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Computer-use configuration and telemetry  `id: docs-features.computer-use-config`
- **Surface:** Config + Env
- **Where:** `computer-use.md` → **"Configuration"**, **"Telemetry"**.
- **What it does:** Config keys and env overrides.
- **How it works:** Config (`:428-431`): `computer_use: {permission_mode: standard, capability_manifest: ""}` with comments "standard (default) | bounded" and "capability manifest path, required for bounded". Env overrides (`:435-441`): `HERMES_CUA_DRIVER_CMD=/path/to/your/cua-driver` ("Override the driver binary path (tests / CI / local builds)"); `HERMES_COMPUTER_USE_BACKEND=noop` ("Swap the backend entirely (for testing)" — "records calls, no side effects").
- **Inputs / options:** Telemetry (`:445-461`): "cua-driver ships with anonymous usage telemetry (PostHog) enabled by default upstream. **Hermes disables it for you** — on every cua-driver invocation (the MCP backend, `status`, `doctor`, and install) Hermes sets `CUA_DRIVER_RS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=0` in the driver's environment." Opt back in: `computer_use: {cua_telemetry: true}` — "default: false (telemetry off)".
- **Outputs / side effects:** "When it's on, `hermes computer-use doctor` reports `telemetry: enabled`; when off (the default), it reports `telemetry: disabled via CUA_DRIVER_RS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`." (`:461`)
- **Config / env:** As above.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Also documented: `computer_use.no_overlay`, `computer_use.allow_unsigned_driver`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Disable a third-party dependency's telemetry by default and report the state in `doctor`.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Testing against a local cua-driver build  `id: docs-features.computer-use-local-build`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `computer-use.md` → **"Testing against a local cua-driver build"**.
- **What it does:** Two ways to run a source build.
- **How it works:** "Hermes resolves the driver with `shutil.which(\"cua-driver\")` and **does not enforce `HERMES_CUA_DRIVER_VERSION`**, so a local build (reported as `0.0.0-local-*`) is accepted as-is." (`:468-471`) **Option A — `install-local`** (`:473-505`): Windows `./libs/cua-driver/scripts/install-local.ps1 -NoAutoStart`; macOS/Linux `./libs/cua-driver/scripts/install-local.sh --release` ("defaults to a debug build without --release"). "Windows stages the build under `%USERPROFILE%\\.cua-driver\\packages\\…` and junctions `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Programs\\Cua\\cua-driver\\bin` (added to your User PATH) to it. macOS/Linux symlinks `cua-driver` into `~/.local/bin` (override with `--bin-dir <path>`)."; "`-NoAutoStart` skips registering the `cua-driver-serve` logon daemon". Verify: `cua-driver --version` ("local builds report 0.0.0-local-release"), `(Get-Command cua-driver).Source` / `which cua-driver`. **Option B** (`:506-522`): `cargo build -p cua-driver` then `HERMES_CUA_DRIVER_CMD=<path>` in `.env` (Windows and macOS/Linux forms given).
- **Inputs / options:** As above.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A local binary on PATH or referenced by env.
- **Config / env:** `HERMES_CUA_DRIVER_CMD`, `HERMES_CUA_DRIVER_VERSION`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Confirmation commands (`:526-530`): `hermes computer-use status` ("prints the resolved binary path and version"); `hermes computer-use doctor` ("confirms the binary is reachable and exercises the full MCP path end-to-end"); `computer_use(action="capture")` ("exercises the spawned `cua-driver mcp` child process"). Notes & gotchas (`:534-549`): "**Hermes spawns a `cua-driver mcp` stdio proxy.** In a normal session the proxy connects to (and may start) the standard machine daemon. In explicit Hermes YOLO, Hermes instead owns a private `cua-driver serve --embedded` child and points the proxy at its private socket or named pipe."; "**Locked binary on Windows.** A running `cua-driver-serve` daemon can hold `cua-driver.exe` and block an overwrite on rebuild… stop it first with `cua-driver autostart disable` (or `schtasks /End /TN cua-driver-serve`)."; "**Rebuild loop.**"; "**Local builds skip the version check.** Hermes warns when the installed cua-driver is older than its per-OS tested baseline, but exempts `0.0.0-local-*` dev builds."
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Computer-use troubleshooting  `id: docs-features.computer-use-troubleshooting`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `computer-use.md` → **"Troubleshooting"**, **"See also"**.
- **What it does:** Six named failure modes.
- **How it works:** "**First action when anything's off: run `hermes computer-use doctor`.**" (`:553`) All five specific modes verbatim (`:557-580`): "**`computer_use backend unavailable: cua-driver is not installed`** — Run `hermes computer-use install`… or run `hermes tools` and enable the Computer Use toolset."; "**Clicks seem to have no effect** — Capture and verify. A modal you didn't see may be blocking input. Dismiss it with `escape` or the close button."; "**Element indices are stale** — SOM indices are only valid until the next `capture`. Re-capture after any state-changing action. The wrapper carries opaque `element_token`s for stale detection — you'll see an explicit error rather than a wrong click."; "**\"blocked pattern in type text\"** — The text you tried to `type` matches the dangerous-shell-pattern list."; "**Empty captures on Linux** — `DISPLAY` not set, or you're on pure Wayland without an XWayland bridge. `hermes computer-use doctor` will flag this as `ax_capability: fail` with a `Set DISPLAY (X11)…` hint."; "**Empty captures on Windows over SSH** — You're in Session 0 (the services session)."
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
