## Page: `memory-providers.md` — Memory Providers

### External memory providers (system)  `id: docs-features.memory-providers`
- **Surface:** Provider
- **Where:** `hermes memory setup|status|off`; `hermes plugins` → **Provider Plugins → Memory Provider**; `memory.provider` in config. Docs title **"Memory Providers"** (`sidebar_position: 4`), description *"External memory provider plugins — Honcho, OpenViking, Mem0, Hindsight, Holographic, RetainDB, ByteRover, Supermemory"*.
- **What it does:** "Hermes Agent ships with 8 external memory provider plugins that give the agent persistent, cross-session knowledge beyond the built-in MEMORY.md and USER.md. Only **one** external provider can be active at a time — the built-in memory is always active alongside it." (`memory-providers.md:9`)
- **How it works:** Six documented automatic behaviors (`:31-36`): "1. **Injects provider context** into the system prompt (what the provider knows)"; "2. **Prefetches relevant memories** before each turn (background, non-blocking)"; "3. **Syncs conversation turns** to the provider after each response"; "4. **Extracts memories on session end** (for providers that support it)"; "5. **Mirrors built-in memory writes** to the external provider"; "6. **Adds provider-specific tools** so the agent can search, store, and manage memories". "The built-in memory (MEMORY.md / USER.md) continues to work exactly as before. The external provider is additive." (`:38`)
- **Inputs / options:** Quick start (`:13-17`): `hermes memory setup` ("interactive picker + configuration"); `hermes memory status` ("check what's active"); `hermes memory off` ("disable external provider"). Manual: `memory: {provider: openviking}` — "or honcho, mem0, hindsight, holographic, retaindb, byterover, supermemory".
- **Outputs / side effects:** Provider-specific storage; extra tools in the schema.
- **Config / env:** `memory.provider`; per-provider config files and env vars (below).
- **Edge cases / guards:** Exactly one external provider active at a time.
- **Rebuild notes:** A provider interface with six lifecycle hooks (inject / prefetch / sync / extract / mirror / tools) plus per-provider config files under the profile home. A better version would allow two providers with declared precedence.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (**note the count drift**: the page's title/description say 8 providers, but the body documents **9** — Honcho, OpenViking, Mem0, Hindsight, Holographic, RetainDB, ByteRover, Supermemory **and Memori** — and the comparison table lists all 9).

### Provider — Honcho (on the providers page)  `id: docs-features.provider-honcho`
- **Surface:** Provider
- **Where:** `memory-providers.md` → **"Honcho"**.
- **What it does:** "AI-native cross-session user modeling with dialectic reasoning, session-scoped context injection, semantic search, and persistent conclusions." (`:45`)
- **How it works:** Fact table (`:47-52`): **Best for** "Multi-agent systems with cross-session context, user-agent alignment"; **Requires** "`pip install honcho-ai` + API key or self-hosted instance"; **Data storage** "Honcho Cloud or self-hosted"; **Cost** "Honcho pricing (cloud) / free (self-hosted)". Architecture and the three cadence knobs are as documented on `honcho.md` (see `docs-features.honcho*` entries).
- **Inputs / options:** **Tools (5):** `honcho_profile` ("read/update peer card"), `honcho_search` ("semantic search"), `honcho_context` ("session context — summary, representation, card, messages"), `honcho_reasoning` ("LLM-synthesized"), `honcho_conclude` ("create/delete conclusions"). Setup `hermes memory setup` → "honcho".
- **Outputs / side effects:** Server-side peers and conclusions.
- **Config / env:** "`$HERMES_HOME/honcho.json` (profile-local) or `~/.honcho/config.json` (global). Resolution order: `$HERMES_HOME/honcho.json` > `~/.hermes/honcho.json` > `~/.honcho/config.json`" (`:81`). The full 22-key config reference is reproduced on this page in a `<details>` block and matches `honcho.md` (see `docs-features.honcho-config`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** "**Headless / remote machines:** for cloud auth on a box without a browser (SSH, remote VM), pick **device** at the wizard's auth-method prompt. The CLI prints a short code and a verification link… The wizard defaults to this option automatically when it detects no usable local browser." (`:79`) "The legacy `hermes honcho setup` command still works (it now redirects to `hermes memory setup`), but is only registered after Honcho is selected as the active memory provider." (`:77`)
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Honcho multi-profile peers (`--clone`, `hermes honcho sync`)  `id: docs-features.honcho-profiles`
- **Surface:** CLI + Config
- **Where:** `memory-providers.md` → **"New profile, fresh Honcho peer"**, **"Existing profiles, backfill Honcho peers"**, **"Per-profile observation"**.
- **What it does:** Gives each Hermes profile its own Honcho AI peer.
- **How it works:** "`hermes profile create coder --clone` … creates a `hermes.coder` host block in `honcho.json` with `aiPeer: \"coder\"`, shared `workspace`, inherited `peerName`, `recallMode`, `writeFrequency`, `observation`, etc. The AI peer is eagerly created in Honcho so it exists before the first message." (`:165-169`) "`hermes honcho sync` — Scans every Hermes profile, creates host blocks for any profile without one, inherits settings from the default `hermes` block, and creates the new AI peers eagerly. Idempotent — skips profiles that already have a host block." (`:171-177`)
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes profile create <name> --clone`; `hermes honcho sync`. Per-profile observation override example verbatim (`:181-190`): `"hermes.coder": {"aiPeer": "coder", "observation": {"user": {"observeMe": true, "observeOthers": true}, "ai": {"observeMe": false, "observeOthers": true}}}`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Host blocks in `honcho.json`; peers created server-side.
- **Config / env:** `honcho.json` `hosts.<profile>`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Gateway identity keys (`:209-215`) repeat the `honcho.md` resolver: `pinUserPeer` ("checked first, so it overrides all aliases"), `userPeerAliases` ("The home for routing distinct identities — including agents that each carry their own peer"), `runtimePeerPrefix` ("Namespaces any unmapped runtime ID… so platforms with same-shaped IDs don't collide"). "Off-gateway these keys do nothing. `hermes memory setup` only prompts for them when it detects a connected gateway platform."
- **Rebuild notes:** Eagerly create the remote identity at profile-creation time so the first message never races it.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Provider — OpenViking  `id: docs-features.provider-openviking`
- **Surface:** Provider
- **Where:** `memory-providers.md` → **"OpenViking"**.
- **What it does:** "Context database by Volcengine (ByteDance) with filesystem-style knowledge hierarchy, tiered retrieval, and automatic memory extraction into 6 categories." (`:284`)
- **How it works:** Fact table (`:286-291`): **Best for** "Self-hosted knowledge management with structured browsing"; **Requires** "OpenViking initialized, validated, and running"; **Data storage** "Self-hosted (local or cloud)"; **Cost** "Free (open-source, AGPL-3.0)". Key features (`:322-325`): "Tiered context loading: L0 (~100 tokens) → L1 (~2k) → L2 (full)"; "Automatic memory extraction on session commit (profile, preferences, entities, events, cases, patterns)"; "`viking://` URI scheme for hierarchical knowledge browsing".
- **Inputs / options:** **Tools (6):** `viking_search` ("semantic search"), `viking_read` ("tiered: abstract/overview/full"), `viking_browse` ("filesystem navigation"), `viking_remember` ("store facts"), `viking_forget` ("delete a memory file by exact `viking://` URI"), `viking_add_resource` ("ingest URLs/docs"). Setup: `openviking-server init`, `openviking-server doctor`, `openviking-server`, then `hermes memory setup` / `hermes config set memory.provider openviking`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Memories under `viking://user/<user>/memories/...`.
- **Config / env:** `OPENVIKING_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:1933`, `OPENVIKING_API_KEY`, `OPENVIKING_ACCOUNT`, `OPENVIKING_USER`, `OPENVIKING_AGENT`; `memory.openviking.agent`. "OpenViking server settings live in `ov.conf` (`--config`, `OPENVIKING_CONFIG_FILE`, or `~/.openviking/ov.conf`). Client connection values live in `ovcli.conf` (`OPENVIKING_CLI_CONFIG_FILE` or `~/.openviking/ovcli.conf`)." (`:318`)
- **Edge cases / guards:** "`OPENVIKING_ACCOUNT` and `OPENVIKING_USER` are used for local/trusted mode. Peer identity is optional. By default, Hermes sends no peer ID and writes explicit memories to `viking://user/<user>/memories/...`… For separate assistant context, set `memory.openviking.agent: work-assistant`." (`:327`) "Existing non-empty peer settings keep their peer-scoped writes and recall… Existing memories are not moved or deleted… Set `memory.openviking.agent: hermes` to restore the old peer-scoped writes. Memories written at user scope before this change stay there and remain searchable. The setting changes future writes, not existing memory locations." (`:333`) "Hermes sends `User-Agent: openviking-memory-hermes/<version>` on OpenViking requests. This standard harness identifier contains no per-user identifier and does not add a separate request." (`:344`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Migrate write scope without moving existing data, and say so explicitly.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Provider — Mem0 (3 connection modes)  `id: docs-features.provider-mem0`
- **Surface:** Provider
- **Where:** `memory-providers.md` → **"Mem0"**.
- **What it does:** "Server-side LLM fact extraction with semantic search, reranking, and automatic deduplication. Three connection modes: **Platform** (Mem0 Cloud), **self-hosted dashboard** (a Mem0 server you run via Docker), and **OSS** (Mem0 in-process with your own LLM + vector store)." (`:354`)
- **How it works:** Fact table: **Best for** "Hands-off memory management — Mem0 handles extraction automatically"; **Requires** "`pip install mem0ai` + API key (platform), a running Mem0 server (self-hosted dashboard), or an LLM + vector store (OSS)"; **Cost** "Mem0 pricing (platform) / free (self-hosted or OSS)".
- **Inputs / options:** **Tools (4):** `mem0_search` ("semantic search; optional reranking in platform mode, off by default"), `mem0_add` ("store verbatim facts"), `mem0_update` ("update by ID"), `mem0_delete` ("delete by ID"). Setup commands verbatim: Platform — `hermes memory setup` → "mem0" → "Platform", or `hermes config set memory.provider mem0` + `MEM0_API_KEY`; OSS — `hermes memory setup mem0 --mode oss --oss-llm openai --oss-llm-key sk-... --oss-vector qdrant`, with `--dry-run` ("Preview without writing files"); Self-hosted — `hermes memory setup mem0 --mode selfhosted --host http://localhost:8888 --api-key your-admin-api-key`, or env `MEM0_HOST` + `MEM0_API_KEY`, or `mem0.json` `{ "host": ..., "api_key": ... }`. "**Switching modes:** Re-run `hermes memory setup mem0 --mode <platform|selfhosted|oss>` or edit `mem0.json` directly."
- **Outputs / side effects:** Memories in the selected backend.
- **Config / env:** `$HERMES_HOME/mem0.json` ("behavioral settings. Only the secret `MEM0_API_KEY` belongs in `~/.hermes/.env`"); `MEM0_API_KEY`, `MEM0_HOST`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The plugin authenticates with `X-API-Key` and uses the server's `/search` / `/memories` routes. `api_key` is optional (omit only for `AUTH_DISABLED` servers). Don't set `mode: oss` — it takes precedence over `host`."
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep behavioral settings in a JSON file and secrets in `.env` — a clean split worth copying.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Provider — Hindsight  `id: docs-features.provider-hindsight`
- **Surface:** Provider
- **Where:** `memory-providers.md` → **"Hindsight"**.
- **What it does:** "Long-term memory with knowledge graph, entity resolution, and multi-strategy retrieval. The `hindsight_reflect` tool provides cross-memory synthesis that no other provider offers. Automatically retains full conversation turns (including tool calls) with session-level document tracking." (`:432`)
- **How it works:** Fact table: **Best for** "Knowledge graph-based recall with entity relationships"; **Requires** "Cloud: API key from ui.hindsight.vectorize.io. Local: LLM API key (OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, etc.)"; **Data storage** "Hindsight Cloud or local embedded PostgreSQL"; **Cost** "Hindsight pricing (cloud) or free (local)".
- **Inputs / options:** **Tools:** `hindsight_retain` ("store with entity extraction"), `hindsight_recall` ("multi-strategy search"), `hindsight_reflect` ("cross-memory synthesis"). Setup: `hermes memory setup` → "hindsight", or `hermes config set memory.provider hindsight` + `HINDSIGHT_API_KEY`. Local UI: `hindsight-embed -p hermes ui start`.

- **Config / env:** `$HERMES_HOME/hindsight/config.json`, complete 12-key table verbatim: `mode` (`cloud`) "`cloud` or `local`"; `bank_id` (`hermes`) "Memory bank identifier"; `recall_budget` (`mid`) "Recall thoroughness: `low` / `mid` / `high`"; `memory_mode` (`hybrid`) "`hybrid` (context + tools), `context` (auto-inject only), `tools` (tools only)"; `auto_retain` (`true`) "Automatically retain conversation turns"; `auto_recall` (`true`) "Automatically recall memories before each turn"; `retain_async` (`true`) "Process retain asynchronously on the server"; `retain_context` (`conversation between Hermes Agent and the User`) "Context label for retained memories"; `retain_tags` (—) "Default tags applied to retained memories; merged with per-call tool tags"; `retain_source` (—) "Optional `metadata.source` attached to retained memories"; `retain_user_prefix` (`User`) "Label used before user turns in auto-retained transcripts"; `retain_assistant_prefix` (`Assistant`) "Label used before assistant turns"; `recall_tags` (—) "Tags to filter on recall".
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The setup wizard installs dependencies automatically and only installs what's needed for the selected mode (`hindsight-client` for cloud, `hindsight-all` for local). Requires `hindsight-client >= 0.4.22` (auto-upgraded on session start if outdated)."
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a

### Provider — Holographic  `id: docs-features.provider-holographic`

Setup: `hermes memory setup` → "holographic", or `hermes config set memory.provider holographic`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A local SQLite DB.
- **Config / env:** `config.yaml` under `plugins.hermes-memory-store`, all 3 keys verbatim: `db_path` (`$HERMES_HOME/memory_store.db`) "SQLite database path"; `auto_extract` (`false`) "Auto-extract facts at session end"; `default_trust` (`0.5`) "Default trust score (0.0–1.0)".
- **Edge cases / guards:** Unique capabilities, all four verbatim: "`probe` — entity-specific algebraic recall (all facts about a person/thing)"; "`reason` — compositional AND queries across multiple entities"; "`contradict` — automated detection of conflicting facts"; "Trust scoring with asymmetric feedback (+0.05 helpful / -0.10 unhelpful)".
- **Rebuild notes:** Asymmetric feedback weights (penalise harder than reward) make trust scores converge sensibly.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Provider — Supermemory  `id: docs-features.provider-supermemory`
- **Surface:** Provider
- **Where:** `memory-providers.md` → **"Supermemory"**.
- **What it does:** "Semantic long-term memory with profile recall, semantic search, explicit memory tools, and session-end conversation ingest via the Supermemory graph API." (`:568`)
- **How it works:** Fact table: **Best for** "Semantic recall with user profiling and session-level graph building"; **Requires** "`pip install supermemory` + cloud API key, or a self-hosted server"; **Data storage** "Supermemory Cloud or self-hosted"; **Cost** "Supermemory pricing (cloud) / free (self-hosted)".
- **Inputs / options:** **Tools:** `supermemory_store` ("save explicit memories"), `supermemory_search` ("semantic similarity search"), `supermemory_forget` ("forget by ID or best-match query"), `supermemory_profile` ("persistent profile + recent context"). Setup: `hermes memory setup` → "supermemory", or `hermes config set memory.provider supermemory` + `SUPERMEMORY_API_KEY`. Self-hosted: `npx supermemory local`, then set `base_url` in `$HERMES_HOME/supermemory.json` to `http://localhost:6767` **before** running setup — "Configuring the endpoint first ensures the setup connection probe also stays local."
- **Outputs / side effects:** Cloud/self-hosted memories and a session graph.
- **Config / env:** `$HERMES_HOME/supermemory.json`, complete 9-key table verbatim: `base_url` (`https://api.supermemory.ai`) "API endpoint for hosted or self-hosted Supermemory. Takes priority over `SUPERMEMORY_BASE_URL`."; `container_tag` (`hermes`) "Container tag used for search and writes. Supports `{identity}` template for profile-scoped tags."; `auto_recall` (`true`) "Inject relevant memory context before turns"; `auto_capture` (`true`) "Store cleaned user-assistant turns after each response"; `max_recall_results` (`10`) "Max recalled items to format into context"; `profile_frequency` (`50`) "Include profile facts on first turn and every N turns"; `capture_mode` (`all`) "Skip tiny or trivial turns by default"; `search_mode` (`hybrid`) "Search mode: `hybrid`, `memories`, or `documents`"; `api_timeout` (`5.0`) "Timeout for SDK and ingest requests". Env: `SUPERMEMORY_API_KEY` (required), `SUPERMEMORY_BASE_URL` ("compatibility fallback when `base_url` is not configured"), `SUPERMEMORY_CONTAINER_TAG` ("overrides config"). "Base URL precedence is `supermemory.json` → `SUPERMEMORY_BASE_URL` → `https://api.supermemory.ai`."
- **Edge cases / guards:** Key features, all seven verbatim: "Automatic context fencing — strips recalled memories from captured turns to prevent recursive memory pollution"; "Full-session ingest — the entire conversation is sent once at session boundaries"; "Session-end conversation ingest (to `/v4/conversations`) for richer profile + graph building"; "End-to-end self-hosted routing — SDK, probe, and conversation-ingest requests use the same configured endpoint"; "Profile facts injected on first turn and at configurable intervals"; "**Profile-scoped containers** — use `{identity}` in `container_tag` (e.g. `hermes-{identity}` → `hermes-coder`) to isolate memories per Hermes profile"; "**Multi-container mode** — enable `enable_custom_container_tags` with a `custom_containers` list to let the agent read/write across named containers. Automatic operations stay on the primary container." Multi-container example verbatim: `{"container_tag": "hermes", "enable_custom_container_tags": true, "custom_containers": ["project-alpha", "shared-knowledge"], "custom_container_instructions": "Use project-alpha for coding context."}`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Context fencing (strip recalled memories before capturing the turn) prevents the recursive-pollution failure mode every auto-capture memory system hits.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

## Page: `tts.md` — Voice & TTS

### Text-to-Speech providers (11)  `id: docs-features.tts-providers`
- **Surface:** Config

- **Surface:** Config

only applies when codec=mp3"), `base_url` ("Override via XAI_BASE_URL env var"). `neutts` — `ref_audio`, `ref_text`, `model: neuphonic/neutts-air-q4-gguf`, `device: cpu`. `kittentts` — `model: KittenML/kitten-tts-nano-0.8-int8` ("25MB int8; also: kitten-tts-micro-0.8 (41MB), kitten-tts-mini-0.8 (80MB)"), `voice: Jasper` ("Jasper, Bella, Luna, Bruno, Rosie, Hugo, Kiki, Leo"), `speed: 1.0` ("0.5 - 2.0"), `clean_text: true` ("Expand numbers, currencies, units"). `piper` — `voice: en_US-lessac-medium` ("voice name (auto-downloaded) OR absolute path to .onnx"), `voices_dir` ("default: ~/.hermes/cache/piper-voices/"), `use_cuda: false` ("requires onnxruntime-gpu"), `length_scale: 1.0` ("2.0 = twice as slow"), `noise_scale: 0.667`, `noise_w_scale: 0.8`, `volume: 1.0` ("0.5 = half as loud"), `normalize_audio: true`.
- **Inputs / options:** As above.
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** `tts.*`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** MiniMax region rules, all four verbatim (`:117-120`): "`region: \"global\"` uses `https://api.minimax.io/v1/t2a_v2` with `MINIMAX_API_KEY`."; "`region: \"cn\"` uses `https://api.minimaxi.com/v1/t2a_v2` with `MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY`."; "If `region` is omitted, `MINIMAX_API_KEY` keeps precedence for backward compatibility. If only `MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY` is configured, Hermes selects `cn`."; "An explicitly selected region must have its matching credential. Hermes never borrows the other region's key. A `base_url` override does not change the selected credential, and an override pointing at the other region's official endpoint is rejected." "**Speed control**: The global `tts.speed` value applies to all providers by default. Each provider can override it with its own `speed` setting… Default is `1.0`." (`:122`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Never borrow a sibling region's credential; reject an override that points at the other region.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Audio tags (Gemini, xAI)  `id: docs-features.tts-audio-tags`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `tts.md` → **"Audio Tags (Gemini, xAI)"**.
- **What it does:** "Google's Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS and xAI's Grok TTS support freeform square-bracket audio tags such as `[whispers]`, `[excitedly]`, `[very slow]`, `[laughs]`, and other expressive delivery notes." (`:141`)
- **How it works:** "Enable `tts.gemini.audio_tags` or `tts.xai.auto_speech_tags` to have Hermes run a hidden rewrite pass before TTS. The rewrite inserts inline tags into the TTS script only; the visible chat reply stays unchanged." "The rewrite uses `auxiliary.tts_audio_tags` and defaults to your main chat model. Override that auxiliary task if you want tag insertion handled by a cheaper or faster model." (`:153`)
- **Inputs / options:** `tts.gemini.audio_tags: true`, `tts.xai.auto_speech_tags: true`; `auxiliary.tts_audio_tags`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Tagged TTS script (invisible in chat).
- **Config / env:** As above.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "**Language (OpenAI-compatible endpoints)**: `tts.openai.language` is forwarded to the endpoint as a `lang_code` request parameter… for example Kokoro-FastAPI, where `language: \"es\"` selects the Spanish phonemizer… Leave it unset when using the official OpenAI API, which does not accept this parameter. When unset, nothing extra is sent." (`:155`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep the rewritten script separate from the visible reply.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### TTS input length limits  `id: docs-features.tts-length-limits`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `tts.md` → **"Input length limits"**.
- **What it does:** "Each provider has a documented per-request input-character cap. Hermes splits longer replies into ordered, sentence-aware chunks before calling the provider, so the full normalized text is preserved instead of silently truncated." (`:152`)
- **How it works:** Complete cap table (`:156-166`), all 10 rows verbatim: Edge TTS 5000; OpenAI 4096; xAI 15000; MiniMax 10000; Mistral 4000; Google Gemini 32000; ElevenLabs "Model-aware (see below)"; NeuTTS 2000; KittenTTS 2000; Piper 5000. ElevenLabs model table (`:170-175`), all 5 rows: `eleven_flash_v2_5` 40000; `eleven_flash_v2` 30000; "`eleven_multilingual_v2` (default), `eleven_multilingual_v1`, `eleven_english_sts_v2`, `eleven_english_sts_v1`" 10000; "`eleven_v3`, `eleven_ttv_v3`" 5000; "Unknown model" "Falls back to provider default (10000)".
- **Inputs / options:** "**Override per provider** with `max_text_length:` under the provider section" — example `tts: {openai: {max_text_length: 8192}}`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Chunked synthesis.
- **Config / env:** `tts.<provider>.max_text_length`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Only positive integers are honored. Zero, negative, non-numeric, or boolean values fall through to the provider default, so a broken config can't accidentally bypass the provider request limit." (`:184`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Chunk rather than truncate, and refuse to let a bad config bypass the provider's own limit.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### TTS custom command providers  `id: docs-features.tts-command-providers`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `tts.md` → **"Custom command providers"**.
- **What it does:** "If a TTS engine you want isn't natively supported (VoxCPM, MLX-Kokoro, XTTS CLI, a voice-cloning script, anything else that exposes a CLI), you can wire it in as a **command-type provider** without writing any Python. Hermes writes the input text to a temp UTF-8 file, runs your shell command, and reads the audio file the command produced." (`:259`)
- **How it works:** "Declare one or more providers under `tts.providers.<name>` and switch between them with `tts.provider: <name>`." Three documented examples (`:264-284`): `voxcpm` (`command: "voxcpm --ref ~/voice.wav --text-file {input_path} --out {output_path}"`, `output_format: mp3`, `timeout: 180`, `voice_compatible: true` — "try to deliver as a Telegram voice bubble"); `mlx-kokoro` (`command: "python -m mlx_kokoro --in {input_path} --out {output_path} --voice {voice}"`, `voice: af_sky`, `output_format: wav`); `piper-custom` (`command: "piper -m /path/to/custom.onnx -f {output_path} < {input_path}"`, `output_format: wav`).
- **Inputs / options:** Complete placeholder table (`:307-315`), all 7 rows verbatim: `{input_path}` ("Path to the temp UTF-8 text file Hermes wrote"); `{text_path}` ("Alias for `{input_path}`"); `{output_path}` ("Path the command must write audio to"); `{format}` ("`mp3` / `wav` / `ogg` / `flac`"); `{voice}` ("`tts.providers.<name>.voice`, empty when unset"); `{model}` ("`tts.providers.<name>.model`"); `{speed}` ("Resolved speed multiplier (provider or global)"). "Use `{{` and `}}` for literal braces." Optional keys table (`:319-325`), all 5 rows verbatim: `timeout` (`120`) "Idle seconds; stdout or stderr output resets the deadline. The process tree is killed after inactivity (Unix `killpg`, Windows `taskkill /T`)."; `output_format` (`mp3`) "One of `mp3` / `wav` / `ogg` / `flac`. Auto-inferred from the output extension if Hermes picks a path."; `voice_compatible` (`false`) "When `true`, Hermes converts MP3/WAV output to Opus/OGG via ffmpeg so Telegram renders a voice bubble."; `max_text_length` (`5000`) "Maximum input characters per command invocation; longer text is split into ordered chunks."; `voice` / `model` (empty) "Passed to the command as placeholder values only." "**Supported `output_format` values:** `mp3` (default), `wav`, `ogg`, `flac`, `m4a`, `aac`, `amr`, `opus`… An unknown value falls back to `mp3`." (`:286`)
- **Outputs / side effects:** An audio file at `{output_path}`.
- **Config / env:** `tts.providers.<name>.*`; `env_passthrough` for the child environment.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "**Subprocess environment:** command providers (TTS and STT) run with Hermes secrets scrubbed from the child environment — gateway bot tokens, LLM provider API keys, and internal relay credentials are removed; `PATH`, `HOME`, locale, and other normal variables are kept. If your command template needs its own API key from the environment… list the variable names under `env_passthrough`." (`:288-296`) Behavior notes, all five verbatim (`:329-333`): "**Built-in names always win.** A `tts.providers.openai` entry never shadows the native OpenAI provider"; "**Default delivery is a document.** Command providers deliver as regular audio attachments on every platform. Opt in to voice-bubble delivery per-provider with `voice_compatible: true`."; "**Command failures surface to the agent.** Non-zero exit, empty output, or timeout all return an error with the command's stderr/stdout included"; "**`type: command` is the default when `command:` is set.**"; "**`{input_path}` / `{text_path}` are interchangeable.**" Security (`:337`): "Command-type providers run whatever shell command you configure, with your user's permissions. Hermes quotes placeholder values and enforces the configured timeout, but the command template itself is trusted local input — treat it the same way you would a shell script on your PATH."
- **Rebuild notes:** Placeholder substitution with context-aware shell quoting, an idle-reset timeout, and a scrubbed child env with an explicit passthrough list.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### TTS Python plugin providers  `id: docs-features.tts-python-plugins`
- **Surface:** Plugin
- **Where:** `tts.md` → **"Python plugin providers"**.
- **What it does:** "For TTS engines that can't be expressed as a single shell command — Python SDKs without a CLI, streaming engines, voice-listing APIs, OAuth-refreshing auth — register a Python plugin via `ctx.register_tts_provider()`." (`:366`)
- **How it works:** Decision table (`:372-379`), all 6 rows verbatim: "A single CLI reading text from a file/stdin and writing audio to a file/stdout" → "**Command provider** (no Python needed)"; "Two or three CLIs chained with shell pipes" → "**Command provider**"; "A Python SDK only — no CLI" → "**Plugin**"; "Streaming bytes you want to deliver chunked (mid-generation voice bubbles)" → "**Plugin** (override `stream()`)"; "A voice-listing API used by `hermes setup`" → "**Plugin** (override `list_voices()`)"; "OAuth refresh flow (not a static bearer token)" → "**Plugin**". Minimal plugin verbatim: `~/.hermes/plugins/my-tts/` with `plugin.yaml` (`name: my-tts`, `version: 0.1.0`, `description: "My custom Python TTS backend"`) and `__init__.py` subclassing `agent.tts_provider.TTSProvider` with `name`, `display_name`, `is_available()` ("Return False when credentials/deps are missing — picker skips this row but the dispatcher still routes here on explicit config."), and `synthesize(text, output_path, *, voice=None, model=None, speed=None, format="mp3", **extra) -> str`.
- **Inputs / options:** `ctx.register_tts_provider()`; overridable `stream()`, `list_voices()`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A new selectable provider name.
- **Config / env:** `tts.provider`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The plugin **coexists with** (does not replace) the Custom command providers registry." "Built-ins always win, and command providers win over a same-name plugin — so plugins are safe to register against any non-built-in name without worrying about shadowing your existing config." (`:381`)
- **Rebuild notes:** A precedence ladder (built-in > command > plugin) makes third-party registration safe by construction.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Voice message transcription (STT)  `id: docs-features.stt`
- **Surface:** Gateway/Telegram
- **Where:** `tts.md` → **"Voice Message Transcription (STT)"**.
- **What it does:** "Voice messages sent on Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, Slack, or Signal are automatically transcribed and injected as text into the conversation. The agent sees the transcript as normal text." (`:445`)
- **How it works:** Provider table (`:447-451`), all 3 rows verbatim: **Local Whisper** (default) — Good — Free — "None needed"; **Groq Whisper API** — "Good–Best" — "Free tier" — `GROQ_API_KEY`; **OpenAI Whisper API** — "Good–Best" — Paid — "`VOICE_TOOLS_OPENAI_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`". ":::info Zero Config Local transcription works out of the box when `faster-whisper` is installed. If that's unavailable, Hermes can also use a local `whisper` CLI from common install locations (like `/opt/homebrew/bin`) or a custom command via `HERMES_LOCAL_STT_COMMAND`." (`:453-455`)
- **Inputs / options:** Config block verbatim (`:460-476`): `stt.provider: "local"` ("\"local\" | \"groq\" | \"openai\" | \"mistral\" | \"xai\" | \"elevenlabs\" | \"deepinfra\""); `stt.language: "en"` ("Global language hint applied to every provider unless a per-provider language overrides it; set \"\" to restore auto-detect"); `stt.local.model: "base"` ("tiny, base, small, medium, large-v3"); `stt.local.language` / `stt.groq.language` ("optional ISO-639-1 hint; blank = use HERMES_LOCAL_STT_LANGUAGE if set, else auto-detect"); `stt.openai.model: "whisper-1"` ("whisper-1, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-transcribe"); `stt.mistral.model: "voxtral-mini-latest"` ("voxtral-mini-latest, voxtral-mini-2602"); `stt.xai.model: "grok-stt"`, `stt.xai.language` ("blank = use HERMES_LOCAL_STT_LANGUAGE if set, else \"en\"").
- **Outputs / side effects:** Transcript text injected into the conversation.
- **Config / env:** `stt.*`; `GROQ_API_KEY`, `VOICE_TOOLS_OPENAI_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`, `HERMES_LOCAL_STT_LANGUAGE`, `HERMES_LOCAL_STT_COMMAND`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Local model table (`:483-489`), all 5 rows: `tiny` ~75 MB Fastest Basic; `base` ~150 MB Fast "Good (default)"; `small` ~500 MB Medium Better; `medium` ~1.5 GB Slower Great; `large-v3` ~3 GB Slowest Best. Provider notes verbatim: "**Groq API** — … Set `stt.groq.language` (or the global `HERMES_LOCAL_STT_LANGUAGE` env var) to skip Whisper's auto-detect and reduce latency"; "**OpenAI API** — Accepts `VOICE_TOOLS_OPENAI_KEY` first and falls back to `OPENAI_API_KEY`"; "**Mistral API (Voxtral Transcribe)** — Requires `MISTRAL_API_KEY`… Supports 13 languages, speaker diarization, and word-level timestamps. Install with `uv pip install -e \".[mistral]\"`"; "**xAI Grok STT** — Requires `XAI_API_KEY`. Posts to `https://api.x.ai/v1/stt` as multipart/form-data… Auto-detection order puts it after Groq — explicitly set `stt.provider: xai` to force it."; "**Custom local CLI fallback** — Set `HERMES_LOCAL_STT_COMMAND`… The command template supports `{input_path}`, `{output_dir}`, `{language}`, and `{model}` placeholders. Hermes tokenizes the rendered template into an argument list and executes it without a shell, so operators such as `|`, `>`, `&&`, and `;` are passed as literal arguments. Your command must write a `.txt` transcript somewhere under `{output_dir}`."
- **Rebuild notes:** Tokenize the legacy env-var template into argv (no shell) so a template cannot smuggle shell operators.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### STT fallback behavior  `id: docs-features.stt-fallback`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `tts.md` → **"Fallback Behavior"**.
- **What it does:** Explicit selection is strict; auto-detect only applies when nothing was ever chosen.
- **How it works:** "An **explicit** `stt.provider` selection (written in `config.yaml`, e.g. via `hermes tools`) is honored strictly — if that provider can't run, transcription fails with a clear error (`stt is configured to use <provider> (set via hermes tools), but <failure>. Run 'hermes tools' to change it.`) instead of silently switching engines. Note that `stt.provider: local` written in your config counts as an explicit selection." (`:526`) Auto-detect rules, all five verbatim (`:530-534`): "**Local faster-whisper unavailable** → Tries a local `whisper` CLI or `HERMES_LOCAL_STT_COMMAND` before cloud providers"; "**Groq key not set** → Skipped; next available provider"; "**OpenAI key not set** → Skipped; next available provider"; "**Mistral key/SDK not set** → Skipped in auto-detect; falls through to next available provider"; "**Nothing available** → Voice messages pass through with an accurate note to the user".
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** A typed error or a pass-through note.
- **Config / env:** `stt.provider`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** n/a
- **Rebuild notes:** Explicit choice never silently degrades — the same rule as `web.backend` and `image_gen.provider`.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### STT custom command providers  `id: docs-features.stt-command-providers`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `tts.md` → **"STT custom command providers"**.
- **What it does:** "If the STT engine you want isn't natively supported (Doubao ASR, NVIDIA Parakeet, a whisper.cpp build, an open-source SenseVoice CLI, anything else that exposes a shell command), wire it in as a **command-type provider**." (`:539`)
- **How it works:** Three documented examples (`:545-563`): `parakeet` (`command: "parakeet-asr --model nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2 --in {input_path} --out {output_path}"`, `format: txt`, `language: en`, `timeout: 300`); `whispercpp` (`command: "whisper-cli -m ~/models/ggml-large-v3.bin -f {input_path} -otxt -of {output_dir}/transcript"`, `format: txt`); `sensevoice` (`command: "sensevoice-cli {input_path} --json | tee {output_path}"`, `format: json`). Transcript read-back, all three steps verbatim (`:583-585`): "1. If `{output_path}` exists and is non-empty → Hermes reads it as UTF-8 text."; "2. Otherwise, if the command wrote to stdout → Hermes uses that."; "3. Otherwise → error: \"Command STT provider wrote no output file and produced no stdout\"."
- **Inputs / options:** Placeholder table (`:571-579`), all 6 rows verbatim: `{input_path}` ("Absolute path to the input audio file (original location, read-only)"); `{output_path}` ("Absolute path the command should write the transcript to"); `{output_dir}` ("Parent directory of `{output_path}` (handy for whisper-style tools)"); `{format}` ("Configured output format: `txt` / `json` / `srt` / `vtt`"); `{language}` ("Configured language code (defaults to `en`)"); `{model}` ("`stt.providers.<name>.model`, empty when unset"). Optional keys (`:591-596`), all 4 rows: `timeout` (`300`) "Seconds; the process tree is killed on expiry (Unix `start_new_session`, Windows `taskkill /T`)."; `format` (`txt`) "One of `txt` / `json` / `srt` / `vtt`. Sets the extension of `{output_path}`."; `language` (`en`) "Forwarded to `{language}`. Defaults to `stt.language` then `en`."; `model` (empty) "Forwarded to `{model}`. The `model=` argument to `transcribe_audio()` overrides this."
- **Outputs / side effects:** A transcript file or stdout.
- **Config / env:** `stt.providers.<name>.*`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Behavior notes verbatim (`:600-601`): "**Built-ins always win.** Declaring `stt.providers.openai: type: command` does NOT override the real OpenAI Whisper handler."; "**Process-tree cleanup.** A command running over `timeout` has its entire process tree killed, not just the shell wrapper." "For `format: json` / `srt` / `vtt`, Hermes returns the raw file content as the `transcript` field. Extracting `.text` from JSON is out of scope for the runner." (`:587`) Legacy comparison (`:565`): "This complements the legacy `HERMES_LOCAL_STT_COMMAND` escape hatch via the built-in `local_command` path. Unlike the shell-driven command-provider registry, the legacy template is tokenized into argv and runs without implicit shell interpretation."
- **Rebuild notes:** File-then-stdout read-back covers both file-writing CLIs and curl one-liners.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Doubao / Volcengine ASR example  `id: docs-features.stt-doubao`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `tts.md` → **"Example: Doubao / Volcengine ASR"**.
- **What it does:** A worked local-command STT recipe.
- **How it works:** Verbatim: `pip install doubao-speech`; `export VOLCENGINE_APP_ID=...`; `export VOLCENGINE_ACCESS_TOKEN=...`; `export HERMES_LOCAL_STT_COMMAND='doubao-speech transcribe {input_path} --out {output_dir}/transcript.txt'`; then `stt: {provider: local_command}`. "Hermes writes the incoming voice message to `{input_path}`, runs the command, and reads the `.txt` file produced under `{output_dir}`. Language is auto-detected by the Volcengine bigmodel endpoint."
- **Inputs / options:** As above.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A transcript file.
- **Config / env:** `HERMES_LOCAL_STT_COMMAND`, `VOLCENGINE_APP_ID`, `VOLCENGINE_ACCESS_TOKEN`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "If a trusted local template intentionally needs pipes, redirects, or another shell feature, invoke the shell explicitly. Keep dynamic paths outside the shell program and pass them as positional arguments" — verbatim example: `export HERMES_LOCAL_STT_COMMAND='sh -c '\''whisper "$1" --output_format txt --output_dir "$2" | tee "$2/whisper.log"'\'' _ {input_path} {output_dir}'`. "On Windows, use an explicit `cmd /c` or PowerShell wrapper instead. An explicit wrapper makes shell interpretation an opt-in part of the configured argv rather than an implicit property of every local STT template."
- **Rebuild notes:** Make shell interpretation an explicit opt-in in the argv, never implicit.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### STT Python plugin providers  `id: docs-features.stt-python-plugins`
- **Surface:** Plugin
- **Where:** `tts.md` → **"Python plugin providers (STT)"**.
- **What it does:** The STT counterpart to the TTS plugin surface, for engines that need Python rather than a shell command.
- **How it works:** Same precedence rule as TTS — built-ins win, then command providers, then plugins — with a `TTSProvider`-analogous STT provider base class registered through the plugin context.
- **Inputs / options:** Plugin registration in `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A new selectable `stt.provider` name.
- **Config / env:** `stt.provider`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** n/a
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (section present at `tts.md:613`; see the `optional`/`providers` shards for the provider base class).

## Page: `api-server.md` — API Server

### API server (OpenAI-compatible endpoint)  `id: docs-features.api-server`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `http://127.0.0.1:8642` when `API_SERVER_ENABLED=true` and the gateway runs. Docs title **"API Server"** (`sidebar_position: 14`), description *"Expose hermes-agent as an OpenAI-compatible API for any frontend"*.
- **What it does:** "The API server exposes hermes-agent as an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint. Any frontend that speaks the OpenAI format — Open WebUI, LobeChat, LibreChat, NextChat, ChatBox, and hundreds more — can connect to hermes-agent and use it as a backend." (`api-server.md:9`) "Your agent handles requests with its full toolset (terminal, file operations, web search, memory, skills) and returns the final response. When streaming, tool progress indicators appear inline." (`:11`)
- **How it works:** Quick start, all three steps verbatim (`:19-53`): "1. Enable the API server" — `.env`: `API_SERVER_ENABLED=true`, `API_SERVER_KEY=change-me-local-dev`, optional `# API_SERVER_CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000`; "2. Start the gateway" — `hermes gateway`, printing `[API Server] API server listening on http://127.0.0.1:8642`; "3. Connect a frontend" — `curl http://localhost:8642/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer change-me-local-dev" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model": "hermes-agent", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'`.
- **Inputs / options:** See the endpoint entries below.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Agent runs with full tool access.
- **Config / env:** `API_SERVER_*`; `gateway.api_server.*`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** ":::warning Security The API server gives full access to hermes-agent's toolset, **including terminal commands**. `API_SERVER_KEY` is **required for every deployment**, including the default loopback bind on `127.0.0.1`." (`:637-639`)
- **Rebuild notes:** OpenAI-compatible surface in front of a full agent loop, with a Hermes-native runs API alongside. A better version would expose per-request tool allowlists.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented (40 literal API-server paths in `hermes_inv/api_server_paths.txt`).

### `POST /v1/chat/completions`  `id: docs-features.api-chat-completions`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `api-server.md` → **"POST /v1/chat/completions"**.
- **What it does:** "Standard OpenAI Chat Completions format. Stateless — the full conversation is included in each request via the `messages` array." (`:60`)
- **How it works:** Request/response shapes given verbatim (`:64-90`), including `usage: {prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens}` and `finish_reason: "stop"`.
- **Inputs / options:** `model`, `messages`, `stream`; plus `provider`, `model_options` (see per-request model selection). "**Inline image input:** user messages may send `content` as an array of `text` and `image_url` parts. Both remote `http(s)` URLs and `data:image/...` URLs are supported" — example includes `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://example.com/cat.png", "detail": "high"}}`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A `chat.completion` object, or SSE when `"stream": true`.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Uploaded files (`file` / `input_file` / `file_id`) and non-image `data:` URLs return `400 unsupported_content_type`." (`:112`) Streaming (`:114`): "For **Chat Completions**, the stream uses standard `chat.completion.chunk` events plus Hermes' custom `hermes.tool.progress` event for tool-start UX." Tool progress (`:116-117`): "**Chat Completions**: Hermes emits `event: hermes.tool.progress` for tool-start visibility without polluting persisted assistant text."
- **Rebuild notes:** A custom SSE event type for tool progress keeps the standard chunk stream clean.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### `POST /v1/responses` and response storage  `id: docs-features.api-responses`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `api-server.md` → **"POST /v1/responses"**, **"GET /v1/responses/{id}"**, **"DELETE /v1/responses/{id}"**.
- **What it does:** "OpenAI Responses API format. Supports server-side conversation state via `previous_response_id` — the server stores full conversation history (including tool calls and results) so multi-turn context is preserved without the client managing it." (`:117`)
- **How it works:** Request verbatim: `{"model": "hermes-agent", "input": "What files are in my project?", "instructions": "You are a helpful coding assistant.", "store": true}`. Conversation chaining (`:186-188`): `{"input": "Run the tests", "conversation": "my-project"}` — "The server automatically chains to the latest response in that conversation. Like the `/title` command for gateway sessions." Streaming events for Responses (`:114`): "`response.created`, `response.output_text.delta`, `response.output_item.added`, `response.output_item.done`, and `response.completed`"; "**Responses**: Hermes emits spec-native `function_call` and `function_call_output` output items during the SSE stream, so clients can render structured tool UI in real time."
- **Inputs / options:** `model`, `input`, `instructions`, `store`, `previous_response_id`, `conversation`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Stored responses in SQLite.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** `GET /v1/responses/{id}` — "Retrieve a previously stored response by ID."; `DELETE /v1/responses/{id}` — "Delete a stored response." Limitation (`:756`): "stored responses (for `previous_response_id`) are persisted in SQLite and survive gateway restarts. Max 100 stored responses (LRU eviction)."
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### `GET /v1/models` and `GET /api/model/options`  `id: docs-features.api-models`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `api-server.md` → **"GET /v1/models"**, **"GET /api/model/options"**.
- **What it does:** `/v1/models` — "Lists the agent as an available model. The advertised model name defaults to the profile name (or `hermes-agent` for the default profile). Required by most frontends for model discovery." (`:199`) `/api/model/options` — "Hermes-aware clients can request the same curated provider/model inventory used by the dashboard and TUI." (`:207`)
- **How it works:** "`/v1/models` is intentionally the cheap OpenAI-compat surface. It does **not** enumerate every authenticated provider/model combination Hermes can route to, and it does not do pricing or capability enrichment." (`:201`) "That payload is the same substrate the dashboard Models page and the TUI `model.options` RPC use. It returns authenticated providers, curated model lists, per-model pricing, and model capability hints." (`:219`)
- **Inputs / options:** `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_SERVER_KEY" "http://127.0.0.1:8642/api/model/options"`; refresh form `?refresh=1`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Provider rows, capability hints, pricing.
- **Config / env:** `API_SERVER_MODEL_NAME`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Normal opens are intentionally conservative for custom providers: Hermes probes only the **currently selected** custom endpoint so a stale or offline saved endpoint does not block the picker. An explicit refresh flips to full probing and busts the provider model cache." (`:221`) "Use `/v1/models` when an OpenAI-compatible client only needs a model name… Use `/api/model/options` when an authenticated UI needs the richer Hermes-specific picker metadata." (`:235`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Two model endpoints — a cheap compat one and a rich native one — so a stale custom endpoint cannot wedge either.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### `GET /v1/capabilities`  `id: docs-features.api-capabilities`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `api-server.md` → **"GET /v1/capabilities"**.
- **What it does:** "Returns a machine-readable description of the API server's stable surface for external UIs, orchestrators, and plugin bridges." (`:241`)
- **How it works:** Payload verbatim (`:243-258`): `{"object": "hermes.api_server.capabilities", "platform": "hermes-agent", "model": "hermes-agent", "auth": {"type": "bearer", "required": true}, "features": {"chat_completions": true, "responses_api": true, "run_submission": true, "run_status": true, "run_events_sse": true, "run_stop": true}}`.
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Use this endpoint when integrating dashboards, browser UIs, or control planes so they can discover whether the running Hermes version supports runs, streaming, cancellation, and session continuity without depending on private Python internals." (`:260`) Additional advertised flags named elsewhere on the page: `run_approval`, `session_*`, `endpoints.session_*`, `endpoints.*`, `session_key_header`, `browser_extension_control`.
- **Rebuild notes:** A capabilities document is the contract that lets clients degrade instead of guessing.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Browser-extension control protocol  `id: docs-features.api-browser-extension`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `api-server.md` → **"Browser-extension control"**.
- **What it does:** "Hermes can route browser tools through an authenticated extension that controls the browser session associated with the current Hermes session. The feature is disabled by default; set `browser.extension_control.enabled` to `true` to opt in." (`:264`)
- **How it works:** Registration, all three steps verbatim (`:311-317`): "1. Send an authenticated `POST /v1/browser-control/register` with `protocol_version`, `session_id`, `controller_id`, `browser_profile_id`, and the requested `capabilities`."; "2. Hermes returns a single-use ticket with a 30-second TTL and the filtered, server-bound controller scope."; "3. Open `GET /v1/browser-control/ws` with both WebSocket subprotocols: `hermes-browser-control-v1` and `hermes-browser-control-ticket.<ticket>`." Frames (`:325-331`): "Hermes sends `browser.controller.command` frames containing `command_id`, `action`, immutable `arguments`, browser/controller ids, and the originating `tool_call_id`. The controller replies with `browser.controller.result`, the same `command_id`, an exact boolean `ok`, and either `result` or `error`. Cancellation and timeout emit `browser.controller.cancel`; late results are ignored."
- **Inputs / options:** Complete capability allowlist (`:283-294`), all 11 entries verbatim: `controller.noop`, `browser_back`, `browser_click`, `browser_navigate`, `browser_press`, `browser_screenshot`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_tab_activate`, `browser_tabs`, `browser_type`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Browser actions executed by the extension.
- **Config / env:** `browser.extension_control.enabled`; `API_SERVER_KEY`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The local API path also requires the API server bearer key. A controller may register only for an existing server session. Hermes derives the controller principal from authenticated server state; a client-supplied `principal_id` is ignored." (`:276`) "Requested capabilities outside that list are filtered out. Raw CDP, arbitrary script evaluation, console access, uploads, image extraction, and vision are not part of the controller protocol." (`:296`) "When a request has no bound controller identity, or when the feature is disabled, Hermes preserves the existing browser backend. Once the gateway binds a controller principal and transport family to the request, that extension lane is authoritative: missing, ambiguous, disconnected, or incapable controllers fail closed instead of silently switching to a different local/cloud browser. After an exact controller is selected, its result or error is authoritative and Hermes never retries the same action through another backend." (`:300-308`) "The ticket is never accepted in the query string. Unknown, expired, reused, or malformed tickets fail before WebSocket upgrade." (`:319`) "An unexpected socket loss marks the controller offline and preserves work already in flight until each command's original deadline."
- **Rebuild notes:** Single-use short-TTL ticket in a WebSocket subprotocol (never the query string), a server-derived principal, and a hard capability allowlist.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Per-request model selection  `id: docs-features.api-per-request-model`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `api-server.md` → **"Per-request model selection"**.
- **What it does:** "Authenticated clients can override Hermes' default model selection per request." (`:353`)
- **How it works:** Three request fields verbatim (`:356-358`): `model` ("the target model id for this turn"); `provider` ("the Hermes provider slug to resolve credentials/runtime for this turn"); `model_options` ("request-scoped reasoning / service-tier controls"). Accepted on five endpoints (`:362-366`): `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `POST /v1/responses`, `POST /v1/runs`, `POST /api/sessions/{session_id}/chat`, `POST /api/sessions/{session_id}/chat/stream`. Precedence, all four steps verbatim (`:370-375`): "1. Session `/model` override, if that session already has one"; "2. A static `gateway.platforms.api_server.model_routes` mapping selected when the request's `model` is a configured route alias"; "3. Direct request `model` / `provider` when no route alias matches"; "4. Global gateway config / environment defaults". Example verbatim: `{"model": "MiniMax-M3", "provider": "minimax", "model_options": {"reasoning_effort": "high", "service_tier": "priority"}, "messages": [...]}`.
- **Inputs / options:** `gateway.platforms.api_server.model_routes`; `gateway.platforms.api_server.direct_model_requests`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Per-turn routing.
- **Config / env:** As above.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "`model_options` stays request-scoped regardless of which model/provider wins." "If a request sends a `provider` that conflicts with a configured `model_routes` alias, Hermes rejects the request with `400` instead of silently remixing route credentials with another provider." (`:379`) "**Bare `model` values on the OpenAI-compatible endpoints are opt-in.** Generic OpenAI clients routinely hardcode model names (`gpt-4o`, ...)… a `model` value sent WITHOUT a `provider` is therefore ignored unless you enable `gateway.platforms.api_server.direct_model_requests: true`. Requests that include an explicit `provider` — and the Hermes-native `/v1/runs` and session-chat endpoints — always honor the requested model regardless of this flag." (`:383-397`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Ignore bare model names by default because generic clients hardcode them — a subtle but essential compatibility decision.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Health endpoints  `id: docs-features.api-health`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `api-server.md` → **"GET /health"**, **"GET /health/detailed"**.
- **What it does:** Liveness and authenticated readiness.
- **How it works:** "`GET /health` — Health check. Returns `{\"status\": \"ok\"}`. Also available at **GET /v1/health** for OpenAI-compatible clients that expect the `/v1/` prefix." (`:416`) "`GET /health/detailed` — Authenticated readiness check for monitoring and control planes. It reports bounded status for the active profile's config, state database, configured model, disk space, gateway/platform state, active API runs, pending process completions, and active delegations." (`:420`)
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** Status JSON.
- **Config / env:** `API_SERVER_KEY` (for the detailed route).
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The response exposes status and counts, not config values, credentials, paths, commands, queue payloads, or raw errors. The public `/health` route remains a cheap liveness probe and does not run readiness checks. A degraded readiness result still uses HTTP 200; inspect the top-level `status` and `readiness.checks` fields." (`:420-428`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Separate cheap liveness from authenticated readiness; never leak config values in a health payload.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Runs API (`/v1/runs`)  `id: docs-features.api-runs`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `api-server.md` → **"Runs API (streaming-friendly alternative)"**.
- **What it does:** "a **runs** API for long-form sessions where the client wants to subscribe to progress events instead of managing streaming themselves." (`:432`)
- **How it works:** All five endpoints verbatim: `POST /v1/runs` — "Create a new agent run. Returns a `run_id`" → `{"run_id": "run_abc123", "status": "started"}`; "Runs accept a simple `input` string and optional `session_id`, `instructions`, `conversation_history`, or `previous_response_id`."; `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}` — "Poll the current run state" → `{"object": "hermes.run", "run_id": ..., "status": "completed", "session_id": ..., "model": ..., "output": "Done.", "usage": {...}}`; `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/events` — "Server-Sent Events stream of the run's tool-call progress, token deltas, and lifecycle events."; `POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/stop` — "Interrupt a running agent turn. The endpoint returns immediately with `{\"status\": \"stopping\"}`"; `POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/approval` — "Resolve a pending approval for a run that is waiting on a human decision… advertised in `/v1/capabilities` as the `run_approval` feature".
- **Inputs / options:** `Idempotency-Key` header — "(1–255 visible ASCII characters). Hermes durably reserves the key before starting work. An identical retry returns the original `run_id` with HTTP 202 and `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, including after a gateway restart and after the run has completed, failed, or been cancelled. Reusing the same key with a different JSON payload returns HTTP 409 with code `idempotency_key_conflict`. Keys are isolated by authenticated API profile/credential and retained for 24 hours after their last status update… Requests without the header retain the legacy behavior and always create a new run." (`:452`)
- **Outputs / side effects:** SSE events including `subagent.start` / `subagent.complete`.
- **Config / env:** `gateway.api_server.max_concurrent_runs`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "When `session_id` identifies an existing Hermes session and no explicit `conversation_history` or `previous_response_id` is supplied, the run loads that session's active transcript. Session turn leases serialize concurrent writers and refresh the transcript after a contended wait." (`:454`) "Statuses are retained briefly after terminal states (`completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`)." (`:470`) Subagent events (`:476-484`): "The `subagent.complete` payload carries the child's status, summary, duration, token/cost figures, and a `child_session_id` for correlation; free-text fields pass forced secret redaction before leaving the process. Per-tool child events (`subagent.tool`, progress ticks) are intentionally **not** forwarded — they are high-volume UI noise; use the per-child live transcript files for play-by-play." "Unconsumed event buffers expire after five minutes so a detached client cannot grow memory indefinitely. This expires transport state only: a run that is still executing remains visible to status polling, approval, stop control, and concurrency accounting until its executor work actually exits." (`:486`) "The run stays tracked as `stopping` until the executor-backed work exits, then settles as `cancelled`; requesting stop never hides a worker that is still running." (`:496`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Durable idempotency keys reserved *before* work starts, plus transport-state expiry that never hides live work.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Jobs API (`/api/jobs`)  `id: docs-features.api-jobs`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `api-server.md` → **"Jobs API (background scheduled work)"**.
- **What it does:** "a lightweight jobs CRUD surface for managing scheduled / background agent runs from a remote client. All endpoints are gated behind the same bearer auth." (`:506`)
- **How it works:** All eight endpoints verbatim: `GET /api/jobs` — "List all scheduled jobs."; `POST /api/jobs` — "Create a new scheduled job. Body accepts the same shape as `hermes cron` — prompt, schedule, skills, provider override, delivery target."; `GET /api/jobs/{job_id}` — "Fetch a single job's definition and last-run state."; `PATCH /api/jobs/{job_id}` — "Update fields on an existing job (prompt, schedule, etc.). Partial updates are merged."; `DELETE /api/jobs/{job_id}` — "Remove a job. Also cancels any in-flight run."; `POST /api/jobs/{job_id}/pause` — "Pause a job without deleting it. Next-scheduled-run timestamps are suspended until resumed."; `POST /api/jobs/{job_id}/resume` — "Resume a previously paused job."; `POST /api/jobs/{job_id}/run` — "Trigger the job to run immediately, out of schedule."
- **Inputs / options:** As above.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Cron job mutations.
- **Config / env:** `API_SERVER_KEY`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Deleting a job also cancels an in-flight run.
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Sessions API (`/api/sessions`)  `id: docs-features.api-sessions`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `api-server.md` → **"Sessions API (session control over REST)"**.
- **What it does:** "External UIs can manage Hermes sessions over REST without standing up the dashboard. All endpoints are gated by `API_SERVER_KEY` and live under `/api/sessions/*`." (`:542`)
- **How it works:** Complete table (`:546-556`), all 9 rows verbatim: `GET /api/sessions` — "List sessions (paginated — `limit`, `offset`, `source`, `include_children`)"; `POST /api/sessions` — "Create an empty session"; `GET /api/sessions/{id}` — "Read session metadata"; `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` — "Update title or `end_reason`"; `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}` — "Delete a session"; `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` — "Message history for a session"; `POST /api/sessions/{id}/fork` — "Branch the session via `SessionDB` lineage (matches CLI `/branch` semantics)"; `POST /api/sessions/{id}/chat` — "Run one synchronous agent turn"; `POST /api/sessions/{id}/chat/stream` — "SSE wrapper over a single turn — emits `assistant.delta`, `tool.started`, `tool.completed`, `run.completed` events".
- **Inputs / options:** Query params `limit`, `offset`, `source`, `include_children`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Session mutations.
- **Config / env:** `API_SERVER_KEY`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "`/v1/capabilities` advertises the full surface via `session_*` feature flags and `endpoints.session_*` entries so external UIs can detect support and fall back safely. Inline images are supported in `chat` and `chat/stream` payloads (multimodal-aware path)." (`:558`)
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Skills and toolsets discovery (`/v1/skills`, `/v1/toolsets`)  `id: docs-features.api-discovery`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `api-server.md` → **"Skills and toolsets discovery"**.
- **What it does:** "`GET /v1/skills` and `GET /v1/toolsets` let external clients enumerate the agent's capabilities deterministically over REST instead of asking the model. Both are read-only and gated by `API_SERVER_KEY`." (`:572`)
- **How it works:** Documented response shapes verbatim (`:577-582`): `/v1/skills` → `[{"name": "github-pr-workflow", "description": "...", "category": "..."}, ...]`; `/v1/toolsets` → `[{"name": "core", "label": "...", "description": "...", "enabled": true, "configured": true, "tools": ["read_file", "write_file", ...]}, ...]`. "`/v1/skills` returns the same metadata the skills hub uses internally. `/v1/toolsets` returns toolsets resolved for the `api_server` platform with the concrete `tools` list each one expands to. Both are advertised under `endpoints.*` in `/v1/capabilities`." (`:584`)
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** Read-only.
- **Config / env:** `API_SERVER_KEY`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** n/a
- **Rebuild notes:** Let clients enumerate capabilities over REST instead of prompting the model for them.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### `X-Hermes-Session-Key` memory scoping header  `id: docs-features.api-session-key`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `api-server.md` → **"Long-term memory scoping (`X-Hermes-Session-Key`)"**.
- **What it does:** "Multi-user frontends like Open WebUI need a stable per-channel identifier for long-term memory (Honcho, etc.) that is **independent** of the transcript-scoped `X-Hermes-Session-Id` (which rotates on `/new`)." (`:589`)
- **How it works:** "Pass `X-Hermes-Session-Key` on `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, or `/v1/runs` and Hermes threads it through to `AIAgent(gateway_session_key=...)`, where the Honcho memory provider uses it to derive a stable scope." Example verbatim: `X-Hermes-Session-Id: transcript-alpha` + `X-Hermes-Session-Key: agent:main:webui:dm:user-42`.
- **Inputs / options:** The two headers above.
- **Outputs / side effects:** "the value is echoed back on responses (JSON + SSE)".
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** "Rules: max 256 chars, control characters (`\r`, `\n`, `\x00`) are rejected… `/v1/capabilities` advertises support via `\"session_key_header\": \"X-Hermes-Session-Key\"`. Without the key, Honcho's `per-session` strategy produces a different scope per `session_id` — exactly the behavior Hermes had before." (`:599`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Separate the transcript identity from the memory identity — they have different lifetimes.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### API server system-prompt layering  `id: docs-features.api-system-prompt`

- **How it works:** "This means you can customize behavior per-frontend without losing capabilities: Open WebUI system prompt: \"You are a Python expert. Always include type hints.\" The agent still has terminal, file tools, web search, memory, etc." (`:604-606`)
- **Inputs / options:** `system` message / `instructions`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** n/a
- **Rebuild notes:** Layer, never replace, the core system prompt.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### API server authentication + multi-profile routing  `id: docs-features.api-auth`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `api-server.md` → **"Authentication"**, **"Multi-profile routing (`/p/<profile>/…`)"**.
- **What it does:** Bearer auth bound to the routed profile.
- **How it works:** "Bearer token auth via the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer ***`. Configure the key via `API_SERVER_KEY` env var." (`:608-616`) Multi-profile rules, all three verbatim (`:625-631`): "Requests to `/p/<profile>/v1/...` must present that profile's own `API_SERVER_KEY` (from `~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/.env`). The default listener's key is rejected on named-profile prefixes."; "Unprefixed routes and `/p/default/...` keep using the default profile's key."; "A named profile with no `API_SERVER_KEY` of its own fails closed — its prefix is unreachable until you set one."
- **Inputs / options:** `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; `/p/<profile>/` prefix.
- **Outputs / side effects:** 401 on mismatch.
- **Config / env:** `API_SERVER_KEY` (per profile), `gateway.multiplex_profiles`, `API_SERVER_CORS_ORIGINS`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** ":::warning Breaking change (July 2026) Before this fix, a valid default-profile key was accepted on any `/p/<profile>/` prefix. If you relied on one shared key across profile prefixes, set a distinct `API_SERVER_KEY` in each profile's `.env` — reused default keys on named prefixes now return `401`." (`:633-635`)
- **Rebuild notes:** Bind the credential to the routed tenant; fail closed when a tenant has no key of its own.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

Defaults to profile name, or `hermes-agent` for default profile." config.yaml block (`:660-670`): `gateway: {api_server: {enabled: true, port: 8642, host: 127.0.0.1, key: your-secret-key, cors_origins: http://localhost:3000, model_name: my-hermes, max_concurrent_runs: 10}}` — "concurrent-run cap; 0 disables the limit".

Environment variables take precedence over `config.yaml` values. The block is also accepted under `gateway.platforms.api_server:` or a top-level `platforms.api_server:` section." (`:672`)

### Concurrent-run cap, security headers, CORS  `id: docs-features.api-limits-cors`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `api-server.md` → **"Concurrent-run cap"**, **"Security Headers"**, **"CORS"**.
- **What it does:** Three server-level behaviors.
- **How it works:** Cap (`:676`): "The API server limits how many agent runs may execute at once across the OpenAI-compatible and Runs endpoints. The cap is read from `gateway.api_server.max_concurrent_runs` (default **10**; `0` disables the limit, negative values clamp to 0). When the cap is reached, new run-starting requests are rejected with **HTTP 429** `Too many concurrent runs (max N)` — clients should back off and retry." Security headers (`:680-682`), both verbatim: "`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` — prevents MIME type sniffing"; "`Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` — prevents referrer leakage". CORS (`:686-699`): "The API server does **not** enable browser CORS by default. For direct browser access, set an explicit allowlist: `API_SERVER_CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000,http://127.0.0.1:3000`. When CORS is enabled: **Preflight responses** include `Access-Control-Max-Age: 600` (10 minute cache); **SSE streaming responses** include CORS headers so browser EventSource clients work correctly; **`Idempotency-Key`** is an allowed request header — clients can send it for deduplication (responses are cached by key for 5 minutes). Most documented frontends such as Open WebUI connect server-to-server and do not need CORS at all."
- **Inputs / options:** `gateway.api_server.max_concurrent_runs`; `API_SERVER_CORS_ORIGINS`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** 429 responses; security headers on every response.
- **Config / env:** As above.
- **Edge cases / guards:** n/a
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

Richer clients can send explicit `provider` / `model_options` overrides on requests." Proxy mode (`:764`): "The API server also serves as the backend for **gateway proxy mode**. When another Hermes gateway instance is configured with `GATEWAY_PROXY_URL` pointing at this API server, it forwards all messages here instead of running its own agent. This enables split deployments — for example, a Docker container handling Matrix E2EE that relays to a host-side agent."

## Page: `plugins.md` — Plugins

### Plugin system overview  `id: docs-features.plugins`
- **Surface:** Plugin
- **Where:** `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/`. Docs title **"Plugins"** (`sidebar_position: 11`), description *"Extend Hermes with custom tools, hooks, and integrations via the plugin system"*.
- **What it does:** "Hermes has a plugin system for adding custom tools, hooks, and integrations without modifying core code." (`plugins.md:9`)
- **How it works:** Directory layout verbatim (`:21-26`): `~/.hermes/plugins/my-plugin/` containing `plugin.yaml` ("manifest"), `__init__.py` ("register() — wires schemas to handlers"), `schemas.py` ("tool schemas (what the LLM sees)"), `tools.py` ("tool handlers (what runs when called)"). "Start Hermes — your tools appear alongside built-in tools. The model can call them immediately." (`:28`)
- **Inputs / options:** Complete minimal example (`:32-84`): `plugin.yaml` with `name: hello-world`, `version: "1.0"`, `description: A minimal example plugin`; `__init__.py` defining `register(ctx)` that builds a `hello_world` schema, a `handle_hello(params, **kwargs)` handler, calls `ctx.register_tool(name="hello_world", toolset="hello_world", schema=schema, handler=handle_hello)`, then registers a `post_tool_call` hook printing `[hello-world] tool called: {tool_name}`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** New tools/hooks/commands in the session.
- **Config / env:** `plugins.enabled`, `plugins.disabled`, `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** "The model-facing tool description belongs in `schema[\"description\"]`. The optional `ctx.register_tool(description=...)` value is separate `ToolEntry` registry metadata: when omitted, it defaults to the schema description, but Hermes does not copy it back into a schema that lacks `description`. Prefer defining the text once in the schema." (`:86`) "Project-local plugins under `./.hermes/plugins/` are disabled by default. Enable them only for trusted repositories by setting `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=true` before starting Hermes." (`:88`)
- **Rebuild notes:** A `register(ctx)` entry point plus a capability-scoped context object. A better version would run plugins out-of-process; the docs are explicit that this one does not (see the capabilities warning).
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Plugin capability API (`ctx.*`)  `id: docs-features.plugins-ctx-api`
- **Surface:** Plugin
- **Where:** `plugins.md` → **"What plugins can do"**.
- **What it does:** "Every `ctx.*` API below is available inside a plugin's `register(ctx)` function." (`:90`)
- **How it works:** Complete capability table (`:92-110`), all 18 rows verbatim: "Add tools" — `ctx.register_tool(name=..., toolset=..., schema=..., handler=...)`; "Add hooks" — `ctx.register_hook("post_tool_call", callback)`; "Add slash commands" — "`ctx.register_command(name, handler, description)` — adds `/name` in CLI and gateway sessions"; "Dispatch tools from commands" — "`ctx.dispatch_tool(name, args)` — invokes a registered tool with parent-agent context auto-wired"; "Add CLI commands" — "`ctx.register_cli_command(name, help, setup_fn, handler_fn)` — adds `hermes <plugin> <subcommand>`"; "Inject messages" — `ctx.inject_message(content, role="user", session_key=...)`; "Ship data files" — `Path(__file__).parent / "data" / "file.yaml"`; "Bundle skills" — "`ctx.register_skill(name, path)` — namespaced as `plugin:skill`, loaded via `skill_view(\"plugin:skill\")`"; "Gate on env vars" — "`requires_env: [API_KEY]` in plugin.yaml — prompted during `hermes plugins install`"; "Distribute via pip" — `[project.entry-points."hermes_agent.plugins"]`; "Register a gateway platform (Discord, Telegram, IRC, …)" — `ctx.register_platform(name, label, adapter_factory, check_fn, ...)`; "Register an image-generation backend" — `ctx.register_image_gen_provider(provider)`; "Register a video-generation backend" — `ctx.register_video_gen_provider(provider)`; "Register a context-compression engine" — `ctx.register_context_engine(engine)`; "Register a terminal execution backend (cloud sandbox)" — `ctx.register_terminal_environment_provider(provider)`; "Route human approval prompts" — `ctx.register_approval_transport(name, present_fn)`; "Register a memory backend" — "Subclass `MemoryProvider` in `plugins/memory/<name>/__init__.py` … (uses a separate discovery system)"; "Run a host-owned LLM call" — "`ctx.llm.complete(...)` / `ctx.llm.complete_structured(...)` — borrow the user's active model + auth for a one-shot completion with optional JSON schema validation"; "Call an MCP tool (capability-gated)" — `ctx.call_mcp(server, tool, arguments, timeout=30)`; "Register an inference backend (LLM provider)" — "`register_provider(ProviderProfile(...))` in `plugins/model-providers/<name>/__init__.py` (uses a separate discovery system)". Also documented: `ctx.has_capability()`, `ctx.platform_actions`, `ctx.register_tts_provider()`, `ctx.register_transcription_provider()`.
- **Inputs / options:** As above.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Registrations in the host.
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** Memory providers and model providers use separate discovery systems.
- **Rebuild notes:** n/a
- **Verification:** implemented as documented.

### Plugin discovery sources and sub-categories  `id: docs-features.plugins-discovery`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `plugins.md` → **"Plugin discovery"**, **"Plugin sub-categories"**.
- **What it does:** Five discovery sources and six sub-category routes.
