Docs tip: for simple information retrieval, prefer `web_search` or `web_extract` — they are faster and cheaper; use browser tools when you need to **interact** with a page.
- **Rebuild notes:** Make navigation the session-creating call so every other tool can assume an initialized session, and return an automatic snapshot to save a round trip. A better version would return a diff against the previous snapshot instead of the whole tree.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — signature at `tools/browser_tool.py:4175`.

### `browser_snapshot`  `id: docs-features.browser-tool-snapshot`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** tool `browser_snapshot`
- **What it does:** Returns a text-based snapshot of the current page's accessibility tree, with interactive elements carrying ref IDs like `@e1`, `@e2` for use with `browser_click` and `browser_type`.
- **How it works:** `tools/browser_tool.py:4409` — `browser_snapshot(full: bool = False, task_id: Optional[str] = None, user_task: Optional[str] = None) -> str`. Snapshots larger than `browser.snapshot_threshold` (default 15,000 characters — the same per-page budget as `web_extract`) are **truncated at line boundaries; no LLM summarization is involved**. On truncation the complete snapshot is saved to `~/.hermes/cache/web/` and the tool output includes the file path plus a ready-to-use `read_file` call, so the agent can page through the full tree — including element refs beyond the cut — without re-snapshotting. Also carries `pending_dialogs` and `frame_tree` when a CDP supervisor is active.
- **Inputs / options:** `full=false` (default) — compact view showing only interactive elements; `full=true` — complete page content; `task_id` (session isolation); `user_task` — **deprecated, accepted for call-site compatibility, unused** (`tools/browser_tool.py:4412`, `:4420`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Snapshot text; on truncation a file under `~/.hermes/cache/web/`; `pending_dialogs: [{"id": "d-1", "type": "alert", "message": "..."}]` when a dialog blocks the page; `frame_tree` with `children[]` entries carrying `is_oopif` and a `truncated: true` flag when limits were hit.
- **Config / env:** `browser.snapshot_threshold` (default `15000`, **minimum 1000**); settable with `hermes config set browser.snapshot_threshold 30000` or YAML `browser: snapshot_threshold: 30000`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** The threshold applies both to explicit `browser_snapshot` calls and the automatic snapshot returned after navigation, **including the Camofox backend**. **Restart the current Hermes session after changing it** so the browser config cache reloads. Frame tree is capped at **30 frames and OOPIF depth 2** to bound payloads on ad-heavy pages; agents needing the full tree use `browser_cdp` with `Page.getFrameTree`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Truncate at line boundaries and always spill the full artifact to disk with a ready-made read command — never summarize with an LLM inside a deterministic tool. A better version would let the agent request a subtree by ref ID instead of paging a flat file.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — signature and deprecation note at `tools/browser_tool.py:4409-4420`; default `15000` with the "(min 1000)" comment at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:587`.

### `browser_click`  `id: docs-features.browser-tool-click`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** tool `browser_click`
- **What it does:** Clicks an element identified by its ref ID from the snapshot.
- **How it works:** `tools/browser_tool.py:4513` — `browser_click(ref: str, task_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str`. Registered at `:2810` / `:6399`.
- **Inputs / options:** `ref` (required, e.g. `@e5`); `task_id`. Docs example: `Click @e5 to press the "Sign In" button`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Page interaction; may trigger navigation or a native dialog.
- **Config / env:** `browser.command_timeout`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Ref IDs come from the most recent snapshot; a stale ref after a page mutation will not resolve.
- **Rebuild notes:** Resolve refs against the snapshot that produced them and error clearly on staleness. A better version would auto-resnapshot and retry once on a stale ref.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `tools/browser_tool.py:4513`.

### `browser_type`  `id: docs-features.browser-tool-type`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** tool `browser_type`
- **What it does:** Types text into an input field — **clears the field first**, then types the new text.
- **How it works:** `tools/browser_tool.py:4553` — `browser_type(ref: str, text: str, task_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str`. Registered at `:2824` / `:6412`.
- **Inputs / options:** `ref` (required); `text` (required); `task_id`. Docs example: `Type "hermes agent" into the search field @e3`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Field content replaced; may trigger page-side JS (autocomplete, validation).
- **Config / env:** `browser.command_timeout`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Clear-then-type means appending to an existing value requires reading it first.
- **Rebuild notes:** Make clear-first the documented default and expose an append mode. A better version would support incremental typing with configurable delay for sites that debounce input.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `tools/browser_tool.py:4553`.

### `browser_scroll`  `id: docs-features.browser-tool-scroll`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** tool `browser_scroll`
- **What it does:** Scrolls the page up or down to reveal more content.
- **How it works:** `tools/browser_tool.py:4611` — `browser_scroll(direction: str, task_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str`. Registered at `:2842` / `:6425`.
- **Inputs / options:** `direction` (required — up/down); `task_id`. Docs example: `Scroll down to see more results`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Viewport position changes; lazy-loaded content may appear in the next snapshot.
- **Config / env:** `browser.command_timeout`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Scroll amount is not parameterised in the documented interface.
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep the scroll verb coarse (direction only) and let snapshots reveal what loaded. A better version would support "scroll until element @eN is visible".
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `tools/browser_tool.py:4611`.

### `browser_press`  `id: docs-features.browser-tool-press`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** tool `browser_press`
- **What it does:** Presses a keyboard key — useful for submitting forms or navigating.
- **How it works:** `tools/browser_tool.py:4711` — `browser_press(key: str, task_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str`. Registered at `:2866` / `:6451`.
- **Inputs / options:** `key` (required); `task_id`. Docs list supported keys as `Enter`, `Tab`, `Escape`, `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp`, "and more". Docs example: `Press Enter to submit the form`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Key event dispatched to the focused element.
- **Config / env:** `browser.command_timeout`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** The key set is passed through to the driver, so validity depends on the backend's key naming.
- **Rebuild notes:** Accept CDP/Playwright key names verbatim and validate against a known list. A better version would document the complete key set and support modifier combinations (`Ctrl+A`).
- **Verification:** doc drift — the page ends the supported-key list with "and more" instead of enumerating it; code takes a free-form `key: str` (`tools/browser_tool.py:4711`) so the real set is the driver's, undocumented.

### `browser_back`  `id: docs-features.browser-tool-back`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** tool `browser_back`
- **What it does:** Navigates back to the previous page in browser history.
- **How it works:** `tools/browser_tool.py:4660` — `browser_back(task_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str`. Registered at `:2857` / `:6438`.
- **Inputs / options:** `task_id` only — no other arguments.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Session history position moves back one entry.
- **Config / env:** `browser.command_timeout`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** No forward equivalent is documented or implemented.
- **Rebuild notes:** One-argument history verbs are cheap; add forward for symmetry. A better version would expose the full history list so the agent can jump N entries.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `tools/browser_tool.py:4660`.

### `browser_get_images`  `id: docs-features.browser-tool-get-images`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** tool `browser_get_images`
- **What it does:** Lists all images on the current page with their URLs and alt text — useful for finding images to analyze.
- **How it works:** `tools/browser_tool.py:5338` — `browser_get_images(task_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str`. Registered at `:2880` / `:6465`.
- **Inputs / options:** `task_id` only.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A list of image URLs plus alt text.
- **Config / env:** `browser.command_timeout`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Returns URLs, not image bytes — downloading is out of scope (the page's "No file downloads" limitation).
- **Rebuild notes:** Return alt text alongside URLs so the model can pick without fetching. A better version would include intrinsic dimensions and above-the-fold position for relevance ranking.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `tools/browser_tool.py:5338`.

### `browser_vision`  `id: docs-features.browser-tool-vision`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** tool `browser_vision`
- **What it does:** Takes a screenshot and analyzes it with vision AI — for CAPTCHAs, complex layouts, or visual verification challenges where text snapshots miss the information.
- **How it works:** `tools/browser_tool.py:5412` — `browser_vision(question: str, annotate: bool = False, task_id: Optional[str] = None) -> Union[str, Dict[str, Any]]`. Screenshots are saved to `get_hermes_dir("cache/screenshots", "browser_screenshots")` (`:5442`, `:5501`) and the file path is returned alongside the AI analysis. Old screenshots are pruned via `_cleanup_old_screenshots(screenshots_dir, max_age_hours=24)` (`:5516-5517`, definition `:5744`). Large data URLs are resized against `_RESIZE_TARGET_BYTES` (`:5705-5706`) so full-res screenshots can't enter immutable history uncapped (`:5606`).
- **Inputs / options:** `question` (required — e.g. `What does the chart on this page show?`); `annotate` (default `false`, **undocumented on this page**); `task_id`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Screenshot file persisted under `~/.hermes/cache/screenshots/`, AI analysis text, and the file path. On messaging platforms (Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp) the user can ask the agent to share the screenshot and it is sent as a native photo attachment via the `MEDIA:` mechanism.
- **Config / env:** vision model configuration (see the `vision.md` entries); `browser.command_timeout`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Screenshots are **automatically cleaned up after 24 hours**. Under the Lightpanda engine there is no graphical renderer, so vision capture is pre-routed to Chrome with the reason string "Lightpanda has no graphical renderer for screenshots; used Chrome for vision capture." (`tools/browser_tool.py:5477-5537`).
- **Rebuild notes:** Persist the screenshot and return its path next to the analysis so downstream tools can reuse it; cap the inline payload so history stays bounded. A better version would cache the analysis keyed on (screenshot hash, question) to avoid re-billing identical asks.
- **Verification:** partial — implemented as documented, but the `annotate: bool = False` argument (`tools/browser_tool.py:5412`) is not documented on this page (doc gap).

### `browser_console` (console read + JS evaluation)  `id: docs-features.browser-tool-console`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** tool `browser_console`
- **What it does:** Returns browser console output (log/warn/error messages) and uncaught JavaScript exceptions from the current page — essential for detecting silent JS errors that don't appear in the accessibility tree — and, with an `expression` argument, evaluates JavaScript like the DevTools console.
- **How it works:** `tools/browser_tool.py:4763` — `browser_console(clear: bool = False, expression: Optional[str] = None, task_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str`. Registered at `:2908` / `:6491`. Results come back parsed: JSON-serialized objects become dicts, primitive values stay primitive. When a CDP supervisor is active for the current session (typical for any session that has run `browser_navigate` against a CDP-capable backend), evaluation runs over the supervisor's persistent WebSocket — no subprocess startup cost; otherwise it falls through to the standard agent-browser CLI path. **Behaviour is identical either way; only latency changes.**
- **Inputs / options:** `clear=True` — clear the console after reading so subsequent calls only show new messages (default `False`); `expression="..."` — JavaScript to evaluate (examples: `browser_console(expression="document.querySelector('h1').textContent")`, `browser_console(expression="JSON.stringify(performance.timing)")`); `task_id`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Console message list and/or the parsed evaluation result; with `clear=True` the console buffer is emptied.
- **Config / env:** `browser.restrict_evaluate` (default `false`); `browser.allow_unsafe_evaluate` (default `false`, legacy override — **undocumented on this page**).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Evaluation is unrestricted by default** — the agent can use `fetch`, read storage, query form values, and run any DOM extraction. Requests targeting private/internal addresses are still blocked on non-local backends (the SSRF guard is independent of this setting). To opt into a strict denylist over sensitive JS primitives (cookies, storage, clipboard, network calls, form values) set `browser.restrict_evaluate: true` — **note the denylist matches primitive *names***, so it also blocks legitimate expressions that merely contain words like `fetch` or `cookie`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Separate "read console" from "evaluate" behind one tool only if the return shapes stay distinguishable; keep the SSRF guard independent of the evaluation policy. A better version would sandbox evaluation with a real capability policy (proxying `document.cookie` through an approval prompt) rather than name-matching a denylist.
- **Verification:** partial — implemented as documented; `browser.allow_unsafe_evaluate` ("Legacy override: when true, browser_console(expression=...) bypasses the restrict_evaluate denylist entirely", `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:640`) exists in code but is **not** documented on this page (doc gap).

### `browser_cdp` — raw Chrome DevTools Protocol passthrough  `id: docs-features.browser-tool-cdp`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** tool `browser_cdp`
- **What it does:** Raw CDP passthrough — the escape hatch for browser operations not covered by the other tools: native dialog handling, iframe-scoped evaluation, cookie/network control, or any CDP verb the agent needs.
- **How it works:** `tools/browser_cdp_tool.py:463` — `browser_cdp(method: str, params: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, target_id: Optional[str] = None, frame_id: Optional[str] = None, timeout: float = 30.0, task_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str`. Browser-level methods (`Target.*`, `Browser.*`, `Storage.*`) omit `target_id`; page-level methods (`Page.*`, `Runtime.*`, `DOM.*`, `Emulation.*`) require a `target_id` from `Target.getTargets`. **Each stateless call is independent — sessions do not persist between calls.** Passing `frame_id` (from `browser_snapshot.frame_tree.children[]` where `is_oopif=true`) routes the call through the supervisor's live session for that iframe, which is how `Runtime.evaluate` inside a cross-origin iframe works on Browserbase where stateless CDP connections would hit signed-URL expiry.
- **Inputs / options:** `method` (required, e.g. `"Target.getTargets"`); `params` (defaults to `{}`); `target_id`; `frame_id`; `timeout` (default `30.0`); `task_id`. Documented patterns: `browser_cdp(method="Target.getTargets")`; `browser_cdp(method="Page.handleJavaScriptDialog", params={"accept": true, "promptText": ""}, target_id="<tabId>")`; `browser_cdp(method="Runtime.evaluate", params={"expression": "document.title", "returnByValue": true}, target_id="<tabId>")`; `browser_cdp(method="Network.getAllCookies")`; `browser_cdp(method="Runtime.evaluate", params={"expression": "document.title", "returnByValue": True}, frame_id="<frame_id from browser_snapshot>")`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** The raw CDP response. Any state change the CDP verb performs (cookies set, network conditions changed, dialogs handled).
- **Config / env:** `browser.cdp_url`; `/browser connect`. Method reference: `https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/` (`CDP_DOCS_URL` in `tools/browser_cdp_tool.py`) — the agent can `web_extract` a specific method's page to look up parameters and return shape.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Only available when a CDP endpoint is reachable at session start** — i.e. `/browser connect` has attached to a running Chrome, Brave, Chromium or Edge, or `browser.cdp_url` is set in `config.yaml`. The default local agent-browser mode, Camofox, and cloud providers (Browserbase, Browser Use, Firecrawl) do **not** currently expose CDP to this tool — cloud providers have per-session CDP URLs but live-session routing is a follow-up. Same-origin iframes don't need `frame_id` — use `document.querySelector('iframe').contentDocument` from a top-level `Runtime.evaluate`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep the passthrough stateless and point the model at the upstream protocol docs instead of duplicating the method catalogue. A better version would route cloud providers' per-session CDP URLs so the escape hatch works on every backend.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — signature at `tools/browser_cdp_tool.py:463-470`.

### `browser_dialog` — native JS dialog handling  `id: docs-features.browser-tool-dialog`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** tool `browser_dialog`
- **What it does:** Responds to a native JS dialog (`alert` / `confirm` / `prompt` / `beforeunload`). Before it existed, dialogs silently blocked the page's JavaScript thread and subsequent `browser_*` calls hung or threw.
- **How it works:** `tools/browser_dialog_tool.py:82` — `browser_dialog(action: str, prompt_text: Optional[str] = None, dialog_id: Optional[str] = None, task_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str`, resolving the supervisor via `SUPERVISOR_REGISTRY.get(effective_task_id)` where `effective_task_id = task_id or "default"` (`:89-91`). Detection happens automatically via a **persistent CDP supervisor** — one WebSocket per task subscribing to Page/Runtime/Target events (`tools/browser_supervisor.py`) — which also populates `frame_tree` in the snapshot. Documented workflow: (1) call `browser_snapshot`; a blocking dialog appears as `pending_dialogs: [{"id": "d-1", "type": "alert", "message": "..."}]`; (2) call `browser_dialog(action="accept")` or `browser_dialog(action="dismiss")`, passing `prompt_text="..."` for `prompt()` dialogs; (3) re-snapshot — `pending_dialogs` is empty and the page's JS thread has resumed.
- **Inputs / options:** `action` (required — `accept` | `dismiss`); `prompt_text` (response for `prompt()` dialogs); `dialog_id`; `task_id`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** The blocked page JS thread resumes; the dialog leaves `pending_dialogs`; the dialog remains visible in `browser_state` history under `auto_dismiss`.
- **Config / env:** `browser.dialog_policy` — `must_respond` (default) | `auto_dismiss` | `auto_accept` (`hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:646`); `browser.dialog_timeout_s` (default `300`, `:647`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Availability matrix** — Local Chrome via `/browser connect` or `browser.cdp_url`: detection ✓, response ✓ full workflow. Browserbase: detection ✓, response ✓ full workflow (via injected XHR bridge). Camofox / default local agent-browser: detection ✗, response ✗ (no CDP endpoint). **On Browserbase**, its CDP proxy auto-dismisses real native dialogs server-side within ~10ms, so `Page.handleJavaScriptDialog` can't be used: the supervisor injects a script via `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` overriding `window.alert`/`confirm`/`prompt` with a synchronous XHR, intercepts those XHRs via `Fetch.enable`, and keeps the page's JS thread blocked on the XHR until `Fetch.fulfillRequest` returns the agent's response; `prompt()` return values round-trip back into page JS unchanged. Under `must_respond` a **safety auto-dismiss fires after `browser.dialog_timeout_s` (default 300s)** so a buggy agent can't stall forever. `auto_accept` is useful for pages with aggressive `beforeunload` prompts.
- **Rebuild notes:** Detect dialogs out-of-band with a persistent event subscription and surface them inside the snapshot the agent already reads; always add a stall-breaking timeout. A better version would make the XHR bridge unnecessary by negotiating dialog control with the cloud provider's proxy.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — signature and supervisor lookup at `tools/browser_dialog_tool.py:82-95`; policy/timeout defaults at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:643-647` ("CDP supervisor — dialog + frame detection via a persistent WebSocket. Active only when a CDP-capable backend is attached (Browserbase or local Chrome via /browser connect)").

### Frame tree in snapshots (OOPIF visibility)  `id: docs-features.browser-frame-tree`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `browser_snapshot.frame_tree`
- **What it does:** Exposes the iframe structure of the current page, including cross-origin (OOPIF) iframes, so the agent can target frame-scoped CDP calls.
- **How it works:** Populated by the same persistent CDP supervisor that detects dialogs (`tools/browser_supervisor.py`). Entries under `frame_tree.children[]` carry `is_oopif`; the `frame_id` of an OOPIF is passed to `browser_cdp` to route through the supervisor's live session for that iframe.
- **Inputs / options:** Read-only field in the snapshot; consumed via `browser_cdp(frame_id=...)`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Adds a `frame_tree` object (and `truncated: true` when capped) to snapshot output.
- **Config / env:** governed by the CDP supervisor's availability (`browser.cdp_url` / `/browser connect` / Browserbase).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Capped to 30 frames and OOPIF depth 2** to keep payloads bounded on ad-heavy pages; a `truncated: true` flag surfaces when limits were hit, and agents needing the full tree use `browser_cdp` with `Page.getFrameTree`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Bound every auto-included structure and always signal truncation with a flag plus an escape hatch. A better version would prioritise frames by viewport area so the 30 kept are the 30 that matter.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — supervisor implementation in `tools/browser_supervisor.py`; behaviour described in the config comment at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:643-645`.

### Session recording (WebM)  `id: docs-features.browser-session-recording`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `browser.record_sessions` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`
- **What it does:** Automatically records browser sessions as WebM video files.
- **How it works:** Recording starts automatically on the first `browser_navigate` and saves to `~/.hermes/browser_recordings/` when the session closes (`tools/browser_tool.py:5303`, `:5772`). Files are named `session_*.webm`. Works in both local and cloud (Browserbase) modes.
- **Inputs / options:** `browser.record_sessions: true` (default `false`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** `.webm` files under `~/.hermes/browser_recordings/`.
- **Config / env:** `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:588`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Recordings older than **72 hours** are automatically cleaned up — `_cleanup_old_recordings(max_age_hours=72)` at `tools/browser_tool.py:5768-5783`, globbing `session_*.webm`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Start recording at session creation, flush at close, and prune on a fixed age so disk use is bounded without a daemon. A better version would index recordings by task id and surface them in the dashboard next to the transcript.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — default `False` at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:588`; 72-hour pruning at `tools/browser_tool.py:5768`.

### Headed mode (visible browser window)  `id: docs-features.browser-headed-mode`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `browser.headed` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`; env `AGENT_BROWSER_HEADED=1`
- **What it does:** Gives a visible Chromium window you can watch and interact with, instead of the default headless local browser.
- **How it works:** Two effects: (1) launches Chromium with a visible window (passes `--headed` to agent-browser in local mode); (2) **keeps the window open between turns** — normally the browser session is cleaned up after every agent reply, but in headed mode the per-turn cleanup is skipped so you can watch the agent work, intervene manually (sign-in challenges, CAPTCHAs), and keep login state warm across the conversation.
- **Inputs / options:** `browser.headed: true|false` (default `false`); env `AGENT_BROWSER_HEADED=1`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A visible browser window persisting across turns.
- **Config / env:** `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:589`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Idle sessions are **still reaped after `browser.inactivity_timeout` (default 120s of no browser activity)**, and all sessions are closed on shutdown. Headed mode **only affects the local browser** — cloud sessions (Browserbase) are unaffected. On a display-less host it always runs headless regardless (see real-profile browsing).
- **Rebuild notes:** Tie window persistence to the same flag as visibility, but keep the idle reaper unconditional so an abandoned window still dies. A better version would auto-detect a display and warn when `headed` is set on a headless host.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — default `False` with the "also skips per-turn cleanup so the window persists between turns; idle reaper still applies" comment at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:589`.

### Stealth features (Browserbase)  `id: docs-features.browser-stealth`
- **Surface:** Provider
- **Where:** browser.md → "Stealth Features" table; Browserbase env vars
- **What it does:** Documents the anti-bot capabilities Browserbase provides automatically and which of them Hermes toggles.
- **How it works:** Four documented rows. **Basic Stealth** — always on: random fingerprints, viewport randomization, CAPTCHA solving. **Residential Proxies** — default on: routes through residential IPs for better access (`BROWSERBASE_PROXIES`, default `"true"`). **Advanced Stealth** — default off: custom Chromium build, requires Scale Plan (`BROWSERBASE_ADVANCED_STEALTH`, default `"false"`). **Keep Alive** — default on: session reconnection after network hiccups (`BROWSERBASE_KEEP_ALIVE`, default `"true"`, requires paid plan).
- **Inputs / options:** `BROWSERBASE_PROXIES`, `BROWSERBASE_ADVANCED_STEALTH`, `BROWSERBASE_KEEP_ALIVE`, `BROWSERBASE_SESSION_TIMEOUT`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Session creation parameters sent to Browserbase.
- **Config / env:** env vars listed above.
- **Edge cases / guards:** If paid features aren't available on the plan, Hermes automatically falls back — **first disabling `keepAlive`, then proxies** — so browsing still works on free plans.
- **Rebuild notes:** Express each stealth capability as an independently droppable session flag with a defined drop order. A better version would query plan entitlements once per process instead of learning them from failures.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — provider-specific; behaviour described in the page's stealth note and Browserbase session construction in `tools/browser_tool.py`.

### Session management & cleanup  `id: docs-features.browser-session-management`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** automatic; `browser.inactivity_timeout`, env `BROWSER_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT`
- **What it does:** Isolates one browser session per task and cleans up inactive/orphaned sessions so cloud credits and local processes don't leak.
- **How it works:** Documented behaviour: each task gets an isolated browser session; sessions are automatically cleaned up after inactivity (default 2 minutes); a background thread checks **every 30 seconds** for stale sessions; emergency cleanup runs on process exit to prevent orphaned sessions; Browserbase sessions are released via the API with `REQUEST_RELEASE` status. `cleanup_browser(task_id)` at `tools/browser_tool.py:5790` reaps both the cloud/primary session and any hybrid-routing local sidecar when given a bare task id; a `::local` suffix targets only the sidecar.
- **Inputs / options:** `browser.inactivity_timeout` (default `120` seconds — `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:585`); env `BROWSER_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT=120`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Sessions closed; Browserbase sessions released; Lightpanda `lightpanda serve` processes reaped; local Chromium processes terminated.
- **Config / env:** `browser.inactivity_timeout`, `browser.command_timeout`, env `BROWSER_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Headed mode skips per-turn cleanup but not the idle reaper. Orphan sweep also reaps Lightpanda processes if Hermes crashes.
- **Rebuild notes:** Key sessions by task id with a suffix convention for auxiliary sessions, and always pair an idle reaper with an atexit sweep. A better version would persist a session registry to disk so a crashed process's cloud sessions are released on the next start.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `cleanup_browser` reaping both primary and `::local` sidecar at `tools/browser_tool.py:5790-5805`; `inactivity_timeout: 120` at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:585`. The documented "every 30 seconds" sweeper interval was not located in `tools/browser_tool.py` by grep (`time.sleep(0.25)` at `:1844`, `time.sleep(1)` at `:2738` are the only sleeps) — unverified.

### Documented practical examples (form filling, dynamic content)  `id: docs-features.browser-examples`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** browser.md → "Practical Examples"
- **What it does:** Shows two end-to-end agent workflows so a model can copy the tool-call sequence.
- **How it works:** **Filling out a web form** — user asks to sign up on example.com with an email; agent runs `browser_navigate("https://example.com/signup")` → `browser_snapshot()` (sees form fields with refs) → `browser_type(ref="@e3", text="john@example.com")` → `browser_type(ref="@e5", text="SecurePass123")` → `browser_click(ref="@e8")` (clicks "Create Account") → `browser_snapshot()` (confirms success). **Researching dynamic content** — user asks for top trending GitHub repos; agent runs `browser_navigate("https://github.com/trending")` → `browser_snapshot(full=true)` (reads trending repo list) → returns formatted results.
- **Inputs / options:** n/a (illustrative)
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** Both examples rely on refs obtained from the immediately preceding snapshot.
- **Rebuild notes:** Ship canonical navigate→snapshot→act→snapshot loops in the tool descriptions themselves so the model doesn't have to infer the protocol. A better version would encode the loop as a built-in skill.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — the tool call shapes match the real signatures (`tools/browser_tool.py:4175`, `:4409`, `:4513`, `:4553`).

### Browser extension controller lane (undocumented)  `id: docs-features.browser-extension-control`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `browser.extension_control.enabled` / `browser.extension_control.developer_mode` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`
- **What it does:** Lets a browser extension that registers through the gateway become the exact controller for a session's `browser_*` tools.
- **How it works:** Implemented in `tools/browser_extension_router.py`; config subtree at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:667-679`. Once bound, the lane is **fail-closed**. Local API registration additionally requires the API server bearer key. `developer_mode` gates the privileged capabilities (`browser_cdp` / `browser_evaluate`) and is described as "never negotiable without it".
- **Inputs / options:** `browser.extension_control.enabled: true|false` (default `false`); `browser.extension_control.developer_mode: true|false` (default `false`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Browser tool calls routed to the registered extension instead of a local/cloud browser.
- **Config / env:** `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:667-679`; API server bearer key for local registration.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Fail-closed once bound; privileged CDP/evaluate capabilities require `developer_mode`; registration is authenticated.
- **Rebuild notes:** Bind the controller exactly once per session and fail closed rather than falling back to a different browser silently; gate privileged verbs behind a separate developer flag. A better version would document the extension protocol and ship a reference extension.
- **Verification:** **documented gap** — the feature exists in code (`tools/browser_extension_router.py`, config at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:667-679`) but browser.md never mentions `browser.extension_control` at all.
