## Page: `extending-the-dashboard.md` — Extending the Dashboard

### Dashboard extension model (three layers)  `id: docs-features.dash-ext-overview`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** `hermes dashboard`; `~/.hermes/dashboard-themes/`, `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/dashboard/`
- **What it does:** Exposes three drop-in layers so the web dashboard can be reskinned and extended without forking: **Themes** (YAML repainting palette/typography/layout/per-component chrome), **UI plugins** (a directory with `manifest.json` + a JS bundle registering a tab, replacing a built-in page, augmenting one via page-scoped slots, or injecting into named shell slots), and **Backend plugins** (a Python file exposing a FastAPI `router` mounted under `/api/plugins/<name>/`).
- **How it works:** All three are drop-in at runtime — **no repo clone, no `npm run build`, no patching the dashboard source**. Themes are read server-side from `~/.hermes/dashboard-themes/` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:18269-18294`); plugins are discovered by `_discover_dashboard_plugins()` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:18434`) and loaded in the browser by `web/src/plugins/usePlugins.ts`; the SDK is exposed by `exposePluginSDK()` in `web/src/plugins/registry.ts:112`.
- **Inputs / options:** Layer 1 — a `.yaml`/`.yml` file in `~/.hermes/dashboard-themes/`. Layer 2 — `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/dashboard/manifest.json` + `dashboard/dist/index.js`. Layer 3 — `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/dashboard/plugin_api.py`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** New themes in the theme switcher, new tabs/slots in the dashboard shell, new API routes under `/api/plugins/<name>/`.
- **Config / env:** `dashboard.theme` (`hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1676`), `dashboard.font`, `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Not the desktop app** — this covers the web dashboard's system (`window.__HERMES_PLUGIN_SDK__`, `manifest.json`, a pre-built JS bundle). The native desktop app (`hermes desktop`) has its own unrelated SDK (`@hermes/plugin-sdk`, a single ESM file, no build step) at `/developer-guide/desktop-plugin-sdk`; **only the backend `plugin_api.py` namespace (`/api/plugins/<name>`) is shared between them**. The CLI skin system (`./skins`) is unrelated to dashboard themes.
- **Rebuild notes:** Split extension into declarative (theme YAML), presentational (UI bundle over a host-provided SDK), and server (mounted router) layers, each independently optional. A better version would version the manifest schema and refuse to load bundles built against an incompatible SDK contract.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — the three layers exist; SDK contract is versioned as `SDK_CONTRACT_VERSION = "1.1.0"` at `web/src/plugins/registry.ts:106` and exposed as `sdkVersion` (`:121`), which the docs never mention (doc gap).

### Dashboard theme files (`~/.hermes/dashboard-themes/`)  `id: docs-features.dash-theme-files`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** `~/.hermes/dashboard-themes/<name>.yaml`; theme switcher = the **palette icon** in the dashboard header
- **What it does:** Lets a YAML file repaint the dashboard; the file appears in the theme switcher after a refresh.
- **How it works:** `_scan_user_themes()` scans `get_process_hermes_home() / "dashboard-themes"` for `*.yaml` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:18269-18294`). The file name doesn't matter — the theme's `name:` field is what the system uses; convention is `<name>.yaml`. **Every field is optional** — missing keys fall back to the built-in `default` theme, so a theme can be as small as one color. Selection persists to `config.yaml` under `dashboard.theme` and is restored on reload.
- **Inputs / options:** Top-level YAML keys: `name`, `label`, `description`, `palette`, `typography`, `layout`, `layoutVariant`, `assets`, `componentStyles`, `colorOverrides`, `customCSS`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** New entry in the theme picker; on apply, CSS vars are set on `:root` and a `<style data-hermes-theme-css>` tag is injected.
- **Config / env:** `dashboard.theme` (`hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1676`, default `"default"`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** File must end in `.yaml` or `.yml` and live in `~/.hermes/dashboard-themes/`. On a YAML parse error the dashboard logs to `errors.log` under `~/.hermes/logs/`. Verify with `curl http://127.0.0.1:9119/api/dashboard/themes`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Make every theme field optional with a cascade to the default so the minimum viable theme is two colors. A better version would hot-reload theme files with a filesystem watcher instead of requiring a page refresh.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — scan path and the built-in fallback at `hermes_cli/web_server.py:18269-18294`; persistence via `PUT /api/dashboard/theme` at `:18328`.

### Theme quick start (two-color theme)  `id: docs-features.dash-theme-quickstart`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** `~/.hermes/dashboard-themes/neon.yaml`
- **What it does:** Shows the smallest working theme — a name, a label, a description, and two palette colors.
- **How it works:** Documented onboarding: `mkdir -p ~/.hermes/dashboard-themes`, then a file with `name: neon`, `label: Neon`, `description: Pure magenta on black`, `palette.background: "#000000"`, `palette.midground: "#ff00ff"`. Refresh the dashboard, click the palette icon in the header, pick **Neon**. Every derived color (card, border, muted, ring, etc.) is recomputed from that 2-color triplet via `color-mix()` in CSS.
- **Inputs / options:** `name`, `label`, `description`, `palette.background`, `palette.midground`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Black background, magenta text and accents; the whole shadcn token set recomputed.
- **Config / env:** `dashboard.theme`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Requires a page refresh before the theme appears in the picker.
- **Rebuild notes:** Derive the full token set from a small palette via `color-mix()` so authors never enumerate tokens. A better version would preview the derived palette live while editing.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — theme normalisation and derivation live in `web/src/themes/context.tsx` and `web/src/themes/types.ts`.

### Theme `palette` (3-layer)  `id: docs-features.dash-theme-palette`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** theme YAML → `palette:`
- **What it does:** Sets a triplet of color layers plus a warm-glow vignette color and a noise-grain multiplier, from which the whole shadcn-compatible token set is derived.
- **How it works:** The design-system cascade derives every token (card, popover, muted, border, primary, destructive, ring, etc.) from the triplet via CSS `color-mix()`. Overriding three colors cascades into the whole UI.
- **Inputs / options:** `palette.background` — deepest canvas color, typically near-black; drives the page background and card fill. `palette.midground` — primary text and accent; most UI chrome reads this (foreground text, button outlines, focus rings). `palette.foreground` — top-layer highlight; the default theme sets this to white at alpha 0 (invisible), themes wanting a bright top accent raise its alpha. `palette.warmGlow` — an `rgba(...)` string used as the vignette color by `<Backdrop />`. `palette.noiseOpacity` — a 0–1.2 multiplier on the grain overlay (lower = softer, higher = grittier). Each layer accepts either `{hex: "#RRGGBB", alpha: 0.0–1.0}` or a bare hex string (alpha defaults to 1.0).
- **Outputs / side effects:** CSS custom properties on `:root` driving the entire palette.
- **Config / env:** theme YAML only.
- **Edge cases / guards:** `noiseOpacity` range is 0–1.2 (not 0–1). A bare hex string implies alpha 1.0.
- **Rebuild notes:** Three layers + a glow + a grain multiplier is enough to express a complete look; derive everything else. A better version would validate contrast ratios and warn when derived text fails WCAG.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — theme type definitions at `web/src/themes/types.ts`; `<Backdrop />` consumes `warmGlow`/grain per `types.ts:84`.

### Theme `typography`  `id: docs-features.dash-theme-typography`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** theme YAML → `typography:`
- **What it does:** Sets the dashboard's font stacks, external font stylesheet, and the base rem scale/line-height/letter-spacing.
- **How it works:** `fontUrl` is injected as `<link rel="stylesheet">` in `<head>` on theme switch; the **same URL is never injected twice**. Works with Google Fonts, Bunny Fonts, self-hosted `@font-face` sheets — anything linkable.
- **Inputs / options:** `fontSans` (string, CSS font-family stack for body copy, applied to `html`, `body`); `fontMono` (string, stack for code blocks, `<code>`, `.font-mono` utilities); `fontDisplay` (string, optional heading/display stack, falls back to `fontSans`); `fontUrl` (string, optional external stylesheet URL); `baseSize` (string root font size controlling the rem scale, e.g. `"14px"`, `"16px"`); `lineHeight` (string, e.g. `"1.5"`, `"1.65"`); `letterSpacing` (string, e.g. `"0"`, `"0.01em"`, `"-0.01em"`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Font CSS vars applied; at most one `<link>` per unique URL.
- **Config / env:** theme YAML only (the UI font override is separate — see `dash-theme-font-picker`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** `fontDisplay` falls back to `fontSans` when absent.
- **Rebuild notes:** Dedupe injected stylesheet links by URL and keep display/sans/mono independent. A better version would preload the font files and expose a FOUT-free swap strategy.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — typography fields in `web/src/themes/types.ts`; injection logic in `web/src/themes/context.tsx`.

### Dashboard font picker (UI override)  `id: docs-features.dash-theme-font-picker`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** theme picker in the dashboard header → **Font** section below the theme list; option **Theme default**
- **What it does:** Overrides the body font of whatever theme is active, independently of the theme, persisting across theme switches.
- **How it works:** The choice is stored in `config.yaml` under `dashboard.font` and served/persisted by `GET /api/dashboard/font` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:18357`) and `PUT /api/dashboard/font` (`:18370`, writing `config["dashboard"]["font"]` at `:18386`, defaulting to `_FONT_DEFAULT_ID` at `:18362`). The catalog lives in `web/src/themes/fonts.ts`.
- **Inputs / options:** A curated catalog (system stacks plus a set of Google-Fonts families across sans / serif / mono) — 17 catalog entries in `web/src/themes/fonts.ts`; plus **Theme default** to clear the override and fall back to the active theme's own `fontSans`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** `dashboard.font` written to `config.yaml`; body font changes immediately.
- **Config / env:** `dashboard.font`; endpoints `GET`/`PUT /api/dashboard/font`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** It deliberately does **not** accept a free-text font URL — the font's stylesheet is injected as a `<link>`, so the catalog keeps the injected origins fixed. For a fully custom face, set `fontSans` + `fontUrl` in a theme YAML. The theme's `fontMono` (code blocks, terminal) is **always left untouched** by the UI override.
- **Rebuild notes:** Fix the set of injectable font origins to a curated catalog so the UI can't be used to pull arbitrary third-party stylesheets. A better version would allow self-hosted uploads through the assets store instead of a URL field.
- **Verification:** partial — implemented as documented, but the two `/api/dashboard/font` endpoints (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:18357`, `:18370`) are **absent from this page's API reference tables** (doc gap).

### Theme `layout` (radius + density)  `id: docs-features.dash-theme-layout`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** theme YAML → `layout:`
- **What it does:** Sets the corner-radius token and the global spacing multiplier.
- **How it works:** `radius` maps to `--radius` and cascades into `--radius-sm/md/lg/xl`, so every rounded element shifts together. `density` is applied as the `--spacing-mul` CSS var and scales Tailwind's base spacing, so padding, gap and space-between utilities all shift proportionally.
- **Inputs / options:** `radius` — any CSS length (`"0"`, `"0.25rem"`, `"0.5rem"`, `"1rem"`, …). `density` — `compact` (0.85×) | `comfortable` (1.0×, default) | `spacious` (1.2×).
- **Outputs / side effects:** `--radius*` and `--spacing-mul` CSS vars set on `:root`.
- **Config / env:** theme YAML only.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Only the three named density values are supported.
- **Rebuild notes:** Express density as a single multiplier var consumed by the utility layer, not by rewriting per-component spacing. A better version would expose separate vertical/horizontal multipliers for dense data tables.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — layout fields in `web/src/themes/types.ts`.

### Theme `layoutVariant` (standard / cockpit / tiled)  `id: docs-features.dash-theme-layout-variant`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** theme YAML → `layoutVariant:`
- **What it does:** Picks the overall shell layout.
- **How it works:** `standard` — single column, 1600px max-width (default). `cockpit` — left sidebar rail (260px) + main content, populated by plugins via the `sidebar` slot; without a plugin the rail shows a placeholder. `tiled` — drops the max-width clamp so pages can use the full viewport width. The current variant is exposed as `document.documentElement.dataset.layoutVariant`, so raw CSS in `customCSS` can target it via `:root[data-layout-variant="cockpit"] …`.
- **Inputs / options:** `layoutVariant: standard | cockpit | tiled` (defaults to `"standard"` when absent).
- **Outputs / side effects:** `data-layout-variant` attribute on `<html>`; different shell structure.
- **Config / env:** theme YAML only.
- **Edge cases / guards:** The `sidebar` slot is **only rendered when `layoutVariant === "cockpit"`** — a plugin registering into it is silently invisible under other variants.
- **Rebuild notes:** Expose the variant as a data attribute so CSS and plugins can both branch on it. A better version would let a plugin declare a required variant so the UI can warn instead of silently not rendering.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `export type ThemeLayoutVariant = "standard" | "cockpit" | "tiled";` at `web/src/themes/types.ts:77`, with the "Defaults to `\"standard\"` when absent" comment at `:163`.

### Theme `assets` (images as CSS vars)  `id: docs-features.dash-theme-assets`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** theme YAML → `assets:`
- **What it does:** Ships artwork URLs with a theme; each named slot becomes a CSS var (`--theme-asset-<name>`) the built-in shell and any plugin can read.
- **How it works:** The `bg` slot is automatically wired into the backdrop (`<Backdrop />`); other slots are plugin-facing. Every asset is also emitted as `--theme-asset-<name>-raw` (the unwrapped URL) in case a plugin needs to pass it to `<img src>` instead of `background-image`. Plugins read them with plain CSS or JS: `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue("--theme-asset-hero").trim()`.
- **Inputs / options:** Documented slots: `bg` (auto-wired into `<Backdrop />`), `hero` (for plugin sidebars), `crest` (for header-left plugins), `logo`, `sidebar`, `header`, and a nested `custom:` map whose keys become `--theme-asset-custom-<key>` (example `scanLines` → `--theme-asset-custom-scanLines`). Value forms: bare URLs (wrapped in `url(...)` automatically); pre-wrapped `url(...)`, `linear-gradient(...)`, `radial-gradient(...)` expressions (used as-is); `"none"` (explicit opt-out).
- **Outputs / side effects:** `--theme-asset-*` and `--theme-asset-*-raw` CSS vars on `:root`.
- **Config / env:** theme YAML only.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Only `bg` has built-in wiring; the rest do nothing unless a plugin reads them.
- **Rebuild notes:** Emit both wrapped and raw forms of every asset so consumers can choose between `background-image` and `<img>`. A better version would validate/pin asset origins the way the font catalog does.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — asset handling in `web/src/themes/context.tsx`; `types.ts:84` references the `backdrop` plugin slot / theme `customCSS` pairing.

### Theme `componentStyles` (component chrome overrides)  `id: docs-features.dash-theme-component-styles`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** theme YAML → `componentStyles:`
- **What it does:** Restyles individual shell components without writing CSS selectors.
- **How it works:** Each bucket's entries become CSS vars named `--component-<bucket>-<kebab-property>` that the shell's shared components read. So `card:` overrides apply to every `<Card>`, `header:` to the app bar, etc. Property names use camelCase (`clipPath`) and are emitted as kebab (`clip-path`).
- **Inputs / options:** Nine supported buckets: `card`, `header`, `footer`, `sidebar`, `tab`, `progress`, `badge`, `backdrop`, `page`. Values are plain CSS strings — anything CSS accepts (`clip-path`, `border-image`, `background`, `box-shadow`, `animation`, …). Documented examples: `card.clipPath` (notched polygon), `card.background` (linear-gradient), `card.boxShadow` (inset ring), `header.background`, `tab.clipPath`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** `--component-*` CSS vars on `:root`, consumed by the shared components.
- **Config / env:** theme YAML only.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Only these nine buckets exist; a bucket the shell doesn't read has no effect. Empty buckets (`sidebar: {}`) are valid no-ops.
- **Rebuild notes:** Have shared components read a fixed set of per-bucket CSS vars so themes never need selectors. A better version would publish the var names per component in a machine-readable schema.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `componentStyles` handling in `web/src/themes/context.tsx` / `types.ts`.

### Theme `colorOverrides`  `id: docs-features.dash-theme-color-overrides`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** theme YAML → `colorOverrides:`
- **What it does:** Pins specific shadcn tokens the 3-layer palette derivation won't produce (a softer destructive red for a pastel theme, a specific brand success green).
- **How it works:** Each key maps 1:1 to the `--color-<kebab>` CSS var (e.g. `primaryForeground` → `--color-primary-foreground`). Any key set here wins over the palette cascade **for the active theme only** — switching to another theme clears the overrides.
- **Inputs / options:** 19 supported keys: `card`, `cardForeground`, `popover`, `popoverForeground`, `primary`, `primaryForeground`, `secondary`, `secondaryForeground`, `muted`, `mutedForeground`, `accent`, `accentForeground`, `destructive`, `destructiveForeground`, `success`, `warning`, `border`, `input`, `ring`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** `--color-*` CSS vars overridden for the active theme.
- **Config / env:** theme YAML only.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Overrides are scoped to the active theme and cleared on theme switch — **by design**. To persist them, put them in the theme's YAML rather than the live switcher.
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep the derivation authoritative and treat overrides as a per-theme patch layer that resets on switch. A better version would let a theme mark specific tokens as "locked" so derivation never touches them.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `colorOverrides` in `web/src/themes/types.ts`; applied in `web/src/themes/context.tsx`.

### Theme `customCSS` (raw CSS escape hatch)  `id: docs-features.dash-theme-custom-css`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** theme YAML → `customCSS: |`
- **What it does:** Injects raw CSS for selector-level chrome that `componentStyles` can't express — pseudo-elements, animations, media queries, theme-scoped overrides.
- **How it works:** The CSS is injected as a single scoped `<style data-hermes-theme-css>` tag on theme apply and cleaned up on theme switch (`web/src/themes/context.tsx:258-272`, applied at `:389` via `applyCustomCSS(theme.customCSS)`). Server-side the value is read from the YAML and clipped (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:18215-18218`, `:18261-18262`).
- **Inputs / options:** A YAML block scalar of arbitrary CSS. Documented example: a scanline overlay scoped with `:root[data-layout-variant="cockpit"] body::before` using `repeating-linear-gradient` and `mix-blend-mode: screen`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** One `<style data-hermes-theme-css="true">` element in `<head>`, removed on theme switch.
- **Config / env:** theme YAML only.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Capped at 32 KiB per theme** — `_THEME_CUSTOM_CSS_MAX = 32 * 1024` at `hermes_cli/web_server.py:18120` with the comment "Cap on customCSS length so a malformed/oversized theme YAML can't blow up"; the value is truncated with `custom_css_val[:_THEME_CUSTOM_CSS_MAX]` (`:18218`). Larger stylesheets should be split across themes, or shipped via a plugin's `css` field (no size cap).
- **Rebuild notes:** Inject theme CSS as one identifiable tag and remove it on switch so themes never leak into each other; cap the payload server-side. A better version would report the truncation to the author instead of silently clipping.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — cap constant at `hermes_cli/web_server.py:18120`, truncation at `:18218`, tag attribute at `web/src/themes/context.tsx:272`.

### Built-in dashboard themes  `id: docs-features.dash-builtin-themes`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** theme switcher (palette icon in the header)
- **What it does:** Ships ready-made themes, each with its own palette, typography and layout, so switching produces visible changes beyond color alone.
- **How it works:** Presets live in `web/src/themes/presets.ts`. Documented table: **Hermes Teal** (`default`) — dark teal + cream, system stack 15px, 0.5rem radius, comfortable. **Hermes Teal (Large)** (`default-large`) — same palette, system stack 18px line-height 1.65, 0.5rem radius, spacious. **Midnight** (`midnight`) — deep blue-violet, Inter + JetBrains Mono 14px, 0.75rem radius, comfortable. **Ember** (`ember`) — warm crimson + bronze, Spectral (serif) + IBM Plex Mono 15px, 0.25rem radius, comfortable. **Mono** (`mono`) — grayscale, IBM Plex Sans + IBM Plex Mono 13px, 0 radius, compact. **Cyberpunk** (`cyberpunk`) — neon green on black, Share Tech Mono everywhere 14px, 0 radius, compact. **Rosé** (`rose`) — pink + ivory, Fraunces (serif) + DM Mono 16px, 1rem radius, spacious.
- **Inputs / options:** Selected from the header theme switcher; persisted to `dashboard.theme`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Theme applied; for themes referencing Google Fonts (all except Hermes Teal) the stylesheet loads on demand — the first switch injects a `<link>` tag into `<head>`.
- **Config / env:** `dashboard.theme` (`hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1676`, documented values `"default"`, `"midnight"`, `"ember"`, `"mono"`, `"cyberpunk"`, `"rose"`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** Built-ins return only `{name, label, description}` from `/api/dashboard/themes`; user themes additionally include a `definition` field with the full normalised theme object.
- **Rebuild notes:** Ship presets that differ in typography and density, not just hue, so the theme system's reach is obvious. A better version would let a user fork a built-in into `~/.hermes/dashboard-themes/` from the picker.
- **Verification:** doc drift — code defines **8** presets at `web/src/themes/presets.ts:42, 58, 83, 111, 135, 164, 189, 216` (`default`, `midnight`, `ember`, `mono`, `cyberpunk`, `rose`, **`nous-blue`**, `default-large`), but the docs table lists only 7 and never mentions `nous-blue`; `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1676`'s comment likewise omits both `nous-blue` and `default-large`.

### Full theme YAML reference (`ocean.yaml`)  `id: docs-features.dash-theme-full-reference`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** extending-the-dashboard.md → "Full theme YAML reference"
- **What it does:** Gives a single copy-and-trim file exercising every theme knob.
- **How it works:** The `ocean` example sets `name`, `label`, `description`, the full `palette` (`background` `{hex,alpha}`, `midground` `{hex,alpha}`, `foreground` alpha 0.0, `warmGlow`, `noiseOpacity`), `typography` (`fontSans`, `fontMono`, `fontDisplay`, `fontUrl`, `baseSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`), `layout` (`radius`, `density`), `layoutVariant`, `assets` (`bg`, `hero`, `crest`, `logo`, `custom.pattern`), `componentStyles` (`card.boxShadow`, `header.background`), `colorOverrides` (`destructive`, `ring`), and `customCSS`.
- **Inputs / options:** All theme keys, as enumerated in the palette/typography/layout/variant/assets/componentStyles/colorOverrides/customCSS entries above.
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a (reference)
- **Config / env:** `dashboard.theme`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Refresh the dashboard after creating the file; switch themes live from the header bar.
- **Rebuild notes:** Ship one exhaustive annotated example rather than fragmenting the schema across sections. A better version would also publish a JSON Schema so editors can validate theme YAML.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — every key in the example maps to a field in `web/src/themes/types.ts`.

### Dashboard plugin quick start  `id: docs-features.dash-plugin-quickstart`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** `~/.hermes/plugins/my-plugin/dashboard/`
- **What it does:** Shows the minimum viable dashboard plugin — a manifest plus a plain IIFE bundle that registers a tab.
- **How it works:** `mkdir -p ~/.hermes/plugins/my-plugin/dashboard/dist`, write `manifest.json` (`name`, `label`, `icon: "Sparkles"`, `version`, `tab.path: "/my-plugin"`, `tab.position: "after:skills"`, `entry: "dist/index.js"`), then `dist/index.js` as an IIFE that reads `window.__HERMES_PLUGIN_SDK__`, destructures `React` and `SDK.components` (`Card`, `CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardContent`), builds a component with `React.createElement`, and finishes with `window.__HERMES_PLUGINS__.register("my-plugin", MyPage)`. Refresh and the tab appears after **Skills**.
- **Inputs / options:** Manifest fields as above; `register(name, Component)`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A new nav tab and route.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Plugins don't bundle React or UI components** — they use the SDK on `window.__HERMES_PLUGIN_SDK__`, keeping bundles tiny (typically a few KB) and avoiding version conflicts. If you prefer JSX, use any bundler (esbuild, Vite, rollup) with React as an external and IIFE output; **the only hard requirement is that the final file is a single JS file loadable via `<script>`**. React is never bundled; it comes from `SDK.React`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Host-provided React + components over a `window` global is what keeps third-party bundles small and version-safe. A better version would ship a tiny typed dev harness so plugin authors get IntelliSense without installing the dashboard.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `window.__HERMES_PLUGINS__ = { register: registerPlugin, registerSlot }` at `web/src/plugins/registry.ts:113-116`; script/CSS URL construction at `web/src/plugins/usePlugins.ts:105-117`.

### Plugin directory layout  `id: docs-features.dash-plugin-layout`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/`
- **What it does:** Defines where each of a plugin's three orthogonal extensions lives, so one install can extend the CLI/gateway and the dashboard at once.
- **How it works:** Documented tree: `plugin.yaml` (optional — existing CLI/gateway plugin manifest); `__init__.py` (optional — existing CLI/gateway hooks); `dashboard/manifest.json` (required for a dashboard plugin — tab config, icon, entry point); `dashboard/dist/index.js` (required — pre-built IIFE bundle); `dashboard/dist/style.css` (optional — custom CSS); `dashboard/plugin_api.py` (optional — backend API routes, FastAPI).
- **Inputs / options:** Three orthogonal layers: `plugin.yaml` + `__init__.py` (CLI/gateway plugin); `dashboard/manifest.json` + `dashboard/dist/index.js` (dashboard UI plugin); `dashboard/plugin_api.py` (dashboard backend routes).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Discovery only picks up directories containing `dashboard/manifest.json`.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **None of the layers are required** — include only the ones you need. The dashboard extension must be in a `dashboard/` subfolder of the plugin directory (a common failure mode when the manifest is placed at the plugin root).
- **Rebuild notes:** Colocate all surfaces of one plugin under one directory with per-surface subfolders, so a single install/uninstall covers everything. A better version would validate the layout at install time and name the missing piece.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — discovery looks for `child / "dashboard" / "manifest.json"` at `hermes_cli/web_server.py:18496`.

### Plugin `manifest.json` reference  `id: docs-features.dash-plugin-manifest`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/dashboard/manifest.json`
- **What it does:** Declares the plugin's identity, its tab placement or override, which shell slots it populates, and which files to load.
- **How it works:** Parsed by `_discover_dashboard_plugins()` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:18434`), served by `GET /api/dashboard/plugins`, consumed by `usePlugins()` in the browser.
- **Inputs / options:** Twelve documented fields. `name` (**required**) — unique identifier, lowercase, hyphens ok, used in URLs and registration. `label` (**required**) — display name shown in the nav tab. `description` (optional) — short description shown in dashboard admin surfaces. `icon` (optional) — Lucide icon name, defaults to `Puzzle`, unknown names fall back to `Puzzle`. `version` (optional) — semver string, defaults to `0.0.0`. `tab.path` (**required**) — URL path for the tab (e.g. `/my-plugin`). `tab.position` (optional) — `"end"` (default), `"after:<path>"`, or `"before:<path>"`, where the value after the colon is the **path segment** of the target tab (no leading slash) — examples `"after:skills"`, `"before:config"`. `tab.override` (optional) — a built-in route path (`"/"`, `"/sessions"`, `"/config"`, …) to **replace** that page instead of adding a tab. `tab.hidden` (optional) — when true, register the component and any slots without adding a nav tab. `slots` (optional) — named shell slots the plugin populates; **documentation aid only**, actual registration happens from the JS bundle via `registerSlot()`. `entry` (**required**) — path to the JS bundle relative to `dashboard/`, defaults to `dist/index.js`. `css` (optional) — path to a CSS file injected as a `<link>` tag. `api` (optional) — path to a Python file with FastAPI routes, mounted at `/api/plugins/<name>/`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Tab registration, route mounting, CSS/JS injection, backend router mounting.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** `slots` is informational — omitting it does not prevent `registerSlot()` from working; listing it makes discovery surfaces more informative. The bundle must call `register()` with the **same name** as `manifest.json:name`. The `api` field's path handling was hardened against an absolute-path RCE primitive (see the security note at `hermes_cli/web_server.py:18474-18481`).
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep the manifest declarative and let the bundle do the binding, so a manifest can't lie about behaviour. A better version would make `slots` authoritative (a plugin may only register into slots it declared), turning it from documentation into a permission.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — manifest parsing at `hermes_cli/web_server.py:18434-18510`; `entry`/`css` URL construction at `web/src/plugins/usePlugins.ts:105-117`.

### Plugin icon map (Lucide names)  `id: docs-features.dash-plugin-icons`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** `manifest.json` → `icon`; mapping in `web/src/App.tsx` → `ICON_MAP`
- **What it does:** Maps a manifest's Lucide icon name to the icon rendered on the plugin's nav tab.
- **How it works:** `const ICON_MAP: Record<string, ComponentType<{ className?: string }>>` at `web/src/App.tsx:226`; `resolveIcon(name)` returns `ICON_MAP[name] ?? Puzzle` at `:253`, so unknown names silently fall back to `Puzzle`.
- **Inputs / options:** Docs list 20 currently mapped names: `Activity`, `BarChart3`, `Clock`, `Code`, `Database`, `Eye`, `FileText`, `Globe`, `Heart`, `KeyRound`, `MessageSquare`, `Package`, `Puzzle`, `Settings`, `Shield`, `Sparkles`, `Star`, `Terminal`, `Wrench`, `Zap`. Docs also say: need a different icon? Open a PR to `web/src/App.tsx`'s `ICON_MAP` — a pure additive change.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Nav-tab icon.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Unknown names silently fall back to `Puzzle` — no warning.
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep an explicit allowlist map rather than dynamic imports, so bundle size stays fixed. A better version would warn in dev mode when a manifest names an unmapped icon instead of falling back silently.
- **Verification:** doc drift — code maps **23** names at `web/src/App.tsx:226-250` (`Activity`, `BarChart3`, `Clock`, `Cpu`, `FileText`, `FolderOpen`, `KeyRound`, `MessageSquare`, `Package`, `Settings`, `Puzzle`, `Sparkles`, `Terminal`, `Globe`, `Database`, `Shield`, `Users`, `Wrench`, `Zap`, `Heart`, `Star`, `Code`, `Eye`); the docs omit **`Cpu`**, **`FolderOpen`** and **`Users`**.

### The Plugin SDK (`window.__HERMES_PLUGIN_SDK__`)  `id: docs-features.dash-plugin-sdk`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** browser global `window.__HERMES_PLUGIN_SDK__`
- **What it does:** Provides everything a plugin needs — React, hooks, UI components, the Hermes API client, a raw fetcher and utilities — so plugins never import React directly.
- **How it works:** `exposePluginSDK()` at `web/src/plugins/registry.ts:112` assigns both `window.__HERMES_PLUGINS__` (`register`, `registerSlot`) and `window.__HERMES_PLUGIN_SDK__`. The public type surface is `web/src/plugins/sdk.d.ts`.
- **Inputs / options:** Documented surface — **React + hooks:** `SDK.React`, `SDK.hooks.useState`, `.useEffect`, `.useCallback`, `.useMemo`, `.useRef`, `.useContext`, `.createContext`. **UI components (shadcn/ui primitives):** `SDK.components.Card`, `.CardHeader`, `.CardTitle`, `.CardContent`, `.Badge`, `.Button`, `.Input`, `.Label`, `.Select`, `.SelectOption`, `.Separator`, `.Tabs`, `.TabsList`, `.TabsTrigger`, `.PluginSlot` (render a named slot, useful for nested plugin UIs). **API client + raw fetcher:** `SDK.api` (typed client — `getStatus`, `getSessions`, `getConfig`, …), `SDK.fetchJSON` (raw fetch for custom endpoints / plugin-registered routes). **Utilities:** `SDK.utils.cn` (Tailwind class merger — clsx + twMerge), `SDK.utils.timeAgo` ("5m ago" from a unix timestamp), `SDK.utils.isoTimeAgo` ("5m ago" from an ISO string). **Hooks:** `SDK.useI18n` (i18n hook for multi-language plugins).
- **Outputs / side effects:** `SDK.fetchJSON` injects the session auth token, surfaces errors as thrown exceptions, and parses JSON automatically. Documented usage: `SDK.fetchJSON("/api/plugins/my-plugin/data").then(...).catch(...)`; `SDK.api.getStatus().then((s) => console.log("Version:", s.version))`; `SDK.api.getSessions(10).then((resp) => console.log(resp.sessions.length))`.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Plugins should **never import React directly** — version conflicts. The full built-in endpoint list is cross-referenced to `./web-dashboard#rest-api`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Expose the host's React instance plus a curated component set on one global, and version the contract. A better version would ship the SDK as a typed npm package that resolves to the global at runtime, so authors get types without bundling.
- **Verification:** doc drift — the real SDK at `web/src/plugins/registry.ts:118-191` exposes **more than documented**: `sdkVersion` (`SDK_CONTRACT_VERSION = "1.1.0"`, `:106`), hooks `useToast` and `useConfirmDelete` (`:135-137`), `authedFetch` (authenticated fetch for non-JSON endpoints/uploads/blob downloads), `buildWsUrl` (ws(s) URL with the right auth param per mode), `buildWsAuthParam`, and components `Checkbox`, `ConfirmDialog`, `Dialog`, `DialogClose`, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogFooter`, `DialogHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `Toast` — none of which appear on this page.

### Shell slots (`registerSlot`)  `id: docs-features.dash-shell-slots`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** `window.__HERMES_PLUGINS__.registerSlot(pluginName, slotName, Component)`
- **What it does:** Lets a plugin inject components into named locations of the app shell — the cockpit sidebar, the header, the footer, an overlay layer — without claiming a whole tab.
- **How it works:** Slot names are validated against `KNOWN_SLOT_NAMES` in `web/src/plugins/slots.ts:61-93`; the shell renders `<PluginSlot name="..." />` at fixed positions in `web/src/App.tsx` (`backdrop` `:524`, `header-banner` `:574`, `header-left` `:612`, `header-right` `:723`, `pre-main` `:765`, `post-main` `:820`, `overlay` `:826`). Multiple plugins can populate the same slot; they render **stacked in registration order**.
- **Inputs / options:** Ten documented shell-wide slots: `backdrop` (inside the `<Backdrop />` layer stack, above the noise layer); `header-left` (before the Hermes brand in the top bar); `header-right` (before the theme/language switchers in the top bar); `header-banner` (full-width strip below the nav); `sidebar` (cockpit sidebar rail); `pre-main` (above the route outlet, inside `<main>`); `post-main` (below the route outlet, inside `<main>`); `footer-left` (footer cell content, replaces default); `footer-right` (footer cell content, replaces default); `overlay` (fixed-position layer above everything else, useful for chrome — scanlines, vignettes — that `customCSS` can't achieve alone).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Components rendered inside the shell at the named position.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** `sidebar` is **only rendered when `layoutVariant === "cockpit"`**. The shell only renders `<PluginSlot name="..." />` for the catalogued slots; **additional names are accepted by the registry** for nested plugin UIs — a plugin can expose its own slots via `SDK.components.PluginSlot`. **Re-registration / HMR:** if the same `(plugin, slot)` pair is registered twice, the later call replaces the earlier one, matching how React HMR expects plugin re-mounts to behave.
- **Rebuild notes:** Render a fixed catalogue of named slot components in the shell and let the registry accept arbitrary names for plugin-owned nesting. A better version would let slots declare an ordering weight instead of relying on registration order.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — all ten shell-wide names present in `KNOWN_SLOT_NAMES` at `web/src/plugins/slots.ts:62-72`; slot-render sites in `web/src/App.tsx` as cited. Note `footer-left` / `footer-right` render sites were not located in `App.tsx` by the same grep (only 7 of 10 `<PluginSlot>` sites matched) — the footer slots are presumably rendered by a footer component, unverified here.

### Page-scoped slots (augmenting built-in pages)  `id: docs-features.dash-page-slots`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** `registerSlot(name, "<page>:top" | "<page>:bottom", Component)`
- **What it does:** Adds a banner, card, or toolbar to an existing built-in page without overriding the whole route — the built-in page keeps working normally and the plugin's component renders alongside it.
- **How it works:** Every built-in page exposes `<page>:top` and `<page>:bottom` slots rendered at the top and bottom of its content area. Names are in `KNOWN_SLOT_NAMES` (`web/src/plugins/slots.ts:73-93`). Documented minimal example pairs `tab.hidden: true` + `slots: ["sessions:top"]` in the manifest with a bundle that calls `register("session-notes", () => null)` as a placeholder and then `registerSlot("session-notes", "sessions:top", Banner)`.
- **Inputs / options:** Documented pairs: `sessions:top` / `sessions:bottom` (top/bottom of `/sessions`); `analytics:top` / `analytics:bottom` (`/analytics`); `logs:top` / `logs:bottom` (top above the filter toolbar / bottom below the log viewer of `/logs`); `cron:top` / `cron:bottom` (`/cron`); `skills:top` / `skills:bottom` (`/skills`); `config:top` / `config:bottom` (`/config`); `env:top` / `env:bottom` (`/env`, the Keys page); `docs:top` / `docs:bottom` (top above the iframe / bottom of `/docs`); `chat:top` / `chat:bottom` (`/chat`, only active when embedded chat is enabled).
- **Outputs / side effects:** The plugin's component renders inside the built-in page.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Zero footprint when no plugin registers** — the built-in page renders exactly as before. Multiple plugins can claim the same page-scoped slot and render stacked in registration order. `tab.hidden: true` keeps a slot-only plugin out of the sidebar. The `slots` manifest field is documentation only — the real binding happens in the JS bundle. A reference plugin (`example-dashboard` in `hermes-example-plugins`, https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-example-plugins/tree/main/example-dashboard) ships a live demo injecting a banner into `sessions:top`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Give every built-in page a top and bottom slot as a standing contract, so augmentation never requires forking a page. A better version would add mid-page and per-row slots for list pages.
- **Verification:** doc drift — code additionally defines **`plugins:top`** and **`plugins:bottom`** in `KNOWN_SLOT_NAMES` (`web/src/plugins/slots.ts:84-85`), and the module docstring at `web/src/plugins/slots.ts:55-59` likewise omits them; the docs table lists 9 page pairs, code has 10.

### Replacing built-in pages (`tab.override`)  `id: docs-features.dash-tab-override`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `manifest.json` → `tab.override`
- **What it does:** Makes the plugin's component replace a built-in page instead of adding a new tab — useful when a theme wants a custom home page (`/`) while keeping the rest of the dashboard intact.
- **How it works:** With `override` set: the original page component at that path is removed from the router; the plugin renders at that path instead; **no nav tab is added for `tab.path`** (the override is the point). Documented manifest: `{"name": "my-home", "label": "Home", "tab": {"path": "/my-home", "override": "/", "position": "end"}, "entry": "dist/index.js"}`.
- **Inputs / options:** `tab.override` = a built-in route path (`"/"`, `"/sessions"`, `"/config"`, …).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Router entry replaced.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Only one plugin can override a given path.** If two plugins claim the same override, **the first wins and the second is ignored with a dev-mode warning**. Full replacement is heavy — the plugin now owns the entire page, including any future updates shipped to it; for adding a card or toolbar, page-scoped slots are the recommended alternative.
- **Rebuild notes:** First-claim-wins with a dev warning avoids nondeterministic page ownership. A better version would surface the conflict in the plugins admin page, not only the console.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — override resolution in `web/src/plugins/usePlugins.ts` / `web/src/App.tsx` route construction.

### Slot-only plugins (`tab.hidden`)  `id: docs-features.dash-tab-hidden`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `manifest.json` → `tab.hidden: true`
- **What it does:** Registers a plugin's component (for direct URL visits) and its slots without adding a tab to the navigation — for plugins that exist only to inject into slots (a header crest, a sidebar HUD, an overlay).
- **How it works:** Documented manifest: `{"name": "header-crest", "label": "Header Crest", "tab": {"path": "/header-crest", "position": "end", "hidden": true}, "slots": ["header-left"], "entry": "dist/index.js"}`. The bundle still calls `register()` with a placeholder component (good practice in case someone hits the URL directly) and then `registerSlot()` to do the real work.
- **Inputs / options:** `tab.hidden: true|false`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** No nav tab; the route still resolves if visited directly.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Combine with page-scoped slots when a plugin only augments existing pages.
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep the route registered even when hidden so direct URLs and deep links don't 404. A better version would let a hidden plugin declare "no route at all" as a third state.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `hidden` handling in the plugin nav/route builder (`web/src/App.tsx` `buildNavItems`, referenced at `:255`).

### Plugin backend API routes (`plugin_api.py`)  `id: docs-features.dash-plugin-backend`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/dashboard/plugin_api.py`; routes served under `/api/plugins/<name>/`
- **What it does:** Lets a plugin register FastAPI routes that its UI can call.
- **How it works:** Set `"api": "plugin_api.py"` in the manifest and export a module-level `router = APIRouter()`. Routes are mounted under `/api/plugins/<name>/`, so `@router.get("/data")` becomes `GET /api/plugins/my-plugin/data` and `@router.post("/action")` becomes `POST /api/plugins/my-plugin/action`. Backend routes run **inside the dashboard process**, so they can import from the hermes-agent codebase directly — documented examples import `SessionDB` from `hermes_state` and `load_config` from `hermes_cli.config` to expose `/session-count` and `/config-snapshot`.
- **Inputs / options:** Manifest `api` field; a Python module exporting `router`. Call from the UI with `SDK.fetchJSON("/api/plugins/my-plugin/data")`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** New authenticated HTTP routes on the dashboard server; whatever the route does inside the Hermes process.
- **Config / env:** none beyond the manifest.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Plugin API routes sit behind the dashboard's normal auth gate — **unauthenticated requests get a `401` before the plugin route runs**, and requests to a **disabled** plugin's routes are rejected at request time. Still, the docs warn: **don't expose the dashboard on a public interface with `--host 0.0.0.0` if you run untrusted plugins** — an authenticated session can reach their routes too. Routes are mounted **once at startup, not on rescan** — a new `plugin_api.py` requires restarting `hermes dashboard`. Only a module-level `router = APIRouter()` is picked up; other export names are ignored. Import errors are logged to `~/.hermes/logs/errors.log` as `Failed to load plugin <name> API routes`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Mount plugin routers under a fixed namespace behind the host's auth gate, and load them once at startup so a rescan can't hot-add server code. A better version would run plugin routers in a restricted context rather than with full in-process imports.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — the `/api/plugins/<name>` namespace is shared with the desktop app per the page's own note; discovery hardened the manifest `api` field against an absolute-path RCE primitive (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:18474-18481`).

### Per-plugin custom CSS  `id: docs-features.dash-plugin-css`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `manifest.json` → `"css": "dist/style.css"`
- **What it does:** Loads a plugin-owned stylesheet for styles beyond Tailwind classes and inline `style=`.
- **How it works:** The file is injected as a `<link>` tag on plugin load — URL built as `${HERMES_BASE_PATH}/dashboard-plugins/${manifest.name}/${manifest.css}` (`web/src/plugins/usePlugins.ts:105`). The docs advise using specific class names to avoid conflicts with the dashboard's styles, and referencing the dashboard's CSS vars to stay theme-aware. Documented example styles `.my-plugin-chart` with `var(--color-border)`, `var(--color-card)`, `var(--color-card-foreground)` and a `:hover` using `var(--color-ring)`.
- **Inputs / options:** `css` manifest field (path relative to `dashboard/`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** One `<link>` per plugin stylesheet.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **No size cap** (unlike theme `customCSS`'s 32 KiB) — the docs recommend it as the escape hatch for large stylesheets. The dashboard exposes every shadcn token as `--color-*` plus theme extras (`--theme-asset-*`, `--component-<bucket>-*`, `--radius`, `--spacing-mul`); referencing those makes a plugin reskin automatically with the active theme.
- **Rebuild notes:** Serve plugin assets from a dedicated path namespace and publish the theme var contract so plugin CSS is theme-aware by default. A better version would scope plugin CSS automatically (shadow DOM or a generated prefix) so class collisions are impossible.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — CSS URL construction at `web/src/plugins/usePlugins.ts:105`.

### Plugin discovery order & rescan  `id: docs-features.dash-plugin-discovery`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** `GET /api/dashboard/plugins/rescan`; directories scanned for `dashboard/manifest.json`
- **What it does:** Finds dashboard plugins across three sources with a defined precedence, and allows a rescan without restarting.
- **How it works:** `_discover_dashboard_plugins()` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:18434`) scans, in order: **user** — `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/dashboard/` (priority 1, wins on conflict); **bundled** — `<repo>/plugins/memory/<name>/dashboard/` and `<repo>/plugins/<name>/dashboard/` (priority 2); **project** — `./.hermes/plugins/<name>/dashboard/` (priority 3, only when `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS` is set). A `seen_names` set makes the first source win. Results are cached per dashboard process in `_dashboard_plugins_cache` (`:18562`), invalidated automatically when a cached plugin's directory disappears (`:18570-18571`).
- **Inputs / options:** `curl http://127.0.0.1:9119/api/dashboard/plugins/rescan` to force a rescan without restart; or restart `hermes dashboard`. Env `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Refreshed plugin list with a `source` label (`user` / `bundled` / `project`).
- **Config / env:** `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** The project source uses shared truthy semantics (`1` / `true` / `yes` / `on`) via `env_var_enabled()` — a prior `os.environ.get()` check treated **any** non-empty string as truthy, so `=0`, `=false` and `=no` silently *enabled* the untrusted project source (GHSA-5qr3-c538-wm9j / #29156, `hermes_cli/web_server.py:18474-18482`). When the process itself is profile-scoped (`--profile <name>` sets `HERMES_HOME=<root>/profiles/<name>`), the launch home has no `plugins/`, so the default root is scanned as well (#87197, `:18455-18468`); the `seen_names` dedupe keeps profile-local plugins authoritative over same-named root plugins. Plugin **API routes are not remounted by a rescan** — that needs a restart.
- **Rebuild notes:** Order sources user → bundled → project, dedupe by name on first-wins, and gate the untrusted project source behind strict truthy env parsing. A better version would show which source each loaded plugin came from in the plugins admin page.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — discovery order, source labels and env gate at `hermes_cli/web_server.py:18434-18486`; rescan route at `:18619-18622`.

### Plugin load lifecycle  `id: docs-features.dash-plugin-lifecycle`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** browser; `main.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `usePlugins()`
- **What it does:** Defines the exact five-step order in which plugins are exposed, fetched, injected, registered and mounted.
- **How it works:** (1) Dashboard loads; `main.tsx` exposes the SDK on `window.__HERMES_PLUGIN_SDK__` and the registry on `window.__HERMES_PLUGINS__`. (2) `App.tsx` calls `usePlugins()` → fetches `GET /api/dashboard/plugins`. (3) For each manifest, the CSS `<link>` is injected (if declared), then a `<script>` tag loads the JS bundle. (4) The plugin's IIFE runs and calls `window.__HERMES_PLUGINS__.register(name, Component)` — and optionally `.registerSlot(name, slot, Component)` for each slot. (5) The dashboard resolves the registered component against the manifest, adds the tab to navigation (unless `hidden`), and mounts the component as a route.
- **Inputs / options:** n/a (automatic)
- **Outputs / side effects:** Tabs, routes and slot content appear.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Plugins have up to **2 seconds** after their script loads to call `register()` — `setTimeout(() => setLoading(false), 2000)` at `web/src/plugins/usePlugins.ts:158`. After that the dashboard stops waiting and finishes the initial render; **if a plugin registers later it still appears — the nav is reactive**. If a plugin's script fails to load (404, syntax error, exception during the IIFE) the dashboard logs a warning to the browser console and continues without it; the i18n string is "Could not load this plugin's script. Check the Network tab (dashboard-plugins/…) and the server's plugin path." (`web/src/i18n/en.ts:50`, translated in de/es/zh/zh-hant/ja/ga/it/tr).
- **Rebuild notes:** Never block first paint on third-party scripts — time-box the wait and make the nav reactive so late registrations still land. A better version would show a per-plugin load status in the plugins admin page rather than only the console.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — the 2-second timeout at `web/src/plugins/usePlugins.ts:158`; localized load-failure message at `web/src/i18n/en.ts:50`.

### Combined theme + plugin demo (`strike-freedom-cockpit`)  `id: docs-features.dash-demo-plugin`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-example-plugins/tree/main/strike-freedom-cockpit
- **What it does:** A complete reskin demo pairing a theme YAML with a slot-only plugin to produce a cockpit-style HUD without forking the dashboard.
- **How it works:** Demonstrates a full theme using palette, typography, `fontUrl`, `layoutVariant: cockpit`, `assets`, `componentStyles` (notched card corners, gradient backgrounds), `colorOverrides` and `customCSS` (scanline overlay); plus a slot-only plugin (`tab.hidden: true`) registering into three slots — `sidebar` (an MS-STATUS panel with live telemetry bars driven by `SDK.api.getStatus()`), `header-left` (a faction crest reading `--theme-asset-crest` from the active theme), and `footer-right` (a custom tagline replacing the default org line). The plugin reads theme-supplied artwork via CSS vars, so swapping themes changes the hero/crest without plugin code changes.
- **Inputs / options:** Install: `git clone https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-example-plugins.git`; theme — `cp hermes-example-plugins/strike-freedom-cockpit/theme/strike-freedom.yaml ~/.hermes/dashboard-themes/`; plugin — `cp -r hermes-example-plugins/strike-freedom-cockpit ~/.hermes/plugins/`. Then pick **Strike Freedom** from the theme switcher.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Cockpit sidebar appears, crest shows in the header, tagline replaces the footer.
- **Config / env:** `dashboard.theme` set to the demo theme.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Switching back to **Hermes Teal** leaves the plugin installed but invisible — the `sidebar` slot only renders under the `cockpit` layout variant. The docs suggest reading `strike-freedom-cockpit/dashboard/dist/index.js` to see how it reads CSS vars, **guards against older dashboards without slot support**, and registers three slots from one bundle.
- **Rebuild notes:** Ship one end-to-end example that exercises every layer at once; make it degrade gracefully on older hosts. A better version would ship the demo in-tree with a one-command installer.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — external companion repo `hermes-example-plugins`; behaviour depends on the `cockpit` variant gate confirmed at `web/src/themes/types.ts:71-77`.

### Dashboard theme & plugin API endpoints  `id: docs-features.dash-ext-api`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `/api/dashboard/themes`, `/api/dashboard/theme`, `/api/dashboard/plugins`, `/api/dashboard/plugins/rescan`, `/dashboard-plugins/<name>/<path>`, `/api/plugins/<name>/*`
- **What it does:** The HTTP surface the theme switcher and plugin loader use, callable directly with `curl`.
- **How it works:** `GET /api/dashboard/themes` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:18294`) lists available themes + the active name — built-ins return `{name, label, description}`; user themes also include a `definition` field with the full normalised theme object (`:18300`). `PUT /api/dashboard/theme` (`:18328`) sets the active theme with body `{"name": "midnight"}` and persists it to `config.yaml` under `dashboard.theme`. `GET /api/dashboard/plugins` (`:18575`) lists discovered plugins with manifests, minus internal fields. `GET /api/dashboard/plugins/rescan` (`:18619`) forces a re-scan without restarting. `GET /dashboard-plugins/<name>/<path>` serves static assets from a plugin's `dashboard/` directory. `/api/plugins/<name>/*` (any method) hits plugin-registered backend routes.
- **Inputs / options:** All six endpoints as listed, plus the `window` globals table — `window.__HERMES_PLUGIN_SDK__` (object, provided by `registry.ts` — React, hooks, UI components, API client, utils), `window.__HERMES_PLUGINS__.register(name, Component)` (function — register a plugin's main component), `window.__HERMES_PLUGINS__.registerSlot(name, slot, Component)` (function — register into a named shell slot).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Theme/plugin state changes; `config.yaml` writes for the theme.
- **Config / env:** `dashboard.theme`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Path traversal is blocked** on `/dashboard-plugins/<name>/<path>`. Plugin routes are behind the dashboard's auth gate.
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep the extension surface fully HTTP-addressable so themes and plugins are debuggable with `curl`. A better version would document the `/api/dashboard/font` pair alongside these and version the plugin manifest schema in the list response.
- **Verification:** partial — all six documented endpoints exist at the cited lines, but the API reference table omits `GET`/`PUT /api/dashboard/font` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:18357`, `:18370`) and `GET /api/dashboard/plugins/hub` (`:18837`), both of which exist in code (doc gap).

### Extending-the-dashboard troubleshooting guide  `id: docs-features.dash-ext-troubleshooting`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** extending-the-dashboard.md → "Troubleshooting"
- **What it does:** Gives six named failure modes with concrete diagnostic steps.
- **How it works:** **(1) My theme doesn't appear in the picker** — check the file is in `~/.hermes/dashboard-themes/` and ends in `.yaml` or `.yml`; refresh; run `curl http://127.0.0.1:9119/api/dashboard/themes`; on a YAML parse error the dashboard logs to `errors.log` under `~/.hermes/logs/`. **(2) My plugin's tab doesn't show up** — five steps: confirm the manifest is at `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/dashboard/manifest.json` (note the `dashboard/` subdirectory); `curl .../api/dashboard/plugins/rescan`; dev tools → Network to confirm `manifest.json`, `index.js` and any CSS loaded without 404s; dev tools → Console for IIFE errors or `window.__HERMES_PLUGINS__ is undefined` (which indicates the SDK didn't initialize, usually a React render crash earlier); verify the bundle calls `register(...)` with the same name as `manifest.json:name`. **(3) Slot-registered components don't render** — the `sidebar` slot only renders when the active theme has `layoutVariant: cockpit`; other slots always render; add `console.log` inside `registerSlot` to confirm the bundle ran. **(4) Plugin backend routes return 404** — confirm `"api": "plugin_api.py"` points at an existing file inside `dashboard/`; restart `hermes dashboard` (routes mount once at startup, **not** on rescan); check `plugin_api.py` exports a module-level `router = APIRouter()` (other export names are not picked up); tail `~/.hermes/logs/errors.log` for `Failed to load plugin <name> API routes`. **(5) Theme change drops my color overrides** — by design; put persistent overrides in the theme YAML, not the live switcher. **(6) Theme customCSS gets truncated** — capped at 32 KiB per theme; split across themes or use a plugin's `css` field (no size cap).
- **Inputs / options:** Diagnostic commands `curl http://127.0.0.1:9119/api/dashboard/themes`, `curl http://127.0.0.1:9119/api/dashboard/plugins/rescan`; log file `~/.hermes/logs/errors.log`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** Also documented: **shipping a plugin on PyPI is not supported** — dashboard plugins are installed by directory layout, not by pip entry point; the cleanest distribution path today is a git repo the user clones into `~/.hermes/plugins/`, and **a pip-based installer for dashboard plugins is not currently wired up**.
- **Rebuild notes:** Pair each failure mode with the exact command that proves it. A better version would ship a `hermes doctor --dashboard-plugins` check that runs all six diagnostics.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — the 32 KiB cap (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:18120`), routes-mounted-once behaviour, and the rescan endpoint (`:18619`) all match code.
