## Page: `skills.md` — Skills System

### Skills system (overview)  `id: docs-features.skills-overview`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `~/.hermes/skills/`
- **What it does:** On-demand knowledge documents the agent loads when needed, following a **progressive disclosure** pattern to minimize token usage, compatible with the agentskills.io open standard.
- **How it works:** All skills live in `~/.hermes/skills/` — **the primary directory and source of truth**. On fresh install, bundled skills are copied from the repo; hub-installed and agent-created skills also go there. **The agent can modify or delete any skill.** Hermes can also be pointed at external skill directories scanned alongside the local one.
- **Inputs / options:** Three tools — `skills_list`, `skill_view`, `skill_manage`. Config tree `skills.*` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`. CLI groups `hermes skills` and `hermes bundles`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Skill directories on disk; skills appear in the system prompt index, in `skills_list`, and as `/skill-name` slash commands.
- **Config / env:** `skills.*` (`hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2248-2317`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** Cross-referenced catalogs: `/reference/skills-catalog` (bundled) and `/reference/optional-skills-catalog` (official optional).
- **Rebuild notes:** One writable source-of-truth directory plus read-mostly extra tiers, with progressive disclosure so the index is cheap and content is loaded on demand. A better version would track per-skill token cost and usage so unused skills can be pruned automatically.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — exactly three skill tools present in `tools_full.json` (`skill_manage`, `skill_view`, `skills_list`); config tree at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2248`.

### Blank-slate profiles (`--no-skills`, `hermes skills opt-out`)  `id: docs-features.skills-blank-slate`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** installer flag `--no-skills`; `hermes profile create <name> --no-skills`; `hermes skills opt-out` / `opt-in`
- **What it does:** Creates or converts a profile that has **no bundled skills** and stays empty across updates.
- **How it works:** All three paths write a `.no-bundled-skills` marker into the profile directory. **While the marker is present, the installer, `hermes update`, and any skill sync all skip bundled-skill seeding for that profile.** Deleting the marker (or running `hermes skills opt-in`) re-enables seeding.
- **Inputs / options:** **At install time** (default `~/.hermes` profile): `curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash -s -- --no-skills`. **At profile-create time**: `hermes profile create research --no-skills`. **At runtime**: `hermes skills opt-out` (stop future seeding — nothing on disk is touched); `hermes skills opt-out --remove` (also delete UNMODIFIED bundled skills, confirms first) with `--yes`/`-y` to skip the confirmation; `hermes skills opt-in` and `hermes skills opt-in --sync` (remove the marker and re-seed now).
- **Outputs / side effects:** `.no-bundled-skills` marker file created/removed; optionally unmodified bundled skills deleted.
- **Config / env:** marker file only (no config key).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Safe by default** — `opt-out` only stops *future* seeding and never deletes anything already on disk. `--remove` deletes bundled skills **only when they are unmodified (byte-identical to the version Hermes installed)**; skills you have edited, skills installed from the hub, and skills you wrote yourself are always kept.
- **Rebuild notes:** Use an on-disk marker rather than a config key so the installer (which runs before config load) honours it too, and make deletion conditional on byte-identity. A better version would report exactly which skills were kept and why.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — help text confirms the marker name and semantics: "Write the .no-bundled-skills marker so the installer, `hermes update`, and any direct sync stop seeding bundled skills into the active profile… Pass --remove to ALSO delete bundled skills that are unmodified (user-edited and hub/local skills are never removed)" (evidence: `cli_help/skills__opt-out.txt`, `cli_help/skills__opt-in.txt`).

### Skills as slash commands  `id: docs-features.skills-slash`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `/<skill-name> [args]` in the CLI or any messaging platform
- **What it does:** Makes every installed skill automatically available as a slash command.
- **How it works:** Invoking `/<skill-name>` loads the skill; text after the command becomes the user instruction. Just the skill name with no arguments loads it and lets the agent ask what you need.
- **Inputs / options:** Documented examples: `/gif-search funny cats`, `/axolotl help me fine-tune Llama 3 on my dataset`, `/github-pr-workflow create a PR for the auth refactor`, `/songsee analyze the frequency spread of this mix`, `/excalidraw` (bare). Natural-conversation equivalents: `hermes chat --toolsets skills -q "What skills do you have?"`, `hermes chat --toolsets skills -q "Show me the axolotl skill"`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Skill content loaded into a fresh user message.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Platform-restricted skills (via `platforms:`) are hidden from slash commands on incompatible OSes.
- **Rebuild notes:** Auto-derive one slash command per installed skill so discovery and invocation share a namespace. A better version would offer tab-completion with the skill's description inline.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — skill slash dispatch in `agent/skill_commands.py`.

### Stacking multiple skills in one command  `id: docs-features.skills-stacking`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `/skill-a /skill-b <instruction>`
- **What it does:** Loads several skills from a single message by chaining slash commands at the start.
- **How it works:** Every leading `/skill` token is loaded (**up to 5**) and the rest becomes your instruction. **Parsing stops at the first token that isn't an installed skill**, so arguments that happen to start with `/` (like file paths) are never swallowed.
- **Inputs / options:** Documented examples: `/github-pr-workflow /test-driven-development fix issue #123 and open a PR` (two skills); `/ocr-and-documents /tmp/scan.pdf extract the tables` (loads one skill; `/tmp/scan.pdf` stays an argument).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Up to five skills loaded into one user message.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Hard cap of five leading skills — `_MAX_STACKED_SKILLS = 5` at `agent/skill_commands.py:725`, referenced as `_cap` at `hermes_cli/commands.py:1701`. For combinations you use repeatedly, the docs recommend a **skill bundle** instead — same effect under one short command.
- **Rebuild notes:** Stop parsing at the first non-skill token so path-like arguments survive, and cap the stack so a pathological message can't blow the context. A better version would warn when the cap truncates a longer chain instead of silently stopping.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — cap and parsing rule at `agent/skill_commands.py:713-735` ("up to `_MAX_STACKED_SKILLS` total leading skills… Parsing stops at the…").

### `/plan` built-in command  `id: docs-features.skills-plan`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `/plan [request]`
- **What it does:** Tells Hermes to inspect context if needed, write a markdown implementation plan instead of executing the task, and save the result.
- **How it works:** Plan mode works the same way as skill invocation but is a **built-in command now**, not a skill. The result is saved under `.hermes/plans/` relative to the active workspace/backend working directory.
- **Inputs / options:** `/plan` with an optional request string.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A markdown plan file under `.hermes/plans/`; no task execution.
- **Config / env:** the active workspace / terminal backend working directory determines where plans land.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Saves relative to the **backend** working directory, so under a Docker/SSH terminal backend the plan lands inside that environment.
- **Rebuild notes:** Make plan mode a built-in rather than a skill so it can't be uninstalled, and persist plans to a predictable repo-relative path. A better version would link the plan to the session that produced it and offer `/plan apply`.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `/plan` handled alongside skill dispatch in `agent/skill_commands.py` / `hermes_cli/commands.py`.

### `/learn` — author a skill from sources  `id: docs-features.skills-learn`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `/learn <anything you can describe>`; dashboard Skills page → **Learn a skill** button
- **What it does:** Turns something you know — or a pile of reference material — into a reusable skill without hand-writing the `SKILL.md`.
- **How it works:** Open-ended: point it at anything describable and the agent gathers material with the tools it already has (`read_file` / `search_files` for local dirs, `web_extract` for URLs), then authors a skill following the house authoring standards (**≤60-char description, the standard section order, Hermes-tool framing, no invented commands**). **There is no model-tool footprint** — `/learn` builds a standards-guided prompt and hands it to the agent as a normal turn; the agent saves the result with `skill_manage`.
- **Inputs / options:** Documented forms: `/learn the REST client in ~/projects/acme-sdk, focus on auth + pagination` (local SDK/doc dir); `/learn https://docs.example.com/api/quickstart` (online doc page); `/learn how I just deployed the staging server` (the workflow just walked through in conversation); `/learn filing an expense: open the portal, New > Expense, attach the receipt, submit` (pasted notes / described procedure); `/learn ~/books/designing-data-intensive-applications.pdf` (whole book / paper stack / large docs corpus). Dashboard panel fields: a **directory field**, a **URL field**, and an **open-ended text box**, which compose a `/learn` request and run it in chat.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A new or updated skill written through `skill_manage`.
- **Config / env:** the **write-approval gate** (`skills.write_approval`) applies if enabled.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Because the live agent does the sourcing, `/learn` works the same in the CLI, the messaging gateway, the TUI and the dashboard — **and on any terminal backend (local, Docker, remote), since there is no separate ingestion engine**.
- **Rebuild notes:** Implement "learn" as a prompt template over the agent's existing tools rather than a bespoke ingestion pipeline, so it inherits every backend and surface for free. A better version would show a preview diff of the generated SKILL.md before saving.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `/learn` prompt construction in `agent/learn_prompt.py` (its injection guidance at `:159` covers zero-width characters, bidi embeddings/overrides/isolates and tag characters).

### `/learn` knowledge-base skills for large sources  `id: docs-features.skills-learn-kb`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `/learn <book | paper stack | spec | large docs folder>`
- **What it does:** For large sources, authors an **expansive knowledge-base skill** instead of one crammed file or a lossy summary.
- **How it works:** A lean `SKILL.md` carries the source's core mental models plus an index, with **one distilled file per chapter or topic under `references/`** (plus a glossary or cheatsheet when the source earns them). Reference files cost nothing until a question needs one — the agent loads them on demand with `skill_view`, so **query cost stays proportional to the answer, not the source**. Re-running `/learn` with new material on the same topic **folds it into the existing skill rather than creating a duplicate**.
- **Inputs / options:** Any large source path or URL.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A multi-file skill with a `references/` tree.
- **Config / env:** `skills.write_approval` if on.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **The distillation synthesizes structure — frameworks, definitions, decision rules, anti-patterns — and never reproduces passages of the source text.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Index-plus-references beats one giant file because the loader is per-file; make re-learning idempotent by folding into the existing skill. A better version would keep a source manifest so the skill can be re-derived when the upstream doc changes.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — the `references/` on-demand pattern matches the Level-2 progressive-disclosure call `skill_view(name, path)`.

### Progressive disclosure (3 levels)  `id: docs-features.skills-progressive-disclosure`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** `skills_list()`, `skill_view(name)`, `skill_view(name, path)`
- **What it does:** Loads skill knowledge in three escalating levels so the agent pays for detail only when it needs it.
- **How it works:** **Level 0:** `skills_list()` → `[{name, description, category}, ...]` (**~3k tokens**). **Level 1:** `skill_view(name)` → full content + metadata (varies). **Level 2:** `skill_view(name, path)` → a specific reference file (varies). The agent only loads the full skill content when it actually needs it.
- **Inputs / options:** `skills_list()` (no args); `skill_view(name)`; `skill_view(name, path)`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Skill index / content injected into context.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** The ~3k-token index cost is the floor paid on every session with skills enabled.
- **Rebuild notes:** Three levels — index, document, sub-document — is enough; make level 0 cheap enough to always include. A better version would rank the index by recent relevance so level 0 can be truncated safely on small-context models.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `skills_list` and `skill_view` both present in `tools_full.json`.

### `SKILL.md` format & frontmatter  `id: docs-features.skills-skillmd-format`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `<skill-dir>/SKILL.md`
- **What it does:** Defines the YAML frontmatter and body structure every skill follows.
- **How it works:** Frontmatter keys documented: `name`, `description`, `version`, `platforms` (optional — restrict to specific OS platforms), and a `metadata.hermes` block with `tags`, `category`, `fallback_for_toolsets`, `requires_toolsets`, and `config` (a list of `{key, description, default, prompt}` entries). Body sections in the documented standard order: `# Skill Title`, `## When to Use` (trigger conditions), `## Procedure` (numbered steps), `## Pitfalls` (known failure modes and fixes), `## Verification` (how to confirm it worked). Tap-publishing docs additionally list `author` as a supported frontmatter key.
- **Inputs / options:** All frontmatter keys above, plus `required_environment_variables` (see `skills-secure-setup`) and `fallback_for_tools` / `requires_tools` (see `skills-conditional-activation`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Governs indexing, filtering, slash-command availability and setup prompts.
- **Config / env:** `metadata.hermes.config` entries land under `skills.config` in `config.yaml`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** The `/learn` house standard enforces a **≤60-char description**.
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep the frontmatter flat with one vendor-namespaced block (`metadata.hermes`) so cross-tool skills stay portable. A better version would publish a JSON Schema and validate on install.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `${HERMES_SKILL_DIR}` / `${HERMES_SESSION_ID}` template substitution is additionally supported via `skills.template_vars` (`hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2265-2269`) and is **not documented on this page** (doc gap).

### Platform-specific skills (`platforms:`)  `id: docs-features.skills-platforms`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `SKILL.md` frontmatter → `platforms:`
- **What it does:** Restricts a skill to specific operating systems.
- **How it works:** When set, the skill is **automatically hidden from the system prompt, `skills_list()`, and slash commands on incompatible platforms**. If omitted, the skill loads on all platforms.
- **Inputs / options:** Three documented values: `macos` (matches macOS/Darwin), `linux` (matches Linux), `windows` (matches Windows). Examples: `platforms: [macos]` (macOS only — e.g. iMessage, Apple Reminders, FindMy); `platforms: [macos, linux]`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Skill hidden from all three discovery surfaces on non-matching OSes.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Hiding is complete — the skill can't be invoked by name on an incompatible platform either.
- **Rebuild notes:** Filter at index time so an unusable skill never reaches the model. A better version would allow arch and distro predicates, not just OS family.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — platform filtering applied in the skill index path.

### Skill media delivery and `[[as_document]]` / `[[audio_as_voice]]`  `id: docs-features.skills-media-directives`
- **Surface:** Gateway/Telegram
- **Where:** any skill/agent response containing a bare absolute media path; directives `[[as_document]]`, `[[audio_as_voice]]`
- **What it does:** Auto-delivers media files referenced by absolute path as native chat attachments, with two directives to control the delivery style.
- **How it works:** When a response includes a bare absolute path to a media file (e.g. `/home/user/screenshots/diagram.png`), the gateway auto-detects it, **strips it from the visible text**, and delivers the file natively (Telegram photo, Discord attachment, …) instead of leaving the raw path in the message. `[[audio_as_voice]]` promotes audio files to native voice-message bubbles on platforms that support them (Telegram, WhatsApp). `[[as_document]]` forces every media path in the same response to be delivered as a document/file attachment rather than an image bubble.
- **Inputs / options:** Two directives — `[[as_document]]` and `[[audio_as_voice]]` — placed anywhere in the response text, typically the last line.
- **Outputs / side effects:** The directive is **stripped before delivery**, so users never see it. Media delivered natively.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Granularity is intentionally all-or-nothing per response** — emit `[[as_document]]` once and every image path in the same response is delivered as a document; this mirrors the scope of `[[audio_as_voice]]`. Rationale given: Telegram's `sendPhoto` recompresses to ~200 KB at 1280 px, destroying readability, while a 1-2 MB PNG sent via `sendDocument` keeps the original bytes intact. Documented use cases: screenshots/charts the user needs as files (for editing elsewhere, archiving, sharing intact); renders where the default lossy preview would obscure detail (small text, pixel-accurate diagrams, color-sensitive renders). **Platforms without a separate document path (e.g. SMS) fall back to whatever attachment mechanism they have.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Detect media by absolute path in the response and let the author override the delivery mode with a stripped inline directive. A better version would allow per-path directives so one response can mix bubbles and documents.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — media-path detection and `MEDIA_DELIVERY_EXTS` at `gateway/platforms/base.py:2007-2026` (see the `browser_vision` entry for the same `MEDIA:` mechanism).

### Conditional activation (fallback skills)  `id: docs-features.skills-conditional-activation`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `SKILL.md` → `metadata.hermes.fallback_for_toolsets` / `fallback_for_tools` / `requires_toolsets` / `requires_tools`
- **What it does:** Lets skills show or hide themselves based on which tools are available in the current session — most useful for **fallback skills**, free or local alternatives that should only appear when a premium tool is unavailable.
- **How it works:** Four fields with documented behaviour: `fallback_for_toolsets` — skill is **hidden** when the listed toolsets are available, shown when they're missing. `fallback_for_tools` — same, but checks individual tools instead of toolsets. `requires_toolsets` — skill is **hidden** when the listed toolsets are unavailable, shown when they're present. `requires_tools` — same, but checks individual tools.
- **Inputs / options:** All four fields take a list. Documented YAML example uses `fallback_for_toolsets: [web]`, `requires_toolsets: [terminal]`, `fallback_for_tools: [web_search]`, `requires_tools: [terminal]`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Skill included in or omitted from the index for that session.
- **Config / env:** depends on which toolsets/tools the session has.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Documented example — the built-in `duckduckgo-search` skill uses `fallback_for_toolsets: [web]`: with `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` set the web toolset is available and the agent uses `web_search`, so the DuckDuckGo skill stays hidden; without the key the toolset is unavailable and the skill automatically appears. **Skills without any conditional fields behave exactly as before — they're always shown.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Evaluate availability at index build time per session, and express both "only when present" and "only when absent" so fallbacks are declarative. A better version would let a skill declare a priority so several fallbacks can be ordered.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — conditional-activation fields consumed by the skill index builder.

### Secure setup on load (`required_environment_variables`)  `id: docs-features.skills-secure-setup`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `SKILL.md` frontmatter → `required_environment_variables:`
- **What it does:** Lets a skill declare required environment variables without disappearing from discovery, prompting for them securely only when the skill is actually loaded.
- **How it works:** Each entry has `name`, `prompt`, `help`, and `required_for`. When a missing value is encountered, Hermes asks for it securely **only when the skill is actually loaded in the local CLI**. You can skip setup and keep using the skill. Once set, declared env vars are **automatically passed through to `execute_code` and `terminal` sandboxes** — the skill's scripts can use `$TENOR_API_KEY` directly.
- **Inputs / options:** Documented example entry: `name: TENOR_API_KEY`, `prompt: Tenor API key`, `help: Get a key from https://developers.google.com/tenor`, `required_for: full functionality`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Value written where Hermes stores secrets (`~/.hermes/.env`); env var available inside sandboxes.
- **Config / env:** for non-skill env vars use `terminal.env_passthrough` (see `/user-guide/security#environment-variable-passthrough`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Messaging surfaces never ask for secrets in chat** — they tell you to use `hermes setup` or `~/.hermes/.env` locally instead.
- **Rebuild notes:** Declare secrets in the skill, prompt lazily and only on a local trusted surface, and auto-pass them into sandboxes so scripts just work. A better version would scope the passthrough to the loading skill's own sandbox rather than the whole session.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `terminal.env_passthrough` is the documented non-skill counterpart; skill env passthrough handled in the skill loader.

### Skill config settings (`metadata.hermes.config`)  `id: docs-features.skills-config-settings`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `SKILL.md` → `metadata.hermes.config`; stored under `skills.config` in `config.yaml`
- **What it does:** Lets a skill declare non-secret config settings (paths, preferences) stored in `config.yaml`.
- **How it works:** Each entry has `key`, `description`, `default`, and `prompt`. Settings are stored under `skills.config` in your `config.yaml`. **`hermes config migrate` prompts for unconfigured settings, and `hermes config show` displays them.** When a skill loads, **its resolved config values are injected into the context so the agent knows the configured values automatically**.
- **Inputs / options:** Documented example: `key: myplugin.path`, `description: Path to the plugin data directory`, `default: "~/myplugin-data"`, `prompt: Plugin data directory path`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** `skills.config.<key>` in `config.yaml`; values injected into the skill's context on load.
- **Config / env:** `skills.config`; commands `hermes config migrate`, `hermes config show`; also `hermes skills config` (interactive skill enable/disable).
- **Edge cases / guards:** Non-secret only — secrets go through `required_environment_variables`. Cross-references: `/user-guide/configuration#skill-settings` and `/developer-guide/creating-skills#config-settings-configyaml`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Separate secret (env) from non-secret (config) declarations and inject resolved config into the skill context so the agent doesn't have to ask. A better version would validate types and reject a default that doesn't match.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `hermes skills config` exists ("Interactive skill configuration — enable/disable individual skills", evidence: `cli_help/skills.txt`).

### Skill directory structure  `id: docs-features.skills-directory-structure`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `~/.hermes/skills/`
- **What it does:** Defines the on-disk layout of the skill store, including category directories, per-skill subfolders, hub state and the bundled manifest.
- **How it works:** Documented tree: `~/.hermes/skills/` (single source of truth) → category directories (e.g. `mlops/`, `devops/`) → per-skill directories containing `SKILL.md` (main instructions, **required**), `references/` (additional docs), `templates/` (output formats), `scripts/` (helper scripts callable from the skill), `examples/` (referenced example outputs), and `assets/` (supplementary files). Plus `.hub/` (Skills Hub state: `lock.json`, `quarantine/`, `audit.log`) and `.bundled_manifest` (tracks seeded bundled skills).
- **Inputs / options:** Six per-skill subdirectory names: `references`, `templates`, `scripts`, `examples`, `assets` (plus the required `SKILL.md`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Hub installs write `skills/.hub/lock.json` entries recording the **source URL, exact content hash, scanner version, findings, timestamp, and fresh-or-cached status**.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Third-party URL and GitHub installs include `SKILL.md` **plus the exact local files it references** under `references/`, `templates/`, `scripts/`, `assets/` and `examples/` — **unreferenced repository files are not copied**. Hermes scans the complete quarantined bundle before install.
- **Rebuild notes:** Copy only referenced support files so a hostile repo can't smuggle extra content, and record provenance (URL + hash + scanner version + findings) in a lock file. A better version would sign the lock entries so tampering is detectable.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — hub state paths and content hashing in `tools/skills_hub.py` (`content_hash` imported at `:38`).

### Advisory NVIDIA SkillEvaluator Tier 1 scan  `id: docs-features.skills-tier1-advisory`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `skills.tier1_advisory` in `config.yaml`; every `hermes skills install`; dashboard Browse-hub scan button (`tier1` response field)
- **What it does:** Runs NVIDIA SkillEvaluator Tier 1 checks on every hub install as a **second opinion** alongside the built-in security scanner.
- **How it works:** Tier 1 is **deterministic and keyless** — PII detection (leaked emails, personal paths, connection strings), unicode-smuggling detection, script lint, license compliance, and a static security scan via NVIDIA SkillSpector. The scan is **advisory only**: findings are printed with file and line before the install confirmation, and the install continues. It runs **alongside** the built-in skills guard, which stays the enforcement layer, and only when the optional `skillevaluator` binary is on PATH.
- **Inputs / options:** Install the optional binaries: `uv tool install --python 3.13 "skillevaluator @ git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator.git@v0.1.0"` and `uv tool install "git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector.git@v2.9.5"` (the second powers the `security` check; without it that check simply reports "not run"). Disable with `skills.tier1_advisory: false`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Findings printed before the install confirmation; the dashboard's Browse-hub scan button returns the same data in its response `tier1` field alongside the built-in scanner's verdict.
- **Config / env:** `skills.tier1_advisory` (default `true` — `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2297`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Without the binary on PATH the scan is silently skipped** — which is why it's on by default ("a no-op without the binary installed"). Findings that look like real credentials (private keys, cloud access keys, tokens, credentialed connection strings) are **highlighted in red**. **PII-class findings are informational** — the upstream scanner has known false-positive classes (e.g. `git@github.com` SSH syntax, documentation example emails), so they never block anything.
- **Rebuild notes:** Layer an advisory third-party scanner beside your own enforcement scanner, defaulting on because it no-ops when absent. A better version would cache scanner results by content hash so re-installs don't re-scan.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — default `True` with the exact rationale ("On by default because it is a no-op without the binary installed") at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2286-2297`.

### External skill directories (`skills.external_dirs`)  `id: docs-features.skills-external-dirs`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `skills.external_dirs` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`
- **What it does:** Tells Hermes to scan additional skill folders — e.g. a shared `~/.agents/skills/` used by multiple AI tools — alongside the local one.
- **How it works:** Documented behaviour: **Create locally, update in place** — new agent-created skills are written to `~/.hermes/skills/`, while existing skills are modified where they are found, **including skills under `external_dirs`**, when the agent uses `skill_manage` actions such as `patch`, `edit`, `write_file`, `remove_file`, or `delete`. **Local precedence** — if the same skill name exists in both the local dir and an external dir, the local version wins. **Full integration** — external skills appear in the system prompt index, `skills_list`, `skill_view`, and as `/skill-name` slash commands, no different from local skills. **Non-existent paths are silently skipped** — useful for optional shared directories not present on every machine.
- **Inputs / options:** A YAML list under `skills.external_dirs`, e.g. `~/.agents/skills`, `/home/shared/team-skills`, `${SKILLS_REPO}/skills`. Paths support `~` expansion and `${VAR}` environment variable substitution.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Extra skills in the index; possible writes into external dirs.
- **Config / env:** `skills.external_dirs` (default `[]` — `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2250`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **External dirs are not a write-protection boundary** — if an external skill directory is writable by the Hermes process, agent-managed skill updates can change files in it; use filesystem permissions or a separate profile/toolset setup if shared external skills must stay read-only. Documented example shows four skills (two local, two external) all appearing in the index, with a locally-created `my-custom-workflow` shadowing the external version.
- **Rebuild notes:** State explicitly that a scan path is not a permission boundary, and rely on the filesystem for read-only enforcement. A better version would offer a `read_only: true` flag per external dir enforced in the writer.
- **Verification:** partial — implemented as documented, but the config comment at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2246-2248` says external dirs are "**Read-only** — skill creation always goes to ~/.hermes/skills/", which reads as a stronger guarantee than the page's explicit "not a write-protection boundary" (the page is the accurate one, since `patch`/`edit` do modify external skills in place — an internal doc/comment inconsistency).

### Project-local skills  `id: docs-features.skills-project-local`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `<project-root>/.hermes/skills/` and `<project-root>/.agents/skills/`
- **What it does:** Lets a repo carry its own skills, active only for sessions started inside that project.
- **How it works:** When Hermes launches inside a git checkout it looks in `<project-root>/.hermes/skills/` (Hermes-native location) and `<project-root>/.agents/skills/` (cross-tool convention shared with other agent CLIs). **The project root is the nearest ancestor directory containing `.git` (worktrees and submodules count).** Project skills are the **highest-precedence tier**: `project → local (~/.hermes/skills/) → external_dirs`; a project skill named `deploy` overrides a same-named profile or bundled skill for sessions inside that repo. Project skills are tagged `[project]` in the agent's skill index so provenance stays visible.
- **Inputs / options:** Two discovery paths; precedence chain as above.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Repo-local skills in the index, tagged `[project]`.
- **Config / env:** `skills.project_discovery` (default `true` — `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2257`); `skills.trusted_project_dirs` (default `[]` — `:2260`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Like external dirs, project skill directories are treated as repo-owned**: autonomous skill maintenance (the curator) never modifies them, and new agent-created skills always go to `~/.hermes/skills/`. Set `skills.project_discovery: false` to turn the feature off entirely (no scanning, no notices).
- **Rebuild notes:** Resolve the project root by walking to `.git` and support both a native and a cross-tool path so repos don't need harness-specific directories. A better version would allow a per-repo config file to name additional skill roots.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — both paths and the precedence rule documented in the config comment at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2251-2257` ("`<root>/.hermes/skills/` and `<root>/.agents/skills/` are sourced as the highest-precedence skill tier").

### Project-skill trust (`hermes skills trust` / `untrust`)  `id: docs-features.skills-project-trust`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes skills trust [path]`, `hermes skills untrust`
- **What it does:** Gates repo-local skills behind an explicit per-repo trust decision, because skills are procedure documents the agent follows.
- **How it works:** Hermes does **not** auto-load project skills from arbitrary cloned repos. The first time you run Hermes in a repo with project skills, the banner shows the notice `◆ 3 project skill(s) found in /home/you/myproject but not loaded — run \`hermes skills trust\` to enable them.` Trust the repo once and the decision persists.
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes skills trust` (trust the current repo — `path` defaults to the enclosing git checkout of cwd); `hermes skills trust ~/myproject` (explicit path); `hermes skills untrust` (revoke). Both take only `-h/--help` besides the optional path.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Trusted roots stored as absolute paths in `skills.trusted_project_dirs` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.
- **Config / env:** `skills.trusted_project_dirs` (`hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2260`), `skills.project_discovery`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Non-interactive surfaces (cron, API, ACP) inherit your interactive trust decision — they never prompt and never auto-trust.** The project root resolves from the surface's working directory (a cron job's `workdir`, via the same mechanism the terminal tool uses): a cron job whose `workdir` is inside a previously-trusted repo loads that repo's project skills; a job in an untrusted or undecided repo loads none.
- **Rebuild notes:** Make trust a repo-level, explicitly-recorded decision, surfaced in the banner rather than as a blocking prompt, and let headless surfaces inherit it without ever auto-granting. A better version would scope trust to a commit range so a `git pull` re-asks.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `trust` / `untrust` subcommands with the exact descriptions "Trust a project so its repo-local skills (./.hermes/skills, ./.agents/skills) load" and "Revoke project-skill trust for a repo" (evidence: `cli_help/skills.txt`, `cli_help/skills__trust.txt`); config key managed by those commands per `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2258-2260`.

### Project-skill scan-time quarantine  `id: docs-features.skills-project-quarantine`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** automatic on every project-skill index build; cache at `~/.hermes/cache/project_skill_scans/`
- **What it does:** Closes the gap between repo-level trust and per-pull content changes by scanning every project skill before it enters the index.
- **How it works:** Every project skill is scanned with **the same security scanner used for Skills Hub installs**. A skill whose verdict is **dangerous** (prompt-injection directives, credential-exfiltration commands, hidden-text tricks) is quarantined: **it does not appear in the skill index, `skills_list`, or slash commands, and refuses to load by name with an explanatory error.** Scans are content-hash cached under `~/.hermes/cache/project_skill_scans/` (**never inside your repo**) and re-run automatically when the skill's content changes.
- **Inputs / options:** n/a (automatic once a repo is trusted)
- **Outputs / side effects:** Cache entries under `~/.hermes/cache/project_skill_scans/`; quarantined skills silently absent from every surface except the by-name load error.
- **Config / env:** governed by `skills.project_discovery` and trust.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Trust is a repo-level decision, but a repo's skill content changes with every `git pull` — this is the mitigation.
- **Rebuild notes:** Re-scan on content hash change, cache outside the repo, and hide dangerous content from every discovery surface while still explaining the refusal on direct load. A better version would show a one-line quarantine notice in the banner so a silently-missing skill is explicable.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — the same guard used for hub installs (`tools/skills_guard.py`), with its `INSTALL_POLICY` verdict table at `:69-72`.

### Skill bundles  `id: docs-features.skills-bundles`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `~/.hermes/skill-bundles/<slug>.yaml`; `/<bundle-name>`; `hermes bundles`; `/bundles`
- **What it does:** Tiny YAML files grouping several skills under a single slash command — running `/<bundle-name>` loads every skill listed at once.
- **How it works:** Bundles live in `~/.hermes/skill-bundles/<slug>.yaml`. The agent receives all listed skills loaded into one user message, with any text after the slash command attached as a user instruction. **Dispatch is centralized in the same place as individual skill commands**, so bundles work in every surface.
- **Inputs / options:** **YAML fields:** `name` (optional — defaults to the filename stem; the bundle's display name, normalized to a hyphen slug for the slash command, e.g. `Backend Dev` → `/backend-dev`); `description` (optional — short text shown in `/bundles` and `hermes bundles list`); `skills` (**required, non-empty list** — skill names or paths relative to your skills directory, using the same identifier you'd pass to `/<skill-name>`); `instruction` (optional — extra guidance prepended to the loaded skill content, useful for codifying "how we always use these together"). **CLI:** `hermes bundles list`; `hermes bundles show <name>`; `hermes bundles create <name> [--skill/-s SKILL ...] [--description/-d DESC] [--instruction/-i TEXT] [--force/-f]` (omit `--skill` flags to enter them one per line interactively); `hermes bundles delete <name>`; `hermes bundles reload` (re-scan `~/.hermes/skill-bundles/` and report changes). **In-chat:** `/bundles` lists every installed bundle and its skills.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A YAML file per bundle; a new slash command.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Bundles take precedence over individual skills when slugs collide** — if you name a bundle `research` and also have a skill called `research`, `/research` invokes the bundle; this is intentional. **Missing skills are skipped, not fatal** — the bundle loads what resolves and the agent gets a note listing what was skipped. **Bundles work in every surface** (interactive CLI, TUI, dashboard chat, and every gateway platform). **Bundles do not invalidate the prompt cache** — they generate a fresh user message at invocation time, the same way `/<skill-name>` does, with no system-prompt mutation. **A bundle is just a YAML alias — it doesn't install skills for you**; the skills must already be present in `~/.hermes/skills/` or an external skill directory.
- **Rebuild notes:** Implement bundles as a pure alias that expands to the same user-message path as a single skill, so prompt caching and surface coverage are inherited for free. A better version would let a bundle pin skill versions so a team profile is reproducible.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — all five subcommands and every `create` flag confirmed by `hermes bundles --help` and `hermes bundles create --help`, including the help text "Skill bundles let you load several skills under one slash command. `/<bundle>` from the CLI or gateway loads every referenced skill at once." (evidence: `cli_help/bundles.txt`, `cli_help/bundles__create.txt`).

### Agent-managed skills (`skill_manage` tool)  `id: docs-features.skills-skill-manage`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** tool `skill_manage`
- **What it does:** Lets the agent create, update and delete its own skills — the agent's **procedural memory**: when it figures out a non-trivial workflow, it saves the approach as a skill for future reuse.
- **How it works:** Skills and memory work together in the self-improvement loop — **memory stores small durable facts that should always be in context, while skills store longer procedures that should load only when relevant**. The background review can suggest or stage skill changes after a session. The system prompt asks the agent to record a non-trivial workflow with `skill_manage` for future reuse; in practice that covers: when it worked out a multi-step workflow worth repeating; when it hit errors or dead ends and found the working path; when the user corrected its approach.
- **Inputs / options:** Six actions. `create` — new skill from scratch; params `name`, `content` (full SKILL.md), optional `category`. `patch` — targeted fixes (**preferred**); params `name`, `old_string`, `new_string`. `edit` — major structural rewrites; params `name`, `content` (full SKILL.md replacement). `delete` — remove a skill entirely; param `name`. `write_file` — add/update supporting files; params `name`, `file_path`, `file_content`. `remove_file` — remove a supporting file; params `name`, `file_path`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Skill files created/modified/deleted on disk (in `~/.hermes/skills/` for new skills, in place for existing ones including external dirs).
- **Config / env:** `skills.write_approval`, `skills.guard_agent_created`, `skills.ledger`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **`patch` is preferred for updates** — more token-efficient than `edit` because only the changed text appears in the tool call. The curator never modifies project or external repo-owned skill directories.
- **Rebuild notes:** Give the agent a patch action distinct from a full rewrite so incremental edits are cheap, and route all writes through one tool so a single gate can cover them. A better version would auto-verify the edited SKILL.md still parses before committing.
- **Verification:** partial — implemented as documented; additionally `skills.ledger` (default `true`, `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2311-2317`) appends every skill mutation to `~/.hermes/skills/.curator_ledger.jsonl` with before/after file hashes and content-addressed blobs under `~/.hermes/.curator_backups/blobs/`, enabling `hermes curator ledger` and `hermes curator rollback <entry-id>` — **not mentioned on this page** (doc gap).

### Gating agent skill writes (`skills.write_approval`)  `id: docs-features.skills-write-approval`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `skills.write_approval` in `config.yaml`; `/skills pending|diff|approve|reject|approval`
- **What it does:** Requires human approval before any agent skill write lands, instead of the default free-write behaviour.
- **How it works:** By default the agent writes skills freely — including from the background self-improvement review that runs after a turn. When `write_approval: true`, **every `skill_manage` write (create / edit / patch / delete / write_file / remove_file) is staged instead of committed** — a SKILL.md is too large to review inline, so **staging applies regardless of whether the write came from a foreground turn or the background review**. Staged writes **survive restarts under `~/.hermes/pending/skills/`** and are reviewed with the same approve/deny flow as dangerous commands.
- **Inputs / options:** `skills.write_approval: false` (default — write freely) | `true` (require approval). Five review commands: `/skills pending` (list staged skill writes + a one-line gist each); `/skills diff <id>` (full unified diff — best viewed in CLI or dashboard); `/skills approve <id>` (apply it, or `all`); `/skills reject <id>` (drop it, or `all`); `/skills approval on` (turn the gate on, or `off`, and persist it).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Pending JSON files under `~/.hermes/pending/skills/`; writes applied or dropped on decision.
- **Config / env:** `skills.write_approval` (`hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2309`); memory's counterpart is `memory.write_approval` (`:2072`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** The review surface works in the interactive CLI and on messaging platforms — **diff output is truncated for chat bubbles; read the full diff on the CLI or in the pending JSON file**. Documented motivations: small models that misjudge what they learned, secure environments, or just wanting eyes on the self-improvement loop. **The separate `skills.guard_agent_created` setting is a content scanner (dangerous-pattern heuristics), not an approval gate — the two are independent.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Always stage (never prompt inline) for artifacts too large to review in a chat bubble, and persist the queue so a restart doesn't drop pending work. A better version would show the diff rendered in the dashboard with an approve button rather than by id.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — default `False` with the full staging/review semantics spelled out at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2303-2309` (including "/skills diff \<id\> (full diff — CLI/dashboard/file, never crammed into a chat bubble)").

### `skills.guard_agent_created` (content scanner on agent writes)  `id: docs-features.skills-guard-agent-created`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `skills.guard_agent_created` in `config.yaml`
- **What it does:** Runs the keyword/pattern security scanner on skills the agent writes via `skill_manage` (create/edit/patch).
- **How it works:** **Off by default** — the config rationale is that the agent can already execute the same code paths via `terminal()` with no gate, so the scan adds friction (blocking skills that merely *mention* risky keywords in prose) without meaningful security. When on, a dangerous verdict surfaces as a **tool error to the agent**, which can retry with the flagged content removed.
- **Inputs / options:** `skills.guard_agent_created: true|false` (default `false`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** A tool error instead of a written skill when the verdict is dangerous.
- **Config / env:** `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2285`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **External hub installs (trusted/community sources) are always scanned regardless of this setting** — this flag only governs agent-authored content. Independent of `skills.write_approval` (scanner vs approval gate). Cross-reference: `/user-guide/configuration#guard-on-agent-created-skill-writes`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Don't scan content the agent could already execute unscanned by another path — it's friction without a security gain; keep untrusted third-party content always scanned. A better version would scan agent-written *scripts* while leaving prose alone.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — default `False` with the exact rationale at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2277-2285`.

### Skills Hub (`hermes skills`)  `id: docs-features.skills-hub`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes skills <subcommand>`; `/skills <subcommand>` in chat
- **What it does:** Browses, searches, installs, inspects, audits, updates and manages skills from online registries, skills.sh, direct well-known skill endpoints, and official optional skills.
- **How it works:** Implemented in `tools/skills_hub.py` with the scanner in `tools/skills_guard.py`. Paths are **resolved per call (not frozen at import) so the profile override is honored** — import-time constants leaked across profiles in single-process multi-profile runtimes; legacy names (`SKILLS_DIR`, …) are re-exposed via `__getattr__` for compatibility (`tools/skills_hub.py:47-53`).
- **Inputs / options:** Twenty-one subcommands from `hermes skills --help`: `trust`, `untrust`, `browse`, `search`, `install`, `inspect`, `list`, `check`, `update`, `audit`, `uninstall`, `reset`, `list-modified`, `diff`, `opt-out`, `opt-in`, `repair-official`, `publish`, `snapshot`, `tap`, `config`. Documented command examples: `hermes skills browse`, `browse --source official`, `search kubernetes`, `search react --source skills-sh`, `search https://mintlify.com/docs --source well-known`, `inspect openai/skills/k8s`, `install openai/skills/k8s`, `install official/security/1password`, `install skills-sh/vercel-labs/json-render/json-render-react --force`, `install well-known:https://mintlify.com/docs/.well-known/skills/mintlify`, `install https://sharethis.chat/SKILL.md`, `install https://example.com/SKILL.md --name my-skill`, `list --source hub`, `check`, `update`, `audit`, `uninstall k8s`, `reset google-workspace`, `reset google-workspace --restore`, `publish skills/my-skill --to github --repo owner/repo`, `snapshot export setup.json`, `tap add myorg/skills-repo`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Skills installed into `~/.hermes/skills/`; hub state in `.hub/`.
- **Config / env:** `GITHUB_TOKEN` for GitHub API rate limits.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **GitHub rate limits** — hub operations use the GitHub API, limited to **60 requests/hour unauthenticated**; set `GITHUB_TOKEN` in `.env` to raise it to **5,000 requests/hour**; the error message includes an actionable hint when this happens.
- **Rebuild notes:** Resolve profile-scoped paths per call, never at import, in any multi-profile process. A better version would batch GitHub API calls and cache index responses to stay under the anonymous limit.
- **Verification:** partial — 21 subcommands confirmed (evidence: `cli_help/skills.txt`), but the page's command list never mentions **`list-modified`** ("List bundled skills you've edited (which `hermes update` keeps)"), **`diff`** ("Show how your copy of a bundled skill differs from the stock version"), **`repair-official`** ("Backfill or restore official optional skills from repo source") or **`config`** ("Interactive skill configuration — enable/disable individual skills") outside of passing references (doc gap).

### Skills Hub sources  `id: docs-features.skills-hub-sources`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `--source` on `hermes skills browse` / `search`; identifier prefixes on `install` / `inspect`
- **What it does:** Defines the eight documented skill sources and their identifier shapes.
- **How it works:** Documented table: **`official`** (`official/security/1password`) — optional skills shipped with Hermes, source in repo `optional-skills/`, install with built-in trust. **`skills-sh`** (`skills-sh/vercel-labs/agent-skills/vercel-react-best-practices`) — Vercel's public skills directory; searchable via `--source skills-sh`; Hermes resolves alias-style skills when the skills.sh slug differs from the repo folder. **`well-known`** (`well-known:https://mintlify.com/docs/.well-known/skills/mintlify`) — skills served directly from `/.well-known/skills/index.json` on a website; a web discovery convention, not a centralized hub; reference server implementation `vercel-labs/skills-handler`. **`url`** (`https://sharethis.chat/SKILL.md`) — direct HTTP(S) URL to `SKILL.md` plus explicitly referenced support files. **`github`** (`openai/skills/k8s`) — direct GitHub repo/path installs and custom taps. **`clawhub`** (clawhub.ai) — third-party skills marketplace. **`lobehub`** (lobehub.com; public agents index chat-agents.lobehub.com; backing repo `lobehub/lobe-chat-agents`) — Hermes searches and converts agent entries into installable skills. **`browse-sh`** (browse.sh) — Browserbase's catalog of **200+ site-specific browser-automation SKILL.md files** (Airbnb, Amazon, arXiv, 12306.cn, Etsy, Xero, and many more); catalog API `https://browse.sh/api/skills`; trust level `community`; identifiers of the form `browse-sh/<hostname>/<task-id>` matching the browse.sh catalog slug; **content is resolved through the per-skill detail endpoint (`/api/skills/<slug>` → `skillMdUrl`), not through the catalog's GitHub `sourceUrl`**.
- **Inputs / options:** `--source` accepts `all`, `official`, `skills-sh`, `well-known`, `github`, `clawhub`, `lobehub`, `browse-sh`, `nvidia`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `huggingface`, `voltagent`, `gstack`, `minimax`. `hermes skills search` also takes `--limit LIMIT` and `--json` (output JSON instead of a table — full identifiers, scripting-friendly); `hermes skills browse` also takes `--page PAGE` (default 1) and `--size SIZE` (default 20).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Search/browse results; installs from the chosen source.
- **Config / env:** `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Documented default GitHub taps browsable without setup: `openai/skills`, `anthropics/skills`, `huggingface/skills`, `NVIDIA/skills` (NVIDIA-verified skills with signed `skill.oms.sig` + governance `skill-card.md`), `garrytan/gstack`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Treat "well-known endpoint" and "direct URL" as first-class sources so authors can publish without a registry. A better version would let `--source` accept several values at once.
- **Verification:** doc drift — the CLI's `--source` choices include **`nvidia`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `huggingface`, `voltagent`, `gstack`, `minimax`** as provider filters (evidence: `cli_help/skills__search.txt`, `cli_help/skills__browse.txt`); the page's source table lists only eight and never mentions `voltagent` or `minimax` at all. Also, `--limit` / `--json` on `search` and `--page` / `--size` on `browse` are undocumented on this page.

### Direct URL skill installs (`url` source)  `id: docs-features.skills-url-install`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes skills install <https URL to SKILL.md>`; `/skills install <url> --name <name>`
- **What it does:** Installs a `SKILL.md` from any HTTP(S) URL — useful when an author hosts a skill on their own site with no hub listing and no GitHub path.
- **How it works:** Hermes also fetches explicitly referenced files under `references/`, `templates/`, `scripts/`, `assets/` and `examples/`, then scans and installs the complete bundle. **Scope: `SKILL.md` plus exact referenced support files in the allowlisted directories — Hermes does not enumerate or copy unrelated files from the host.** The URL is stored as the install identifier, so `hermes skills update` re-fetches from the same URL automatically.
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes skills install <url>`; `--name NAME` (override the skill name — "useful when installing from a URL whose SKILL.md has no `name:` frontmatter"); `--category CATEGORY` (category folder to install into); `--force` (install despite blocked scan verdict); `--yes`/`-y` (skip the confirmation prompt, needed in TUI mode). Documented examples: `hermes skills install https://sharethis.chat/SKILL.md`, `hermes skills install https://example.com/my-skill/SKILL.md --category productivity`, `hermes skills install https://example.com/SKILL.md --name sharethis-chat`, and in chat `/skills install https://example.com/SKILL.md --name sharethis-chat`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Skill installed with the URL recorded as its identifier.
- **Config / env:** URL safety checks via `tools/url_safety.py` and `tools/website_policy.py` (imported in `tools/skills_hub.py:40-41`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Name resolution, in order:** (1) `name:` field in the SKILL.md YAML frontmatter (recommended — every well-formed skill has one); (2) parent directory name from the URL path (e.g. `.../my-skill/SKILL.md` → `my-skill`, or `.../my-skill.md` → `my-skill`) **when it's a valid identifier (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$`)**; (3) interactive prompt on a terminal with a TTY; (4) on non-interactive surfaces (the `/skills install` slash command inside the TUI, gateway platforms, scripts) a **clean error pointing at the `--name` override**. **Trust level is always `community`** — the same security scan runs as for every other source.
- **Rebuild notes:** Allowlist the support directories you'll fetch and never enumerate the host; degrade gracefully through a documented name-resolution chain ending in an actionable error. A better version would pin the content hash at install so `update` can show a diff before re-fetching.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — install flags confirmed by `hermes skills install --help` including the `--name` help text "Override the skill name (useful when installing from a URL whose SKILL.md has no `name:` frontmatter)" (evidence: `cli_help/skills__install.txt`); URL-safety imports at `tools/skills_hub.py:40-41`.

### Skill security scanning, `--force`, and trust levels  `id: docs-features.skills-trust-levels`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** every hub install; `--force` flag
- **What it does:** Runs a security scanner on all hub-installed skills and applies a per-trust-level install policy.
- **How it works:** The scanner checks for **data exfiltration, prompt injection, destructive commands, supply-chain signals, and other threats**. `INSTALL_POLICY` in `tools/skills_guard.py:69-72` maps `(trust level) → (safe, caution, dangerous)` verdict handling — e.g. `"builtin": ("allow", "allow", "allow")`, `"trusted": ("allow", "allow", "block")`.
- **Inputs / options:** `--force` on `hermes skills install` ("Install despite blocked scan verdict"). Four trust levels: **`builtin`** (ships with Hermes) — always trusted; **`official`** (`optional-skills/` in the repo) — built-in trust, no third-party warning; **`trusted`** (trusted registries/repos such as `openai/skills`, `anthropics/skills`, `huggingface/skills`, `NVIDIA/skills`) — more permissive policy than community sources; **`community`** (everything else — skills.sh, well-known endpoints, custom GitHub repos, most marketplaces) — non-dangerous findings can be overridden with `--force`, `dangerous` verdicts stay blocked.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Install allowed, warned, or blocked; findings recorded in `skills/.hub/lock.json`.
- **Config / env:** `skills.tier1_advisory` for the advisory second opinion.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **`--force` can override policy blocks for caution/warn-style findings; `--force` does NOT override a `dangerous` scan verdict.** Official optional skills (`official/...`) are treated as built-in trust and do not show the third-party warning panel. `hermes skills inspect ...` surfaces upstream metadata when available: repo URL, skills.sh detail page URL, install command, weekly installs, upstream security audit statuses, and well-known index/endpoint URLs.
- **Rebuild notes:** Encode trust × verdict as an explicit policy table and make `dangerous` non-overridable at every level below builtin. A better version would show the specific findings inline in the confirmation prompt with line numbers.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `TRUSTED_REPOS = {"openai/skills", "anthropics/skills", "huggingface/skills", "NVIDIA/skills"}` at `tools/skills_guard.py:58-67` and the `INSTALL_POLICY` table at `:69-72` (`"trusted": ("allow", "allow", "block")`).

### Skill update lifecycle (`check` / `update`)  `id: docs-features.skills-update-lifecycle`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes skills check`, `hermes skills update [name] [--force]`
- **What it does:** Re-checks upstream copies of installed hub skills and reinstalls only those that changed.
- **How it works:** The hub tracks enough provenance to detect drift using **the stored source identifier plus the current upstream bundle content hash**.
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes skills check` (report which installed hub skills changed upstream); `hermes skills update` (reinstall only the skills with updates available); `hermes skills update react` (update one specific installed hub skill — the positional `name` defaults to all outdated skills); `hermes skills update react --force` ("Overwrite skills you have edited locally (they are skipped by default)"); `hermes skills audit` (re-scan all hub skills for security); `hermes skills uninstall <name>`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Skills reinstalled from upstream; `.hub/lock.json` updated.
- **Config / env:** `GITHUB_TOKEN` for rate limits.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Skills you have edited locally (the on-disk content no longer matches the hash recorded at install time) are skipped by `hermes skills update` so your changes are never silently overwritten** — pass `--force` to replace them anyway.
- **Rebuild notes:** Detect drift by content hash on both sides and skip locally-edited copies by default. A better version would offer a three-way merge instead of skip-or-overwrite.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `--force` help text matches verbatim (evidence: `cli_help/skills__update.txt`).

### Publishing a custom skill tap  `id: docs-features.skills-taps`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes skills tap add|list|remove`; `~/.hermes/skills/.hub/taps.json`
- **What it does:** Lets you share a curated set of skills as a **tap** — a GitHub repository other Hermes users add with one command. No server, no registry sign-up, no release pipeline.
- **How it works:** A tap is any GitHub repo (public or private — private needs `GITHUB_TOKEN`) with each skill in its own directory under the tap's root path (default `skills/`). **The directory name becomes the skill's install slug.** Each skill directory must contain a `SKILL.md` with standard frontmatter (`name`, `description`, plus optional `metadata.hermes.tags`, `version`, `author`, `platforms`, `metadata.hermes.config`). Subdirectories `references/`, `templates/`, `scripts/`, `assets/` are downloaded alongside `SKILL.md` at install time. **Hermes discovers skills by listing every subdirectory of the tap path and probing each for `SKILL.md`.**
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes skills tap list` (show all configured taps and the effective path per tap); `hermes skills tap add myorg/skills-repo` (add, default path `skills/`); `hermes skills tap remove myorg/skills-repo`. In-session equivalents: `/skills tap list`, `/skills tap add myorg/skills-repo`, `/skills tap remove myorg/skills-repo`. Install a single skill without adding a tap: `hermes skills install owner/repo/skills/my-workflow`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Taps stored in `~/.hermes/skills/.hub/taps.json` (created on demand).
- **Config / env:** `GITHUB_TOKEN` for private repos and rate limits.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Skills whose directory name starts with `.` or `_` are ignored.** **Non-default paths** — the CLI defaults new taps to `path: "skills/"`; edit `taps.json` directly for a different path, e.g. `{"taps": [{"repo": "my-org/platform-docs", "path": "internal/skills/"}]}`. **New taps are assigned `community` trust by default** — skills from them run through the standard security scan and show the third-party warning panel on first install; higher trust requires adding the repo to `TRUSTED_REPOS` **(a Hermes core PR)**.
- **Rebuild notes:** Make a plain GitHub repo the distribution unit and discover by directory probing, so publishing needs no infrastructure. A better version would let a tap declare its own trust attestation (signature) so trust doesn't require a core PR.
- **Verification:** partial — tap subcommands confirmed (`list`, `add`, `remove` — evidence: `cli_help/skills__tap.txt`); **doc drift on the location of `TRUSTED_REPOS`**: the page says "add its repo to `TRUSTED_REPOS` in `tools/skills_hub.py`", but the set is actually defined at **`tools/skills_guard.py:58`** and merely *imported* into `tools/skills_hub.py:38` (the code comment at `tools/skills_hub.py:685` names `tools/skills_guard.py::TRUSTED_REPOS` correctly).

### Tap category groupings (`skills.sh.json`)  `id: docs-features.skills-tap-groupings`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `<tap-repo>/skills.sh.json`
- **What it does:** Lets a GitHub tap ship real category labels for the Skills Hub page instead of a tag-derived guess.
- **How it works:** A tap may ship a `skills.sh.json` at its repo root following the skills.sh schema (`https://skills.sh/schemas/skills.sh.schema.json`). Its `groupings` — each with a `title` and a list of skill names — are **read at index time** and become the category labels shown in the Skills Hub page. **This is generic: any tap that ships the file gets real categorization, with no Hermes-side changes required.**
- **Inputs / options:** JSON with `$schema` and `groupings: [{title, skills: [...]}, ...]`. Documented example uses titles `"Inference AI"` (skills `dynamo-recipe-runner`, `dynamo-router-sla`) and `"Decision Optimization"` (skills `cuopt-developer`, `cuopt-install`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Category labels in the Skills Hub UI.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Without the file, categories fall back to a tag-derived guess.
- **Rebuild notes:** Adopt an existing ecosystem schema for grouping metadata so taps written for one tool work in another. A better version would validate the file against the schema and warn on unknown skill names.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — tap indexing in `tools/skills_hub.py`.

### Bundled skill updates & `hermes skills reset`  `id: docs-features.skills-reset`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes skills reset <name> [--restore] [--yes]`; `/skills reset <name>`
- **What it does:** Clears a bundled skill's "user-modified" tracking so `hermes update` stops skipping it, and optionally restores the pristine bundled version.
- **How it works:** Hermes ships bundled skills in `skills/` inside the repo. On install and every `hermes update`, a sync pass copies them into `~/.hermes/skills/` and records a manifest at `~/.hermes/skills/.bundled_manifest` mapping each skill name to the content hash at sync time (the **origin hash**). On each sync Hermes recomputes the hash of your local copy and compares: **unchanged** → safe to pull upstream changes, copy the new bundled version in, record the new origin hash; **changed** → treated as **user-modified and skipped forever**, so your edits never get stomped. The sharp edge: if you edit a bundled skill and later copy-paste the bundled version back from `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/skills/`, the manifest still holds the *old* origin hash, so sync keeps flagging it as user-modified. `hermes skills reset` is the escape hatch.
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes skills reset <name>` (safe — clears the manifest entry; your current copy is preserved but the next sync re-baselines against it); `--restore` (also delete your local copy and re-copy the current bundled version); `--yes`/`-y` (skip the `--restore` confirmation, e.g. in scripts or TUI mode). Slash equivalents: `/skills reset google-workspace`, `/skills reset google-workspace --restore`. Related: `hermes skills list-modified` (list bundled skills you've edited), `hermes skills diff` (show how your copy differs from stock).
- **Outputs / side effects:** `.bundled_manifest` entry removed; with `--restore`, the local copy is deleted and re-copied from the bundle.
- **Config / env:** `~/.hermes/skills/.bundled_manifest`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Profiles** — each profile has its own `.bundled_manifest` under its own `HERMES_HOME`, so `hermes -p coder skills reset <name>` only affects that profile.
- **Rebuild notes:** Track an origin hash per bundled file and never overwrite a divergent copy; provide an explicit re-baseline command for the copy-paste-back case. A better version would auto-detect that a local copy is byte-identical to the *current* bundle and re-baseline silently.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — help text matches verbatim: "Clear a bundled skill's entry from the sync manifest (~/.hermes/skills/.bundled_manifest) so future 'hermes update' runs stop marking it as user-modified. Pass --restore to also replace the current copy with the bundled version." (evidence: `cli_help/skills__reset.txt`).

### `/skills` slash commands  `id: docs-features.skills-slash-hub`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `/skills <subcommand>` inside chat
- **What it does:** Exposes the same hub commands as `hermes skills` from inside a session.
- **How it works:** Dispatch is shared with the CLI implementation.
- **Inputs / options:** Documented examples: `/skills browse`; `/skills search react --source skills-sh`; `/skills search https://mintlify.com/docs --source well-known`; `/skills inspect skills-sh/vercel-labs/json-render/json-render-react`; `/skills install openai/skills/skill-creator --force`; `/skills check`; `/skills update`; `/skills reset google-workspace`; `/skills list`. Plus the approval-gate set (`/skills pending`, `/skills diff <id>`, `/skills approve <id>`, `/skills reject <id>`, `/skills approval on|off`) and the tap set (`/skills tap list|add|remove`).
- **Outputs / side effects:** Same as the CLI equivalents.
- **Config / env:** same as the CLI.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Official optional skills still use identifiers like `official/security/1password` and `official/migration/openclaw-migration`. Non-interactive surfaces need `--name` for URL installs (no TTY prompt) and `--yes` in TUI mode.
- **Rebuild notes:** Share one dispatcher between the CLI and the in-chat slash surface so flags stay identical. A better version would render hub browse/search results as an interactive picker in the TUI.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — the `--yes` flag exists specifically for TUI mode ("Skip confirmation prompt (needed in TUI mode)", evidence: `cli_help/skills__install.txt`).

## Page: `cron.md` — Scheduled Tasks (Cron)

### Scheduled tasks (cron) overview  `id: docs-features.cron-overview`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `cronjob` tool; `hermes cron`; `/cron`
- **What it does:** Schedules tasks to run automatically with natural language or cron expressions, exposed through a **single `cronjob` tool** with action-style operations instead of separate schedule/list/remove tools.
- **How it works:** Implementation in `cron/scheduler.py`, `cron/jobs.py`, `cron/scheduler_provider.py`, driven by the gateway daemon. All lifecycle operations are available to Hermes itself through the `cronjob` tool, so jobs can be created, paused, edited and removed by asking in plain language — no CLI required.
- **Inputs / options:** Documented capability list — schedule one-shot or recurring tasks; pause, resume, edit, trigger, and remove jobs; attach zero, one, or multiple skills to a job; deliver results back to the origin chat, local files, or configured platform targets; run in fresh agent sessions with the normal static tool list; run in **no-agent mode** (a script on a schedule, its stdout delivered verbatim, zero LLM involvement).
- **Outputs / side effects:** `~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json`, per-run output under `~/.hermes/cron/output/{job_id}/{timestamp}.md`, the execution ledger at `~/.hermes/cron/executions.db`.
- **Config / env:** `cron.*` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Cron-run sessions cannot recursively create more cron jobs by default** — Hermes disables cron management tools inside cron executions to prevent runaway scheduling loops (opt in with `cron.allow_agent_scheduling`).
- **Rebuild notes:** One action-style tool plus a flat JSON job table is enough; disable the scheduling tool inside scheduled runs by default so recursion needs an explicit opt-in. A better version would express the whole job as a declarative record validated against a schema at write time.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `cron.allow_agent_scheduling` default `False` at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py` cron block with the "cron-librarian" comment.

### Cron model resolution & drift guard  `id: docs-features.cron-model-resolution`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** per-job `--model`/`--provider`; `cron.model` / `cron.model_provider`; `cron.model_drift_guard`
- **What it does:** Decides which model a cron job runs on at fire time, and fails closed rather than silently inheriting a changed global default.
- **How it works:** Resolution order at fire time is **per-job pin → `cron.model` in `config.yaml` → the global default from `hermes model`**. **Per-job pin** is set by *you* via the dashboard, `hermes cron create/edit --model … --provider …`, or by editing `~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json`; once set it sticks. **The agent's `cronjob` tool cannot set or change per-job models — inference pins are user-owned.** **`cron.model` / `cron.model_provider`** is a cron-fleet default: every unpinned job runs on it, independent of your chat model, so switching your chat model with `hermes model` or `/model` never touches the cron fleet. **Global default** applies only when neither is set; in that case Hermes **snapshots** provider and model at creation, and if the global default later changes the job **fails closed**: it skips the run, makes no inference call, and alerts you **once** — the job stays skipped and silent on subsequent ticks until you act or the config is restored (#44585).
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes cron create/edit --model MODEL --provider MODEL_PROVIDER` ("Pin this job to a specific inference model (user-owned; the agent's cronjob tool cannot set this)"; on `edit`, pass an empty string to clear the pin and follow `cron.model` / `model.default`). Config `cron.model` (default `""`), `cron.model_provider` (default `""`), `cron.model_drift_guard` (default `true`). `hermes config set cron.model <name>`, `hermes config set cron.model_drift_guard false`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Jobs may store `model` and `provider` as `null` — when omitted, Hermes resolves them at execution time from global config; they only appear in the job record when a per-job override is set.
- **Config / env:** `cron.model`, `cron.model_provider`, `cron.model_drift_guard`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** For recurring or otherwise repeatable jobs, pin explicitly (`hermes cron edit <job_id> --provider <provider> --model <model>`) to proceed. **A consumed finite one-shot cannot be updated** — create a new future one-shot with an explicit provider and model instead. The guard exists to prevent an unattended job silently inheriting a switch to a paid provider/model; it **does not engage for an axis covered by** `cron.model` or a per-job pin. Disabling `model_drift_guard` turns off **both** the runtime block and the warning shown when global inference settings change; **existing snapshots remain stored**, so setting it back to `true` re-enables protection without recreating jobs. Warning: with the guard disabled, unattended unpinned jobs immediately inherit changed global defaults, so a switch to a paid provider or model can spend money on every scheduled run. Whichever provider a job resolves to, its provider-specific request settings (e.g. `request_overrides` such as `extra_body`/`extra_headers` for custom providers) carry into the scheduled run just like an interactive session. `hermes setup --portal` is recommended for unattended runs since OAuth refresh is automatic.
- **Rebuild notes:** Snapshot the resolved inference identity at creation and fail closed on drift, alerting exactly once; make the fleet default a separate axis from the chat default. A better version would offer a one-command "re-pin all drifting jobs to the current default".
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `cron.model` (`""`), `cron.model_provider` (`""`) and `cron.model_drift_guard` (`True`) present in the cron config block; CLI flag help text matches verbatim (evidence: `cli_help/cron__create.txt`, `cli_help/cron__edit.txt`).

### Per-job reasoning effort  `id: docs-features.cron-reasoning-effort`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes cron create/edit --reasoning-effort <level>`
- **What it does:** Pins a job's own thinking level, independent of the model pin.
- **How it works:** When set, it **overrides both the global `agent.reasoning_effort` and per-model `agent.reasoning_overrides`** for that job's runs (`none` disables thinking).
- **Inputs / options:** Eight levels: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, `ultra`. Pass an **empty string on edit** to clear the pin and follow config again.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Per-job reasoning setting stored on the job record.
- **Config / env:** overrides `agent.reasoning_effort` and `agent.reasoning_overrides` for that job.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Deliberately not exposed on the agent's `cronjob` tool — model configuration stays a user decision.** **Levels a model doesn't support are clamped or omitted by the provider at request time** — pinning `xhigh` on a model that caps at `high` runs at `high`. **The pin has no effect on `no_agent` jobs** (there is no LLM call to tune). Documented use: run heavy scheduled analyses at `high` while cheap recurring jobs run at `minimal`, without touching the global default.
- **Rebuild notes:** Make thinking effort an independent per-job axis from the model pin, and clamp rather than error on unsupported levels. A better version would report the effective (post-clamp) level in the run record.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — all eight levels and the clamping note appear verbatim in `hermes cron create --help` (evidence: `cli_help/cron__create.txt`).

### Creating cron jobs (`/cron add`, `hermes cron create`, natural language)  `id: docs-features.cron-create`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `/cron add`, `hermes cron create`, or plain conversation
- **What it does:** Three equivalent ways to schedule a task.
- **How it works:** All three converge on the `cronjob` tool / job store. `hermes cron create` takes `schedule` and `prompt` as positionals.
- **Inputs / options:** **In chat:** `/cron add "in 30m" "Remind me to check the build"`; `/cron add "every 2h" "Check server status"`; `/cron add "every 1h" "Summarize new feed items" --skill blogwatcher`; `/cron add "every 1h" "Use both skills and combine the result" --skill blogwatcher --skill maps`. **CLI:** `hermes cron create <schedule> [prompt]` with flags `--name NAME`, `--deliver DELIVER`, `--repeat REPEAT`, `--skill SKILLS` (repeatable), `--script SCRIPT`, `--no-agent`, `--monitor-script MONITOR_SCRIPT`, `--monitor-url MONITOR_URL`, `--workdir WORKDIR`, `--model MODEL`, `--provider MODEL_PROVIDER`, `--reasoning-effort REASONING_EFFORT`, `--continuity`, `-h/--help`. **Natural conversation:** e.g. "Every morning at 9am, check Hacker News for AI news and send me a summary on Telegram." — Hermes uses the unified `cronjob` tool internally.
