- **Verification:** implemented as documented — both primitives exist (`delegate_task` in `tools_full.json`; the 14 `kanban_*` tools).

### Kanban core concepts (board, task, link, comment, workspace, dispatcher, tenant)  `id: docs-features.kanban-core-concepts`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** kanban.md → "Core concepts"
- **What it does:** Defines the seven objects the whole system is built from.
- **How it works:** **Board** — a standalone queue with its own SQLite DB, workspaces directory, and dispatcher loop; one install can have many. **Task** — a row with title, optional body, one assignee (a profile name), status, optional tenant namespace, optional idempotency key (dedup for retried automation). **Link** — a `task_links` row recording a parent → child dependency; the dispatcher promotes `todo → ready` when all parents are `done`. **Comment** — the inter-agent protocol; agents and humans append comments, and when a worker is (re-)spawned it reads the full comment thread as part of its context. **Workspace** — the directory a worker operates in (three kinds, see the workspace entry). **Dispatcher** — a long-lived loop that every N seconds (default 60) reclaims stale claims, reclaims crashed workers (PID gone but TTL not yet expired), promotes ready tasks, atomically claims, and spawns assigned profiles. **Tenant** — an optional string namespace *within* a board; one specialist fleet can serve multiple businesses (`--tenant business-a`) with data isolation by workspace path and memory key prefix.
- **Inputs / options:** Task statuses documented as `triage | todo | ready | running | blocked | review | done | archived`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Rows in `tasks`, `task_links`, `task_comments`, `task_events`, `task_runs`.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.dispatch_interval_seconds` (default 60), `kanban.failure_limit` (default 2), `kanban.dispatch_in_gateway` (default true).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Tenants are a soft filter; boards are the hard isolation boundary.** **After `kanban.failure_limit` consecutive spawn failures on the same task (default 2) the dispatcher auto-blocks it with the last error as the reason** — preventing thrashing on tasks whose profile doesn't exist or whose workspace can't mount. **One dispatcher sweeps all boards per tick; workers are spawned with `HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD` pinned so they can't see other boards.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Model dependencies as explicit link rows the dispatcher evaluates, not as fields on the task, so a DAG is expressible without schema changes. A better version would make the status set a first-class enum in the schema so an invalid transition is impossible.
- **Verification:** doc drift — the documented status list omits **`scheduled`**, which `hermes kanban list --status` accepts (`{archived,blocked,done,ready,review,running,scheduled,todo,triage}`, evidence: `cli_help/kanban__list.txt`) and which the `hermes kanban schedule` verb parks tasks in ("Park one or more tasks in Scheduled", evidence: `cli_help/kanban.txt`). Config defaults `dispatch_interval_seconds: 60` and `failure_limit: 2` confirmed in `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py`'s kanban block.

### Kanban workspace kinds (`scratch` / `dir:` / `worktree`)  `id: docs-features.kanban-workspaces`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `--workspace scratch|worktree|worktree:<path>|dir:<path>` on create; `$HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE` in the worker
- **What it does:** Chooses the directory a worker operates in and whether it survives completion.
- **How it works:** **`scratch` (default)** — a fresh tmp dir under `~/.hermes/kanban/workspaces/<id>/` (or `~/.hermes/kanban/boards/<slug>/workspaces/<id>/` on non-default boards), **deleted when the task completes**; scratch is ephemeral by design. Files explicitly declared through `kanban_complete(artifacts=[...])` are **copied into durable per-task attachment storage before cleanup**, and existing deliverable paths in legacy completion summaries receive the same treatment; other scratch files are removed. **A missing declared scratch artifact keeps the task in-flight so the worker can correct the path and retry.** **`dir:<path>`** — an existing shared directory (Obsidian vault, mail ops dir, per-account folder), **preserved on completion**. **`worktree`** — a git worktree under `.worktrees/<id>/` for coding tasks; `worktree:<path>` pins the exact target path; worker-side `git worktree add` creates it, using `--branch` when provided; **preserved on completion**.
- **Inputs / options:** `--workspace scratch | worktree | worktree:<path> | dir:<path>` (default `scratch`); `--branch <name>` for worktree tasks (e.g. `wt/t6-wire`); `--project PROJECT` (link to a project by id or slug, anchoring the worktree under the project's primary repo with a deterministic branch). Board-level default: `kanban.default_workdir`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A directory per task, preserved or deleted per kind; declared artifacts promoted to attachment storage.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.default_workdir` (board-level default applied when neither `--workspace` nor the task overrides it; **per-task `workspace:` still wins**).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **`dir:` must be an absolute path** — relative paths like `dir:../tenants/foo/` are **rejected at dispatch** because they'd resolve against whatever CWD the dispatcher happens to be in, which is ambiguous and a **confused-deputy escape vector**. The path is otherwise trusted — "it's your box, your filesystem, the worker runs with your uid. This is the trusted-local-user threat model; kanban is single-host by design." **The first time a scratch workspace is created on an install, the dispatcher logs a warning and emits a `tip_scratch_workspace` event on the task** (visible via `hermes kanban show <id>`). A board's `default_workdir` is subject to a containment guard (#28818, `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:5941`).
- **Rebuild notes:** Make ephemerality explicit per workspace kind and require the worker to *declare* deliverables before deleting scratch, keeping the task in-flight when a declared path is missing. A better version would let a worker promote a scratch dir to persistent mid-run.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `default_workdir` handling at `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:847-948` and `:3424-3440`; the containment guard at `:5881-5941`; `--workspace` / `--branch` / `--project` flags confirmed (evidence: `cli_help/kanban__create.txt`).

### Kanban boards (multi-project isolation)  `id: docs-features.kanban-boards`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes kanban boards <verb>`; `hermes kanban --board <slug> …`; dashboard board switcher
- **What it does:** Separates unrelated streams of work — one per project, repo, or domain — into isolated queues.
- **How it works:** A new install has exactly one board called `default` (DB at `~/.hermes/kanban.db` for back-compat); the feature is opt-in and single-stream users never need to know about it. **Per-board isolation is absolute:** separate SQLite DB per board (`~/.hermes/kanban/boards/<slug>/kanban.db`); separate `workspaces/` and `logs/` directories; workers spawned for a task see **only** their board's tasks (the dispatcher sets `HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD` in the child env and every `kanban_*` tool reads it); **linking tasks across boards is not allowed** (keeps the schema simple — use free-text mentions and look ids up manually if you really need cross-project refs).
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes kanban boards list`; `hermes kanban boards create <slug> --name "…" --description "…" --icon 🎮 [--switch]`; `hermes kanban --board <slug> <verb>` (operate without switching); `hermes kanban boards switch <slug>`; `hermes kanban boards show` (who's active right now); `hermes kanban boards rename <slug> "New Name"` (**the slug is immutable — it's the directory name**); `hermes kanban boards rm <slug>` (archive — moves the board dir to `boards/_archived/<slug>-<ts>/`, recoverable by moving it back); `hermes kanban boards rm <slug> --delete` (**hard delete — `rm -rf` the board dir, no recovery**). Group flag `--board <slug>`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Board directories, per-board DBs, the `~/.hermes/kanban/current` pointer.
- **Config / env:** env `HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Board resolution order (highest precedence first):** (1) explicit `--board <slug>` on the CLI call; (2) `HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD` env var (set by the dispatcher when spawning a worker, so workers can't see other boards); (3) `~/.hermes/kanban/current` — the slug persisted by `hermes kanban boards switch`; (4) `default`. **Slugs are validated:** lowercase alphanumerics + hyphens + underscores, **1-64 chars**, must start with alphanumeric; uppercase input is auto-downcased; **anything else (slashes, spaces, dots, `..`) is rejected at the CLI layer so path-traversal tricks can't name a board.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Make the board a directory whose slug *is* the path segment, validate the slug at the CLI boundary, and pin workers to a board via env so they physically cannot address another. A better version would support read-only cross-board references for reporting without allowing links.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `hermes kanban boards` subcommand present ("Manage kanban boards (one board per project / workstream)") and the group-level `--board <slug>` flag confirmed (evidence: `cli_help/kanban.txt`, `cli_help/kanban__boards.txt`).

### Kanban boards in the dashboard  `id: docs-features.kanban-boards-dashboard`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** `hermes dashboard` → **Kanban** tab → board switcher at the top
- **What it does:** Adds board management to the dashboard, appearing only once more than one board exists (or any board has tasks).
- **How it works:** Single-board users see only a small **+ New board** button; the switcher is hidden until it matters.
- **Inputs / options:** **Board dropdown** — pick the active board; **your selection is saved to the browser's `localStorage`** so it persists across reloads **without shifting the CLI's `current` pointer out from under a terminal you left open**. **+ New board** — a modal asking for slug, display name, description, and icon, with an option to auto-switch to the new board. **Settings** — a modal for editing the current board's display name, description, and **project directory** (`default_workdir`) — the board-level workspace default every new task inherits (git repo → preserved worktree, plain dir → preserved directory), overridable per task; **clearing the field reverts new tasks to disposable scratch workspaces**. **Archive** — **only shown on non-`default` boards**; confirms, then moves the board dir to `boards/_archived/`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Board records; `localStorage` selection.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.default_workdir` per board.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **All dashboard API endpoints accept `?board=<slug>` for board scoping.** **The events WebSocket is pinned to a board at connection time; switching in the UI opens a fresh WS against the new board.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep the browser's board selection in `localStorage` rather than mutating the CLI's global pointer, so the two surfaces don't fight. A better version would show the board's task counts in the switcher.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — dashboard plugin at `plugins/kanban/`; board-scoped endpoints described in the page's REST table.

### Kanban file attachments  `id: docs-features.kanban-attachments`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** dashboard task drawer → **Attachments** section → *Upload file*; tools `kanban_attach` / `kanban_attach_url` / `kanban_attachments`; CLI `hermes kanban attach` / `attachments` / `attach-rm`
- **What it does:** Lets tasks carry file attachments — PDFs, images, source documents — so a worker has the source material without pasting paths into the body and hoping it finds them.
- **How it works:** **Storage:** files land under `<hermes-home>/kanban/attachments/<task_id>/` for the default board, or `<hermes-home>/kanban/boards/<slug>/attachments/<task_id>/` for a named board. **What the worker sees:** when the dispatcher hands a task to a worker, the worker's context includes an **Attachments** section listing each file's name and its **absolute path**; the worker has full file/terminal tool access so it reads attachments directly (`read_file`, or shell tools like `pdftotext`).
- **Inputs / options:** Dashboard *Upload file* button (**multiple files at once are fine**); **each upload is capped at 25 MB**. Tools: `kanban_attach` (pass bytes inline as base64, stored under the task's attachments dir, 25 MB cap), `kanban_attach_url` (attach by `url`), `kanban_attachments` (list a task's attachments). CLI: `hermes kanban attach` ("Attach a local file to a task"), `hermes kanban attachments` ("List a task's attachments"), `hermes kanban attach-rm` ("Delete an attachment by id"). Env `HERMES_KANBAN_ATTACHMENTS_ROOT` pins a custom location.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Files on disk plus a metadata row. **Removing an attachment deletes both the metadata row and the on-disk file.** The drawer lists each attachment with a download link and a remove (×) control.
- **Config / env:** `HERMES_KANBAN_ATTACHMENTS_ROOT`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Remote terminal backends:** attachment paths resolve directly on the **local** terminal backend, which is the default for Kanban workers; if you run workers on a remote backend (Docker, Modal), **mount the board's `attachments/` directory into the sandbox** so the absolute paths in the worker context are reachable.
- **Rebuild notes:** Put absolute attachment paths in the worker's context and let the existing file tools read them, instead of building a bespoke retrieval API. A better version would resolve paths per backend so remote workers work without a manual mount.
- **Verification:** partial — the three tools and three CLI verbs exist (`kanban_attach`, `kanban_attach_url`, `kanban_attachments` in `tools_full.json`; `attach`, `attachments`, `attach-rm` in `cli_help/kanban.txt`), but **the CLI attachment verbs are absent from the page's CLI command reference block** (doc gap).

### Kanban quick start & gateway-embedded dispatcher  `id: docs-features.kanban-dispatcher`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes kanban init`, `hermes gateway start`, `hermes kanban create/watch/list/stats`; `kanban.dispatch_in_gateway`
- **What it does:** Sets up a board and runs the dispatcher inside the gateway process — nothing to install, no separate service to manage.
- **How it works:** Documented five-step quick start: (1) `hermes kanban init` (create the board); (2) `hermes gateway start` (hosts the embedded dispatcher); (3) `hermes kanban create "research AI funding landscape" --assignee researcher`; (4) `hermes kanban watch` (watch activity live); (5) `hermes kanban list` / `hermes kanban stats`. **If the gateway is up, ready tasks get picked up on the next tick (60 s by default).** When the dispatcher picks up a task and spawns the profile, **the very first thing that worker's model does is call `kanban_show()` — it doesn't run `hermes kanban show t_abcd`.**
- **Inputs / options:** Config: `kanban.dispatch_in_gateway: true` (default); `kanban.dispatch_interval_seconds: 60` (default); `kanban.review_dispatch: true` (default — spawn the assigned profile with the bundled `sdlc-review` skill; **set false for human-only review boards**). Runtime override: `HERMES_KANBAN_DISPATCH_IN_GATEWAY=0` for debugging.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Workers spawned; tasks claimed and moved.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.dispatch_in_gateway`, `kanban.dispatch_interval_seconds`, `kanban.review_dispatch`; env `HERMES_KANBAN_DISPATCH_IN_GATEWAY`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Without a running gateway, `ready` tasks stay where they are until one comes up** — `hermes kanban create` warns about this at creation time. Standard gateway supervision applies: run `hermes gateway start` directly, or wire the gateway up as a systemd user unit. **`hermes kanban daemon` as a separate process is deprecated** — a `--force` escape hatch keeps the old standalone daemon alive for one release cycle, but **running both a gateway-embedded dispatcher AND a standalone daemon against the same `kanban.db` causes claim races and is not supported.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Host the scheduler inside an existing long-lived process so there is one supervision story, and make the standalone daemon a deprecated escape hatch. A better version would refuse to start the standalone daemon when a gateway dispatcher holds the singleton lock.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `dispatch_in_gateway: True`, `dispatch_interval_seconds: 60`, `review_dispatch: True` all present in the kanban config block; `daemon` help reads "DEPRECATED — dispatcher now runs in the gateway. Use `hermes gateway start`." (evidence: `cli_help/kanban.txt`).

### Idempotent kanban create  `id: docs-features.kanban-idempotency`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes kanban create … --idempotency-key KEY`
- **What it does:** Deduplicates task creation for automation and webhooks — the first call creates the task, and any subsequent call with the same key returns the existing task id instead of duplicating.
- **How it works:** The key is stored on the task row; a repeat create with the same key short-circuits.
- **Inputs / options:** `--idempotency-key IDEMPOTENCY_KEY`; documented example uses `--idempotency-key "nightly-ops-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)"` with `--json`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** One task per key; the existing id is returned on repeats.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Scoped per board (boards have separate DBs).
- **Rebuild notes:** Put dedup in the kernel keyed on a caller-supplied string so every surface (CLI, tool, REST) inherits it. A better version would also return whether the call created or matched.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `--idempotency-key IDEMPOTENCY_KEY` confirmed (evidence: `cli_help/kanban__create.txt`).

### Bulk kanban CLI verbs  `id: docs-features.kanban-bulk-verbs`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes kanban complete|archive|unblock|block|promote|reopen-review`
- **What it does:** Accepts multiple ids so a batch can be cleaned up in one command.
- **How it works:** Documented examples: `hermes kanban complete t_abc t_def t_hij --result "batch wrap"`; `hermes kanban archive t_abc t_def t_hij`; `hermes kanban unblock t_abc t_def`; `hermes kanban block t_abc "need input" --ids t_def t_hij`.
- **Inputs / options:** Multiple positional ids on `complete`, `archive`, `unblock`, `promote`, `reopen-review`; `block <id> "<reason>" [--ids <id>...]`; `schedule <task_id> [reason ...] [--ids IDS ...]`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** One transition per id.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **`hermes kanban complete a b c --summary X` is refused** — structured handoff is per-run, so copy-pasting the same summary to N tasks is almost always wrong; bulk close *without* `--summary` / `--metadata` still works for the "I finished a pile of admin tasks" case.
- **Rebuild notes:** Allow bulk transitions but refuse bulk *handoff*, because a shared summary is almost always a lie. A better version would report per-id outcomes in a table rather than a single exit code.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `complete` is "Mark one or more tasks done", `block` "Mark one or more tasks blocked", `archive` "Archive one or more tasks", `promote` "Manually move one or more todo/blocked tasks to ready (recovery path)", `reopen-review` "Send one or more review tasks back for changes" (evidence: `cli_help/kanban.txt`); `--ids` bulk flag confirmed on `schedule` (evidence: `cli_help/kanban__schedule.txt`).

### Unblock routing & the unblock-loop breaker  `id: docs-features.kanban-unblock-loop`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `hermes kanban unblock`, `kanban_unblock`; constant `BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT`
- **What it does:** Returns a blocked task to the correct source phase, and breaks the unblock↔re-block loop by escalating to `triage` after repeated same-cause blocks.
- **How it works:** **`unblock` restores the safe source phase:** `review` for reviewer-origin work whose parents are complete, `ready` for implementation work whose parents are complete, or `todo` while any parent remains open. A `todo` task **keeps its source-phase provenance** and returns to `review` or `ready` automatically when the dependency gate clears. **`unblock` never routes directly to `triage`.** After a task is blocked → unblocked → re-blocked **for the same cause** `BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT` times (default `2`), the loop breaker stops sending it back to `blocked` — where a cron would just keep unblocking it — and **routes it to `triage` for a human decision**.
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes kanban unblock <id>...`; `kanban_unblock(task_id=…)`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A `block_loop_detected` event with `{reason, kind, recurrences, limit}` when the breaker fires.
- **Config / env:** `BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT` (default 2).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **This is a deterministic DB guard, not an LLM judgment call, and a task's body text cannot opt out of it.** **The recurrence counter deliberately survives each unblock — it resets only on a successful `complete`.** To keep an unblocked task in the work pool, resolve *why it keeps re-blocking* (unfinished parent, missing input, unmet capability) before unblocking, or raise `BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT` if the loop is expected. The `unblocked` event **resets the dispatcher's `consecutive_failures` but deliberately preserves `block_recurrences`** so the loop breaker keeps its memory.
- **Rebuild notes:** Put loop-breaking in the database, not the prompt, so no agent (and no body text) can talk its way out of it; reset the counter only on genuine success. A better version would surface *which* cause repeated in the triage card body.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT = 2` at `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:134`, escalation check `if recurrences >= BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT` at `:6376` emitting `"limit": BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT` at `:6411`, and the "reset to 0 only on a [successful completion]" comment at `:6938`; documented at `:122`, `:1142`, `:1421` and `:6281`.

### `kanban_*` worker tool surface  `id: docs-features.kanban-tools`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** the 14 `kanban_*` tools, enabled by `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` (workers) or the `kanban` toolset (orchestrators)
- **What it does:** Gives the model direct board access without shelling out.
- **How it works:** When the dispatcher spawns a worker it sets `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK=t_abcd` in the child's env, and **that env var flips on a dedicated kanban toolset in the model's schema**. The same toolset is available to orchestrator profiles that enable `kanban` in their toolsets config. **These tools read and mutate the board directly via the Python `kanban_db` layer, same as the CLI does.**
- **Inputs / options:** Fourteen tools with documented purpose and required params. `kanban_show` — read the current task (title, body, prior attempts, parent handoffs, comments, full pre-formatted `worker_context`); defaults to the env's task id; no required params. `kanban_list` — list task summaries with filters for `assignee`, `status`, `tenant`, archived visibility, and limit; intended for orchestrators discovering board work; no required params. `kanban_complete` — finish with `summary` + `metadata` structured handoff; requires at least one of `summary` / `result`. `kanban_request_review` — start same-card review with a durable `summary`, optional `metadata`, and optional reviewer profile; the task moves to `review`, **this is not a block**; requires `summary`. `kanban_request_changes` — reviewer verdict from an active review run; closes that run, reapplies parent gating, and routes the task to its original implementer **without block-loop accounting**; requires `reason`. `kanban_block` — stop work and route by why: `kind=dependency` (waits in `todo`, auto-resumes), `needs_input`/`capability`/`transient` (surface to a human); repeated same-kind re-blocks auto-escalate to `triage`; requires `reason`. `kanban_heartbeat` — signal liveness during long operations; pure side-effect; no required params. `kanban_comment` — append a durable note to the task thread; requires `task_id`, `body`. `kanban_attach` — attach a file by inline base64 bytes (25 MB cap); requires file bytes + name. `kanban_attach_url` — attach by URL; requires `url`. `kanban_attachments` — list a task's attachments; no required params. `kanban_create` — (orchestrators) fan out into child tasks with an `assignee`, optional `parents`, `skills`, etc.; requires `title`, `assignee`. `kanban_link` — (orchestrators) add a `parent_id → child_id` dependency edge after the fact; requires `parent_id`, `child_id`. `kanban_unblock` — (orchestrators) restore a blocked task to its source phase (`review` or `ready`), or `todo` while a parent remains open; requires `task_id`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Structured JSON tool results; DB writes.
- **Config / env:** `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`, `HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD`, `HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE`; the `kanban` toolset for orchestrators.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Zero schema footprint on normal sessions** — a regular `hermes chat` session has zero `kanban_*` tools unless the active profile explicitly enables the `kanban` toolset. **Dispatcher-spawned workers are still task-scoped for destructive lifecycle operations and cannot mutate unrelated tasks.** The "(Orchestrators)" tools are available through the same toolset; the convention (encoded in the auto-injected kanban guidance) is that worker profiles don't fan out or route unrelated work, and orchestrator profiles don't execute implementation work.
- **Rebuild notes:** Gate the tool surface on an env var the spawner controls, and scope destructive verbs to the spawned task so a worker can't wreck the board. A better version would make the orchestrator/worker split a real capability flag rather than a prompt convention.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — all 14 tool names present in `tools_full.json`, exactly matching the docs' table.

### Why kanban tools instead of shelling to the CLI  `id: docs-features.kanban-why-tools`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** kanban.md → "Why tools instead of shelling to `hermes kanban`"
- **What it does:** Gives the three reasons the worker surface is tools rather than shell commands.
- **How it works:** **(1) Backend portability** — workers whose terminal tool points at a remote backend (Docker / Modal / Singularity / SSH) would run `hermes kanban complete` *inside* the container, where `hermes` isn't installed and `~/.hermes/kanban.db` isn't mounted; the kanban tools run in the agent's own Python process and always reach `~/.hermes/kanban.db` regardless of terminal backend. **(2) No shell-quoting fragility** — passing `--metadata '{"files": [...]}'` through shlex + argparse is a latent footgun; structured tool args skip it entirely. **(3) Better errors** — tool results are structured JSON the model can reason about, not stderr strings it has to parse.
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** The auto-injected kanban guidance teaches the model which tool to call when and in what order.
- **Rebuild notes:** Any agent capability that must work under a remote terminal backend has to live in the agent's own process, not behind the shell. A better version would state this rule once as an architectural invariant for all tool design.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — the tools live in the agent process (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py` called directly), which is why they work under any terminal backend.

### Recommended kanban handoff metadata  `id: docs-features.kanban-handoff-metadata`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** `kanban_complete(summary=…, metadata={…})`
- **What it does:** Recommends a metadata shape so downstream agents, reviewers, and dashboards can reuse the handoff without scraping prose.
- **How it works:** The `summary` is the human-readable closeout; `metadata` is the machine-readable handoff. Recommended optional shape for engineering and review tasks: `changed_files` (list of paths), `verification` (list of commands, e.g. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py -q`), `dependencies` (parent task id or external issue), `blocked_reason` (null when not blocked), `retry_notes` (what failed before, if this was a retry), `residual_risk` (list of what was not tested or still needs human review).
- **Inputs / options:** Six recommended keys as above.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Metadata stored on the run row; children see it serialized alongside the summary.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **These keys are a convention, not a schema requirement.** The useful property is that every worker leaves enough evidence to answer four questions: what changed; how it was verified; what can unblock or retry this if it fails; what risk is still deliberately left open. **Keep secrets, raw logs, tokens, OAuth material, and unrelated transcripts out of `metadata`** — store pointers and summaries instead. If a task has no files or tests, say so explicitly in `summary` and use `metadata` for the evidence that does exist (source URLs, issue ids, manual review steps).
- **Rebuild notes:** Recommend a metadata convention rather than enforcing a schema, so unusual tasks aren't forced to lie. A better version would lint the metadata for secret-shaped strings before persisting.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `metadata` is a free-form JSON dict on the run row (see the runs entry).

### Kanban worker lifecycle (`KANBAN_GUIDANCE`)  `id: docs-features.kanban-worker-lifecycle`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** injected into every kanban worker's system prompt at spawn
- **What it does:** Teaches every worker the full lifecycle in **tool calls**, with nothing to install or configure.
- **How it works:** Four documented steps: (1) on spawn, call `kanban_show()` to read title + body + parent handoffs + prior attempts + full comment thread; (2) `cd $HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE` (via the terminal tool) and do the work there; (3) call `kanban_heartbeat(note="...")` every few minutes during long operations — **if your work may run longer than 1 hour, call `kanban_heartbeat` at least once an hour**; (4) complete with `kanban_complete(summary="…", metadata={…})`, or `kanban_block(reason="…")` if stuck. **The lifecycle plus the load-bearing reference details (workspace kinds, deliverable `artifacts`, claiming created cards) ship in that system-prompt block, so every worker has them regardless of which profile it runs under — no per-profile skill setup required.**
- **Inputs / options:** A typical worker turn: `kanban_show()` → work → `kanban_heartbeat(note="halfway through — 4 of 8 files transformed")` → `kanban_complete(summary="migrated limiter.py to token-bucket; added 14 tests, all pass", metadata={"changed_files": [...], "tests_run": 14})`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Heartbeat events; a terminal completion or block.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.dispatch_stale_timeout_seconds` (default 4 h).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **The dispatcher reclaims tasks that have been running past `kanban.dispatch_stale_timeout_seconds` (default 4 h) with no heartbeat in the last hour**, on the assumption the worker crashed without cleanup. **A reclaim is benign** (the task goes back to `ready` for re-dispatch without a failure-counter tick) **but you lose your current run's progress.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Ship the protocol in the system prompt rather than as an installable skill, so every worker has it unconditionally. A better version would make the heartbeat automatic on tool activity rather than requiring an explicit call.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — the 1-hour heartbeat threshold is "Hardcoded at 1 hour" per the comment at `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:8556`, checked against `dispatch_stale_timeout_seconds` (`:8071`).

### Kanban protocol-violation guard (stop nudges + bounded retry)  `id: docs-features.kanban-protocol-violation`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** worker exit path; env `HERMES_KANBAN_STOP_NUDGE`; dispatcher retry budget
- **What it does:** Catches a worker that exits successfully while its task is still `running` — the common case where the model narrates the next step ("Let me write the report") and stops without calling a terminal board tool.
- **How it works:** **Agent-side prevention:** before the worker exits, Hermes injects **up to two synthetic nudges** when it detects the model is about to stop without a terminal board tool call (`finish_reason=stop`); the nudge reminds the model to call `kanban_complete` or `kanban_block` immediately. **This guard is active only for dispatcher-spawned workers (`HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` is set).** **Dispatcher-side recovery:** if the nudges are exhausted or the worker crashes before reaching the nudge, the dispatcher gives the violation a **bounded retry** — up to `_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION_FAILURE_LIMIT` **consecutive** violations (default **3**) — before auto-blocking the task instead of respawning it into the same loop.
- **Inputs / options:** Disable the agent-side nudge with `HERMES_KANBAN_STOP_NUDGE=0`. Per-task `max_retries` overrides the bound.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A `protocol_violation` event with `{pid, claimer, exit_code, protocol_violation}`; on exhaustion also a `gave_up` event and an auto-block.
- **Config / env:** env `HERMES_KANBAN_STOP_NUDGE`; per-task `--max-retries`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **The budget counts only *consecutive* clean-exit protocol violations** — interleaved rate-limited requeues are neutral, and any other failure kind resets the streak. This usually means the model wrote a plain-text answer and exited without using the Kanban tool surface.
- **Rebuild notes:** Detect the "narrated but didn't act" stop and nudge in-session before falling back to a dispatcher-side retry budget that counts only the same failure class. A better version would make the terminal tool call structurally required (e.g. a forced tool choice on the final turn).
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION_FAILURE_LIMIT = 3` at `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:8804`.

### Pinning extra skills to a kanban task  `id: docs-features.kanban-task-skills`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `kanban_create(skills=[…])`; `hermes kanban create --skill <name>` (repeatable); dashboard create dialog **skills** field
- **What it does:** Attaches specialist skills to a single task without editing the assignee's profile.
- **How it works:** **The dispatcher emits one `--skills <name>` flag per skill listed**, so the worker spawns with all of them loaded **on top of the auto-injected kanban guidance**.
- **Inputs / options:** **From an orchestrator agent** (the usual case): `kanban_create(title="translate README to Japanese", assignee="linguist", skills=["translation"])`; `kanban_create(title="audit auth flow", assignee="reviewer", skills=["security-pr-audit", "github-code-review"])`. **From a human (CLI / slash command):** repeat `--skill` for each one. **From the dashboard:** type the skills comma-separated into the **skills** field of the create-task dialog.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Extra skills in the worker's session.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **The skill names must match skills that are actually installed on the assignee's profile** (run `hermes skills list` to see what's available); **there's no runtime install.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Attach capability at the task level so routing doesn't require editing a profile per job. A better version would validate the skill names against the assignee's profile at create time.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `--skill SKILLS` on `hermes kanban create` (evidence: `cli_help/kanban__create.txt`).

### Per-task model override (`hermes kanban set-model`)  `id: docs-features.kanban-model-override`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes kanban create --model … --provider …`; `hermes kanban set-model <id> <model> [--provider …]`; dashboard per-task model dropdown
- **What it does:** Pins a task's worker to a specific model (and optionally provider), independent of the assignee profile's default.
- **How it works:** The dispatcher spawns the worker with the pinned model — `--provider <name>` is passed when set, and **`--provider` requires a model**. **The dashboard's per-task model dropdown drives the same `model_override` field.** With no override, the worker uses its profile's configured model.
- **Inputs / options:** At creation: `hermes kanban create "hard refactor" --assignee coder --model claude-opus-4.6 --provider anthropic` (create-flag help: "Pin the worker to this model (passed as `-m <model>`) without changing the profile's configured model"; `--provider` is "passed as `--provider <name>` to the worker. Requires --model"). Later: `hermes kanban set-model t_abcd claude-opus-4.6 --provider anthropic`; `hermes kanban set-model t_abcd none` (clear the override). Takes effect on the next dispatch.
- **Outputs / side effects:** `model_override` on the task row.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** `set-model` help: "Set or clear a task's model/provider override (takes effect on the next dispatch)."
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep the model pin a task field the spawner translates into worker flags, so no profile edit is needed for a one-off. A better version would show the effective model in `hermes kanban show`.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `set-model` subcommand and both create flags confirmed (evidence: `cli_help/kanban.txt`, `cli_help/kanban__create.txt`, `cli_help/kanban__set-model.txt`).

### Kanban cost strategy: frontier orchestrator, inexpensive workers  `id: docs-features.kanban-cost-strategy`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** kanban.md → "Cost strategy"
- **What it does:** Explains how per-profile configs make the planner/worker cost split natural.
- **How it works:** **Decomposing a project into well-scoped cards takes frontier-level judgment; executing a card that already carries a clear goal, context, and handoff evidence usually doesn't — and the workers are where the vast majority of tokens are spent, so the worker model is where the cost lives.** Each profile has its own `config.yaml` under `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/`, and **the dispatcher injects the profile-scoped `HERMES_HOME` when it spawns `hermes -p <assignee>`**, so each worker reads its own profile's model settings.
- **Inputs / options:** Orchestrator profile `~/.hermes/config.yaml` with `model.default: "your-frontier-model"`; worker profiles `~/.hermes/profiles/coder/config.yaml` and `~/.hermes/profiles/researcher/config.yaml` with `model.default: "your-inexpensive-model"`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Different models per worker process.
- **Config / env:** per-profile `model.default`; env `HERMES_HOME` injected per spawn.
- **Edge cases / guards:** For the occasional quality-sensitive card, pin just that task back to a stronger model with the per-task model override — **no profile edits needed.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Let each worker resolve its own config from a profile-scoped home injected by the spawner, so cost policy is a config concern not a code concern. A better version would report per-profile token spend on the board.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — profile-scoped `HERMES_HOME` injection is the same mechanism used elsewhere (see the profiles handling in `hermes_cli/web_server.py:18455-18468`).

### Kanban lifecycle plugin hooks  `id: docs-features.kanban-hooks`
- **Surface:** Tool
- **Where:** plugin hooks `kanban_task_claimed`, `kanban_task_completed`, `kanban_task_blocked`
- **What it does:** Fires plugin hooks on board transitions so external code can react.
- **How it works:** Each hook carries `task_id` and `profile_name`. **Hooks fire after the board DB change commits, so callbacks always see durable state.** **Note the process split:** `kanban_task_claimed` fires in the **dispatcher** process, while `kanban_task_completed` / `kanban_task_blocked` fire in the **worker** process — **register the hook in the dispatcher profile to observe every transition centrally.**
- **Inputs / options:** Three hook names. Documented registration: `def register(ctx): def on_blocked(task_id=None, profile_name=None, **kw): ctx.dispatch_tool("terminal", {"command": f"notify-send 'kanban blocked: {task_id}'"}); ctx.register_hook("kanban_task_blocked", on_blocked)`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Whatever the callback does.
- **Config / env:** plugin system (see `/user-guide/features/hooks#plugin-hooks`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** The process split means a worker-process hook won't see claims, and a dispatcher-process hook won't see completions unless registered in both.
- **Rebuild notes:** Fire hooks after commit and document which process each runs in, since that determines where the plugin must be installed. A better version would relay worker-process hooks back to the dispatcher so one registration covers all three.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — plugin hook names in the plugins subsystem (see the `plugins.md` and `hooks.md` entries).

### Goal-mode kanban cards (`--goal`)  `id: docs-features.kanban-goal-mode`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes kanban create --goal [--goal-max-turns N]`; `kanban_create(goal_mode=True)`; dashboard create dialog
- **What it does:** Runs a card's worker in a **goal loop** — the same Ralph-style engine behind the `/goal` slash command — instead of the default one-shot.
- **How it works:** By default each worker gets **one shot** at its card: do the work, call `kanban_complete`/`kanban_block`, exit. With `--goal`, **after every turn an auxiliary judge checks the worker's output against the card's title + body (treated as the acceptance criteria)**, and if the work isn't done — and the turn budget remains — the worker keeps going **in the same session** until the judge agrees, the worker terminates the task itself, or the budget runs out (**which blocks the card for human review rather than exiting silently**).
- **Inputs / options:** `--goal`; `--goal-max-turns N` (**default 20**, ignored without `--goal`). Documented example: `hermes kanban create "Translate the docs site to French" --body "Acceptance: every page translated, no English left, links intact." --assignee linguist --goal --goal-max-turns 15`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A multi-turn worker session; card blocked on budget exhaustion.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Use it for open-ended, multi-step, or "keep going until X is true" cards; **skip it for cheap one-shot work** — the per-turn judge overhead isn't worth it, and the dispatcher's existing retry/circuit-breaker already handles transient worker failures. **The judge is only as good as your goal text, so write the body as explicit acceptance criteria.** **Goal-mode cards borrow the `/goal` engine — they don't connect to it:** `--goal` runs the continuation loop *inside that one card's worker session*; setting a `/goal` in a chat session never creates, claims, or moves a kanban card, and a goal-mode card's loop is **invisible to any chat session's `/goal status`**.
- **Rebuild notes:** Share the continuation engine but not the state, so a card's loop and a chat's loop can't interfere. A better version would surface the judge's per-turn verdicts on the card so a stuck loop is diagnosable.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `--goal` and `--goal-max-turns N` (default 20) with the "blocks the card for review" note confirmed verbatim (evidence: `cli_help/kanban__create.txt`).

### Kanban orchestrator behaviour  `id: docs-features.kanban-orchestrator`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** orchestrator guidance injected into the worker's system prompt
- **What it does:** Teaches an orchestrator profile to decompose and route rather than do the work itself.
- **How it works:** **A well-behaved orchestrator does not do the work itself** — it decomposes the user's goal into tasks, links them, assigns each to one of the profiles you've set up, and steps back. The guidance — **anti-temptation rules, a Step-0 profile-discovery prompt** (the dispatcher silently fails on unknown assignee names, so the orchestrator must ground every card in profiles that actually exist on your machine), **and a decomposition playbook keyed on `kanban_create` / `kanban_link` / `kanban_comment`** — is injected into the worker's system prompt automatically; there is nothing to install or sync per profile.
- **Inputs / options:** A canonical orchestrator turn: two `kanban_create` calls for parallel researchers, one `kanban_create` with `parents=["t_r1", "t_r2"]` for the writer (promoted to `ready` when both complete), an optional `kanban_link(parent_id=…, child_id=…)` for deps discovered later, then `kanban_complete(summary=…)`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A task graph.
- **Config / env:** For best results, pair it with a profile whose toolsets are **restricted to board operations (`kanban`, `gateway`, `memory`)** so the orchestrator literally cannot execute implementation tasks even if it tries.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Decide before you fan out** — design decisions belong to the orchestrator, not the workers. If two parallel cards would each have to pick the same thing (a naming scheme, a schema, a file format, an API shape), the orchestrator decides it once and **stamps the decision into both card bodies**. **Workers cannot see sibling cards**, so every child card body must carry every decision it depends on. Worked example: for parallel "build the exporter" and "build the importer" cards, pick the format up front (say, newline-delimited JSON with a `version` field) and write it into both bodies, or the two halves will never round-trip.
- **Rebuild notes:** Enforce the orchestrator/worker split with toolset restrictions, not just prompt guidance, and require shared decisions to be duplicated into every child body because siblings are invisible to each other. A better version would let a card reference a shared "decisions" record the orchestrator owns.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — guidance injected at spawn (same mechanism as `KANBAN_GUIDANCE`); the "dispatcher silently fails on unknown assignee names" behaviour is mitigated by `kanban.default_assignee` (see the decomposer entry).

### Kanban dashboard plugin  `id: docs-features.kanban-dashboard`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** `hermes dashboard` → **Kanban** tab (appears after "Skills"); bundled plugin at `plugins/kanban/`
- **What it does:** A visual board for humans-in-the-loop: triage, cross-profile supervision, reading comment threads, and dragging cards between columns.
- **How it works:** Shipped as a **bundled dashboard plugin** — not a core feature, not a separate service — following the model in "Extending the Dashboard". Open with `hermes kanban init` (one-time) then `hermes dashboard`.
- **Inputs / options:** **Columns** — one per status: `triage`, `todo`, `ready`, `running`, `blocked`, `done` (plus `archived` when the toggle is on). **Cards** show the task id, title, priority badge, tenant tag, assigned profile, comment/link counts, a **progress pill** (`N/M` children done when the task has dependents), and "created N ago"; a per-card checkbox enables multi-select. **Per-profile lanes inside Running** — a toolbar checkbox toggles sub-grouping of the Running column by assignee. **Live updates via WebSocket** — the plugin tails the append-only `task_events` table on a short poll interval; reloads are debounced so a burst of events triggers a single refetch. **Drag-drop** cards between columns to change status; the drop sends `PATCH /api/plugins/kanban/tasks/:id` which routes through the same `kanban_db` code the CLI uses; **moves into destructive statuses (`done`, `archived`, `blocked`) prompt for confirmation**; touch devices use a pointer-based fallback so the board is usable from a tablet. **Create-task dialog** — click `+` on any column header for a modal with title, assignee, priority, skills, workspace kind/path (seeded from the board's project directory, per-task override), goal mode, and optionally a parent task from a dropdown over every existing task; **Enter** creates, **Shift+Enter** inserts a newline in the title field, **Escape** cancels; creating from the Triage column automatically parks the new task in triage. **Multi-select with bulk actions** — shift/ctrl-click a card or tick its checkbox; a bulk action bar appears with batch status transitions, archive, and reassign (by profile dropdown, or "(unassign)"); destructive batches confirm first; per-id partial failures are reported without aborting the rest. **Toolbar filters** — free-text search, tenant dropdown (defaults to `dashboard.kanban.default_tenant`), assignee dropdown, "show archived" toggle, "lanes by profile" toggle, and a **Nudge dispatcher** button so you don't have to wait for the next 60 s tick. **Trash drop zone** — drag any card into it to delete the task (cascades through `task_events`, child links, and subscriptions), with a confirmation prompt; bulk delete via `DELETE /api/plugins/kanban/tasks` with body `{"ids": [...]}`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Same DB writes as the CLI.
- **Config / env:** `dashboard.kanban.*`; disable without removing via `dashboard.plugins.kanban.enabled: false` (or delete `plugins/kanban/dashboard/manifest.json`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** Visual target is the familiar Linear / Fusion layout: dark theme, column headers with counts, coloured status dots, pill chips for priority and tenant. **The plugin reads only theme CSS vars (`--color-*`, `--radius`, `--font-mono`, …), so it reskins automatically with whichever dashboard theme is active.** **Scope boundary:** the GUI is deliberately thin — everything it does is reachable from the CLI; auto-assignment, budgets, governance gates, and org-chart views remain user-space.
- **Rebuild notes:** Make the GUI a read-through/write-through layer over the same kernel the CLI uses so the surfaces cannot drift, and keep all domain logic out of it. A better version would stream board deltas instead of refetching the whole board on every burst.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — bundled plugin discovered from `<repo>/plugins/<name>/dashboard/` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:18468-18470`).

### Kanban task drawer  `id: docs-features.kanban-drawer`
- **Surface:** Web dashboard
- **Where:** click a card (without shift/ctrl) → side drawer (Escape or click-outside closes)
- **What it does:** Provides full per-task editing and history in one panel.
- **How it works:** Documented sections: **Editable title** (click the heading to rename); **Editable assignee / priority** (click the meta row to rewrite); **Editable description** — markdown-rendered by default (headings, bold, italic, inline code, fenced code, `http(s)` / `mailto:` links, bullet lists) with an "edit" button that swaps in a textarea; **Dependency editor** — a chip list of parents and children each with an `×` to unlink, plus dropdowns over every other task to add a new parent or child; **Status action row** (→ triage / → ready / → running / block / unblock / complete / archive) with confirm prompts for destructive transitions, and for **Triage** cards two LLM-driven actions **⚗ Decompose** and **✨ Specify**; **Result section** (also markdown-rendered); **comment thread** with Enter-to-submit; **the last 20 events**; **Run History** (one coloured row per attempt).
- **Inputs / options:** All controls above.
- **Outputs / side effects:** DB writes via the plugin REST API.
- **Config / env:** `dashboard.kanban.render_markdown` (set false for plain `<pre>` rendering).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Markdown rendering is a tiny, XSS-safe renderer — every substitution runs on HTML-escaped input, only `http(s)` / `mailto:` links pass through, and `target="_blank"` + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` are always set.** **Cycle attempts in the dependency editor are rejected server-side with a clear message.** **Live drawer refresh:** when the WebSocket event stream reports new events for the task being viewed, the drawer reloads itself (via a per-task event counter threaded into its `useEffect` dependency list) — closing and reopening is no longer required.
- **Rebuild notes:** Escape first and allowlist link schemes when rendering user/agent markdown, and reject dependency cycles in the kernel rather than the UI. A better version would show a live diff of what a status action will do before confirming.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — cycle rejection and markdown rendering handled in the plugin (`plugins/kanban/dashboard/`).

### Kanban auto vs manual orchestration (Triage decomposer)  `id: docs-features.kanban-decomposer`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** **Orchestration: Auto/Manual** pill at the top of the kanban page; `kanban.auto_decompose`
- **What it does:** Decides what happens to a task dropped into the Triage column — automatic LLM decomposition into a task graph, or nothing until you act.
- **How it works:** **Auto (default, `kanban.auto_decompose: true`)** — the gateway-embedded dispatcher runs the **decomposer** on each tick, capped by `kanban.auto_decompose_per_tick` (default 3) **so a bulk-load of triage tasks doesn't burst-spend the auxiliary LLM**. The decomposer uses the built-in decomposition prompt plus the `auxiliary.kanban_decomposer` model path, **reads your installed profiles + their descriptions**, and asks the LLM to produce a JSON task graph: which tasks to spawn, who they go to, and which depend on which. **The original triage task becomes the parent of every leaf in the graph, so it stays alive until the whole graph completes — and then promotes back to `ready`** so its assignee (`kanban.orchestrator_profile`, or the active default profile when unset) can judge completion and add more tasks if the work isn't done. This is the "drop a one-liner, walk away" flow. **Manual (`auto_decompose: false`)** — triage tasks stay in triage until you act: click **⚗ Decompose** on a card, run `hermes kanban decompose <id>` (or `--all`), or use `/kanban decompose <id>` from a chat.
- **Inputs / options:** Six documented config keys under `kanban:` — `auto_decompose` (default `true`); `auto_decompose_per_tick` (default `3`; excess defers to the next tick); `orchestrator_profile` (default `""`; profile assigned to the root/orchestration task after decomposition; empty = fall back to active default profile); `default_assignee` (default `""`; where a child task lands when the LLM picks an unknown profile; empty = fall back to active default); `auto_subscribe_on_create` (default `true`); `done_sub_retention_days` (default `30`). Two auxiliary LLM slots: `auxiliary.kanban_decomposer` (model that produces the task graph) and `auxiliary.profile_describer` (model that auto-generates profile descriptions, called by `hermes profile describe --auto`). Also `auxiliary.triage_specifier` for **✨ Specify**.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Child tasks + links created atomically; the root flipped `triage → todo`.
- **Config / env:** all `kanban.*` and `auxiliary.*` keys above.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Important boundary:** manual mode disables **only** the built-in Triage decomposer — it does **not** prevent a profile from calling `kanban_create`, and it does **not** disable creator-session wake-ups. **The decomposer NEVER lands a child task with `assignee=None`:** when the LLM picks an unknown profile, the child gets routed to `kanban.default_assignee` (or the active default profile if unset). **`kanban.orchestrator_profile` does not load that profile's prompt, skills, or custom logic into the decomposition call** — it controls who owns the root/orchestration task after fan-out; to change the decomposer's model/provider configure `auxiliary.kanban_decomposer`, and to use a profile's custom task-splitting logic switch to Manual mode. **For provenance, built-in decomposer children use `created_by=auto-decomposer`; tasks created by a resumed profile carry that profile name instead.** Routing quality depends on profile descriptions, set with `hermes profile create --description "…"`, `hermes profile describe <name> --text "…"`, `hermes profile describe <name> --auto`, or the dashboard's per-profile editor in the expanded **Orchestration settings** panel; **profiles without a description still appear in the roster — routable by name, just less precisely.** **Decompose falls back to specify-style promotion when the LLM decides the task doesn't benefit from fan-out, so it's a strict superset of Specify.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Cap LLM-driven fan-out per tick so a bulk import can't burst-spend, and never land an unassigned child — always fall back to a configured default. A better version would show the proposed graph for approval before creating it in Auto mode.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `auto_subscribe_on_create: True`, `orchestrator_profile: ""`, `default_assignee: ""` present in the kanban config block; `--created-by CREATED_BY` flag on create confirms the provenance field (evidence: `cli_help/kanban__create.txt`).

### Kanban dashboard REST surface  `id: docs-features.kanban-rest`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `/api/plugins/kanban/*`
- **What it does:** The HTTP surface the dashboard plugin uses, all thin wrappers over `kanban_db`.
- **How it works:** The GUI is strictly a **read-through-the-DB + write-through-`kanban_db`** layer with no domain logic of its own. **The plugin is ~700 lines of Python (router + WebSocket tail + bulk batcher + config reader) and adds no new business logic.** A tiny `_conn()` helper **auto-initializes `kanban.db` on every read and write**, so a fresh install works whether the user opened the dashboard first, hit the REST API directly, or ran `hermes kanban init`.
- **Inputs / options:** Documented routes — `GET /board?tenant=<name>&include_archived=…` (full board grouped by status column, plus tenants + assignees for filter dropdowns); `GET /tasks/:id` (task + comments + events + links, plus a `runs[]` array); `POST /tasks` (create — wraps `kanban_db.create_task`, accepts `triage: bool` and `parents: [id, …]`); `PATCH /tasks/:id` (status / assignee / priority / title / body / result; with `{status: "done", summary, metadata}` forwards both to the kernel so the dashboard's "mark done" button is CLI-equivalent); `POST /tasks/bulk` (apply the same patch — status / archive / assignee / priority — to every id in `ids`, per-id failures reported without aborting siblings); `POST /tasks/:id/comments`; `POST /tasks/:id/specify`; `POST /tasks/:id/decompose`; `GET /profiles`; `PATCH /profiles/:name`; `POST /profiles/:name/describe-auto`; `GET /orchestration`; `PUT /orchestration`; `POST /links`; `DELETE /links?parent_id=…&child_id=…`; `POST /dispatch?max=…&dry_run=…`; `GET /config`; `WS /events?since=<event_id>`; `DELETE /tasks` (bulk delete with `{"ids": [...]}`); `GET /workers/active`; `GET /runs/{id}`; `POST /runs/{run_id}/terminate`; `GET /inspect`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Board mutations; `/specify` returns `{ok, task_id, reason, new_title}` and `/decompose` returns `{ok, task_id, reason, fanout, child_ids, new_title}`.
- **Config / env:** `dashboard.kanban.*`; `?board=<slug>` on every endpoint.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **`ok=false` with a human-readable reason on "not in triage" / no aux client / LLM error is a 200, not a 4xx** — the same convention for `/specify` and `/decompose`. `PUT /orchestration` **validates that non-empty profile names actually exist**. `POST /profiles/:name/describe-auto` persists with `description_auto: true` so the dashboard can surface a "review" badge; `PATCH /profiles/:name` sets user-authored descriptions with `description_auto: false`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Return 200 with a structured `ok:false` for expected LLM/state failures so the UI can render a reason instead of a stack trace. A better version would version the plugin API so a stale bundle fails loudly.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — plugin routes mounted under `/api/plugins/<name>/` per the dashboard plugin contract (`hermes_cli/web_server.py`).

### Kanban worker visibility endpoints  `id: docs-features.kanban-worker-endpoints`
- **Surface:** API
- **Where:** `/api/plugins/kanban/workers/active`, `/runs/{id}`, `/runs/{run_id}/terminate`, `/inspect`
- **What it does:** Read-only worker/run visibility for external monitors, plus one run-control verb.
- **How it works:** `GET /api/plugins/kanban/workers/active` returns currently spawned workers with **PID, profile, task id, started-at, last heartbeat**. `GET /api/plugins/kanban/runs/{id}` returns single-run detail — **task id, status, started/ended, exit code, log path**. `POST /api/plugins/kanban/runs/{run_id}/terminate` **terminates a reclaimable run** — stops the worker and frees the task for re-dispatch. `GET /api/plugins/kanban/inspect` returns a combined dispatcher snapshot — **backlog, in-progress count vs. `max_in_progress`, recent events**.
- **Inputs / options:** Four endpoints as above.
- **Outputs / side effects:** `terminate` kills a worker and requeues the task.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.max_in_progress` (surfaced by `/inspect`).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **All of these are gated by the same dashboard plugin auth as the rest of the kanban plugin API.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Expose PID + heartbeat + log path so an external monitor can act without touching the DB. A better version would stream worker stdout over the same WebSocket.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `hermes kanban reclaim` provides the CLI equivalent ("Release an active worker claim on a running task", evidence: `cli_help/kanban__reclaim.txt`).

### Kanban dashboard config (`dashboard.kanban`)  `id: docs-features.kanban-dashboard-config`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `dashboard.kanban.*` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`
- **What it does:** Sets the Kanban tab's defaults, read at load time via `GET /config`.
- **How it works:** Four documented keys.
- **Inputs / options:** `default_tenant: acme` (preselects the tenant filter); `lane_by_profile: true` (default for the "lanes by profile" toggle); `include_archived_by_default: false`; `render_markdown: true` (set false for plain `<pre>` rendering).
- **Outputs / side effects:** UI defaults.
- **Config / env:** `dashboard.kanban.*`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Each key is optional and falls back to the shown default.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Read UI defaults from the same config file the CLI uses so a team can ship one config. A better version would let a user override them per browser without editing config.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `GET /config` route listed in the plugin's REST table.

### Kanban security model  `id: docs-features.kanban-security`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** dashboard plugin auth; `hermes dashboard --host`
- **What it does:** States exactly who can reach the kanban REST surface and what that grants.
- **How it works:** **The dashboard's HTTP auth middleware explicitly skips `/api/plugins/`** — plugin routes are unauthenticated by design **because the dashboard binds to localhost by default**. That means the kanban REST surface is **reachable from any process on the host**. **The WebSocket takes one additional step:** it requires the dashboard's ephemeral session token as a `?token=…` query parameter (browsers can't set `Authorization` on an upgrade request), matching the pattern used by the in-browser PTY bridge.
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0` exposes everything.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **If you run `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0`, every plugin route — kanban included — becomes reachable from the network. "Don't do that on a shared host."** The board contains task bodies, comments, and workspace paths; **an attacker reaching these routes gets read access to your entire collaboration surface and can also create / reassign / archive tasks.** **Tasks in `~/.hermes/kanban.db` are profile-agnostic on purpose (that's the coordination primitive)** — opening the dashboard with `hermes -p <profile> dashboard` still shows tasks created by any other profile on the host; same user owns all profiles, but worth knowing if multiple personas coexist. **Kanban is single-host by design** — the trusted-local-user threat model.
- **Rebuild notes:** State the threat model plainly (trusted local user, localhost bind) rather than implying isolation the design doesn't provide. A better version would authenticate plugin routes too so `--host 0.0.0.0` isn't a cliff.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — the auth-skip for `/api/plugins/` is the documented dashboard plugin contract (cross-referenced from `extending-the-dashboard#backend-api-routes`), which additionally states unauthenticated requests get a 401 before a plugin route runs — an **internal doc inconsistency** between the two pages worth noting.

### Kanban live updates (`task_events` WebSocket)  `id: docs-features.kanban-live-updates`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `WS /api/plugins/kanban/events?since=<event_id>`
- **What it does:** Streams board changes to the dashboard as they land.
- **How it works:** **`task_events` is an append-only SQLite table with a monotonic `id`.** The WebSocket endpoint holds each client's last-seen event id and pushes new rows as they land. **When a burst of events arrives, the frontend reloads the (very cheap) board endpoint — simpler and more correct than trying to patch local state from every event kind.** **WAL mode means the read loop never blocks the dispatcher's `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` claim transactions.**
- **Inputs / options:** `?since=<event_id>` cursor; `?token=…` for auth.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Pushed event rows; debounced board refetches.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** The WS is **pinned to a board at connection time**; switching boards in the UI opens a fresh WS.
- **Rebuild notes:** Append-only events with a monotonic id plus WAL is enough for live UI without a message broker; refetch on burst rather than patching state per event kind. A better version would send compact deltas for the common single-task case.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — append-only `task_events` and per-run `run_id` grouping described in the event reference; WAL usage in `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`.

### Kanban CLI command reference  `id: docs-features.kanban-cli`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes kanban <verb>`
- **What it does:** The full human/automation surface for driving the board.
- **How it works:** Every CLI verb routes through `kanban_db`, the same kernel the tools use, **so the two surfaces agree by construction**.
- **Inputs / options:** **44 subcommands** (incl. aliases) from `hermes kanban --help`: `init` (create kanban.db if missing, idempotent); `boards` (manage boards); `create` (new task); `swarm` (create a Kanban Swarm v1 graph); `list` / `ls`; `show`; `assign` (assign or reassign; `none` to unassign); `set-model`; `reclaim` (release an active worker claim on a running task); `reassign` (bulk re-assign, optionally reclaiming first); `diagnostics` / `diag` (list active diagnostics on the current board); `link`; `unlink`; `claim` (atomically claim a ready task, prints the resolved workspace path, `--ttl SECONDS`); `comment` (`--author NAME`); `attach`; `attachments`; `attach-rm`; `complete`; `edit`; `block`; `schedule`; `unblock`; `request-review`; `request-changes`; `reopen-review`; `promote`; `archive`; `tail` (follow a task's event stream); `dispatch` (one pass: reclaim stale, promote ready, spawn workers; `--dry-run`, `--max N`, `--failure-limit N`, `--json`); `daemon` (DEPRECATED, `--force`, `--failure-limit N`, `--pidfile PATH`, `-v`); `watch` (live-stream `task_events`; `--assignee`, `--tenant`, `--kinds completed,blocked,…`, `--interval SECS`); `stats` (per-status + per-assignee counts + oldest-ready age, `--json`); `notify-subscribe` / `notify-list` / `notify-unsubscribe`; `log` (worker log, `--tail BYTES`); `runs` (attempt history, `--json`); `heartbeat` (`--note "…"`); `assignees` (profiles on disk + per-assignee task counts, `--json`); `context` (what a worker sees); `specify` (`[<id> | --all] [--tenant T] [--author NAME] [--json]`); `decompose`; `gc` (`--event-retention-days N`, `--log-retention-days N`); `repair`. Group flag `--board <slug>`. `hermes kanban list` accepts `--mine`, `--assignee`, `--status {archived,blocked,done,ready,review,running,scheduled,todo,triage}`, `--tenant`, `--session SESSION`, `--archived`, `--json`, `--sort {assignee,created,created-desc,priority,priority-desc,status,title,updated}`, `--workflow-template-id ID`, `--step-key KEY`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Board mutations; `--json` machine output on several verbs.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.failure_limit`; per-task `--max-retries`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **`--max-retries` is a per-task circuit-breaker override for the dispatcher** — `--max-retries 1` blocks the task on the first non-successful attempt, `--max-retries 3` allows two retries and blocks on the third failure; omit it to use `kanban.failure_limit` from `config.yaml`, then the built-in default. `hermes kanban claim --ttl` defaults to `DEFAULT_CLAIM_TTL_SECONDS` (15 minutes).
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep one argparse tree and reuse it for the slash surface so flags never diverge. A better version would generate the docs' command block from `--help` so it can't drift.
- **Verification:** **doc drift, three findings.** (1) **`hermes kanban edit` is documented wrong**: the page shows `hermes kanban edit <id> [--title ...] [--body ...] [--priority N]` ("edit task title / body / priority in place"), but the real command is `hermes kanban edit [-h] --result RESULT [--summary SUMMARY] [--metadata METADATA] task_id` — "Edit recovery fields on an already-completed task", with `--result` **required** and no `--title`/`--body`/`--priority` at all (evidence: `cli_help/kanban__edit.txt`, `cli_help/kanban.txt`). (2) **`hermes kanban schedule --at <ISO8601>` does not exist**: the real signature is `hermes kanban schedule [--ids IDS ...] task_id [reason ...]` with no `--at` flag (evidence: `cli_help/kanban__schedule.txt`). (3) **Five verbs are missing from the page's reference block**: `reclaim`, `attach`, `attachments`, `attach-rm`, `repair` (evidence: `cli_help/kanban.txt`); and `--session` / `--step-key` on `list` are undocumented (the page writes `--current-step-key`).

### Kanban concurrency & promotion config  `id: docs-features.kanban-concurrency-config`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `kanban.max_in_progress`, `kanban.max_in_progress_per_profile`, `kanban.auto_promote_children`, `kanban.default_workdir`
- **What it does:** Caps concurrent worker spawns board-wide and per profile, controls automatic child promotion, and sets a board-level default working directory.
- **How it works:** **`max_in_progress`** (default unset = unlimited) caps simultaneously running tasks; when the board already has N running the dispatcher skips spawning more — **useful for slow workers (local LLMs, resource-constrained hosts) so they finish what they have before more pile up and time out**; **invalid or below-1 values log a warning and behave as unlimited**. **`max_in_progress_per_profile`** (default unset = unlimited) is the per-profile variant — **applies alongside the board-wide cap; both must allow a spawn for it to proceed**. **`auto_promote_children`** (default `true`) — after `decompose_triage_task()` produces children with no parent-blocker dependencies they're automatically promoted to `ready`; **set to `false` to require manual review** (children stay in `todo` until you promote them). **`default_workdir`** (default unset) — board-level default working directory applied to new tasks when neither `--workspace` nor the task itself overrides it; **per-task `workspace:` still wins**.
- **Inputs / options:** Documented YAML: `kanban: {max_in_progress: 2, auto_promote_children: false, default_workdir: ~/work/active-project}`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Fewer concurrent spawns; children held in `todo`; inherited workspace.
- **Config / env:** all four keys under `kanban:`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Invalid `max_in_progress` degrades to unlimited with a warning rather than erroring.
- **Rebuild notes:** Provide both a global and a per-assignee concurrency cap, and require *both* to permit a spawn. A better version would compute the cap from observed worker latency instead of a static number.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `max_in_progress: None` present in the kanban config block; `default_workdir` handling at `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:847-948`, `:3424-3440`.

### Scheduled task starts (`scheduled_at`)  `id: docs-features.kanban-scheduled-at`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** task field `scheduled_at`
- **What it does:** Delays dispatch until a specific time.
- **How it works:** **The dispatcher skips ready tasks whose `scheduled_at` is in the future and picks them up on the first tick after that timestamp.**
- **Inputs / options:** The page documents `hermes kanban create "nightly backup audit" --assignee ops --scheduled-at "2026-06-01T03:00:00Z"`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Task held until the timestamp passes.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Related but distinct: the `scheduled` status and the `hermes kanban schedule` verb ("Park one or more tasks in Scheduled (waiting on time, not human input)"), and `hermes kanban unblock` which "Return blocked/**scheduled** tasks to ready".
- **Rebuild notes:** Treat a future start time as a dispatch filter rather than a separate queue. A better version would surface the scheduled time on the card and in `list`.
- **Verification:** **doc drift** — `hermes kanban create` has **no `--scheduled-at` flag** (evidence: `cli_help/kanban__create.txt` — the full option list is `--body --assignee --parent --workspace --branch --project --tenant --priority --triage --idempotency-key --max-runtime --created-by --skill --max-retries --model --provider --goal --goal-max-turns --initial-status --json`), and `hermes kanban schedule` takes no `--at` either, so the documented invocation cannot work as written.

### Kanban respawn guard  `id: docs-features.kanban-respawn-guard`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** dispatcher spawn decision; event `respawn_guarded`
- **What it does:** Refuses to re-spawn a ready task under three conditions, preventing repeat worker storms on the same bug or task while a human catches up.
- **How it works:** Three documented reasons: **`blocker_auth`** — the previous run hit a quota/auth/429 error, so wait for the rate window to reset; **`recent_success`** — a completed run happened within the guard window (documented as the last hour), so wait for review before re-running; **`active_pr`** — a GitHub PR URL appears in a recent task comment, meaning a prior worker already opened a PR.
- **Inputs / options:** n/a (automatic)
- **Outputs / side effects:** A `respawn_guarded` event with `{reason}`; **the task stays in `ready` and the next tick gets another chance to spawn.**
- **Config / env:** interacts with `kanban.failure_limit`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **If the underlying condition persists, the normal `consecutive_failures` circuit breaker will auto-block via `gave_up` after `failure_limit` failures.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Guard on observable signals (last error class, recent success, a PR link in comments) rather than a blanket cooldown, and leave the task in `ready` so recovery is automatic. A better version would surface the guard reason on the card so a human isn't left wondering why nothing spawned.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `respawn_guarded` listed in the event reference with the three reasons.

### Kanban Swarm topology helper (`hermes kanban swarm`)  `id: docs-features.kanban-swarm`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes kanban swarm "<goal>" --workers a,b,c --verifier <p> --synthesizer <p>`
- **What it does:** Creates a durable **Kanban Swarm v1** graph in one shot: a completed root/blackboard card, N parallel worker cards, a verifier card gated on all workers, and a synthesizer card gated on the verifier.
- **How it works:** **Shared swarm context (the "blackboard") is stored as structured JSON comments on the root card so any worker can read it.** **The resulting graph is committed atomically:** dispatchers and dashboard readers see either no new swarm or the complete topology, **never a partially linked root/worker/verifier graph**. It then dispatches normally — workers run in parallel, the verifier wakes after they all finish, and the synthesizer wakes after the verifier marks the work clean.
- **Inputs / options:** Documented invocation: `hermes kanban swarm "Design a multi-region failover plan" --workers researcher,architect,sre --verifier reviewer --synthesizer writer`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Root + N worker + verifier + synthesizer cards with links.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Atomic commit prevents a half-built graph from being dispatched.
- **Rebuild notes:** Commit a whole topology in one transaction so no reader ever sees a partial graph, and put the shared context on the root card rather than duplicating it into every worker. A better version would let the topology be templated (workers/verifier/synthesizer counts) rather than fixed.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `swarm` subcommand present ("Create a Kanban Swarm v1 graph (parallel workers → verifier → synthesizer)", evidence: `cli_help/kanban.txt`, `cli_help/kanban__swarm.txt`).

### `/kanban` slash command  `id: docs-features.kanban-slash`
- **Surface:** Gateway/Telegram
- **Where:** `/kanban <action>` in `hermes chat` and every gateway platform
- **What it does:** Makes every `hermes kanban <action>` verb reachable from inside a chat session and from any messaging platform.
- **How it works:** **Both surfaces call the exact same `hermes_cli.kanban.run_slash()` entry point that reuses the `hermes kanban` argparse tree**, so the argument surface, flags, and output format are identical across CLI, `/kanban`, and `hermes kanban`.
- **Inputs / options:** Platforms: Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Matrix, Mattermost, email, SMS. Documented examples: `/kanban list`; `/kanban show t_abcd`; `/kanban create "write launch post" --assignee writer --parent t_research`; `/kanban comment t_abcd "looks good, ship it"`; `/kanban unblock t_abcd`; `/kanban dispatch --max 3`; `/kanban specify t_abcd`; `/kanban specify --all --tenant engineering`. **Quote multi-word arguments the same way you would on a shell — `run_slash` parses the rest of the line with `shlex.split`, so `"…"` and `'…'` both work.**
- **Outputs / side effects:** Same board mutations as the CLI.
- **Config / env:** none.
