- **Edge cases / guards:** **Output truncation in messaging** — if `/kanban list`, `/kanban show`, or `/kanban tail` produce more than **~3800 characters**, the response is truncated with a `… (truncated; use \`hermes kanban …\` in your terminal for full output)` footer; **the CLI surface has no such cap.** **Autocomplete:** typing `/kanban ` and hitting Tab in the interactive CLI cycles through `list`, `ls`, `show`, `create`, `assign`, `link`, `unlink`, `claim`, `comment`, `complete`, `block`, `unblock`, `archive`, `tail`, `dispatch`, `context`, `init`, `gc`; the remaining verbs (`watch`, `stats`, `runs`, `log`, `assignees`, `heartbeat`, `notify-subscribe`, `notify-list`, `notify-unsubscribe`, `daemon`) also work — **they're just not in the autocomplete hint list yet.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Share the argparse tree between CLI and slash surfaces so a new flag lands everywhere at once. A better version would keep the autocomplete list generated from the parser rather than hand-maintained.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `run_slash()` in `hermes_cli/kanban.py` reuses the argparse tree (the CLI help dumps in `cli_help/kanban*.txt` come from that same tree).

### `/kanban` bypasses the running-agent guard  `id: docs-features.kanban-midrun`
- **Surface:** Gateway/Telegram
- **Where:** `/kanban` while an agent turn is in flight
- **What it does:** Lets board reads and writes go through immediately even while an agent is still thinking, unlike other slash commands and user messages.
- **How it works:** **The gateway normally queues slash commands and user messages while an agent is still thinking** — that's what stops a second turn starting while the first is in flight. **`/kanban` is explicitly exempted from this guard** because the board lives in `~/.hermes/kanban.db`, not in the running agent's state, so reads (`list`, `show`, `context`, `tail`, `watch`, `stats`, `runs`) and writes (`comment`, `unblock`, `block`, `assign`, `archive`, `create`, `link`, …) all go through immediately, even mid-turn.
- **Inputs / options:** Any `/kanban` verb.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Board mutation without interrupting the running agent.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Three documented payoffs: a worker blocks waiting on a peer → `/kanban unblock t_abcd` from your phone and the dispatcher picks the peer up on its next tick (**the blocked worker isn't interrupted — it just stops being blocked**); you spot a card that needs human context → `/kanban comment t_xyz "use the 2026 schema, not 2025"` lands on the task thread and **the *next* run of that task will read it in `kanban_show()`**; you want to know what your fleet is doing without stopping the orchestrator → `/kanban list --mine` or `/kanban stats` inspects the board without touching your main conversation.
- **Rebuild notes:** Exempt commands that touch only out-of-process durable state from the in-flight-turn queue — the guard exists to protect agent state, not the database. A better version would classify every slash command by which state it touches instead of special-casing one.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — the board is a separate SQLite file, so `/kanban` needs no agent-state access.

### Auto-subscribe on `/kanban create` (gateway)  `id: docs-features.kanban-autosubscribe`
- **Surface:** Gateway/Telegram
- **Where:** `/kanban create "…"` from any gateway platform
- **What it does:** Automatically subscribes the originating chat (platform + chat id + thread id) to that task's terminal events, so you get one message back per terminal event without polling or remembering the task id.
- **How it works:** Terminal events are `completed`, `blocked`, `gave_up`, `crashed`, `timed_out`; the `completed` message includes **the first line of the worker's result summary**. Documented exchange: `you> /kanban create "transcribe today's podcast" --assignee transcriber` → `bot> Created t_9fc1a3 (ready, assignee=transcriber) (subscribed — you'll be notified when t_9fc1a3 completes or blocks)` → later → `bot> ✓ t_9fc1a3 completed by transcriber / transcribed 42 minutes, saved to podcast/2026-05-04.md`.
- **Inputs / options:** Automatic on `/kanban create`; **skipped when `--json` is passed** — "the assumption is that scripted callers want to manage subscriptions explicitly via `/kanban notify-subscribe`."
- **Outputs / side effects:** A subscription row in `notify+wake` mode.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.auto_subscribe_on_create` (default `true`); `kanban.done_sub_retention_days` (default `30`; `0` disables the sweep).
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Subscriptions survive a task reaching `done`** — completion is reversible (a reviewer or controller can reopen a done task), so the origin session keeps getting notified through reopen cycles; **they auto-remove on `archived`** (the irreversible end state). **On boards that never archive, a GC sweep purges subscriptions for tasks that have sat in `done` with no new activity for `kanban.done_sub_retention_days` days** so stale rows don't accumulate. **A chat-originated auto-subscribe is created in `notify+wake` mode:** on a terminal event the destination agent both receives the passive message **and** takes a real turn, so it can read the board context and reply in its own voice.
- **Rebuild notes:** Keep subscriptions alive through reversible end states and remove them only on the irreversible one, with a GC sweep for boards that never reach it. A better version would let the user opt a single create out of auto-subscribe without switching to `--json`.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `auto_subscribe_on_create: True` in the kanban config block; `done_sub_retention_days` documented default 30 in the page's config table.

### Kanban notification subscriptions & delivery modes  `id: docs-features.kanban-notify`
- **Surface:** CLI
- **Where:** `hermes kanban notify-subscribe|notify-list|notify-unsubscribe`
- **What it does:** Manages which chats get notified about a task's terminal events, and how strongly (message, agent turn, or both).
- **How it works:** **The gateway's background notifier polls `task_events` every few seconds** and delivers one message per terminal event (`completed`, `blocked`, `gave_up`, `crashed`, `timed_out`) to the subscribed chat. Completed tasks also send **the first line of the worker's `--result`**.
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes kanban notify-subscribe <id> --platform <name> --chat-id <id> [--thread-id <id>] [--user-id <id>] [--chat-type dm|group|channel|thread] [--delivery-mode notify|notify+wake|wake]`; `hermes kanban notify-list [<id>] [--json]`; `hermes kanban notify-unsubscribe <id> --platform <name> --chat-id <id> [--thread-id <id>]`. **Three delivery modes:** `notify` (passive message yes, wake no — the default and original behavior; "you just want a heads-up message in the chat"); `notify+wake` (both — "you also want the destination agent to take a real turn — read the board context and reply in its own voice"; **chat-originated auto-subscribes use this**); `wake` (no passive message, wake yes — "you only want the agent to act on the event, with no separate ping").
- **Outputs / side effects:** Subscription rows; delivered messages and/or synthetic wake turns.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.done_sub_retention_days`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **A "wake" forges a synthetic inbound message to the destination gateway agent so it takes a normal turn** (reads the comment + result, reasons, replies) instead of a one-line passive notification; **it only fires when the notifier runs inside a live gateway process** — otherwise a `notify+wake` subscription still delivers its passive message, while a `wake`-only subscription does nothing in that process. **Which events wake:** `completed`, `blocked`, `gave_up`, `crashed`, `timed_out`, `review_requested` (a worker finished the implementation and handed off via `kanban_request_review`) and `block_loop_detected` (the task was routed to `triage` after repeated blocks). **`status`, `archived` and `unblocked` are delivered but never wake — they are bookkeeping transitions, not decisions.** When a `completed` or `review_requested` event carries a summary, **that handoff rides the wake turn**. **`--chat-type` records the originating chat's type so a woken turn resolves the operator's real session:** `build_session_key` keys groups, channels, and threads differently from DMs, so an inaccurate `chat_type` would route the wake into a separate, context-less session; the `/kanban` auto-subscribe and slash-command paths capture this automatically — set it by hand only when subscribing from a script or cron; **omit it to leave an existing subscription unchanged (new subscriptions default to `dm`)**. **A subscription removes itself automatically once the task reaches `done` or `archived`; no cleanup needed** (note this contradicts the auto-subscribe section's "subscriptions survive `done`" — an internal doc inconsistency).
- **Rebuild notes:** Separate "tell me" from "act on it" as distinct delivery modes, and only wake on events that hand a decision back. A better version would reconcile the two contradictory statements about whether a subscription survives `done`.
- **Verification:** partial — the three notify verbs exist (evidence: `cli_help/kanban.txt`, `cli_help/kanban__notify-subscribe.txt`), but the page contradicts itself on subscription lifetime at `done`: the auto-subscribe section says subscriptions survive `done` and are removed on `archived`, while the gateway-notifications section says "A subscription removes itself automatically once the task reaches `done` or `archived`" (doc drift, internal).

### Multi-profile kanban delivery ownership  `id: docs-features.kanban-multi-gateway`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** one-gateway-per-profile deployments; `kanban.dispatch_in_gateway`
- **What it does:** Splits dispatch (single-owner) from notification delivery (profile-owned) so several gateways can coexist against one board.
- **How it works:** **Dispatch stays single-owner** — exactly one gateway keeps `kanban.dispatch_in_gateway: true` and runs the dispatcher; **every other gateway sets it to `false`**. **Notification delivery is profile-owned** — every gateway, including non-dispatch ones, runs the notifier and **polls only subscriptions stamped with a profile whose platform adapters it hosts**; a task created from the `writer` profile's Telegram gets its `completed`/`blocked` message delivered by the `writer` gateway, even though the `default` gateway did the dispatching. **Legacy subscriptions** created before profile stamping (no `notifier_profile` on the row) **are delivered only by the gateway that holds the actual dispatcher singleton lock**, so two gateways never race for them.
- **Inputs / options:** `kanban.dispatch_in_gateway: true` on exactly one gateway, `false` on the rest.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Delivery through each profile's own adapters.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.dispatch_in_gateway`; the multi-gateway guide at `docs/kanban/multi-gateway.md`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Duplicate delivery across gateways is prevented by the atomic per-event claim in the board DB. No relays, credential sharing, or extra dispatchers are needed.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Make delivery ownership a stamped field on the subscription and de-duplicate with an atomic per-event claim, so scaling out gateways needs no coordination protocol. A better version would migrate legacy unstamped subscriptions on first delivery.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `dispatch_in_gateway: True` default in the kanban config block; per-event claim in `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`.

### Kanban runs (one row per attempt)  `id: docs-features.kanban-runs`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `task_runs` table; `hermes kanban runs <id>`; dashboard Run History; `GET /api/plugins/kanban/tasks/:id` → `runs[]`
- **What it does:** Records every attempt to execute a task as its own row, with structured handoff attached.
- **How it works:** **A task is a logical unit of work; a run is one attempt to execute it.** When the dispatcher claims a ready task it creates a row in `task_runs` and points `tasks.current_run_id` at it; when the attempt ends — completed, blocked, crashed, timed out, spawn-failed, reclaimed — the run row closes with an `outcome` and the task's pointer clears. **A task attempted three times has three `task_runs` rows.** Rationale: **you need full attempt history for real-world postmortems and a clean place to hang per-attempt metadata** — which files changed, which tests ran, which findings a reviewer noted; **those are run facts, not task facts.**
- **Inputs / options:** Three handoff fields: `summary` (tool param) / `--summary` (CLI) — human handoff, goes on the run, downstream children see it in their `build_worker_context`; `metadata` (tool param) / `--metadata` (CLI) — free-form JSON dict on the run, children see it serialized alongside the summary; `result` (tool param) / `--result` (CLI) — short log line on the task row (**legacy field, kept for back-compat**). CLI closeout: `hermes kanban complete t_abcd --result "…" --summary "…" --metadata '{"changed_files": [...], "tests_run": 14}'`. Inspect with `hermes kanban runs t_abcd` (a table of `#  OUTCOME  PROFILE  ELAPSED  STARTED` plus the summary line per attempt).
- **Outputs / side effects:** `task_runs` rows; `task_events` rows carry the `run_id` they belong to so the UI can group them by attempt; **the `completed` event embeds the first-line summary in its payload (capped at 400 chars)** so gateway notifiers can render structured handoffs without a second SQL round-trip.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Downstream children read the most recent completed run's summary + metadata for each parent. Retrying workers read the prior attempts on their own task** (outcome, summary, error) so they don't repeat a path that already failed. **Reclaimed runs from status changes:** dragging a running task off `running` in the dashboard (back to `ready` or straight to `todo`), or archiving a still-running task, closes the in-flight run with `outcome='reclaimed'` rather than orphaning it — **the `task_runs` row is always in a terminal state when `tasks.current_run_id` is `NULL`, and vice versa, an invariant that holds across CLI, dashboard, dispatcher, and notifier.** **Synthetic runs for never-claimed completions:** completing or blocking a task that was never claimed (a human closing a `ready` task from the dashboard with a summary, or `hermes kanban complete <ready-task> --summary X`) inserts a **zero-duration run row (`started_at == ended_at`)** carrying the summary / metadata / reason so attempt history stays complete, and the `completed` / `blocked` event's `run_id` points at that row. **`PATCH /api/plugins/kanban/tasks/:id` with `{status: "done", summary, metadata}` forwards both to the kernel**, so the dashboard's "mark done" button is CLI-equivalent.
- **Rebuild notes:** Separate task facts from attempt facts into two tables, and maintain a strict invariant between `current_run_id` and run terminality. A better version would let a run carry its own artifact list rather than folding artifacts into metadata.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `hermes kanban runs` is "Show attempt history for a task (one row per run: profile, outcome, elapsed, summary)" (evidence: `cli_help/kanban.txt`).

### Kanban forward-compatibility columns  `id: docs-features.kanban-forward-compat`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `tasks.workflow_template_id`, `tasks.current_step_key`
- **What it does:** Reserves two nullable columns for v2 workflow routing so a v2 release needs no further schema migration.
- **How it works:** `workflow_template_id` records which template this task belongs to, `current_step_key` which step in that template is active. **The v1 kernel ignores them for routing but lets clients write them.**
- **Inputs / options:** Filterable today via `hermes kanban list --workflow-template-id ID --step-key KEY`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Values stored, not acted on.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Writing them has no routing effect in v1.
- **Rebuild notes:** Reserve nullable columns for planned routing so the migration cost is paid once. A better version would ship a v1 validator that rejects an unknown template id.
- **Verification:** doc drift — both columns exist and are filterable, but the CLI flag is **`--step-key KEY`**, not the `--current-step-key` the page's CLI block shows (evidence: `cli_help/kanban__list.txt`).

### Kanban event reference  `id: docs-features.kanban-events`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `task_events` table; `hermes kanban tail <id>`; `hermes kanban watch [--kinds …]`
- **What it does:** Records every transition as an append-only event row, grouped into three clusters so filtering is easy.
- **How it works:** **Each row carries an optional `run_id` so UIs can group events by attempt.** **Lifecycle events (what changed about the task as a logical unit):** `created` `{assignee, status, parents, tenant}` (task inserted, `run_id` NULL); `promoted` (no payload — `todo → ready` because all parents hit `done`, `run_id` NULL); `claimed` `{lock, expires, run_id}`; `completed` `{result_len, summary?}` (`summary` is the first-line handoff, 400-char cap; full version on the run row; a never-claimed task with handoff fields synthesizes a zero-duration run); `blocked` `{reason, kind, recurrences}` (`kind` is `needs_input`, `capability`, `transient`, or `null` for a generic block; `recurrences` is the unblock-loop counter); `dependency_wait` `{reason, kind}` (worker blocked with `kind=dependency` — routes to `todo`, parent-gated and auto-promoted, **no human needed**); `block_loop_detected` `{reason, kind, recurrences, limit}`; `unblocked` (no payload — resets `consecutive_failures`, preserves `block_recurrences`, `run_id` NULL); `archived` (carries the `run_id` of the run reclaimed as a side effect if the task was still running). **Edit events (human-driven changes that aren't transitions):** `assigned` `{assignee}`; `edited` `{fields}`; `reprioritized` `{priority}`; `status` `{status}` (dashboard drag-drop wrote a status directly; carries the `run_id` of a run reclaimed when dragging off `running`, otherwise NULL). **Worker telemetry (about the execution process, not the logical task):** `spawned` `{pid}`; `heartbeat` `{note?}`; `reclaimed` `{stale_lock}`; `crashed` `{pid, claimer}`; `timed_out` `{pid, elapsed_seconds, limit_seconds, sigkill}` (**`max_runtime_seconds` exceeded; dispatcher SIGTERM'd then SIGKILL'd after 5 s grace and re-queued**); `stale` `{elapsed_seconds, last_heartbeat_at, heartbeat_age_seconds, timeout_seconds, pid, terminated}` (**does NOT tick the failure counter — stale is dispatcher-side absence detection, not a worker fault**); `reconciled` `{reason, claim_lock, claim_expires, worker_pid}`; `respawn_guarded` `{reason}`; `spawn_failed` `{error, failures}`; `protocol_violation` `{pid, claimer, exit_code, protocol_violation}`; `gave_up` `{failures, effective_limit, limit_source, error}`.
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes kanban tail <id>` shows these for a single task; `hermes kanban watch` streams them board-wide with `--kinds completed,gave_up,timed_out`, `--assignee`, `--tenant`, `--interval SECS`.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Append-only rows driving the dashboard, the notifier, and the CLI streams.
- **Config / env:** `kanban.reconcile_orphans` (default `true`); `kanban.dispatch_stale_timeout_seconds` (default 4 h); `kanban.failure_limit`; per-task `max_retries`.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **`reconciled`** covers orphaned-card reconciliation: the card was `running` with broken claim bookkeeping (`claim_lock` or `claim_expires` NULL — crash mid-claim, manual SQL, DB restore) **and no live worker, so none of the TTL/crash/stale paths could ever recover it**; the dispatcher requeues it to `ready` with an explanatory comment, gated by `kanban.reconcile_orphans`. **`gave_up`'s effective limit resolves as task `max_retries`, then dispatcher `failure_limit` / `kanban.failure_limit`, then the built-in default.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Group event kinds into lifecycle / edits / telemetry so a consumer can subscribe to only what it cares about, and never let dispatcher-side absence detection tick a worker-fault counter. A better version would publish the event schema as machine-readable JSON so external consumers can validate.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `reconcile_orphans: bool = True` at `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:9832`, `:9914`, applied at `:9957`; `_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION_FAILURE_LIMIT = 3` at `:8804`; `BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT = 2` at `:134`.

### Kanban collaboration patterns (P1–P9)  `id: docs-features.kanban-patterns`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** kanban.md → "Collaboration patterns"
- **What it does:** Lists nine patterns the board supports **without any new primitives**.
- **How it works:** **P1 Fan-out** — N siblings, same role ("research 5 angles in parallel"). **P2 Pipeline** — role chain: scout → editor → writer (daily brief assembly). **P3 Voting / quorum** — N siblings + 1 aggregator (3 researchers → 1 reviewer picks). **P4 Long-running journal** — same profile + shared dir + cron (Obsidian vault). **P5 Human-in-the-loop** — worker blocks → user comments → unblock (ambiguous decisions). **P6 `@mention`** — inline routing from prose (`@reviewer look at this`). **P7 Thread-scoped workspace** — `/kanban here` in a thread (per-project gateway threads). **P8 Fleet farming** — one profile, N subjects (50 social accounts). **P9 Triage specifier** — rough idea → `triage` → `hermes kanban specify` expands body → `todo`.
- **Inputs / options:** n/a
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** The header says "eight patterns" but nine (P1–P9) are listed — a minor internal inconsistency. Worked examples live in `docs/hermes-kanban-v1-spec.pdf`.
- **Rebuild notes:** Design the primitives so common multi-agent shapes need no new features, then document the shapes. A better version would ship each pattern as a `hermes kanban` topology helper the way `swarm` already is.
- **Verification:** doc drift (minor) — the prose says "these eight patterns" immediately above a table listing **nine** rows (P1–P9). Also `/kanban here` (P7) is not in the `hermes kanban` subcommand list (evidence: `cli_help/kanban.txt`).

### Parent links as context handoff  `id: docs-features.kanban-parent-handoff`
- **Surface:** Core
- **Where:** `--parent <id>` on create; `build_worker_context` → `## Parent task results`
- **What it does:** Makes a parent link the **context handoff channel** from a completed card to a new one, not just a scheduling gate.
- **How it works:** Two things happen when you create a card with `--parent <done-card-id>`: **(1) It's immediately eligible** — `create_task` sets status by parent state, so a child whose parents are all `done` is created directly in `ready`, no waiting and no manual promotion (children of still-open parents sit in `todo` until `recompute_ready` promotes them when the last parent finishes). **(2) The parent's handoff rides along** — the worker context assembled for the child (`build_worker_context`, what `kanban_show()` returns) contains a `## Parent task results` section with each parent's completion `summary` and `metadata`, verbatim, e.g. `### t_77c26979 (completed just now)` / the summary / `_metadata_: {"changed_files": [...], "decisions": [...]}`.
- **Inputs / options:** `--parent PARENT` (repeatable) on create; `parents=[…]` on `kanban_create`; `kanban_link(parent_id, child_id)` after the fact.
- **Outputs / side effects:** `task_links` rows; parent summaries in the child's context.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **"This is why the pattern for follow-up work on a finished card is a new child card, not reopening the done card. Completed cards are immutable history — their context flows forward through the parent link."** **Same-card rework (retry loops on a failing card) is a different mechanism** — prior attempts on the *same* card surface as "prior attempts" in that card's own context. **A worktree or branch alone is not a substitute:** repo state tells the follow-up worker *what* the code looks like but not *why* — the decisions, tests run, and files touched live in the parent's structured handoff, not in git. **Evidence that didn't exist when the parent completed (e.g. a CI log that failed later) belongs in the new card's body.** Documented example creates a "Fix CI failure from t_impl" card with `--parent t_impl` and a heredoc body carrying the CI run number, log excerpt, acceptance criteria, and an instruction to use a fresh worktree/branch.
- **Rebuild notes:** Make the dependency edge carry structured context, not just ordering, so a follow-up card starts informed. A better version would let a child request specific metadata keys from its parents rather than receiving everything.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `--parent PARENT` "Parent task id (repeatable)" (evidence: `cli_help/kanban__create.txt`); parent-state-driven initial status in `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`'s `create_task`.

### Reconciling colliding worker branches  `id: docs-features.kanban-reconciliation`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** kanban.md → "Reconciling colliding worker branches"
- **What it does:** Prescribes a third-party reconciliation card when two workers' branches conflict.
- **How it works:** **Don't let either worker self-adjudicate** — the colliding agent lacks its peer's context and reliably overwrites the other side or abandons its own. Instead, **create a reconciliation card assigned to a third, neutral profile with both conflicted cards linked as parents**: the parent links carry both sides' completion summaries into the reconciler's context, so it receives **both diffs and both intents**.
- **Inputs / options:** The bundled `agent-merge-conflict-arbiter` optional skill (`optional-skills/autonomous-ai-agents/agent-merge-conflict-arbiter/SKILL.md`) gives that worker the full procedure: **classify each conflicted hunk, resolve impartially, verify, and hand back a summary naming every decision.**
- **Outputs / side effects:** A reconciled branch plus a decision summary.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** Applies to engineering pipelines (P1/P2 with worktrees).
- **Rebuild notes:** Route conflicts to a neutral third party with both parents linked, because the mechanism that supplies context (parent links) is exactly what the arbiter needs. A better version would detect the collision automatically and mint the reconciliation card.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — the `agent-merge-conflict-arbiter` skill lives under `optional-skills/autonomous-ai-agents/`.

### Collision hotspots in parallel campaigns  `id: docs-features.kanban-hotspots`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** task comments with the `hotspot:` prefix; completion `metadata`
- **What it does:** A comment convention (not a new primitive) for flagging files that become merge-conflict magnets in wide campaigns.
- **How it works:** **A worker that notices its diff keeps colliding with siblings in one file — or that a file it touches keeps appearing in other cards' recent comments — should not silently pile on.** Instead it leaves a comment on its own card with a recognizable prefix, e.g. `hotspot: hermes_cli/kanban_db.py — third conflicting edit to the dispatch loop this wave`, and **repeats the flag in its completion `metadata`**.
- **Inputs / options:** The `hotspot:` comment prefix.
- **Outputs / side effects:** A greppable signal on the board.
- **Config / env:** none.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Orchestrators (or humans reviewing the board) who see two or more `hotspot:` comments naming the same path should create a dedicated refactor/decomposition card for that file *before* queuing more work that touches it** — splitting the magnet file is cheaper than reconciling every future collision it would cause. For conflicts that have *already* happened, use the reconciliation-card pattern; **hotspot flagging is the upstream fix that keeps the reconciler from becoming a standing lane.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Solve coordination problems with a naming convention over the existing comment channel before adding a primitive. A better version would let the dashboard aggregate `hotspot:` comments by path automatically.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — convention only; uses the existing `kanban_comment` / `hermes kanban comment` channel.

### Kanban multi-tenant usage  `id: docs-features.kanban-tenants`
- **Surface:** Config
- **Where:** `--tenant <name>` on create; env `$HERMES_TENANT` in the worker
- **What it does:** Lets one specialist fleet serve multiple businesses with data isolation by workspace path and memory key prefix.
- **How it works:** Tag each task with a tenant; **workers receive `$HERMES_TENANT` and namespace their memory writes by prefix.** **The board, the dispatcher, and the profile definitions are all shared; only the data is scoped.**
- **Inputs / options:** `hermes kanban create "monthly report" --assignee researcher --tenant business-a --workspace dir:~/tenants/business-a/data/`; `--tenant T` filters on `list`, `watch`, `specify`; the dashboard's tenant dropdown.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Tenant tag on the task; `$HERMES_TENANT` in the worker env.
- **Config / env:** `dashboard.kanban.default_tenant` preselects the filter.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Tenants are a soft filter; boards are the hard isolation boundary.**
- **Rebuild notes:** Provide a soft namespace for reporting/filtering and a hard one (separate DB) for isolation, and say plainly which is which. A better version would enforce that a tenant's tasks can only use workspaces under that tenant's directory.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — `--tenant TENANT` "Tenant namespace" on create and `--tenant` filters on `list` (evidence: `cli_help/kanban__create.txt`, `cli_help/kanban__list.txt`).

### Kanban desktop notifications  `id: docs-features.kanban-desktop-notifications`
- **Surface:** Desktop app
- **Where:** Desktop app Kanban plugin; **Settings ▸ Notifications ▸ Plugin notifications**
- **What it does:** Surfaces the same terminal events natively in the desktop app — no gateway platform required.
- **How it works:** **While the Kanban board's live event socket is connected**, each `completed`, `blocked`, `gave_up`, `crashed`, `timed_out`, or routed-to-triage (`block_loop_detected`) event raises an **in-app toast** with the worker's handoff (summary, block reason, or error) and an **"Open Kanban"** action. **When you're away from the Hermes window, the same event also fires a native OS notification**, gated by Settings ▸ Notifications ▸ Plugin notifications.
- **Inputs / options:** The **Plugin notifications** toggle in desktop settings.
- **Outputs / side effects:** Toasts and OS notifications.
- **Config / env:** desktop settings only.
- **Edge cases / guards:** **Coverage window:** desktop notifications ride the live event stream, so **they fire only while the app is running with the Kanban plugin enabled. Events that land while the app is closed are not replayed as notifications on next launch** — use a gateway subscription for delivery that must survive the app being closed.
- **Rebuild notes:** State the coverage window plainly (live stream only, no replay) and point at the durable alternative. A better version would replay missed terminal events on launch from the event id watermark.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — same six terminal/routing event kinds as the gateway notifier (see the event reference).

### Kanban out-of-scope: single-host by design  `id: docs-features.kanban-single-host`
- **Surface:** Docs
- **Where:** kanban.md → "Out of scope"
- **What it does:** States the hard architectural boundary.
- **How it works:** **`~/.hermes/kanban.db` is a local SQLite file and the dispatcher spawns workers on the same machine. Running a shared board across two hosts is not supported** — there's no coordination primitive for "worker X on host A, worker Y on host B," and **the crash-detection path assumes PIDs are host-local.**
- **Inputs / options:** If you need multi-host, **run an independent board per host and use `delegate_task` / a message queue to bridge them.**
- **Outputs / side effects:** n/a
- **Config / env:** n/a
- **Edge cases / guards:** The complete design — architecture, concurrency correctness, comparison with other systems, implementation plan, risks, open questions — lives in `docs/hermes-kanban-v1-spec.pdf`; **"Read that before filing any behavior-change PR."**
- **Rebuild notes:** State the single-host assumption explicitly and name the mechanism that depends on it (host-local PIDs), so nobody assumes distribution is a config change. A better version would abstract liveness detection behind an interface so a distributed backend becomes possible.
- **Verification:** implemented as documented — crash detection compares PIDs and process-start fingerprints locally (same approach as the cron execution ledger).
